job.title: Compliance and Systems Analyst (Union City)
job.description:
What This Role Covers

MidPen Housing manages over 142 affordable communities across Northern California, housing more than 22,800 residents. The Compliance and Systems Analyst sits inside the Compliance Department and serves as a connective resource between site staff, Asset Management, Development, and the regulatory agencies that govern affordable housing funding programs. This is a technical and analytical position, not a leasing or operations role.

The core of the work is making sure properties stay current with their regulatory obligations. That means Tax Credit annual reporting, HCD Schedules of Rental Income, income and rent limit calculations, utility allowance updates, and centralized compliance documentation. You'll also own the compliance-related settings inside the property management software and help site staff understand how those settings translate to real-world requirements.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Produce and manage annual reporting deliverables for Tax Credit and HCD requirements across the portfolio
  • Calculate and maintain income limits, rent limits, and utility allowances as regulations change
  • Configure and maintain compliance settings in property management software; train staff on implementation
  • Analyze and document changes in program requirements and work with Asset Management and Development to validate regulatory impacts
  • Support other departments with compliance data needed for funding applications and property budgets
  • Develop and deliver compliance training to property management staff
  • Research and resolve regulatory interpretation questions from site and management teams
  • Build and maintain monitoring processes and analytical tools for ongoing compliance tracking

What Strong Candidates Bring

Three years of affordable housing compliance experience is the benchmark. Candidates with direct exposure to Tax Credits, HOME, HCD, Section 8, or similar programs will get up to speed faster than those coming from conventional property management. HCCP or COS certifications signal that you've already worked within these frameworks rather than learning them on the job.

Advanced Excel proficiency matters here. A meaningful portion of the work involves building, maintaining, and auditing calculation tools tied to regulatory data. If your Excel skills are conversational rather than fluent, this role will be a grind. Strong written communication also matters because you're regularly translating dense regulatory language into practical guidance for site staff who don't live in compliance documentation.

The annual compensation range is $70,304 to $78,300. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, and pet insurance, among others.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

The Assistant Community Manager position at Hawthorne Residential Partners draws on a specific combination of financial literacy and people skills that most leasing roles don't require in equal measure. You'll be processing rent payments, reviewing ledgers for billing accuracy, tracking delinquency, and coordinating eviction procedures when necessary. At the same time, you're conducting tours, following up on leads, and working toward occupancy goals through both new leases and resident renewals. The financial and the relational sides of this job are genuinely intertwined, and candidates who handle both naturally tend to advance quickly.

Greenville's rental market is shaped heavily by East Carolina University's enrollment cycles, which means occupancy trends, traffic patterns, and renewal timing here can look different from a typical suburban garden-style community. Understanding that rhythm matters. Strong candidates will recognize how seasonal demand affects leasing urgency and adjust their approach accordingly.

What You'll Be Managing Day to Day

On the leasing side, you'll guide prospects from first contact through signed lease, handle applications and renewals accurately, and contribute to the community's social media presence to support engagement and visibility. On the financial side, expect to monitor delinquency weekly, post payments, and conduct regular ledger reviews to catch discrepancies before they compound. You'll also assist with reporting for the Community Manager and regional leadership.

When the Community Manager is out, you step in. That means maintaining team continuity, keeping priorities clear, and handling resident concerns with enough composure to de-escalate without escalating to leadership every time. The role runs on a 40-hour schedule across a Monday through Saturday office week, with one weekday off. Some evening and weekend availability may be required depending on community events.

What Separates Strong Candidates

  • Financial fluency: You can read a rent roll, spot a ledger error, and have a confident conversation about budget implications.
  • Conflict resolution without escalation: Resident disputes get resolved at your level. You don't need a script or a supervisor to close the loop.
  • Leasing instinct: You identify what a prospect actually needs and connect that to what the community offers, rather than running through a generic pitch.
  • Consistency under pressure: Delinquency follow-up, eviction coordination, and high-traffic leasing periods all happen simultaneously. Staying organized matters more than moving fast.

Hawthorne operates a formal Career Path Program, which makes this role a genuine on-ramp to a Community Manager position. The company is a top-50 multifamily operator with deep roots in the Southeast, and their internal development track reflects that scale. Assistant Community Managers here are eligible for monthly leasing and renewal commissions, quarterly performance bonuses, and a full benefits package that includes dental at no cost, medical and vision options, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and paid time off that includes your birthday. A valid driver's license is required. Prior property management experience is preferred, and a CALP accreditation is a plus.

job.title: Market Assistant Property Manager I
job.description:
John M. Corcoran & Company has been managing residential communities in New England since 1951. The Assistant Property Manager role at The Elmstead in South Easton, MA sits at the center of daily operations: leasing, resident relations, compliance, and administrative oversight all run through this position.

What the Job Covers

This is a full-cycle operations role at the property level. You'll support leasing activity from initial inquiry through application approval, handle resident accounts including rent collection and delinquency follow-up, and coordinate move-ins, move-outs, and inspections. Resident concerns come to you first, and you're expected to handle them or route them effectively.

Affordable housing compliance is a real part of this role. JMC specifically calls out affordable housing experience and Fair Housing knowledge as requirements, so this position involves maintaining accurate files and preparing compliance-related reports, not just general leasing support. If you've worked in tax credit or project-based properties, that background applies directly here.

Day-to-day, you'll work closely with the property manager on occupancy targets and community operations. Yardi is the platform, so comfort with that system matters from day one.

What JMC Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent; relevant experience considered
  • At least 3 years of property management experience
  • Hands-on affordable housing compliance background
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Yardi
  • Strong communication and organizational skills

The pay range runs $25 to $36 per hour depending on experience, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, PTO, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match. Schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5.

The Longer View

What separates strong candidates here is affordable housing fluency. Many APM candidates come in with solid leasing backgrounds but limited compliance experience. At a company like JMC, where affordable communities are part of the portfolio, understanding recertifications, income qualifications, and regulatory reporting gives you a real edge and opens the path to a Property Manager role faster than general experience alone would.

JMC has a track record of internal promotion. Team members who build competency in both operations and compliance tend to move into site management roles within the company. If that's the trajectory you're after, this position offers the right foundation.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This Community Manager position at Paragon Properties in Harrison Township draws on three skills more than anything else: sales instinct, operational discipline, and people management. You're reading delinquency reports and coaching a leasing agent in the same afternoon. You're tracking lease expirations while handling a resident complaint at the front desk. The work is varied, and the person who does it well stays organized without losing the interpersonal touch.

Yardi proficiency helps. Fair Housing knowledge is non-negotiable. If you've worked as a Leasing Manager or Assistant Manager on-site, you already know the rhythm of this role. If your background is supervisory from outside property management, you'll need at least two years of that experience plus genuine customer service orientation to be considered.

What the Job Actually Covers

You'll carry full responsibility for day-to-day site operations: physical and economic occupancy, rent collection, lease expirations, fiscal oversight, and compliance with company policy and owner objectives. You'll supervise both leasing and maintenance staff, which means you're setting expectations, running performance conversations, and building development plans for your team members.

  • Physical and economic occupancy management
  • Rent collection and delinquency follow-through
  • Lease expiration tracking and renewal strategy
  • Leasing and maintenance staff supervision and development
  • Resident satisfaction across all touchpoints
  • Fiscal management and adherence to owner objectives
  • Fair Housing, state, local, and federal compliance

Strong written and verbal communication matters here because you're the person residents escalate to, the person ownership hears from on performance, and the person your team looks to for direction. All three audiences require a different register, and switching between them quickly is part of the job.

What Makes a Strong Candidate at This Level

The gap between average and strong at the Community Manager level usually comes down to follow-through and team development. Plenty of candidates can lease an apartment. Fewer can consistently hold a maintenance tech and a leasing consultant accountable to the same performance standard while keeping both engaged. If you've built that habit already, it shows up fast in an interview.

Paragon offers a compensation structure that includes quarterly bonuses tied to property performance goals, a 401(k) with employer contribution, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits with a short waiting period, paid holidays, volunteer hours, and a rent discount. A formal training program with advancement potential is in place, which matters if you're thinking beyond this site and toward a portfolio or regional role down the road.

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required before start. This is a full-time, 40-hour, on-site position in Harrison Township, Michigan.

job.title: Regional Real Estate Asset Manager
job.description:
Ackermann Group has been developing and managing real estate in the Midwest since 1938, which means this isn't a startup piecing together a portfolio. It's a mature, privately held organization with deep Cincinnati roots and the kind of institutional memory that shapes how decisions actually get made. The Regional Real Estate Asset Manager role sits at the intersection of financial oversight, pricing strategy, and acquisition analysis, reporting from the company's Cincinnati headquarters.

The core of the job is fiduciary: you represent ownership and investor interests across a regional portfolio of multifamily assets. That means you're setting NOI targets during the annual budget cycle, recommending concession strategy when occupancy softens, analyzing loss-to-lease on the rent roll, and making daily rent approvals through AIRM. You're also the one who walks competitive properties, critiques make-ready quality and unit fit relative to market position, and communicates findings to property management with enough specificity that the operational team can act on them. This is a role that requires you to move fluently between the ledger and the leasing office.

The acquisitions component adds real weight to the position. You'll build submarket expertise, maintain broker relationships, underwrite deals using data-driven operating assumptions, and frame buy-versus-hold decisions on existing assets. That annual exit-horizon analysis for each property is the kind of work that influences capital allocation at the ownership level, so the expectation is that your recommendations are grounded in primary research and secondary data sources like CoStar and Hello Data, not just intuition.

What the Role Requires

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, real estate, economics, or a related discipline; master's degree preferred
  • Five or more years of experience in commercial real estate, with direct exposure to financial analysis, valuation, and acquisitions
  • Comfort reading and presenting accounting reports, rent rolls, and financial forecasts to cross-functional partners
  • Advanced Excel proficiency, particularly for underwriting and scenario modeling
  • Familiarity with AIRM, CoStar, or comparable pricing and market research platforms is a meaningful advantage

Cincinnati's multifamily market has been relatively stable compared to the high-growth Sun Belt markets that absorbed most of the 2021 to 2023 lease-up activity. That stability cuts both ways: rent growth has been measured, which puts real pressure on expense management and capex allocation to protect NOI. For an asset manager, that environment demands sharper underwriting discipline and a close read on submarket-level supply. Someone who's been watching Class B garden-style performance across the I-71 corridor, or tracking how suburban Hamilton County has absorbed new inventory, will find that knowledge directly applicable here.

Strong candidates for this type of role tend to distinguish themselves not just by financial modeling competency, but by their ability to connect physical asset condition to economic performance. Knowing why a property's T-12 looks the way it does, diagnosing whether it's a pricing problem, an operational problem, or a capital problem, and presenting a credible path forward to senior management is what separates an analyst from someone who can actually run a portfolio.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Pavilions Apartments
job.description:
A prospect pulls up to Pavilions Apartments after scheduling a self-guided tour on their lunch break. Before they ever meet a leasing agent, the tour unit needs to be clean, unlocked, stocked with materials, and set up to make a strong first impression. That preparation falls on this role.

What This Role Covers

The Customer Experience Specialist at Pavilions serves as the primary point of contact for prospects, current residents, and vendors. That means greeting everyone who walks through the door, managing incoming calls, logging accurate notes in the property management system, and making sure service requests get handed off to maintenance clearly and completely. You'll also support the full leasing cycle: answering availability and pricing questions, assisting applicants through the documentation process, and following up with prospects to support occupancy goals.

Beyond the front office, this role carries real responsibility for how the community looks and feels. You'll walk the property regularly, maintain self-guided tour units, assist with signage and directional materials, and help plan and execute resident events. When a resident needs a package retrieved, a work order submitted, or a quick answer about their move-out date, you're the person who handles it or finds someone who can.

What You'll Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year of customer-facing experience, strong interpersonal communication, and genuine comfort working in a high-traffic, detail-sensitive environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office is expected from day one, and you'll need to pick up property management software quickly. Cottonwood uses Entrata, so any prior exposure helps. A high school diploma or GED is required. Prior multifamily experience is a plus, but Cottonwood has built the role to be accessible to candidates coming from hospitality, retail, or administrative backgrounds who demonstrate the right instincts.

What you'll build here is a working knowledge of how a multifamily community actually runs. You'll learn how leasing traffic connects to occupancy, how maintenance coordination affects resident satisfaction scores, and how the front office shapes the financial health of a property through retention. Those skills transfer directly to leasing consultant and assistant manager roles, and they're the foundation that makes future experience with NOI, delinquency, and T-12 reporting make sense when you're ready for that next step.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • 1+ years of in-person, customer-facing experience
  • 1+ years of customer service, administrative, sales, or hospitality experience
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office; ability to learn Entrata or similar platforms
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to walk the property, stand for extended periods, and work indoors and outdoors
  • Flexibility for extended hours, including pre-opening availability when needed
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly and occasionally more

Candidates who stand out in this role tend to be the ones who treat the self-guided tour setup with the same care as a staffed showing. The prospect who walks through an unattended unit is forming an opinion about the property, the company, and whether they want to sign a lease. That attention to detail, applied consistently, is what separates strong performers from average ones here.

job.title: Area Property Manager
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on a Tuesday, and you're already one property down and four to go. You've checked in with your maintenance tech at the first site, flagged a curb-appeal issue on the way out, and you're pulling into the next community two minutes later. That's what this portfolio looks like in practice: five small apartment communities in Hawthorne and Lawndale, all within a tight geographic cluster, totaling 110 units.

What This Role Actually Involves

Property Management Associates is hiring an Area Property Manager to run day-to-day operations across this portfolio. Because the properties sit close together, you're not burning half your day in traffic between sites. You're on the ground, present, and visible in ways that matter to both residents and ownership.

The work covers the full range of community operations. You'll conduct regular property inspections with a sharp eye for preventative maintenance, curb appeal, and safety. You'll coordinate maintenance staff and outside vendors, keeping work orders moving and turnovers clean. On the leasing side, you'll market available units, conduct tours, and follow up with prospects to hold strong occupancy. The administrative side is real, too: applications, move-ins, move-outs, renewals, resident communications, and financial tracking all run through Yardi Voyager. You'll assist with budgeting, monitor income and expenses, and keep records accurate.

One weekend day per week is part of the schedule, and on-call rotation comes with the territory. That's the honest reality of residential property management at this scale.

This is an on-site role. PMA offers a free two-bedroom, two-bathroom apartment as part of the compensation package, along with a $300 monthly auto allowance, $25 monthly cell allowance, and a pay range of $24 to $27 per hour. Full-time employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contributions, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short and long-term disability, and generous paid time off.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Minimum 3 years of conventional multifamily property management experience
  • Comfortable with Yardi Voyager or similar property management software
  • Solid grasp of property accounting and operational reporting
  • Proven track record in leasing, marketing, and resident relations
  • Able to supervise and coordinate maintenance staff and vendors effectively
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with real organizational discipline
  • Valid driver's license and auto insurance required; background, DMV, and pre-employment physical checks are part of the hiring process

The candidates who tend to thrive in portfolios like this one are managers who don't need a lot of hand-holding but do want real support behind them. PMA has been operating in greater LA County for over 30 years as a full-service residential and commercial management company. They're not a startup learning as they go. If you want a stable environment with room to grow into a larger portfolio or a regional role over time, the structure is there.

What separates strong applicants here is the combination of genuine resident-relations instincts and financial literacy. This isn't a leasing-only role and it isn't a pure administrative role. You're the person residents call when something's wrong, the one vendors report to on job status, and the one ownership expects to flag a budget variance before it becomes a problem. If those three dynamics feel familiar and manageable, this is worth a close look.

job.title: Sales & Resident Experience Consultant - DT Los Angeles, CA
job.description:
Thurman Lofts sits in the middle of downtown Los Angeles, which means your prospect pool is genuinely diverse: remote workers eyeing a live-work setup, transplants who just landed a job downtown, people upgrading from a lease-up they outgrew. Berkshire Residential Investments is looking for a leasing consultant who can read that traffic quickly and convert it. The target closing ratio here is at least 20 percent, which is a real benchmark, not a suggestion.

The core of this role is sales with a resident experience wrapper around it. You'll handle the full leasing cycle: greeting prospects, running tour routes, following up, and closing. But you'll also carry ongoing responsibility for the atmosphere in the leasing office, the condition of model units, and the written and verbal communication that goes out to current residents. Administrative accuracy matters here just as much as personality, because sloppy files and missed follow-ups quietly kill conversion rates and retention alike.

What separates a strong candidate from an average one at a property like this is market awareness. Downtown LA has its own rental rhythm, and Berkshire wants someone who already tracks local concessions, knows what competitors are offering, and can feed useful intelligence back to the property manager. That input shapes marketing decisions and pricing. A leasing consultant who treats comp shopping as optional usually caps out at the leasing desk. One who takes it seriously tends to move up.

Berkshire owns and manages its own assets, so there's no fee management layer here. That tends to mean faster decisions and a tighter connection between site-level performance and company leadership. The team culture skews entrepreneurial for a company of this size, which some people thrive in and others find ambiguous. Know which one you are before you apply.

What Berkshire is looking for

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, ideally in leasing or a sales environment
  • A documented ability to close, not just show
  • Comfort with property management software and willingness to pick up new platforms
  • Strong written communication skills, since resident correspondence is part of the job
  • Attention to detail on administrative tasks, move-in paperwork, follow-up logs, and tour readiness

Compensation runs between $21.50 and $25.00 per hour depending on experience, plus bonus eligibility and a benefits package that includes health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a 25 percent rent discount. For someone early in a leasing career who wants to work on a recognized portfolio in a high-visibility market, this is a reasonable place to build toward an assistant manager role.

job.title: Leasing Specialist - Full - Time
job.description:
A prospect walks in without an appointment, rent payments are due, and your phone's already ringing. That's a standard Tuesday in leasing. If you handle that without losing your composure, you'll fit right in here.

The Role

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the largest third-party student housing managers in the country. Their South Bend property is part of a growing conventional multifamily portfolio, and this full-time Leasing Specialist position sits at the front line of daily operations.

Your primary focus is leasing: working toward daily and weekly goals, responding to prospective residents, converting traffic into signed leases. But the job runs wider than that. You'll handle rent payment questions, walk ledger issues with current residents, and keep detailed working knowledge of the community so you can answer inquiries quickly and accurately. You'll work alongside Community and Leasing Managers, contributing to overall KPI performance for the property.

This is a customer-facing, team-driven role. Redstone describes its culture as entrepreneurial, meaning staff members are expected to take ownership and pitch in across tasks rather than wait for narrow direction. That suits people who prefer staying busy over watching the clock.

Qualifications

  • 1 to 2 years of customer service or sales experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable with basic computer tasks: correspondence, memos, and data entry
  • Familiarity with Entrata or other property management software is a plus, not a requirement
  • Ability to stay calm and focused when things get hectic
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Compensation is $18.00 per hour plus commission. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, 3 paid service days, a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, short-term disability insurance, an employee assistance program, and a continued education benefit.

One thing worth knowing about leasing roles in student-adjacent conventional housing: the sales cycle can move fast, and traffic patterns tend to bunch around lease renewal seasons. Candidates who've worked retail, hospitality, or any high-volume customer environment tend to transition into leasing well. The skills transfer more directly than most people expect, and a Leasing Specialist role at a national operator like Redstone is a practical starting point for moving into a Leasing Manager or Assistant Community Manager position down the line.

job.title: Director, Development Operations – New York
job.description:
What This Role Demands From Day One

New York City multifamily is its own discipline. Rent stabilization, rent regulation, HQS inspections, Local Law compliance, mixed residential/commercial buildings, and layered subsidy programs create a regulatory environment that professionals from other markets spend years learning. This Director role requires you to already know it. Fairstead is building a dedicated leadership position for its New York City-area portfolio precisely because that complexity warrants full-time, senior-level ownership, and the person stepping into this seat needs 13 to 16 years of direct New York multifamily experience to operate at the level the role requires from the start.

The financial analysis skills you'll draw on constantly here go well beyond reading a T-12. You'll own business plan execution across all Fairstead New York assets, track fee collection, model capital events including dispositions, refinancings, LP buyouts, and recapitalizations, and monitor lease-up progress on new and repositioned assets through stabilization. You'll need to hold those numbers while simultaneously serving as Fairstead's primary external representative to lenders, joint venture partners, institutional investors, and public housing authorities. That combination of regulatory depth and capital markets fluency is exactly what makes this a senior-level seat and a narrow candidate pool.

The Scope of Accountability

Fairstead's national portfolio spans more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, but this role focuses entirely on New York. You're the single point of accountability for every asset in the region. That means you're not advising on New York deals. You own them. Business plan implementation, rent maximization under stabilization and subsidy programs, compliance with applicable Local Laws, coordination with property management on delinquency and rent collection, and oversight of mixed residential/commercial assets all sit with you.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading capital events from positioning through closing, including dispositions, refinancings, and recapitalizations
  • Overseeing lease-up of new and repositioned assets to support stabilization timelines and refinancing readiness
  • Ensuring rents are maximized to the full legal extent under rent stabilization, rent regulation, and applicable subsidy programs
  • Managing compliance with HQS, Local Laws, and capex programming requirements
  • Building and leading a team as the New York portfolio grows
  • Representing Fairstead on New York-specific regulatory and industry matters

What This Role Builds and Why It's a Distinctive Opportunity

Even at the Director level, there's real development here. Fairstead operates as an integrated owner, operator, and developer under one platform, which means this role sits at the intersection of asset management, development operations, and property management in a way that few single-employer roles offer. You'll sharpen deal transition skills as you take ownership of newly acquired or repositioned assets and drive them from close to stabilized performance. You'll also develop team leadership depth as the New York portfolio scales.

What separates strong candidates from qualified ones in this search is the combination of regulatory specificity and capital event experience. Many New York multifamily professionals know rent stabilization cold. Fewer also have direct experience leading LP buyouts, coordinating partner capital calls, and managing lender relationships through a refinancing. Fairstead needs both in the same person, and the salary range of $185,000 to $250,000 reflects that the firm knows what it's asking for.

Fairstead's tech-forward approach also shapes how this role operates day to day. The firm actively incorporates AI tools into workflows, and this Director is expected to adopt and iterate on those tools as they evolve, not simply tolerate them. For a senior professional who wants to work in an environment where data-driven decision-making and operational efficiency are actual priorities rather than talking points, that orientation matters.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Alderbrook
job.description:
CloudTen Residential operates across the West with a portfolio that spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning plays. The Portland metro group is active, and Alderbrook in Vancouver, WA is part of that mix. This Assistant Manager role sits squarely in the middle of daily operations, which means you're close enough to the work to stay sharp and close enough to leadership to actually grow.

The financial side of this role is real and consistent. You'll post rent, reconcile bank accounts, run weekly and monthly reports, and process invoices without someone holding your hand. Delinquency follow-up is part of the job too, including serving notices and coordinating with the Community Manager when accounts head toward eviction proceedings. If numbers make you uncomfortable, that's worth knowing before you apply.

On the leasing side, you'll handle traffic, conduct tours, support lease-up and renewal activity, and keep an eye on competitive properties to inform pricing recommendations. Move-in and move-out administration falls here as well, including inspections and timely security deposit dispositions. Fair Housing compliance runs through all of it.

When the Community Manager is out, you're running the site. That's not a ceremonial title. It means making decisions, keeping the team on track, and maintaining resident experience without escalating every issue upward. The operators who do well in assistant manager seats tend to treat those stretch moments as useful practice rather than stressful interruptions.

Pay runs $25 to $27 per hour depending on experience, with leasing bonuses available on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, FSA, and company-paid life insurance.

What you'll need

  • At least two years in property management, leasing, or a closely related role
  • Working knowledge of property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Solid grounding in landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing requirements, and local regulations in Washington state
  • Basic accounting literacy and comfort with operational reporting
  • Strong organizational habits and the ability to shift priorities without losing track of details

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this aren't the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who already think like a manager, ask questions before problems compound, and treat delinquency and move-out processes with the same care they give to leasing. If that description fits how you already work, this is a natural next step.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - Fiddler's Green
job.description:
Griffis Residential operates a portfolio of luxury apartment communities, and the Assistant Community Manager role at Fiddler's Green in Centennial sits at the center of daily operations: part leasing, part administrative oversight, part resident relations. It's a support role in structure but a decision-making role in practice.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

You'll work alongside the Community Manager on the full range of property operations. That means conducting apartment tours and moving prospects through the leasing process using iPad-based leasing tools, drafting lease agreements and renewal letters, and following up to keep timelines on track. On the administrative side, you'll review resident files, address unpaid fees, and enforce lease terms. You'll run market surveys and prepare reports for the corporate office, support resident programming and loyalty initiatives, and step in wherever the Community Manager needs coverage.

Centennial sits in the southeast Denver metro, where Class A multifamily has seen real absorption pressure as new supply from surrounding submarkets competes for the same renter pool. At a community like Fiddler's Green, keeping delinquency tight and renewal rates healthy takes consistent follow-through, not just good leasing traffic. That's the kind of environment where an ACM who's sharp on lease enforcement and resident retention earns real visibility fast.

What Griffis Is Looking For

  • At least two years of experience in multifamily housing or a closely related field
  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree or CAM/ARM certification is preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of lease terms, contract enforcement, and property operations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, and Word
  • Strong time management, communication, and organizational skills
  • Genuine commitment to customer service standards and an inclusive team environment

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly range is $26.50 to $30.00. Beyond base pay, Griffis builds meaningful earning potential into this role through a quarterly bonus of up to 15% of annual salary, an occupancy bonus starting at $175 per lease, and a retention bonus program. Associates also receive a 50% rental discount, 11 paid holidays, a minimum of three weeks PTO accruing immediately, and a 401(k) with up to 4% company match. Medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and supplemental insurance are all included, along with up to $5,250 annually in tuition reimbursement, paid new parent leave, and an employee assistance program.

For someone looking to move from ACM to Community Manager, the bonus structure here also gives you early exposure to the occupancy and NOI metrics that CM-level performance reviews center on. That hands-on experience with the numbers, not just the leasing floor, is what tends to shorten the path.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Avanath has built its portfolio around affordable and workforce housing, which puts a different kind of pressure on the operations team than you'd find at a Class A market-rate community. Delinquency management, compliance file maintenance, and resident services carry real weight here. The Assistant Community Manager role at their Suisun City property sits at the center of all of it.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A lot of this role is financial and compliance work. You'll collect, post, and deposit rent and security deposits, track ledger balances, follow up on outstanding amounts, and move through the delinquency process systematically. LIHTC compliance is not a side task here. Avanath works within the tax credit framework, so compliance file maintenance is part of your regular rhythm, done in coordination with the Compliance department and the Community Manager.

Beyond the books, you're running the front office when it's your shift. That means phones, walk-ins, tours, lease files, and resident concerns. When the Community Manager is out, you step into the operational lead role for the property, which includes overseeing on-site staff.

Resident retention is taken seriously at affordable communities because concessions aren't the typical lever. You'll organize retention events, respond to service issues, and act as a resource for residents dealing with circumstances that affect their housing stability. That last part matters more in workforce and affordable housing than most people expect going in.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • At least two years of experience as an Assistant Community Manager
  • Working knowledge of LIHTC and Tax Credit programs (this is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have)
  • Yardi Voyager experience
  • Solid bookkeeping and rent collection background
  • Strong command of Fair Housing and landlord/tenant law
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel
  • The interpersonal range to work with diverse residents, staff, and regulatory partners

Where This Role Can Take You

ACMs who come in strong on both the compliance side and the resident relations side tend to move into Community Manager roles relatively quickly in affordable housing portfolios. The compliance knowledge is genuinely specialized. It transfers well and opens doors that general market-rate experience doesn't always provide. If you're looking to build toward a CM seat, this is a reasonable path.

One honest note: working in workforce and affordable housing means your residents are sometimes managing real financial stress. That's part of the job, and it requires patience and consistency in equal measure. The candidates who thrive here tend to be process-oriented enough to run a clean ledger and people-oriented enough to handle difficult conversations without losing their composure.

job.title: Houskeeper - Temporary
job.description:
This is a temporary housekeeper position at a student housing community in Kent, Ohio managed by PeakMade Real Estate, a company focused on off-campus student housing and build-to-rent properties. The work is straightforward but physical, and the standard for cleanliness directly affects how residents feel about where they live.

What You'll Actually Do

A lot of this role is make-ready work: getting vacant units cleaned and presentable for incoming residents. You'll also keep common areas in good shape, including the leasing office, amenity spaces, and laundry facilities, on a schedule set by the property manager. Tracking inventory and supplies is part of the job too, so staying organized matters. When residents or management have needs, you respond promptly and professionally. OSHA safety standards apply to how you handle cleaning chemicals and equipment, so familiarity with safe handling practices is expected from day one.

The physical side is real. You'll be lifting up to 75 pounds, bending frequently, and spending most of your shift on your feet. That's not unusual for this kind of role, but it's worth knowing before you apply.

What You Bring

  • Previous housekeeping experience across a range of cleaning functions
  • A high school diploma or equivalent
  • Clear communication skills, both spoken and written
  • Ability to track supplies and keep accurate records
  • Comfort working as part of a team and alongside maintenance staff
  • A consistent, dependable approach to your schedule and your work

A Note on the Environment

Student housing runs on a tight seasonal calendar. Move-in periods are high-volume and fast, and the expectation is that units are clean and ready on time. The candidates who do well here tend to be the ones who don't need to be reminded twice, who spot what needs doing without waiting to be told, and who take the cleanliness of a space personally. That reliability matters more than any single skill on a resume. PeakMade operates communities across the country, so temporary roles like this one can sometimes open doors to longer-term work if the fit is right.

job.title: Baytown- Bilingual Leasing Agent
job.description:
A prospect walks in speaking only Spanish, nervous about the application process and unsure what documents they need. You greet them in their language, walk them through the floor plan that fits their budget, and by the end of the tour they're asking about move-in dates. That moment is the core of this role.

What This Job Actually Involves

Karya Property Management is hiring a full-time, bilingual leasing consultant for their Baytown, Texas portfolio. KPM manages more than 16,000 units across Texas, Nevada, and Florida, so the systems, expectations, and support structure are mature. This is an on-site, hourly-plus-commission position where your results show up directly in occupancy numbers and closing ratios.

Day to day, you'll handle walk-in traffic, internet leads, and phone inquiries in both English and Spanish. You'll conduct tours, match prospects to available floor plans, process applications through the full screening cycle, and prepare lease documents and addenda. Follow-up is a real part of the job: every lead gets worked until it closes or goes cold. You'll also walk vacant units before showings to confirm make-ready condition, contribute to competitor market surveys, support resident events, and run renewal outreach for expiring leases. Keeping accurate guest cards and traffic logs in the property management system is part of the daily discipline, not an afterthought.

  • Conduct tours and present amenities and community features to prospective residents
  • Translate and interpret leasing documents for Spanish-speaking applicants
  • Process applications: income verification, credit screening, and approval coordination
  • Maintain leasing activity records and conversion data in property management software
  • Support outreach efforts, resident events, and social media content as needed
  • Run lease-expiration follow-up and renewal paperwork

What Strong Candidates Bring

Fluency in both English and Spanish is required. Beyond language, the candidates who perform well here combine genuine comfort with asking for the sale and the organizational discipline to keep their follow-up current. One year of experience in leasing, sales, hospitality, or a customer-facing role is the baseline. Prior multifamily experience and familiarity with platforms like Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage are advantages. Weekend availability is part of the job during peak leasing season.

From a career standpoint, this role builds a skill set that compounds quickly. Leasing consultants who develop strong closing ratios and clean operational habits tend to move into assistant manager roles within two to three years, where they start owning the delinquency report, running the leasing team, and contributing to NOI decisions. The bilingual component specifically adds real value at that next level, particularly in Texas markets where Spanish-speaking resident populations are significant and properties actively compete to serve them well.

KPM's stated values include integrity, teamwork, and empathy. The practical translation of that for this role: you'll be expected to treat a nervous first-time renter with the same attention you'd give someone signing a premium unit.

job.title: Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community PLUS HOUSING
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Churchill Meadows Estates is a 159-home all-ages manufactured housing community in Eugene, Oregon. As Community Manager, you're the person who keeps that community running. That means rent collection, delinquency follow-up, overseeing move-in applications, coordinating vendors, handling resident grievances, and managing on-site staff. Investment Property Group expects you to own the financial and operational performance of this property, which includes staying current on accounting reports and understanding where the numbers are heading each month.

This role requires you to live on-site. IPG provides a 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom double-wide manufactured home (approximately 1,440 sq. ft.) as part of your compensation. That's a genuine perk, but it also means your work and home life share a zip code. Residents will find you. That's the honest reality of on-site management, and it's worth knowing before you apply.

Your standard schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with occasional weekend hours when the property needs it. You'll supervise staff, run performance reviews, handle hiring and discipline, and act as the liaison between residents and local agencies including community development organizations and law enforcement when situations require it.

What You Bring

  • At least one year managing a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Hands-on experience with delinquency management and rent collection processes
  • Comfort with property management software and basic accounting systems
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing requirements
  • Strong conflict resolution skills, especially with residents who have genuine concerns and need to feel heard
  • Experience coordinating vendors from scheduling through quality checks
  • Ability to market vacant lots or homes to maintain occupancy

Context Worth Knowing

Manufactured housing communities operate differently from conventional apartment properties. Resident relationships here tend to run longer and run deeper. Many residents own their homes and lease the land beneath them, which shapes how you enforce community rules and handle disputes. That dynamic rewards managers who are consistent, fair, and genuinely accessible, not managers who post notices and avoid conversations.

Pay runs $28.00 to $32.00 per hour depending on your background, and the on-site housing is included on top of that. IPG also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO. The company operates 150 properties across 13 states, so for a manager who performs well, there's real room to grow into regional oversight as the portfolio expands.

The candidates who tend to thrive in this type of role aren't the ones who prefer a clean, predictable workday. They're the ones who can pivot from a staff coaching conversation to a resident grievance to a vendor invoice review inside the same afternoon, without letting any of it slide.

job.title: Regional Director | HOA
job.description:
Worth Ross Management Company manages luxury multifamily and HOA communities and has built a reputation for high-touch service and operational discipline. This Regional Director role sits above individual properties. You're managing the people who manage the buildings, and that distinction matters for how you spend your time.

What You'll Actually Do

Your portfolio spans multiple residential HOA communities across the Denver region. The General Managers on your team handle day-to-day operations at each site. Your job is to make sure they have what they need, hold them accountable to financial and service standards, and step in when a property is underperforming. You'll meet regularly with Boards of Directors, present on financial performance, and manage those relationships directly. When a new community comes on board, you'll lead the onboarding process.

Budget oversight is core to this role. You need to understand how community association financials work, spot variance before it becomes a problem, and drive process improvements that hold up across multiple sites. You'll also carry a staffing responsibility. Hiring, coaching, and developing site-level leaders falls squarely in your lane.

Travel within the region is frequent. Board meetings happen evenings. Emergencies don't follow a schedule. This role pays $110,000 to $120,000 annually and operates on standard business hours with the flexibility the job genuinely requires.

What You Bring

  • 5 to 7 or more years in property operations, HOA management, or hospitality leadership at a multi-site level
  • Direct experience managing General Managers or other site leaders across multiple locations
  • Comfort working with Boards of Directors and presenting financial and operational information clearly
  • Solid grasp of community association budgeting and accounting principles
  • CMCA, AMS, or PCAM designation preferred; HOA background is a strong differentiator here
  • Bachelor's degree in business or related field preferred; high school diploma required

Where This Role Fits

HOA regional leadership is a distinct discipline. Unlike multifamily, you're accountable to elected Boards who each have their own priorities, communication styles, and governing documents. The General Managers under you are often juggling vendor relationships, resident concerns, and compliance issues simultaneously. Your value is in creating consistency across that complexity without micromanaging it.

Strong candidates tend to have one thing in common: they've already operated at a remove from daily site work and learned to lead through others rather than around them. If your instinct is still to fix problems directly instead of building the team that fixes them, this role will feel like friction. If you've made that shift, it's a natural fit.

job.title: Dover Farms- Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on a Friday. Delinquency reports are open in one tab, an application file is pending in another, and a prospect just walked in asking for a tour. This is the rhythm at Dover Farms, and the right Assistant Property Manager doesn't flinch at it.

What the Role Covers

Banyan Living is adding an experienced Assistant Property Manager to its team at Dover Farms in North Royalton, Ohio. This is a full-cycle leasing and operations role. You'll handle everything from driving traffic and conducting property tours to processing applications, running credit and background checks, and qualifying applicants in compliance with Fair Housing regulations. Lease preparation, documentation accuracy, and legal compliance are non-negotiable parts of the job.

On the operations side, you'll work directly alongside the Property Manager to keep daily functions running. That means posting rent, monitoring delinquency, and helping maintain the operational health of the community. You'll also take ownership of resident relationships, with the goal of improving retention and generating referrals. When leasing staff need guidance, you'll provide it. Some prior experience mentoring junior team members is a plus, though not a strict requirement.

Marketing is part of the picture too. You'll collaborate with management to build and execute strategies aimed at improving occupancy and leasing velocity. That requires both a working knowledge of the leasing funnel and the communication skills to convert traffic into signed leases.

What Banyan Living Is Looking For

  • At least one year of residential leasing or property management experience
  • Solid understanding of leasing procedures, Fair Housing regulations, and property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with real negotiation ability
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort with property management platforms
  • Availability for evenings and weekends when needed
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and capable of juggling competing priorities without dropping the ball on compliance or resident experience

Candidates who stand out tend to have a track record of leasing consistency, not just activity. If you can speak to occupancy gains, delinquency reduction, or retention improvements you contributed to in a previous role, that carries weight.

Benefits include health, dental, life, and disability insurance, PTO, sick time, paid holidays, a 35% rent discount, and access to ongoing training opportunities.

The Assistant Property Manager role is a natural bridge to a Property Manager position. At properties like Dover Farms, where you're touching both the leasing funnel and day-to-day operations, you build the full skill set that owner-operators and third-party management companies look for when they're hiring a PM. Time spent here compounds quickly for someone willing to own the numbers.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Denton Floyd Real Estate Group manages multi-family communities across the region, and they're adding a Maintenance Technician to their Jeffersonville, Indiana property. This is a full-scope, hands-on role working under the Community Manager, handling everything from daily work orders to apartment turns and after-hours emergencies.

What You'll Actually Do

Your days won't look identical. Some mornings start with a stack of occupied work requests. Others begin with a make-ready punch list on a unit that needs to turn quickly. You'll troubleshoot and repair HVAC systems, plumbing fixtures and drains, appliances, electrical components (light fixtures, switches, receptacles, thermostats, smoke detectors), and irrigation systems. Preventative maintenance on HVAC units and water heaters is part of the routine, not an afterthought.

Curb appeal matters here. You'll keep an eye on the overall condition of the property and flag anything unusual to the Community Manager. Carpentry, drywall, and key cutting experience are genuinely useful. CPO certification or an EPA card will get you noticed, but they're not hard requirements to apply.

On-call rotation is real. After-hours emergencies are part of the job, and the team needs someone who takes that seriously. If that kind of availability doesn't fit your life right now, this probably isn't the right match.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of residential property maintenance or equivalent hands-on experience
  • At least one year of plumbing experience specifically
  • Strong mechanical and electrical aptitude across multiple trade areas
  • Working knowledge of drywall, key cutting, and fire extinguisher maintenance
  • HVAC/EPA certification or CPO preferred, not required
  • Valid driver's license, auto insurance, and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Spanish language skills are a plus
  • Must clear a drug screen and background check

The Team Dynamic

Maintenance techs at multi-family properties sit at an interesting crossroads. You interact with residents when they're frustrated, with vendors who need direction, and with a Community Manager who depends on your updates to keep operations running. How you show up in those moments, your communication, your follow-through, shapes the reputation of the entire property. Denton Floyd puts real emphasis on that interpersonal piece, and it shows up in how they describe their internal culture too.

The company has a track record of consistent growth, which tends to create real career pathways for people who perform well. A technician who demonstrates competency across trades and builds trust with the management team often moves toward a lead tech or maintenance supervisor role as a portfolio grows. If you're looking for a place where showing up and doing good work actually leads somewhere, that context is worth knowing.

Benefits include health, dental, vision, 401(k) with matching, paid time off, parental leave, an employee assistance program, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, an employee discount, and a referral program.

job.title: Assistant Leasing & Marketing Manager | Rambler Riverfront - West Lafayette, IN
job.description:
Student housing leasing roles carry more complexity than they look like from the outside. You're managing individual bedspace placements, roommate dynamics, Greek outreach, guarantor screening, and renewal strategy all at once, often for a property that runs on an academic calendar with one high-stakes lease-up window per year. At LV Collective's Rambler Riverfront in West Lafayette, the Assistant Leasing and Marketing Manager sits squarely in that environment, supporting the Community Manager and Leasing Manager while taking genuine ownership of sales performance, outreach, and team development.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A large part of this role lives inside Entrata and HubSpot. You'll work your lead pipeline daily, generate and audit leases, keep pricing and availability accurate, and make sure no prospect goes 24 hours without a personal follow-up. Tour standards, model unit condition, and curb appeal are yours to maintain. Beyond the desk, you're in the field: visiting Greek organizations, running prospect and resident events, coaching leasing team members, and building the weekly schedule around peak traffic periods.

The reporting side is real and consistent. Daily Leasing Reports, Master Sheet 4.0 audits, market surveys, competitor rate monitoring, concession tracking, and contribution to weekly call agendas with the Leasing Manager all sit in your lane. You'll bring rate and special recommendations with data behind them, not gut feelings. The role also owns the renewal cycle from first outreach through execution, with proactive identification of at-risk residents before they go quiet.

  • Full leasing cycle management: lead intake through lease execution and renewal
  • Daily pipeline management in Entrata and HubSpot with 24-hour follow-up standards
  • Bedspace and unit placement coordinated against availability, lease term, and preferences
  • Application and guarantor screening against the Rental Criteria and Qualifications SOP
  • Market surveys, competitor concession monitoring, and rate recommendations
  • Greek and student org outreach, brand ambassador programs, and community events
  • Onboarding, coaching, scheduling, and mentoring for the leasing team
  • Renewal strategy development, resident retention, and roommate conflict resolution
  • Fair Housing compliance across all leasing activity and team communication

Where This Role Leads

Student housing gives you a compressed, high-volume version of skills that transfer directly into conventional multifamily. You'll come out of this role with real conversion data behind your name, documented experience running a leasing team, and fluency in systems like Entrata that most mid-size operators use. The natural next step is a Leasing and Marketing Manager title, then Community Manager. If you stay in student housing, the lease-up intensity you build here makes you a strong candidate for portfolio-level leasing director roles earlier than you'd typically reach them in conventional property management.

Strong candidates here already know that pre-lease velocity is the whole game in student housing. If you've tracked your own conversion ratios, thought critically about why prospects go dark, and coached a junior leasing consultant through their first close, you're the profile this role is built for.

job.title: Resident Resolutions Coordinator
job.description:
Southgate Towers sits right on the edge of Biscayne Bay, and the residents who live there expect service that matches the address. AIR Communities is hiring a Resident Resolutions Coordinator to work the afternoon and evening shift, Monday through Friday, 3 p.m. to 11 p.m., at this Miami Beach high-rise community. That schedule is worth understanding before you apply: you're the point of contact when the leasing office has wound down and residents are home from work, which is exactly when complaints surface and service expectations peak.

The role sits at the intersection of resident relations and light operations coordination. On a given evening, you might field a noise complaint, follow up on an open work order, register a new vehicle for a resident, enter a service request, and walk someone through the notice-to-vacate process, all in the same shift. It's not a desk-only job. Residents will approach you with everything from genuine maintenance concerns to policy questions to frustrations that have been building for weeks, and you'll need to triage, respond, and loop in the right people without letting things sit.

Miami Beach carries its own rhythms. Turnover in coastal luxury communities tends to accelerate in summer when seasonal renters cycle out, and resident expectations at a property with bay views run high relative to the broader South Florida market. The ability to de-escalate gracefully under pressure, in person or over the phone, is a practical daily requirement here.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is follow-through. Residents don't just want to be heard; they want confirmation that something actually happened after they reported a problem. Coordinators who close the loop proactively, calling back after a work order is marked complete or sending a quick note after a policy conversation, build the kind of trust that keeps renewal rates stable. If your background is in hospitality or property management and you've already learned how to manage volume without letting details slip, that experience translates directly.

What AIR is looking for

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience in a high-volume environment (property management, hospitality, and retail are all relevant)
  • Comfortable working evenings and occasional weekends
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Reliable transportation
  • Project management or property operations experience is a plus, not a requirement

Compensation runs $19 to $22 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, HSA and FSA options, company-paid short and long-term disability, a 401(k) with employer contribution, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance and full reimbursement for job-related certifications, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community. Paid time off covers vacation, sick time, and 11 holidays, plus 15 paid hours annually for community service.

job.title: Leasing Consultant | Pay $18 hr. + Commission
job.description:
Village Green has been managing multifamily communities since 1919, which puts them in genuinely rare company. Over a century of operations means their training infrastructure, processes, and career pathways are built out in ways you won't find at smaller regional operators. This Leasing Consultant opening in O'Fallon, IL sits inside that framework, paying $18/hr plus commissions, with a full benefits package that includes 401(k) with a company match, medical, dental, vision, and a bonus program.

The core of this role is occupancy. You're the front line between a vacant unit and a signed lease, which means your daily output shows up directly in the numbers. Tours convert or they don't. Applications get processed or they stall. Renewals get negotiated or the unit turns. Strong Leasing Consultants treat traffic-to-lease ratio as a personal metric, not just something the property manager watches. You'll handle showings, work through lease negotiations, coordinate move-ins and move-outs, and keep resident relationships in good shape so renewals don't become surprises.

Beyond the floor, you'll support marketing efforts through online listings, social media, and community outreach, and you'll represent the property at networking and local events. That outside visibility matters in a market like O'Fallon, where community ties drive referral traffic more than paid advertising alone.

What separates candidates who thrive here: the ability to hold a leasing conversation that feels like genuine help rather than a pitch. Residents who feel pressured sign less often and renew even less. The consultants who consistently hit occupancy targets tend to listen well, respond quickly, and follow up without being asked. Sales instincts matter, but so does the patience to walk someone through the application process without losing them to friction.

Weekend availability is required. A leasing license is required before starting. An undergraduate degree is strongly preferred, and 1-2 years of sales experience in multifamily or hospitality gives you a real leg up, though Village Green states that prior leasing experience isn't a hard requirement for the right candidate.

  • Strong sales and customer service fundamentals
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Comfortable working independently and alongside a property team
  • Familiarity with property management software is a plus; Microsoft Office proficiency is expected
  • Weekend availability required
  • Valid leasing license required

For someone early in a property management career, a Leasing Consultant role at an operator with Village Green's depth is a reasonable place to build toward Assistant Manager or Property Manager. The skills you develop here, reading traffic patterns, understanding lease structure, managing resident expectations, transfer directly into those next-level roles. The commission structure also means your earnings grow with your performance, not just your tenure.

job.title: LIHTC Community Manager (30023)
job.description:
LIHTC compliance work takes a specific kind of discipline. You're managing a 118-unit affordable housing community in Fort Collins, but a meaningful part of the job lives in the details of income certifications, rent limits, and regulatory timelines. If your compliance knowledge is thin, the rest of the role gets harder fast.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Leasing, occupancy management, and resident communication are table stakes for any community manager. What separates this role is the LIHTC layer. You need to understand income limits, annual recertifications, and what happens when a file isn't airtight. Cirrus is managing 118 units at Country Ranch under affordable housing restrictions, which means every application you process and every file you close needs to hold up to investor and agency scrutiny. Yardi experience helps here, especially when you're generating compliance-related reports or tracking tenant data against program requirements.

Beyond compliance, the day-to-day draws on the same skills any community manager needs: closing qualified walk-in traffic, working phone leads, coordinating maintenance, collecting rent, and issuing timely delinquency notices within legal requirements. Move-out inspections and deposit accounting fall to you as well, with Colorado's state timelines governing when statements go out.

What the Schedule Actually Looks Like

Standard hours run Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm. That's the baseline. The honest caveat: the property is going through resyndication, which means evenings and weekends will be part of the job during that period. Resyndication on a LIHTC property is a heavy lift. New financing, new compliance timelines, resident communication, and documentation demands all stack up at once. If you've been through a resyndication before, you know what to expect. If you haven't, it's worth understanding before you apply.

What Fits This Role

  • Minimum three years of property management experience
  • Demonstrated working knowledge of LIHTC regulations, income limits, and compliance requirements
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook; Yardi experience preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Organized enough to manage compliance files, leasing activity, and maintenance coordination simultaneously
  • Comfortable owning decisions and handling resident issues without escalating everything

Candidates who do well in LIHTC management tend to have a specific mindset: they treat documentation as protection, not paperwork. A well-kept file covers the property, the resident, and the program. That attention carries over into every part of the job, from budget prep to property walks to vendor relationships.

Cirrus Asset Management operates as a third-party management company, which means community managers here work within a structure that values both owner reporting and resident outcomes. The salary range for this position is $73,000 to $75,000 annually, with health, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, and a 401k plan included.

job.title: Apartment Service Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work is fundamentally a skills game. Electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliance repair , the breadth of what you can diagnose and fix on your own directly determines how fast work orders close and how smooth a make-ready turn runs. At Morguard's Cary, NC community, those skills get put to work daily across a full range of resident needs and unit prep cycles.

The Skills This Role Leans On

The core technical requirement here is basic to moderate proficiency across the main trades: electrical troubleshooting, plumbing repairs, HVAC service, and appliance work. EPA Type I and II certification is the floor; Universal certification is the target. That HVAC credential matters more than it might seem on a first read. In a North Carolina climate, cooling calls spike hard from May through September, and a tech who can handle refrigerant work without waiting on a third-party vendor keeps both residents comfortable and service response times tight.

Beyond the hands-on technical work, this role uses a different set of skills for make-readies. Preparing a unit for a new resident is detail-oriented work with real consequences: a sloppy punch list at move-in shows up in reviews, affects renewal rates, and chips away at NOI over time. Morguard calls it their "Plus-One Customer Service" standard, which essentially means every touchpoint , a completed work order, a clean unit, a prompt response to an after-hours call , should exceed what the resident expected.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Complete resident service requests promptly, coordinating with the Lead Service Technician and Community Manager on priorities and workload
  • Execute make-ready turns from start to finish, with close attention to unit condition at each stage
  • Run preventative maintenance on units and common areas to get ahead of larger repair costs
  • Keep the maintenance shop clean, organized, and properly stocked
  • Maintain community grounds as part of daily upkeep
  • Participate in after-hours on-call rotation for resident emergencies
  • Attend monthly safety meetings and operate in compliance with OSHA standards and applicable regulations

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

A year of residential maintenance experience is the stated minimum, and that baseline matters. Candidates who stand out typically carry a wider HVAC skillset, hold Universal EPA certification already, and have a track record of running make-readies efficiently without the Lead Technician having to loop back on punch list items. This role also carries a mentorship expectation , sharing knowledge with less experienced team members is part of the job, so people who've worked in organized maintenance teams tend to fit well.

Morguard is a large, vertically integrated operator with a North American multifamily portfolio, which gives their on-site maintenance staff access to systems, resources, and training infrastructure that smaller fee management shops often can't match. The employee housing discount and 401(k) dollar-for-dollar match with immediate vesting are worth noting as tangible benefits on top of the medical coverage and paid time off. For a maintenance tech building a career in residential property management, the path from Service Technician to Lead Tech to Maintenance Supervisor is well-defined here.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Multifamily properties run on two engines: leasing and maintenance. When maintenance lags, occupancy suffers, renewals drop, and the asset loses value faster than any market shift can explain. Bozzuto understands this, and their Assistant Maintenance Manager role at their Delray Beach community exists to keep that engine running cleanly, every day, not just during crises.

This is a hands-on leadership position. You'll carry your tools and direct others who carry theirs. The make-ready process will be one of your steadiest responsibilities: coordinating turns so apartments are punched out, cleaned, and ready to lease without dragging timelines. At a well-run property, that cycle hums. When it doesn't, the leasing team feels it immediately. Your ability to manage that rhythm matters as much as your technical skills.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Resident service tickets in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair will fill a significant portion of your week. Bozzuto expects timely follow-up and careful completion, not just a closed ticket. Beyond unit-level work, you'll own preventative maintenance programs that protect the building's systems over time. Depending on the property's complexity, that could include central plant components, split systems, or boilers. Grounds upkeep, safety compliance (OSHA, local codes), and participating in the emergency on-call rotation round out the picture. Weekend availability is part of this role.

You'll also be a culture carrier for the maintenance team. That means modeling standards, communicating expectations clearly, and building in the people around you a sense of ownership over the property's condition.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Five or more years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and basic carpentry and drywall
  • Familiarity with risk management, OSHA requirements, and MSDS protocols
  • Some supervisory experience, or a clear readiness to step into that responsibility
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order systems, and basic Microsoft Office tools
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying outdoor conditions

Candidates who stand out tend to bring something specific: they think about the building the way a builder would. They notice what's wearing down before it fails. They treat a resident's service call with the same focus they'd give a major capital repair. That mindset, more than any single certification, is what Bozzuto is looking for in this seat.

The salary for this position falls in the range of $58,000 to $58,500, with bonus eligibility included. Benefits cover medical, dental, and vision, plus 20 days of paid time off, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement for those who want to keep developing their skills. For a technician ready to grow into leadership, or a supervisor who wants to sharpen their craft at a company that takes culture seriously, this role is worth a close look.

job.title: Centralized Painter, IFM - Denver, CO
job.description:
Cortland runs a centralized painting operation across its multifamily portfolio, and this role sits at the heart of that model. Based out of the Colorado Springs area, you'd be moving between properties as workload demands, handling the full range of unit turn painting and surface repair work that keeps apartments ready for new residents on schedule.

The day-to-day is production-oriented. Expect to complete a full-unit repaint or a couple of touch-ups daily, depending on the turn queue. That means brush, roller, and spray application, drywall patching, texture matching, and prep work done to a consistent standard across different unit conditions and ages. Spray equipment maintenance is part of the job, not an afterthought. You'll also be responsible for keeping the paint shop organized and stocked, logging completed work in the CMMS, and flagging anything that could affect schedule or material supply before it becomes a problem.

What makes the centralized model worth understanding: rather than being assigned to a single property, you're a shared resource across the portfolio. That gives Cortland's service teams flexibility during heavy turn seasons and lease-up periods, and it gives you exposure to a wider range of property conditions, unit types, and workloads than a single-site painter typically sees. It also means you need to operate with real independence since there's no on-site supervisor tracking your progress hour to hour.

From a career standpoint, this kind of role builds a track record that translates well. Painters who consistently hit turn timelines, demonstrate quality control discipline, and communicate proactively tend to move into lead or supervisory roles within facilities teams. Cortland's vertically integrated structure means there's internal mobility across maintenance, facilities coordination, and project management paths for people who show that combination of craft skill and operational reliability.

What you'll need to be considered

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least two years of interior residential painting experience; custom home background is a plus
  • Proficiency with brush, roller, and spray application, including spray prep and equipment upkeep
  • Ability to perform drywall repairs including patching, sanding, and texture matching
