  • Comfort working at heights using ladders, lifts, or scaffolding
  • Valid driver's license, required vehicle insurance, and willingness to travel regularly between properties
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards, MSDS requirements, and elevated-work safety procedures
  • Experience with CMMS platforms or willingness to learn one
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • Availability for all shifts, including weekends as needed

Cortland is a drug-free workplace and participates in E-Verify. The company is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians are the operational backbone of any multifamily property. When work orders stack up, turns stall, or a resident calls at midnight with a plumbing emergency, the technician is the one who keeps occupancy intact and NOI protected. Village Green, a recognized name in multifamily management, is hiring a Maintenance Technician at one of their communities in Woodbury, MN, with pay ranging from $25 to $29 per hour plus a quarterly bonus.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The day-to-day splits between reactive and planned work. On the reactive side, you're completing work orders across plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and handling on-call emergencies as directed by the property and service managers. On the planned side, you're running apartment turns: plumbing, electrical, drywall repair, painting, and appliance repair or replacement. Turns are where your technical range gets tested most, because a make-ready has to be right before a new resident moves in, and there's no ambiguity about the deadline.

Beyond interior work, the role includes daily exterior upkeep for curb appeal, snow removal in winter, housekeeping duties as needed, and pool and spa maintenance where applicable. HVAC knowledge is expected. Customer service matters here too: residents are the end customer, and how you show up at the door shapes their experience with the property.

What Village Green Is Looking For

  • One to three years of experience in multifamily housing or the hotel industry
  • Solid hands-on skills in plumbing, electrical, appliances, and painting
  • HVAC knowledge
  • General computer literacy for work order systems
  • Availability for on-call rotation and weekend work when needed
  • Plumbing, contracting, or builder certifications are a plus

Strong candidates tend to be the ones who can self-triage a work order list under pressure, communicate clearly with residents on the spot, and complete turns without needing constant direction. If you've come up through hotel maintenance or multifamily and you have a broad technical base rather than expertise in just one trade, this role fits that profile well.

From a career standpoint, a technician role at a professionally managed company like Village Green builds the kind of documented, cross-trade experience that positions you for a lead technician or service manager role within a few years. The combination of turn experience, on-call responsibility, and customer-facing work maps directly onto what regional operators look for when promoting into supervisory maintenance positions.

job.title: Floating Maintenance Technician - Commercial Buildings
job.description:
Cirrus Asset Management runs a third-party management operation across retail, industrial, and commercial properties throughout Redondo Beach and LA County. This floating maintenance technician role puts you across multiple buildings rather than anchoring you to a single address, which means no two days run the same route or hit the same punch list.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your week centers on completing work orders on time and keeping building systems running within health and safety standards. That covers a wide range of trades: electrical maintenance (lighting, circuit breaker panels), plumbing and heating components, door hardware and locking mechanisms, and general manual repairs. You'll also carry responsibility for fire suppression documentation, extinguisher logs, and alarm system contacts, which on the commercial side carries more compliance weight than most residents-facing roles. Curb appeal and grounds upkeep are part of the job too. Documentation follows every task, including materials procurement records. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with occasional early 7 AM starts and on-call availability for emergencies.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year of maintenance experience specifically in retail, mall, or industrial buildings
  • Reliable transportation to move between properties across Redondo Beach and LA County as needed
  • Working knowledge of general maintenance processes, common tools, and building systems
  • Manual dexterity, attention to detail, and genuine problem-solving ability
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Any relevant certifications (electrical, CMRP, or similar) strengthen your application

The Floating Advantage

Commercial floating roles build a broader skill set than single-property positions. Retail and industrial buildings run different MEP configurations, have different code considerations, and operate on tighter landlord-tenant maintenance obligations than residential. Technicians who get comfortable working across property types and building classes tend to move into lead or facilities management positions faster. At $23 to $25 per hour, plus health, dental, vision, life insurance, 401k, and paid time off, the compensation sits competitively for the LA South Bay market at this experience level.

job.title: Property Administrator (Industrial)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits inside Stream Realty Partners' property management team in Houston, supporting a commercial industrial portfolio. The work splits between accounting tasks, tenant communication, and keeping the administrative side of the operation running clean.

On the AP side, you'll code and enter invoices against the approved budget, verify backup documentation, and push invoices to the Property Manager for approval. On the AR side, you'll review aging reports monthly and help prepare late notices and default notices as needed. You'll also assist with monthly and quarterly financial reporting.

Beyond the numbers, you're the first point of contact for vendors, tenants, and visitors. You'll field calls, greet guests, accept deliveries, and route everything to the right person. Work orders come through you. Certificates of insurance for vendors and tenants get tracked by you. When a tenant moves in or out, you're coordinating the schedule and confirming insurance is in place.

Service contracts, tenant events, vendor coordination: the Property Manager depends on you to handle the detail work so they can focus on higher-level decisions.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Word
  • Yardi experience is a plus, though not required
  • Basic accounting skills with real attention to detail
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Customer service instincts that translate well with tenants and vendors
  • Organized enough to track COIs, work orders, and contracts simultaneously without things falling through

Context Worth Knowing

Industrial property management in Houston runs at a different pace than office or multifamily. Tenant rosters often include logistics, distribution, and manufacturing operations, which means move-in and move-out activity can be large-scale and time-sensitive. COI tracking matters more than it might in other asset classes because vendor and tenant activity on the loading dock carries real liability exposure. If you're detail-oriented and want to build a foundation in commercial real estate, this kind of admin role is a recognized path into Property Manager positions, particularly at a firm like Stream that manages a full-service commercial portfolio across multiple markets.

Stream offers medical, dental, vision, pharmacy benefits, HSA, FSA, 401(k) with company match, PTO, and holiday pay. Compensation is based on experience and qualifications.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant-Cortland at the Village
job.description:
Leasing is one of those roles where the skills you build are genuinely portable. Pipeline management, consultative selling, CRM discipline, objection handling, resident psychology. Done well, this position at Cortland at the Village in Smyrna, GA builds the foundation for a long career in multifamily, whether that path leads to a Senior Leasing Consultant role, an Assistant Manager seat, or eventually a full property management position. The skills compound fast when you're in a goal-oriented environment that actually tracks performance.

What This Role Demands

The core skill set here is sales, applied specifically to multifamily leasing. You'll own your pipeline from first contact through signed lease. That means prompt follow-up, consistent CRM entries, conversion tracking, and knowing how to read where a prospect is in their decision process. Cortland uses consultative selling as its framework, which means you're not running through a standard script. You're asking questions, identifying what matters to each person, and building a case around fit rather than just features. That approach transfers directly to any high-end or Class A lease-up environment later in your career.

Beyond the sales mechanics, there's a relationship layer. You'll handle resident events, support social media presence for the community, and serve as the face of the brand for every prospective resident who walks through the door. Objection handling gets a lot of attention here, and for good reason. Turning a hesitant prospect into a signed resident often comes down to how well you listen and how credibly you address real concerns.

Qualifications Worth Highlighting

  • At least six months in a sales, customer-facing, or performance-measured role
  • Comfort being evaluated against specific targets and KPIs
  • CRM experience or the aptitude to learn one quickly
  • Strong written and verbal communication, especially in high-traffic, face-to-face settings
  • Coachability. Cortland is a data-driven operator and they will give feedback. The candidates who grow fastest are the ones who implement it quickly.

Doing This Role at Cortland

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator, meaning design, construction, and management all sit under one roof. That matters for your day-to-day because when something needs attention at the property level, there's real infrastructure behind it. You're not leasing for a small fee-management shop where maintenance is an afterthought. You're representing a brand that has intentionally built its product around resident experience, which makes the job of selling lifestyle more credible and more consistent.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is follow-up discipline. Traffic alone doesn't drive occupancy. It's the organized, persistent, well-timed outreach after the tour that closes the gap between interest and lease. If you've built that habit somewhere else, whether in retail, hospitality, or another leasing role, it translates directly here.

job.title: Groundskeeper - Olympus Hudson Oaks
job.description:
Curb appeal is a leasing tool. Prospects form opinions about a community before they ever speak to an agent, and what they see when they pull into the parking lot carries real weight. The Groundskeeper role at Olympus Hudson Oaks exists to protect that first impression every single day, while also keeping the common areas that current residents use comfortable and clean.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a Monday through Friday, 8 to 5 position, which means your schedule is predictable and your weekends are yours. The core of the job is grounds maintenance: trash and debris pickup across parking lots, breezeways, hallways, laundry rooms, and other shared spaces, plus operating equipment like blowers and power washers to keep surfaces clean. You'll handle light cleaning and touch-ups to assist with make-readies before new residents move in, track cleaning supply inventory, and occasionally post notices on resident doors when the office team needs a hand. Working outdoors in Texas weather is part of the job. If you're comfortable in the heat and adaptable when conditions shift, that fits what this role requires.

Olympus looks for candidates who already bring some relevant background. Experience in landscaping, grounds maintenance, facilities work, or janitorial roles is required, as is the ability to lift 25 pounds and handle light equipment safely. This isn't a role that trains the fundamentals from scratch; it rewards people who already understand what a well-kept property looks like and take satisfaction in maintaining it.

What You'll Build Here

What Olympus offers beyond the daily work is worth noting. The company has earned recognition from the National Apartment Association as a top employer three consecutive years running, and they put real structure behind career growth through formal career pathing. For someone who wants to stay in multifamily operations, groundskeeping is a legitimate starting point. Many maintenance technicians and lead make-ready techs began in grounds roles. You learn the physical layout of a property, how common areas wear over time, and what residents care about most in shared spaces. That knowledge transfers directly into broader maintenance work.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, and educational assistance with tuition reimbursement. Eligible team members also receive monthly bonuses.

  • Full-time schedule: Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm
  • Prior experience in grounds, landscaping, facilities, or janitorial work required
  • Must be comfortable working outdoors in varying weather conditions
  • Equipment operation: blowers, power washers, and light maintenance tools
  • Ability to lift 25 pounds

Olympus Hudson Oaks is part of a national portfolio, which means the culture and growth pathways here connect to something larger than a single property.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance work at a residential community pulls on a wider range of technical knowledge than most trades positions do. At Bexley at Left Bank in Fort Worth, you'd be working across HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry, often within the same day. The EPA certification requirement here is real. Type II or Universal certification is a baseline, and so is genuine hands-on experience diagnosing HVAC problems rather than just swapping parts. Weinstein Properties is specifically looking for someone who can walk into an issue, reason through it independently, and get it resolved without needing hand-holding at every step.

Beyond the technical side, this role asks for a customer service instinct. Residents notice how maintenance staff communicate, not just how quickly the work gets done. Someone who can explain what they fixed, treat an occupied apartment with respect, and follow through without being chased tends to build real trust with the community. That's the kind of person who does well here.

What Your Days Actually Look Like

The core schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm. You'll cycle through work orders in occupied units, contribute to apartment turns and make-readies between leases, and help maintain the broader property: grounds, amenities, pool areas. Rotating emergency on-call is part of the arrangement, and Weinstein pays $150 per week for on-call availability regardless of call volume, with an additional $150 for holiday coverage. That's a meaningful structure for technicians who've been burned by on-call arrangements at other properties where the compensation didn't match the inconvenience.

The base pay starts at $24 per hour and goes up with experience. There's also a quarterly bonus tied to property and team performance, up to $980 per quarter. On top of that, a $1,500 sign-on bonus is available (details confirmed during the interview).

What Makes This Worth a Closer Look

Weinstein Properties owns and manages its communities rather than operating as a third-party management firm. That distinction matters day-to-day. Decisions move faster, standards stay consistent across the portfolio, and when leadership says they support career growth, there's an actual structure behind it. Many long-term Weinstein team members have advanced within the company, and that kind of internal mobility is easier to achieve when ownership and operations sit in the same organization.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of technical depth and self-direction. The team is collaborative, but this role needs someone who doesn't wait to be assigned every next step. If you've been doing apartment maintenance for three or more years and you're comfortable moving between HVAC diagnosis, appliance repair, and plumbing in a single shift, the work here will feel familiar and sustainable rather than chaotic.

  • At least 3 years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA certification, Type II or Universal
  • Demonstrated HVAC troubleshooting and repair skills
  • Experience with appliances, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • Comfortable with work order software and mobile tools
  • Able to lift up to 75 lbs and work outdoors year-round
  • Reliable transportation required
  • Background check required

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Lakeridge Living
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do at Lakeridge Living

This role sits between wrench-turning and team coordination. As Lead Maintenance Technician, you're responsible for the physical condition of the community at all times, which means you're not just completing service requests, you're managing the system that handles them. The goal is 24-hour turnaround on resident issues when possible, and you'll oversee the technicians doing that work as much as you'll do it yourself.

Day to day, that looks like prioritizing the make-ready queue, running punch lists on turned units, fielding emergency calls after hours, and keeping preventive maintenance on schedule before small issues become capital problems. You'll handle appliance repairs, HVAC troubleshooting, plumbing, electrical, painting, and lock changes. You'll also manage parts inventory so the team isn't waiting on a supply run to close a work order. When grounds need attention, you're involved there too. The scope is wide and the pace is real.

Beyond the hands-on work, you'll run safety meetings with the full staff, keep SDS sheets current, and make sure your team is operating within OSHA and EPA guidelines, particularly around refrigerants, flammables, and other regulated materials. You'll maintain records on preventive maintenance, work-in-progress, and make-ready status, and you'll coordinate scheduling with the property manager to ensure 24/7 emergency coverage is always in place.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, preferably on a 200-unit or larger property
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair
  • HVAC Universal certification (CPO certification also required or expected)
  • Comfort with Yardi maintenance systems, including processing service requests through the mobile app
  • Valid driver's license with current liability insurance
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds and handle the physical demands of indoor/outdoor work throughout the year
  • High school diploma or equivalent, or five years of maintenance experience in lieu of education

The Operational Reality

What separates a strong lead tech from an average one at a property like this is reliability under pressure and the ability to triage. When three service requests come in at once, the technicians look to you to decide what gets done first, what gets delegated, and what needs a contractor call. That judgment, built from real experience across trades, is what keeps occupancy steady and resident satisfaction from slipping. Delinquency and retention are leasing metrics on paper, but maintenance responsiveness drives both more than most people outside operations realize.

MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, with a portfolio that spans acquisition, rehab, and ongoing management. Lakeridge Living in Reno puts you inside a company that runs properties at scale and takes internal development seriously, including online training through Grace Hill and Yardi for supervisory skills. If you're looking to grow toward a Maintenance Supervisor role, the structure is there to support it.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a rhythm unlike conventional multifamily. Move-ins cluster around academic calendars, tours spike during campus visit weekends, and the turn period compresses an enormous volume of make-ready activity into a matter of weeks. The Experience Team Member role at Scion's 44 North community in Minneapolis exists right at the center of that rhythm, handling the daily human work that keeps occupancy strong and residents genuinely satisfied.

What This Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

This position blends leasing, community programming, and property administration into one continuous stream of interaction. On a given day, you might walk a prospective resident through a unit and amenity spaces, follow up on a maintenance request to make sure it closed out properly, sort and log resident packages, and pitch in on a social media post promoting an upcoming community event. The administrative side of the job is real: office organization, opening and closing procedures, and after-hours lockout calls are part of the rotation. This isn't a desk-only role, and it isn't purely a leasing role either. The job requires you to be comfortable moving between tasks and personalities quickly.

Availability matters here more than it does at a typical apartment community. Turn periods in student housing are demanding, summers are high-volume leasing seasons, and holiday coverage is part of the expectation. If your schedule has firm limits around those windows, it's worth factoring that in before applying.

Who Fits Well Here

Scion calls this position an ETM rather than a Leasing Consultant for a reason. The sales component is real, but it sits alongside relationship-building, event support, and community marketing in a way that asks for genuine people skills rather than a purely transactional approach. Strong candidates tend to be comfortable talking with a wide range of residents, parents, and prospects, handling objections honestly, and flagging patterns back to management rather than just pushing through the sales process.

  • Customer-first mindset with real follow-through, not just a friendly demeanor
  • Comfort with a schedule that shifts around academic calendar peaks
  • Reliable self-management, especially during after-hours on-call rotations
  • Some exposure to social media content or community engagement is a plus
  • Ability to work professionally in a collegiate environment without being thrown off by the energy of it

What separates a strong ETM from an average one is usually follow-through. The job generates a constant flow of small tasks: package pickups, maintenance check-ins, tour scheduling, community posts. The people who do this well build systems to stay on top of that volume rather than letting it pile up. Residents notice when things get dropped, and in student housing, word travels fast among roommates, floor groups, and campus networks.

Pay for this role falls in the $17 to $21 per hour range in Minnesota, with an annual discretionary bonus, health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement rounding out the package.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Crystal Springs)
job.description:
It's a Saturday afternoon. Three prospects walk in within fifteen minutes of each other, your phone is ringing with a current resident question, and you've got a lease renewal sitting on your desk waiting for signatures. That's a pretty average Saturday in leasing, and at Crystal Springs, Prometheus wants someone who handles that rhythm without breaking a sweat.

What the Role Actually Covers

Prometheus calls this position a Neighbor Ambassador, which is a little marketing-y, but the underlying job is real leasing work. You're guiding prospects through tours and application, following up on traffic, and closing leases. At the same time, you're the face of the community for current residents who need help or have concerns. The administration side includes market surveys, rental agreements, occupancy reports, and apartment advertising. It's a full leasing cycle role with genuine resident relations built in.

Weekend availability is required. That's non-negotiable at most communities this size, and Prometheus is upfront about it. Your regular days off fall during the week. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing role with a similar schedule, the adjustment is minimal.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • Customer service or sales background, whether in property management or another industry entirely
  • Strong communicator who can shift from a leasing presentation to a maintenance concern to a lease question without losing momentum
  • Someone who can self-manage through a busy Saturday without needing to be told what to do next
  • Comfort with the administrative side: reports, advertising, compliance paperwork

Prometheus hires from outside property management regularly and trains people into the industry. If you've got the customer instincts and the work ethic, the leasing mechanics are learnable. That said, candidates who come in already familiar with traffic tracking, lease documentation, or basic occupancy reporting will move faster in the role.

Compensation runs $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, plus a $200 per-lease incentive, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, weekend shift premium pay, and additional bonuses tied to referrals, lease-up performance, and leasing contests. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision (dependents included), 401(k) with employer match, and tenure-based housing discounts that become meaningfully valuable if you stay long-term in the Bay Area.

One honest observation: San Bruno rents are high enough that traffic quality matters. Prospects who make it through your door are often making a significant financial decision, and they'll ask pointed questions. The consultants who build real trust and explain the value clearly outperform those who rely on a scripted pitch. That's the skill that separates good leasing numbers from average ones here, and it's also the skill that travels well if you eventually move into an Assistant Manager or Community Manager role down the road.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning at the Lofts at Seacrest Beach. You've already reviewed last night's online reviews, pulled your delinquency report from Yardi, and you're walking the property before your leasing team arrives. By 9 AM, you're coaching a leasing consultant on how to handle an objection, and by noon you're on a call with a vendor about a service delay. This is the rhythm of the community manager role at Hawthorne Residential Partners, and it suits people who think in systems while staying genuinely present with their teams and residents.

What the Role Covers

Hawthorne manages this coastal Florida community, and the full scope of operations runs through this position. On the financial side, you'll own budget management, rent collection, deposit accounting, and delinquency tracking. You'll read and act on financial reporting, which means understanding how leasing performance, concessions, and renewals all connect to NOI. Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms; comfort with both matters from day one.

Operationally, you're the link between the leasing office, maintenance, and ownership. You'll set pricing and renewal strategies to protect occupancy, oversee vendor performance, conduct property inspections, and partner with maintenance on work orders and preventative care schedules. You'll also support leasing directly when volume demands it, conducting tours, closing applications, and ensuring lease documents are completed accurately and on time.

Team leadership is a core function, not a secondary one. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff. Weekly team meetings, performance conversations, and creating a culture where people want to stay and grow are all part of the job. Hawthorne has a formal career path program, and community managers are expected to invest in their teams with the same intention the company invests in them.

Who's Ready for This Role

  • At least two years of multifamily property management experience, including time as a leasing consultant and assistant community manager
  • Six months of community manager experience is strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office tools
  • A valid driver's license; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate or property management license is a plus
  • Demonstrated ability to read financial reports and make budget-conscious decisions
  • Conflict resolution skills that hold up when situations get difficult

The candidates who tend to thrive here already understand that community management requires two distinct skill sets working at the same time: the operational discipline to manage numbers, compliance, and property condition, and the interpersonal range to coach a team member, de-escalate a frustrated resident, and represent the community well to ownership. Both have to be present. The role builds financial fluency and leadership depth over time, and Hawthorne's stated trajectory from community manager to regional manager is a path the company actively supports, not just lists on a posting.

Office hours run Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends come up for resident events or community needs. Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses.

job.title: Property Manager (Lake's Edge)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

As Property Manager at Lake's Edge Apartments in Greensboro, you're the person everyone on-site looks to, residents with concerns, leasing consultants hitting walls on a tough lead, maintenance techs waiting on a bid approval, and your Regional Manager watching the numbers. The role touches all of it, and you have to be comfortable moving between those conversations in the same afternoon.

Day to day, you'll oversee leasing activity and help shape pricing and concessions based on what the local market is doing. You'll hold your team accountable through regular huddles, coach leasing and maintenance staff, and make sure market-ready inspections actually meet the standard, not just check a box. On the financial side, you'll prepare annual budgets, run quarterly forecasts, monitor income and expenses, and compile the reports that keep leadership informed. Delinquency management is real work here: you'll track receivables for current and prior residents and follow through on the eviction process when it comes to that. Move-out deposit accounting, contract negotiation on maintenance bids, lease renewals, and regular lead follow-up all sit on your plate as well.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with some weekend availability expected when the property needs it.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with direct team supervision in that time
  • Financial fluency: budgeting, variance analysis, and reading a T-12 without needing a hand-hold
  • Familiarity with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Solid grounding in fair housing law and local landlord-tenant regulations
  • Communication skills that hold up across a staff meeting, a tense resident conversation, and a written report to ownership
  • The kind of organizational discipline that keeps punch lists, renewals, and reporting deadlines from slipping

The Fit and the Context

Van Metre has been building and managing properties since 1955, and they carry a long reputation in the mid-Atlantic and beyond. Coming in as a site-level manager, you're not operating in a vacuum. Your Regional Manager is a real resource, and the expectation is that you use that relationship well while still owning the day-to-day without needing to escalate everything.

What tends to separate strong candidates in a role like this is the ability to hold the financial picture and the people picture at the same time. Managers who focus only on occupancy and let delinquency creep, or who keep tight NOI discipline but burn through staff and hurt retention, both struggle here. The job rewards people who treat the leasing team as a resource to develop, not just a headcount to manage.

Compensation runs between $68,640 and $72,800 annually depending on experience, with quarterly bonus potential, leasing and renewal commissions, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, and wellness reimbursement up to $900 per year. Van Metre also offers rental discounts for employees, which is worth noting if you're looking to live on-site or nearby.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Autumn Ridge Apartments
job.description:
Autumn Ridge Apartments in Raleigh is adding a Customer Experience Specialist to its on-site team. Cottonwood Residential operates a national multifamily portfolio and runs this role as the front-line face of the community, handling everything from walk-in traffic to resident service requests to leasing support.

Day to day, you're the first person prospects and residents interact with. That means greeting visitors, answering calls, logging information accurately in the property management system, and routing maintenance requests to the right people. You're also keeping tabs on unit availability and pricing, following up with prospects who've toured, and helping move-ins go smoothly. When things get busy, you're managing several of those things at once.

Cottonwood runs Self-Guided Tours at their communities, so part of this role involves keeping those tour units clean, stocked, and ready at all times. You'll also walk the property regularly to make sure amenities and common areas meet presentation standards, and you'll pitch in on resident events and social media when needed.

Raleigh's rental market moves fast. The Research Triangle draws a steady wave of relocating professionals, grad students, and healthcare workers, all of whom expect a sharp, responsive leasing experience. First impressions and follow-up speed matter more here than in slower markets. If you've worked in hospitality or retail and developed real instincts for reading what a customer needs, that background translates directly to this kind of role.

What you'll need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year of in-person, customer-facing experience
  • At least one year in customer service, sales, administrative work, or hospitality
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office; willing to learn Entrata or similar platforms
  • Able to walk the property, stand for extended periods, and lift up to 50 pounds
  • Flexible schedule, including early starts when the role requires it
  • Multifamily experience is a plus, but not required

Strong candidates tend to be the ones who take ownership of small details without being asked. Keeping the tour unit spotless, following up with a prospect on day two instead of day four, catching a burned-out light on the amenity walk before a resident mentions it. Those habits are what separate people who do this job from people who do it well.

job.title: Multi-Site Property Manager
job.description:
Multi-site property management is one of the more demanding skill sets in residential operations. You're not just running a building. You're maintaining financial oversight, client relationships, team development, and occupancy performance across multiple communities simultaneously. This role with Bozzuto in Santa Monica puts all of those skills to work at once.

Skills This Role Requires From Day One

You'll need a developed command of P&L management. Bozzuto expects you to own the financial performance of your properties, which means reading T-12 trends, managing NOI against budget, and explaining variances to clients with clarity and accuracy. Reporting to clients isn't a checkbox here. It's a relationship-building act, and your written and verbal communication has to reflect that.

On the operational side, you'll need to hold occupancy and retention goals through disciplined execution of leasing and marketing strategies. That means staying sharp on competitive marketplace intelligence, understanding where your communities sit relative to comparable product in the Santa Monica submarket, and working with consumer marketing to put the right strategy in place. The Santa Monica rental market skews toward Class A renters with real options. Your competitive awareness has to be precise, not general.

Leadership experience matters here because you'll be setting the standard for your teams daily. Bozzuto's expectation is that this role models behavior, not just manages tasks. Rolling up your sleeves when the situation calls for it is part of that standard, not a footnote.

  • 5 or more years in property management, hospitality, or retail, with leadership responsibility
  • Four-year degree or equivalent field experience
  • Demonstrated P&L and budget management history
  • Proficiency with property management software, Yardi preferred
  • Working knowledge of general accounting principles
  • Strong client relationship track record

Skills This Role Builds

Multi-site responsibility sharpens your ability to prioritize across competing urgencies, a capability that's foundational for anyone moving toward a regional manager position. When you're responsible for more than one asset, you develop the habit of thinking in systems rather than reacting property by property. That shift in thinking is exactly what regional and portfolio-level roles require.

Client management at the multi-site level also builds a specific skill: delivering financial narratives that earn trust. Producing accurate reports is the baseline. Translating performance data into a clear story for ownership is the craft. That skill transfers across fee management, third-party management, and even ownership structures you haven't encountered yet.

What's Distinctive About This Role

Bozzuto operates with a culture that takes professional development seriously, backing that commitment with tuition reimbursement and structured growth programming. For a property manager who wants to build toward a regional role, the combination of multi-site scope and an organization with actual infrastructure for advancement is a meaningful pairing. The salary range sits between $92,000 and $93,000, with bonus eligibility and a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 20 days of paid time off, and a 401k with company match.

One scheduling note worth flagging: the role requires one weekend per month on-site, with two weekdays off in exchange. That's a standard trade-off in lease-up and stabilized markets alike, and knowing it upfront helps you decide if the structure fits your life.

job.title: Regional Vice President
job.description:
What This Role Runs On

This is a relationship-management and operational oversight role at its core. The Regional Vice President position at Asset Living requires two distinct skill sets working simultaneously: the ability to coach and develop Regional Managers who are running their own portfolios, and the ability to hold client relationships with ownership groups at a level where those clients trust you with their assets. Both matter equally. Neither covers for a weakness in the other.

Asset Living operates as a third-party management firm, which means client retention is tied directly to performance visibility. You're not managing an owner's single asset; you're representing Asset Living across a regional portfolio that spans multifamily, student housing, affordable housing, and build-to-rent properties. The RVP is the person ownership groups call when something is off, and the person Regional Managers rely on to clear obstacles and set direction.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

A large portion of this role is people development. You set performance expectations for Regional Managers, review operational results with them, identify where they need support, and build toward succession planning across your region. That means knowing when to coach and when to intervene.

On the financial side, you'll review budgets, track NOI performance, weigh in on capex decisions, and work with Regional Managers when properties are underperforming. You're not running spreadsheets from a back office. You're in the data enough to have informed conversations with clients and executives, then out in the region enough to see what's actually happening at the site level.

Client engagement is a standing responsibility. You'll lead business reviews, represent Asset Living at industry events, and stay close to ownership groups so you can spot both risks and new business opportunities early. The firm has grown organically since 1986, and client relationships are a direct part of that model.

Travel runs between 25 and 50 percent annually. That's property visits, conferences, client meetings, and internal training. Kansas City is the base location, but the region extends beyond it.

  • Prior experience as a Regional Manager in multifamily or student housing is required
  • Demonstrated track record managing teams across multiple properties
  • Comfort with budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting processes
  • Strong client-facing communication skills, including formal presentations
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent experience considered
  • CAM, CAPS, or CPM designation is a plus

What Asset Living Brings to This Role

Asset Living is ranked in the NMHC top 50 and holds AMO accreditation through IREM. The portfolio spans property types that most regional operators never touch in a single career: conventional multifamily, student, affordable, build-to-rent, and active adult. For an RVP, that breadth means exposure to operating models and resident profiles that sharpen judgment in ways a single-asset-class role doesn't.

Strong candidates at this level tend to separate themselves less on market knowledge and more on how they handle ambiguity at scale. Managing Regional Managers is a different discipline than being one. The transition requires trusting your team to execute while staying close enough to the numbers and the clients to catch problems early. That balance is what Asset Living is evaluating here.

job.title: Maintenance Technician- Thorncroft Farms
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and a resident's water heater gave out overnight. By 8 a.m., you've already pulled the work order, confirmed the parts situation, and you're on your way to their unit with a plan. That's the rhythm of this role at Thorncroft Farms, a community in Hillsboro, OR managed by MG Properties.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

MG Properties has been operating apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, and they run a tight, experienced operation. At Thorncroft Farms, the maintenance team handles a full spectrum of daily work: service requests across plumbing, electrical, and HVAC; appliance repairs; painting; grounds and common area upkeep; and apartment turns. When a unit turns, you're walking it, working the punch list, and getting it make-ready for the next resident. When you're on call, you're the person residents count on after hours. That's a real responsibility, and MG takes it seriously enough to build a rotation so no single person carries it alone.

The team here is looking for someone with at least two years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of 200 units or more. Multi-trade competency isn't optional. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC basics, you should be comfortable moving between them without needing to call out for every specialized task. Reliable transportation is required since the job sometimes means getting there before the front office opens.

Who Fits Well Here

The technical side matters, but so does how you show up for residents. Maintenance techs at apartment communities are often the face people see most. A resident having a rough week doesn't just want their faucet fixed. They want to feel heard and respected during the visit. MG specifically calls out customer service orientation as a core qualification, and that's worth taking at face value.

Strong candidates will have:

  • At least 2 years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience
  • Demonstrated skills across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC/AC, and general repair
  • Comfort working both independently and as part of a maintenance team
  • Flexibility to participate in an on-call rotation
  • Reliable transportation

MG offers monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, and medical, dental, and vision coverage. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, paid sick time, and a rental discount round out the package.

One thing worth noting for anyone coming from commercial or facilities work: residential apartment maintenance has its own pace. Resident relationships are ongoing, not transactional. The person whose dishwasher you fixed last month will see you in the parking lot next week. That familiarity can be one of the best parts of the job for people who genuinely enjoy that kind of community dynamic.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and a resident is at the door before the office officially opens, upset about a charge on their ledger. Twenty minutes later, you're pulling a prospect through a tour of a two-bedroom while your phone buzzes with a renewal reminder. That's the rhythm here, and if you can hold it without losing your composure, you'll do well.

Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the top 50 multifamily management companies in the country and a Southeast-rooted operator, is hiring an Assistant Community Manager in Asheville, NC. This is a real second-in-command position: you'll work directly alongside the Community Manager to keep the property's leasing, finances, and resident experience running well.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On the leasing side, you'll handle incoming leads, conduct tours, guide prospects through applications, and work toward occupancy goals alongside your team. Renewals fall in your lap too, so resident retention is part of your daily mindset, not an afterthought.

Financially, you'll oversee rent collection, payment posting, and ledger accuracy. Delinquency follow-up is a regular part of the job, including weekly calls and coordinating eviction procedures when it gets to that point. You'll also help prepare financial reporting for regional leadership. This isn't a role where the numbers stay at arm's length.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the show. That means keeping the team focused, handling escalated resident issues, and making sure daily operations don't skip a beat. Social media content for the community is also in your corner, specifically promoting events and keeping residents engaged.

The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. You'll have one weekday off each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours, though evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events.

Who Fits Here

  • At least two years of property management experience, with six months in an assistant manager seat preferred
  • Comfortable reading financial reports and making decisions within budget constraints
  • A track record of de-escalating resident situations calmly and following through on resolutions
  • High School diploma or GED required; a CALP credential is a plus
  • Valid driver's license

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits cover medical, dental, and vision; a 401k match; paid time off (including your birthday); paid parental and adoption leave; pet insurance; telehealth access; and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers a formal Career Path Program for employees ready to move from Assistant Community Manager into a full Community Manager role.

What separates candidates who grow in this seat from those who plateau: the ability to treat the financial side of the job with the same care as the people side. Strong ACMs don't hand ledger questions off or avoid delinquency conversations. They stay close to both.

job.title: Community Manager - Temporary - Casa La Mesa Apartments
job.description:
Sunrise Management runs Casa La Mesa Apartments in La Mesa, CA, and they're bringing in a temporary Community Manager to keep things running well while this position is covered. The assignment is expected to last three to six months, full-time, with pay between $25 and $27 per hour depending on experience. Benefits eligibility and leasing bonuses are included, which isn't always the case for temp roles at this level.

What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-scope site management role. You're not just holding the seat warm. You'll oversee leasing activity, rent collection, delinquency management, vendor coordination, and move-in/move-out inspections. You'll supervise on-site staff, which means hiring, training, and giving real feedback when it's needed. Budget monitoring and expense tracking are part of the job, and so is making sure the property stays physically clean, safe, and up to standard.

On the resident side, the expectation is 24 to 48 hour turnaround on service requests, and genuine follow-through on concerns when things get complicated. California landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing compliance shape how you handle most of what comes up day-to-day, so familiarity with both is a genuine requirement here, not a formality.

You'll also manage marketing for available units and analyze local market conditions to keep pricing competitive. Sunrise focuses on what they call resident hospitality, so the culture does lean toward warmth and engagement rather than pure transactional efficiency.

What You Bring

  • At least one to two years of on-site property management experience
  • Working knowledge of California landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Experience supervising at least a small team
  • Basic accounting understanding, specifically around rent collections and bank deposits
  • Strong communication skills across residents, vendors, and ownership

A college degree is preferred but not required if your experience is solid. What tends to matter more in a role like this is whether you can hold the team together and keep residents reasonably satisfied during a transition period, which is inherently a little uncertain for everyone involved.

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Interim community manager roles carry a specific kind of pressure. Staff already on-site may be adjusting to a temporary leader, and residents often sense when management is in flux. The candidates who do well in these placements are the ones who establish credibility quickly through consistency: following through on requests, being visible on the property, and being clear with the team about expectations without over-asserting authority they haven't earned yet.

La Mesa sits in the east San Diego metro, a stable but competitive submarket where Class B and C garden-style communities compete on service quality as much as price. Knowing how to position a community there and retain residents through renewal conversations is a real skill, and this role gives you room to use it.

If you're a property management professional between roles or looking for a bridge opportunity that actually pays and offers benefits, this is a legitimate one worth considering.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager Multi-Site Denver
job.description:
Customer service instincts and financial precision don't always show up together in the same person. At RedPeak, the Assistant Community Manager role at their Downing Street portfolio requires both, and the balance between them is what makes this position genuinely interesting for the right candidate.

Skills That Drive This Role

The day-to-day work here leans heavily on two skill sets: interpersonal communication and accounting discipline. You'll be the second-in-command across a 549-unit, 12-building portfolio, which means residents, vendors, leasing staff, and your Community Manager all count on you to be a steady, knowledgeable presence. That's the communication side. On the financial side, you'll own accounts payable in a meaningful way: coding and approving invoices, posting rent and utility charges, managing delinquency, overseeing collections, and contributing to month-end reporting. Neither half of this role is a supporting act for the other. They carry equal weight.

The multi-site setup adds a layer of complexity that single-property roles don't have. You're covering 12 buildings spread across a portfolio, which means your organizational habits and follow-through need to be reliable without close oversight. If you've managed delinquency or budget variances at a 200-plus unit community before, that experience translates directly here.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical week mixes resident-facing moments with back-office responsibilities. You might walk apartments and prep move-in gifts in the morning, then spend part of the afternoon in Yardi Voyager reviewing invoice approvals or reconciling charges against the annual budget. Vendor relationships are yours to manage too: communicating service expectations, reviewing bids, and making sure the properties hold up against comparable Class A product in the Denver market. When leasing traffic picks up, you'll work alongside the leasing staff to keep occupancy where it needs to be, handling concessions or adjustments as needed with the Community Manager's direction.

Conflict resolution comes with the territory. Resident concerns at this scale don't stay small if they go unaddressed. Your ability to follow up consistently and de-escalate calmly has a direct impact on turnover, and RedPeak places a clear emphasis on keeping that number low.

Doing This Role at RedPeak

RedPeak is a Denver-based company managing its own portfolio, which matters in this context. Fee management environments often separate financial decisions from on-site teams. Here, the accountability sits closer to the property level, which means your reporting, your budget awareness, and your relationships with residents reflect directly on the company's ownership position. That's a different kind of professional weight than you'd feel at a third-party management shop, and for a lot of people, it's more satisfying.

  • 3 or more years of on-site property management experience, including at communities above 200 units
  • Supervisory background with leasing or maintenance staff
  • Yardi Voyager proficiency (this is a firm requirement, not a preference)
  • Experience writing or maintaining community budgets
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, with hourly pay ranging from $26 to $29 depending on experience and certifications, plus bonus eligibility. If you've been looking for a role that actually uses both sides of your property management background, this is a reasonable place to land.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Troubleshooting is the core skill here. At a 541-unit garden-style community in Saint Paul, a Maintenance Technician III spends a meaningful portion of each day diagnosing problems before fixing them. HVAC systems cycle through Minnesota winters hard. Boilers need attention. Plumbing issues don't announce themselves politely. The technician who thrives in this role reads a situation quickly, decides what it needs, and gets to work without waiting to be told twice.

What the Work Actually Involves

The day-to-day splits into a few consistent categories: completing work orders, keeping building systems running, and turning vacated units into make-readies. You'll work directly with the Property Manager and a Zone Building Engineer, which means there's structure and support behind you, but you're expected to handle standard repairs independently. Plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, HVAC, boiler systems, pool and sauna operations, irrigation, and groundskeeping all fall within scope depending on the season.

Winter here adds real weight to the job. Snow removal from walkways and driveways is part of your responsibilities, and Saint Paul winters are not forgiving. The on-call rotation brings after-hours emergency calls into the picture. The expectation is a 30-minute response time. That's realistic if you live nearby, but worth knowing before you apply.

Within six months of hire, you'll need to hold a Certified Pool Operators License, a Special Boiler's License, and a Type II Refrigerant Certification if you don't already. The company provides educational assistance, so the path to getting there isn't unsupported.

Skills This Role Demands Most

  • Hands-on diagnostic ability across plumbing, HVAC, electrical, and appliance systems
  • Time management when multiple work orders compete for your attention
  • Physical stamina: frequent lifting up to 80 lbs. with assistance, working in confined spaces, rooftops, and exterior conditions year-round
  • Clear communication with residents, vendors, and management under pressure
  • Self-direction on preventative maintenance without waiting for someone to remind you

A high school diploma or GED is required. An AA or certification in HVAC, electrical, or mechanical is preferred but not mandatory. At least one year of residential maintenance experience carries real weight here because the volume at 541 units doesn't leave room for learning the basics on the job.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Technicians who do well in large residential communities tend to be organized about parts and inventory, honest about what they can and can't fix alone, and consistent about flagging issues upward before they become emergencies. At this property, you're coordinating with a Zone Building Engineer and working alongside vendors on larger projects, so being a communicative team member matters as much as technical skill. The technicians who struggle usually underestimate either the physical demands of Minnesota winters or the documentation side of the work.

Bigos Management has earned a Star Tribune Top Workplace designation twelve times, which suggests the internal culture has staying power. The pay range runs $23 to $27 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal bonuses available, a 401(k) with employer match, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, and a benefits package that starts the first of the month after hire.

job.title: Sales Support Specialist
job.description:
Student housing leasing operates on a compressed, high-stakes calendar. When pre-lease velocity slows at any point in that cycle, the gap compounds quickly, and catching up requires someone who can convert leads at volume without sacrificing the relationship-building that drives renewals. That's the problem this role solves.

PeakMade Real Estate, headquartered in Atlanta, manages off-campus student housing alongside multi-family, co-living, and build-to-rent communities across the country. The Sales Support Specialist sits at the revenue center of that portfolio, working across properties to lift occupancy and pre-lease numbers through direct, high-volume leasing activity.

What the Work Actually Involves

This is a lead-to-lease role with real accountability to outcomes. You'll manage prospects through the buying funnel, turning inquiries into applications and applications into signed leases. That means handling a large pipeline simultaneously, knowing when to push and when to let a conversation breathe, and tracking every interaction in Entrata so nothing falls through the cracks. EliseAI experience helps here, since PeakMade uses it to support lead nurturing at scale.

Beyond conversion, you'll evaluate each property's position within its local market, identifying where the value proposition is strong and where it needs sharpening. That analysis feeds into leasing messaging across channels, so stakeholders are working from the same story. On the retention side, you'll identify residents with high renewal potential and reach them through personalized outreach before they start looking elsewhere.

The Profile That Fits

  • 2 or more years of sales experience, with direct leasing exposure
  • Background in student housing specifically (the leasing calendar and customer dynamic are distinct from conventional multi-family)
  • Demonstrated ability to manage high-volume lead conversion without losing quality
  • Strong verbal and written communication, including handling objections under pressure
  • Proficiency in Entrata preferred; EliseAI familiarity is a plus
  • Eligible to work in the United States

What separates strong candidates here is market evaluation instinct. Converting leads is a skill, but refining a value proposition based on competitive positioning requires a different kind of thinking. Candidates who've looked at a T-3 occupancy trend or a concessions comparison and adjusted their leasing pitch accordingly will move faster in this role than those who rely purely on scripted technique.

From a career standpoint, this role builds a skill set that travels well. High-volume conversion experience combined with market analysis work is exactly what regional and portfolio leasing roles require. If you're aiming toward a Leasing Director, Regional Manager, or revenue-focused operations seat, the exposure across PeakMade's verticals, student housing, multi-family, build-to-rent, gives you a broader foundation than a single-asset role typically would.

job.title: Leasing Specialist- Dallas, Tx 75243
job.description:
A prospect walks in without an appointment on a Saturday afternoon, and you're the only one in the office. By the time they leave, they've toured two units, submitted an application, and have a move-in date in mind. That's the job in a single frame.

What the Role Covers

Karya Property Management is hiring a Leasing Specialist for their Dallas portfolio in the 75243 zip code. The core of this position is converting traffic into signed leases, then keeping those residents satisfied through their tenancy. You'll handle walk-ins, phone calls, and internet leads, tour available units, process applications from screening through approval, and execute lease documents and addenda. Renewal outreach is part of the job too: you'll follow up on expiring leases and work to keep occupancy where it needs to be.

Beyond the leasing cycle itself, you'll coordinate with the maintenance team on make-ready status before showings, walk vacants to confirm they're show-ready, and flag curb appeal or safety issues as you move around the property. You'll log guest cards, track your conversion data in the property management system, and run competitor market surveys to keep pricing and concessions current. When residents move in, you'll handle orientations and paperwork. When they have service requests, you'll route them and follow up. The administrative side is real: Fair Housing compliance, file maintenance, and general office coverage come with the territory.

The outreach component asks you to contribute content for social media and listing platforms, assist with resident events, and support relationships with local employers and referral sources. Hours include Saturdays and occasional evenings during peak leasing periods.

What Karya Wants to See

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year in a customer-facing role: leasing, sales, hospitality, retail, or similar
  • Comfort asking for the sale and following up consistently without crossing into pushy territory
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including a professional phone presence
  • Basic computer skills; Microsoft Office or Google Workspace proficiency
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Prior multifamily leasing experience is a plus
  • Familiarity with Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, Rent Manager, or similar software is preferred
  • Knowledge of Fair Housing requirements and the Texas Residential Landlord and Tenant Act is an advantage
  • Bilingual English/Spanish candidates are encouraged to apply

The candidates who tend to outperform in leasing roles like this one are the ones who treat follow-up as a system, not an afterthought. Closing ratio and occupancy are measurable, and strong leasing specialists check those numbers the way others check email. If you've worked a sales role where you owned a pipeline and tracked your own performance, that habit translates directly here.

This role is a solid entry point into multifamily operations. Leasing Specialists who build strong conversion habits and learn the operational side often move into Senior Leasing Consultant or Assistant Property Manager positions within a few years, particularly at growing regional operators like KPM.

job.title: Assistant Community Association Manager
job.description:
HOA management in a mountain resort community carries demands you won't find in a typical suburban portfolio. Homeowners may be part-time residents with high expectations, boards often include people accustomed to running businesses, and the physical environment adds real complexity: snow, ice, steep terrain, and properties that sit vacant for weeks at a time before an owner arrives and finds something wrong. Mountain Valley Property Management has worked across the Vail Valley for over two decades, and this assistant role is designed to bring someone into that environment with a real support structure around them.

What the Job Actually Involves

You'll work alongside experienced Community Association Managers, handling the operational work that keeps HOA communities running day to day. That includes vendor coordination with a 24-hour response standard on maintenance requests, property inspections using a mobile app (expect stairs, uneven ground, and winter conditions), compliance tracking from courtesy notices through resolution, and board meeting prep including agendas and minutes. The associations you'll support range from small communities of six units to larger ones with 150-plus, and budgets from $50,000 to over $1 million.

Most mornings start at the EagleVail office or from home, working through emails, owner calls, and vendor follow-up before heading into the field in a company vehicle. Some evenings include board meetings. That's part of the role, and it's worth knowing upfront rather than finding out after you've started.

  • Coordinate maintenance requests and vendor work, tracking against response standards
  • Assist with budget preparation and analysis across multiple association accounts
  • Conduct site inspections and document conditions with preventive maintenance recommendations
  • Support board meeting logistics and prepare minutes following each meeting
  • Manage owner and board member communication as a primary point of contact
  • Handle compliance processes from initial notice through resolution

Who Fits This Role

Mountain Valley says 100% of their Community Association Managers started in this assistant position and most moved up within 18 to 24 months. They cover CAM exam fees, provide paid study time, and pair you with a certified manager as a mentor. That path is real, but it requires someone who takes the administrative side as seriously as the relationship side. Board minutes don't write themselves, and an inspection report that's vague or incomplete creates problems down the road.

The skills that separate strong candidates here aren't glamorous. It's consistent follow-through on vendor calls, clean documentation, and the ability to stay calm when a homeowner is frustrated about something that happened at their property while they were out of state. Hospitality and customer service backgrounds translate well to this, particularly around managing expectations under pressure.

You need to already live in the Vail Valley or Eagle County area. The company is clear that relocation assistance isn't available, and given how much field time the role involves, that's a practical requirement.

  • Required: Microsoft Office and Adobe Acrobat proficiency, strong written and verbal communication, valid driver's license with clean record, ability to pass a background check, U.S. work authorization, local residency
  • Preferred but trainable: Prior property management, hospitality, or customer service experience; HOA or community governance familiarity; property management software experience; Spanish language skills

Compensation runs $60,000 to $75,000 depending on experience, with a 4% 401(k) match vested immediately, ICHRA health contribution, medical/dental/vision, 17 days PTO to start, paid sick time, CAM certification support, a $1,500 annual education budget, company vehicle, and a $50 monthly wellness credit. For this valley, that combination of benefits and a clear advancement track is worth noting.

job.title: Apartment Leasing Sales Consultant - Creekside
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning at Creekside, and you've got three tours scheduled before noon, two follow-up calls sitting in your queue from yesterday's traffic, and a prospect who toured on Saturday just texted asking about move-in specials. That's the job in a single hour.

The Role at Creekside

AIR Communities operates apartment communities in major markets, and Creekside in Denver is one of them. As a Leasing Consultant here, your core responsibility is converting traffic into signed leases. That means working AIR's defined sales process: prompt follow-up with prospects, conducting tours that actually sell the community's value, and closing. Monthly leasing goals are real and tracked, and AIR builds commission tiers around hitting and exceeding them. Longer lease terms (18 months or more), premium units with updated finishes or better views, and goal-tier bonuses all layer onto your base pay of $20 to $21 per hour. The earning upside is genuine for someone who can close consistently.

Beyond your own lease count, you'll support marketing efforts at the community level and may provide leasing backup to other properties in the AIR portfolio during need periods. Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable, as it always is. The standard schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10:00am to 6:30pm, with some seasonal variation.

One thing worth knowing about AIR's model: they build in an extended Winter Break after peak season. You keep benefits and the 25% rent discount during the unpaid break. If you've worked lease-up seasons before, you know that a structured off-ramp before the next turn of the calendar is not nothing.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least one year of sales and customer service experience, in property management, hospitality, retail, or a similar environment where you had actual goals to hit
  • Demonstrated ability to follow a structured sales process and show results against targets
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • Availability for a Tuesday through Saturday schedule
  • Reliable transportation

What separates candidates who do well in this specific kind of leasing role from those who wash out early is mostly this: comfort with structured sales process combined with genuine people skills. Pure hospitality backgrounds sometimes struggle with the close. Pure sales backgrounds sometimes blow the relationship side. The consultants who last and earn well here tend to hold both. If you've hit commission targets in a previous role and you actually like working with people through a decision, that combination travels well into leasing.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance; HSA and FSA options; short and long-term disability covered by AIR; a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match; up to 16 weeks paid parental leave; tuition assistance and certification reimbursement; and 15 hours of paid community service time annually.

job.title: Service Technician II | Pay: $23-$26/hr. + Bonus
job.description:
Maintenance work in multifamily breaks down into two categories: the people who can handle a little of everything and the people who can handle a little of everything without being reminded twice. Village Green is hiring a Service Technician II for The View at Rock Run in Joliet, and they want the second kind.

The Skills This Role Leans On

The core of this position is hands-on trade work across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and drywall. Turns are a significant part of the workload. That means moving through a punch list efficiently, painting clean, pulling and replacing appliances, patching drywall that actually looks patched, and making sure the unit is ready to show on schedule. HVAC knowledge matters here too, both for work orders during occupied residency and as part of make-ready prep. If your HVAC background is thin, that's worth being honest about upfront.

Beyond the technical side, resident interaction is constant. Service requests aren't dropped at the door; they involve real communication with people who live there. Customer service isn't a soft skill in this role, it's part of the job description in the same sentence as electrical and plumbing.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You're pulling work orders, moving between units, handling curb appeal walkthroughs, and staying available for on-call emergencies on a rotating basis. In winter, that includes snow removal. Pool maintenance may apply depending on the season. The Property Manager and Service Manager direct the on-call response cadence, so communication with leadership is built into the rhythm. This isn't a siloed role where you work independently all day. You're part of a maintenance team, and coordination matters.

The pay range is $23 to $26 per hour plus a bonus program, with benefits that include medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k) with a company match.

What Village Green Brings to the Table

Village Green has been in multifamily management since 1919. That's not a small thing. Long-tenured management companies tend to have more structured training, clearer advancement paths, and maintenance programs that have been refined over time. For a Service Tech II, that means you're not walking into a disorganized shop. The technician career track in this industry typically moves from Tech II toward Senior Technician, Lead Tech, or Service Manager, and companies with deep operational history tend to promote from within more consistently than newer operators.

  • 1 to 3 years of experience in multifamily housing or the hotel industry preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and painting
  • HVAC experience expected at this level
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • General computer competency for work order systems
  • Ability to handle on-call emergencies and physically demanding tasks year-round

Pre-employment drug screening and background check are required. Village Green participates in E-Verify.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Lease-up pressure and high resident turnover have made the leasing consultant role more demanding than it looks from the outside. At a well-run apartment community, a leasing consultant carries the full weight of first impressions: prospect to tour to signed lease, with the resident experience beginning the moment someone picks up the phone or fills out an online form. Bozzuto, a name well-regarded in the mid-Atlantic and Southeast markets for its management standards, is hiring for this role in Nashville's 37203 zip code, which puts you squarely in the Gulch and Midtown corridor, one of the most competitive Class A rental submarkets in the city.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A large share of this role lives in lead follow-up. Nashville's rental market generates strong traffic, but converting that interest into tours, and tours into signed leases, takes consistent outreach and genuine skill in reading what a prospect actually needs. You'll conduct personalized community tours, work your social media channels (Instagram and Facebook, primarily) to build organic awareness, and handle the communication that keeps prospects warm between their first inquiry and move-in day.

The schedule reflects the reality of when people look for apartments: three weekends per month are part of the rotation, offset by two weekdays off. That's worth understanding before you apply. Weekend availability isn't a footnote here, it's a core part of the role's value to the property.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, specifically the ability to tailor a conversation to the person in front of you
  • Comfort with social media content creation, not just posting, but producing content that actually generates engagement
  • A polished, professional presentation
  • Sales instincts and follow-through, the ability to move a conversation forward without being pushy
  • Competency with leasing software, apps, and general tech tools

The base salary range is $46,000 to $50,000, with additional bonus opportunities tied to performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: the ability to sell the neighborhood, not just the floor plan. In a market like Nashville's Midtown, the walkability, dining, and proximity to major employers are part of the value proposition. Prospects who are relocating, especially from other metros, are often making decisions based on the broader area as much as the unit itself. Consultants who can speak knowledgeably and enthusiastically about where the property sits tend to close at a higher rate than those who keep the conversation inside the building.

job.title: Maintenance Technician-Cortland North Plano
job.description:
Cortland runs one of the larger vertically integrated multifamily platforms in the country, which means their maintenance teams operate inside a structure that includes in-house design and construction. For a technician, that matters. You're not just turning work orders. You're working alongside people who understand the physical asset at a deeper level, and that environment tends to sharpen your diagnostic instincts faster than a typical third-party managed community would.
