What You'll Actually Do

This role covers the full range of building systems maintenance at a Plano community. Day to day, that means diagnosing and repairing electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances, flooring, and structural components like stairs and railings. You'll also own a piece of the preventative maintenance calendar, particularly around HVAC units, which in North Texas is not a small responsibility given the summer load those systems carry. Part of the job is keeping your eyes on the property's condition broadly: lighting, gates, access points, surveillance systems, automatic doors. When something looks wrong, you document it and flag it. You'll carry an on-call rotation and respond to emergencies when they come up.

Resident interaction is a real part of the role. Cortland positions itself around the resident experience, so how you show up at someone's door matters, not just what you fix when you get there.

What You Bring

  • EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) required before starting
  • 1 to 3 or more years of maintenance experience, ideally in multifamily or facilities
  • Hands-on competency across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Comfort managing multiple open work orders and prioritizing on the fly
  • Physical readiness for ladder work, outdoor conditions, and lifting
  • Willingness to participate in on-call schedules
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Where This Role Leads

Maintenance Technician is one of the most transferable roles in property management. The technical depth you build here, especially HVAC diagnostics and preventative maintenance systems, creates a clear path toward Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor positions. At a company like Cortland with a substantial portfolio, internal movement is a realistic option rather than a theoretical one. Technicians who also develop their communication skills and start thinking about capex planning and asset condition reporting tend to reach supervisory roles faster. The skills you build here also transfer directly if you ever move toward facilities management, construction management, or service coordination at larger housing operators.

Strong candidates tend to be the ones who treat preventative maintenance as seriously as reactive repairs. The technicians who get noticed at portfolio-scale operators are the ones who catch problems before they become work orders.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Your Monday morning starts with a delinquency report that's two points above target on one asset and a vacancy spike on another that the on-site team flagged over the weekend. Before 9 a.m., you're already triaging two properties at once. That's the rhythm of a Regional Manager role, and it's exactly the kind of work that builds the instincts no classroom teaches.

What This Role Actually Covers

Asset Living, a third-party management firm with an NMHC top-50 ranking and an AMO designation through IREM, is hiring a Regional Manager to oversee a portfolio of multifamily communities in the Charlotte, NC market. The scope is full-cycle operations: personnel, financial performance, leasing strategy, maintenance oversight, and risk management, all executed from an offsite leadership position.

On the people side, you'll handle everything from screening and hiring on-site staff to coaching Community Managers through performance issues, salary review requests, and HR documentation. You're the layer between the property teams and senior leadership, which means you're approving timesheets, signing off on counseling statements, and making sure the right people are in the right seats.

Financially, the job centers on NOI. You'll build annual operating budgets, write monthly variance explanations for income and expense line items running over budget, track capex needs, monitor vendor contracts and invoices, and make sure property closeouts and ownership reports go out accurately and on time. You're not reviewing numbers once a quarter. You're watching them weekly and adjusting strategy accordingly.

On the leasing side, you'll develop yearly marketing plans, evaluate whether on-site teams are converting traffic effectively, and build resident retention programs that reduce turnover costs. Administrative and maintenance oversight rounds out the role: regular property inspections, emergency response coordination, service request monitoring, and making sure the punch list actually gets completed.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a multifamily portfolio across multiple properties, with direct accountability for NOI and occupancy outcomes
  • Comfort reading financial statements at the line-item level, not just the summary
  • Experience developing and coaching on-site teams, including handling terminations and HR documentation correctly
  • Familiarity with third-party management dynamics, where the client relationship adds a layer of accountability beyond internal expectations
  • Solid grounding in fair housing compliance and risk management protocols

The candidates who stand out in regional roles aren't necessarily the ones with the longest tenure. They're the ones who can hold a team accountable without demoralizing it, read a T-12 and spot what the numbers aren't saying out loud, and shift priorities mid-week without losing momentum on the slower-burn issues. If you've managed a lease-up or stabilized a struggling asset, that experience translates directly here.

From a career trajectory standpoint, Regional Manager is the clearest path toward VP-level operations or a Director of Real Estate role within a third-party management firm. The financial fluency and multi-site leadership experience you build here are exactly what those roles require. Asset Living's portfolio spans multifamily, single-family rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing, which means your exposure to asset types at this level is broader than most regional roles at a single-strategy owner-operator.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Olympus Corsair
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer in the National Apartment Association three years running, 2023 through 2025. That kind of recognition usually reflects something real about the internal culture, and the Olympus Corsair team in San Diego is a good example of how that plays out at the property level. The Assistant Manager role here sits at the center of daily community life, and what you do every day has a direct impact on how residents feel about where they live.

What You'll Actually Do

A lot of this role is financial accountability. You'll handle rent collection, verify deposits hit the bank before close each day, process move-out dispositions, and keep the books clean. When the Property Manager is out, you step into that seat fully. That's worth noting: this isn't a shadowing position. You're expected to handle operations independently when it's needed.

You'll also be on the leasing floor when the team needs you. Showing make-ready apartments, participating in retention events, covering traffic, keeping an eye on the sub-market nearby. San Diego's rental market moves fast, so staying current on new construction, competing communities, and local hiring trends is genuinely part of the job, not a footnote.

Beyond the numbers and leasing support, you'll be the person residents turn to when something goes wrong. That means fielding complaints promptly, fielding them professionally, and knowing when to escalate liability issues or legal matters to the Regional Manager. The job has real interpersonal weight to it.

What You Bring

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant at an apartment community
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Onesite, or Knock is strongly preferred
  • Comfort managing financial records with accuracy and confidentiality
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for the first weekend of each month and occasional after-hours resident events
  • A detail-oriented approach to file management, compliance, and collections
  • Strong interpersonal instincts, because you'll interact with residents, vendors, co-workers, and ownership-side contacts regularly

The Fit and the Path Forward

The candidates who tend to thrive in Assistant Manager roles are the ones who can shift from reviewing delinquency reports in the morning to hosting a resident appreciation event in the afternoon without losing focus on either. It's a range that not everyone has. If you do, the experience you build here, handling collections, covering for the Property Manager, managing vendor relationships, positions you well to step into a Business Manager or Property Manager role within the Olympus portfolio.

Pay runs between $28.00 and $30.00 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and a sabbatical program, among others.

job.title: Apartment Service Technician
job.description:
Maintenance staffing in multifamily has gotten tighter. Certified techs, especially those holding EPA Universal or HVAC Type I/II credentials, have real leverage right now, and operators with quality assets are competing harder to keep them. Morguard's opening at their Rockville, MD community fits that picture: a structured, full-time role at a company that manages its own portfolio rather than farming out management, with a schedule that actually has logic behind it.

The Work Itself

The schedule runs Sunday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. That's a deliberate choice for a multifamily property: front-load your tech availability on the weekend when residents are home and reporting issues, and get the work done before the traditional Monday crunch becomes a backlog. You'll carry a mix of daily responsibilities: clearing the grounds on your morning walk, working through assigned work orders, assisting on make-readies and turns, and jumping in on capital and routine maintenance projects alongside the Lead Maintenance Technician and Community Manager.

Work orders here cover the range: plumbing, drywall, painting, appliance repair, minor electrical troubleshooting, carpentry. The expectation is accurate diagnosis first, then a clean close-out. Residents notice the difference between a tech who actually fixed the problem and one who patched around it. HVAC certification is required, not preferred, and you'll participate in the on-call rotation with your teammates. Each rotation week pays a $100 stipend whether or not you're called out.

Pay runs $27 to $28 per hour, full-time up to 40 hours weekly. Quarterly performance bonuses are available, up to 5% of annual salary. Benefits include employer-provided medical coverage, a dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match with immediate vesting, an education reimbursement program, and an employee discount for living within the Morguard portfolio.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

  • EPA Universal or HVAC Type I and Type II certification (required, not negotiable)
  • Hands-on experience closing work orders and completing turns, ideally at a Class A or B community
  • Solid generalist foundation: plumbing, painting, drywall, carpentry, appliance repair, minor electrical
  • Comfortable with on-call rotation and after-hours response
  • High school diploma required; trade or technical school is a plus
  • Fair Housing awareness and a habit of communicating proactively with supervisors when timelines shift

The techs who do well in a role like this tend to be the ones who treat the morning property walk as real intelligence gathering rather than a formality. Knowing your buildings, spotting a slow leak before it becomes a remediation project, flagging a turn unit issue before move-in day: that's where a maintenance tech's judgment actually shows up in the NOI. At a company like Morguard that owns and operates its own assets, that kind of attentiveness gets noticed.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates across a portfolio that spans Class A mid-rise and high-rise residential communities, and the Assistant Maintenance Manager role at their Philadelphia property sits at the intersection of hands-on trade work and team leadership. This isn't a pure technician position, but it's also not a desk job. You'll be turning wrenches and directing others who are doing the same.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this role is asset preservation and resident service, working in parallel. On any given day, you might be diagnosing an HVAC issue in a unit, reviewing the make-ready punch list to confirm turns are on schedule for upcoming move-ins, and walking common areas to flag anything that needs attention before a resident notices it. The preventative maintenance program is yours to execute consistently, not just check off, and that discipline is what separates communities that hold their physical value from those that don't.

Service tickets require timely follow-through and clear communication with residents. You'll work alongside the broader maintenance team, so your ability to model standards and motivate people matters as much as your technical skills. The on-call rotation and weekend availability are real commitments here, and candidates who've done emergency maintenance response before will adjust to that rhythm more quickly than those who haven't.

Skills This Role Requires

  • 5 or more years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Demonstrated proficiency in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems, including boilers, chillers, central plant, and split systems
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills for make-ready work
  • Physical capability to frequently handle 25 to 50 pounds of force, climb stairs, use ladders, and work in variable weather
  • Supervisory or leadership experience, even informal, is preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic proficiency with Microsoft Office

Skills This Role Builds

If your background has been primarily technical with limited team oversight, this position develops your supervisory instincts. You'll learn to manage trade priorities across multiple work orders, coordinate make-ready timelines against leasing deadlines, and hold a team accountable to both quality and safety standards. Those skills translate directly to a Maintenance Manager title at a larger property or a more complex asset class. Bozzuto also supports that trajectory through tuition reimbursement and career development programs, which matters if you're working toward a certification or a management credential.

The salary for this position is $62,000, with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant-The Heritage at Leesburg
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles exist at the intersection of sales performance and human connection. At a community like The Heritage at Leesburg, you're often the first real impression a prospect has of what living there would feel like. That first conversation, that tour, that follow-up call carries a lot of weight, and Cortland builds its leasing teams around people who understand that instinctively.

What This Role Actually Involves

Cortland's Leasing and Sales Consultant position is a genuine sales role, with targets, conversion metrics, CRM accountability, and pipeline management built into the daily rhythm. You'll work leads from first contact through signed lease, using consultative techniques rather than pressure to get there. That means listening carefully to what a prospect actually needs, presenting the community in a way that speaks to their situation, and following up consistently without being forgettable.

Beyond the sales mechanics, you'll also carry responsibility for the resident experience side: planning community events, maintaining the property's social media presence, and being the kind of neighbor-facing contact that makes residents want to refer their friends. Objections are part of the job. So is finding a way to work through them without losing the relationship.

Cortland operates as a vertically integrated firm, meaning design, construction, and management all sit under one roof. That structure tends to make decision-making faster and brand standards more consistent, which you'll feel on the ground when coordinating with other departments or escalating a maintenance concern on behalf of a prospect or resident.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least six months of experience in sales, leasing, hospitality, or any role where you were held to performance goals and direct customer interaction
  • Comfort with CRM systems for tracking leads and documenting follow-up activity
  • Genuine ability to build rapport quickly, without it feeling like a technique
  • Coachable. Leasing managers at high-performing communities give real-time feedback, and you'll need to absorb and apply it without defensiveness
  • Strong personal organization, because dropped follow-ups lose leases
  • A presentation style that reflects a premium brand without feeling stiff or scripted

One thing that separates good leasing consultants from great ones in a market like Northern Virginia: local knowledge combined with product confidence. Leesburg has a mix of newer Class A inventory and longer-established communities competing for similar renters. Knowing why The Heritage fits a prospect's specific life stage, commute pattern, or lifestyle priorities, and being able to articulate that crisply, closes more leases than any sales script.

This role tends to be a natural stepping stone toward assistant manager or leasing manager positions, particularly at operators like Cortland that promote from within. Consultants who demonstrate pipeline discipline and CRM accuracy early often move into those roles faster than those who rely on personality alone.

job.title: Dual-Site Assistant Manager - Olympus Gainesville & Olympus Everly
job.description:
It's 9:15 on a Tuesday and a resident is at the front desk frustrated about a charge on their ledger, a leasing tour is waiting in the lobby, and your property manager is at a regional meeting. That's the dual-site assistant manager position in a nutshell, and the people who thrive here don't just manage the interruptions. They move through them.

What This Role Actually Covers

This position supports two sister communities, Olympus Gainesville and Olympus Everly, both located in Gainesville, GA. You'll be the operational anchor when the property manager is unavailable and the first line of support for residents, the leasing team, and daily financial functions. That means collecting and depositing rent daily, maintaining accurate resident files, processing move-out account statements, and inspecting make-ready apartments before residents take possession. When a liability claim surfaces or a legal complaint comes in, you're responsible for getting that information to the right people quickly.

Beyond the back-office work, this role keeps you visible. You'll step in on leasing tours when the team needs coverage, participate in resident retention efforts and community events, and help set the tone for how the office feels to walk into. Olympus asks that the whole team stay warm and accessible with residents, and the assistant manager carries a lot of the responsibility for modeling that standard day to day.

You'll also keep an eye on the surrounding submarket: nearby construction, retail activity, hiring trends, anything that could shift occupancy or affect how the community is positioned. That awareness feeds into how leadership makes decisions about concessions, pricing, and traffic strategy.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Prior onsite experience as an assistant manager or a cross-trained leasing consultant
  • Comfortable with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for the first weekend of each month and occasional after-hours resident events
  • Detail-oriented with money handling. You understand that every dollar received needs to be deposited and recorded the same day
  • Calm when priorities shift fast, which they will

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: comfort with ambiguity at the office level. Dual-site support means you're not always working with the same team dynamic or the same rhythms from one property to the next. The candidates who struggle tend to need more structure than this role offers. The ones who do well are self-directed and don't wait to be told what needs attention.

Olympus Property has ranked as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025). The benefits package includes medical, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, and paid time off. Monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses apply to eligible team members.

job.title: Housekeeper
job.description:
Apartment communities run on first impressions. A prospective resident walking through a clubhouse, a model unit, or a leasing office makes decisions fast, and the cleanliness of those spaces shapes the outcome. The housekeeper role at Weinstein Properties exists to hold that standard every single day.

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company with 70-plus years in the business, managing more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. This opening is at Bexley Left Bank in Fort Worth.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm position. You'll cover common areas, the clubhouse, leasing offices, amenity spaces, and the coffee station on a recurring daily basis. You'll also clean vacant units, prep model homes, and handle freshens to keep those spaces show-ready. Some tasks are unglamorous. All of them matter.

The role intersects regularly with maintenance and leasing teams. You're not operating in isolation. When a unit turns or a prospect is walking in, your work either supports or undercuts what everyone else is doing.

Pay starts at $17/hour. There's a $1,000 stay-on bonus after 90 days in good standing, plus quarterly bonuses. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, rent discount, paid holidays, birthday time off, and vacation and sick time.

Who Does Well in This Role

  • Reliable and punctual. This job has daily recurring tasks; if you're not there, the gaps show.
  • Self-directed. A supervisor won't follow you through each room. You need to see what needs doing and do it.
  • Physically capable. Prolonged standing and walking are part of every shift. Accommodations are available as needed.
  • Detail-oriented. The difference between a clean space and a show-ready space is in the details you catch before anyone else does.
  • Comfortable with repetition. The clubhouse gets cleaned every day. That's the job.

Weinstein emphasizes training and internal development. For the right person, this role is a real starting point inside a stable, long-tenured organization, not a dead end.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Bristol at Sunset
job.description:
Strong leasing consultants carry two skill sets at once: they read people quickly, and they manage details precisely. This role at Bristol at Sunset Apartments in Henderson calls on both. You're converting traffic into signed leases while keeping files accurate, move-ins coordinated, and residents satisfied after they're through the door.

Skills This Role Works Hard

Sales instincts drive the front half of this job. You're greeting prospects, qualifying applicants, guiding tours, and preparing leases. The goal is protecting occupancy, which means you need to close without being pushy and follow up without being forgettable. Customer service skills carry the back half. Once someone signs, you become a point of contact for maintenance coordination, rent questions, and complaints. Residents expect professionalism whether they're picking up keys or reporting a problem three months into their lease.

Administrative accuracy sits underneath all of it. Rental data entry, file management, and monthly paperwork aren't the glamorous parts of leasing, but errors in those areas create downstream problems for the whole property team. Attention to detail here is a real job requirement, not filler language in a posting.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

A typical day might start with follow-up calls to prospects from the day before, then shift into tours with walk-ins. Between those, you're coordinating with maintenance on upcoming move-ins, making sure units are punched out and ready. You're also entering lease data, organizing files, and handling resident interactions that come across the leasing desk. Monthly admin cycles add their own rhythm to the schedule.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of operational depth matters for a leasing role because processes are established, support exists, and there's a real track record of internal promotion. For someone one year into property management looking to move toward an assistant manager or property manager role, the path here is documented, not theoretical.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Henderson's rental market sits in a metro that continues to absorb significant population growth, which means lease-up pressure and traffic volume can be real. Consultants who thrive know how to manage a busy leasing office without letting follow-up fall through. The combination MG Properties is looking for is someone who already carries at least a year of property management experience, works well inside a team structure, and treats professional etiquette as a baseline rather than an add-on.

  • At least one year of property management experience, with leasing exposure preferred
  • Demonstrated sales ability and genuine customer service instincts
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry
  • Ability to coordinate across maintenance and administrative functions
  • Professional communication in every resident and prospect interaction

Compensation includes monthly and quarterly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, paid holidays, and rental discounts. MG Properties is an equal opportunity employer and participates in E-Verify.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a calendar that conventional multifamily doesn't. Turn isn't a scattered, unit-by-unit process here. It's a compressed, all-hands event where hundreds of units flip in a matter of days, and the General Manager at The Flats at West Village owns that process from forecast to punch list. If that kind of organized chaos doesn't appeal to you, this role probably isn't the right fit.

The Flats is a Scion-managed student community in Charlottesville, VA, sitting close to the University of Virginia. The GM role here covers the full scope of property leadership: financial performance, team development, facilities accountability, and the resident experience. You're preparing annual and capital budgets, monitoring NOI, reviewing variance reports, and working through month-end processes while simultaneously keeping an eye on leasing velocity, concessions, and gain-to-lease metrics. The financial and operational sides of this job run in parallel, not in sequence.

On the people side, you're responsible for hiring, scheduling, developing, and retaining a team. That includes being the primary on-call responder when things go sideways after hours. Student housing has a younger resident base and a more transient staff pool than conventional properties, and both of those dynamics require a manager who reads situations quickly and communicates clearly under pressure.

The annual turn process deserves its own mention because it defines the rhythm of student housing management. You'll plan it months out, coordinate with Talent Acquisition for seasonal staffing support, manage vendor bids, track progress through Turnable, conduct move-out inspections, and when it's crunch time, you're expected to pitch in physically. Moving furniture, clearing units, running punch lists alongside your facilities team. This role doesn't sit in an office while turn happens around it.

Scion uses a fairly specific tech stack, and familiarity with Entrata is preferred. You'll also work in Vena for budgeting, Greenhouse for hiring, Lattice for performance management, ADP for payroll and scheduling, and Qualtrics for experience tracking. The platforms aren't optional. They're part of how the company measures and manages performance.

What Scion is looking for:

  • 3 or more years managing a living community with a team of at least three direct reports
  • Demonstrated experience with property management systems, Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication, especially under pressure
  • Vendor management and contract administration experience
  • Comfort with financial reporting, budgeting, and variance analysis
  • Ability to manage confidential employee and resident information appropriately
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Compensation includes a discretionary annual bonus, PTO, full health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, parental and maternal leave, and learning reimbursement. This is an exempt, salaried position.

GMs who thrive in student housing tend to move into regional roles faster than their conventional multifamily counterparts, largely because the operational complexity per door is higher and the exposure to full-cycle management, including capex, intensive turn, and lease-up dynamics, is compressed into a shorter learning window.

job.title: Asset Manager (Foster City)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the center of a 50-property affordable housing portfolio, where your job is to keep each asset financially healthy across its entire useful life. On any given week, you might be reviewing a T-12 against budget benchmarks to flag a property trending toward cash-flow strain, then pivoting to a call with a tax credit investor asking about surplus cash distributions, then sitting down with Property Management to work through a corrective action plan for a site underperforming on operating expense per unit. The work is analytical but it doesn't stay at the desk. Site visits and property condition reviews are part of the job, and you'll need to connect what you see on the ground to what shows up in the financials.

MidPen's portfolio spans 12 Northern California counties and serves working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. The Bay Area affordable housing market operates under dense layers of regulatory agreement, ground lease, and tax credit compliance. An Asset Manager here has to read partnership agreements and HUD regulatory documents fluently, track reserve balances against long-term capital plans, and negotiate with lenders when agreements need amending. You'll also present property performance summaries to the Board Committee, so you need to communicate complex financial situations clearly to a range of audiences.

The cross-functional reach of this role is real. You'll work alongside Accounting, Facilities, Legal, Development, and site staff, and you'll maintain relationships with outside consultants, regulatory agencies, lenders, and investors simultaneously. When a new property transitions into operations, you'll monitor its financial performance against the original proforma through the first full fiscal year and beyond.

What You Bring

  • A bachelor's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Accounting, or a related field
  • At least three years of experience in real estate or finance with a concentration in financial analysis across large portfolios
  • Demonstrated experience in at least four of the following: non-profit affordable housing, debt refinancing, HUD regulatory programs, real estate accounting, financial analysis, property management, or project development
  • Strong Excel skills and the ability to build financial feasibility analyses, strategic plans, and narrative reports
  • Comfort presenting to large groups and to external partners including lenders and investors
  • The capacity to manage a complex portfolio independently with minimal supervision

Context Worth Knowing

Asset management in the affordable housing sector carries a different set of demands than conventional multifamily. Surplus cash distributions are constrained by regulatory agreement, capital projects require lender and investor approval, and proformas are built against compliance requirements that can span decades. What separates strong candidates here isn't just financial modeling ability. It's the judgment to know when a variance is noise versus a signal, and the communication skills to bring lenders, investors, and internal teams to the same understanding at the same time. Experience with LIHTC properties or HUD programs gives candidates a meaningful head start. This position is hybrid, based in Foster City, with in-office days on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Faxon Commons is a residential property in Quincy, MA managed by John M. Corcoran and Company, a firm that's been operating in New England since 1951. This leasing consultant role is a front-line sales and customer service position. You'll be the first person prospective residents meet, and the last touchpoint before they sign.

Day to day, that means touring apartments, walking prospects through pricing and lease terms, processing applications, and putting together lease packages for move-ins. You'll also keep an eye on curb appeal through regular property inspections and stay in contact with current residents throughout their tenancy. On the marketing side, you'll set leasing goals and work toward them through social media, online advertising, and local networking.

The schedule is Tuesday through Saturday, with a 10am to 6pm shift on Wednesdays and 9am to 5pm the rest of the week. That's worth flagging if your availability is Monday-Friday only.

JMC offers a $2,500 sign-on bonus, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off plus holidays, and a 401k with company match. The pay range is $23 to $27.50 per hour depending on experience.

What they're looking for

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable with computers and standard office software
  • Organized, with solid time management habits
  • Customer service experience, ideally in a sales-adjacent role

Candidates who tend to do well in leasing roles bring genuine follow-through. It's easy to give a good tour. The people who hit their occupancy targets are the ones who follow up consistently, track their traffic carefully, and treat every prospect interaction as a managed process rather than a conversation. If you've worked in retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing sales environment, those instincts translate directly here.

This role is also a solid entry point into property management broadly. Leasing consultants who develop fluency in lease administration, resident communication, and marketing frequently move into assistant manager or property manager roles within a few years. JMC's retention history suggests that path is realistic here.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Running a Hillpointe community in Columbus takes a specific mix of skills: financial discipline, people judgment, and the ability to hold a lot of moving parts together without dropping them. This Community Manager role uses all three, most days at the same time.

The Skills This Role Leans On

Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and their communities are designed to feel like a cut above what residents expect at this price point. That means occupancy and NOI targets are taken seriously, but so is the lived experience of people who actually live there. The Community Manager has to hold both of those accountable at once.

On the financial side, you'll manage accounts payable, track budget performance, and work with your Regional Manager to hit and maintain occupancy and rent goals. That means knowing your numbers well enough to spot a delinquency trend early or flag a revenue opportunity before someone else has to point it out. Proficiency in Entrata is preferred because reporting, lease administration, and communication all run through it. If you've used other property management software and you're adaptable, that matters too.

On the operations side, you're the connection point between residents, the facilities maintenance team, and vendors. You'll walk the property regularly, keep amenities at like-new standards, and make sure units are ready for move-in without shortcuts. If a vendor invoice needs to get submitted or a maintenance request is falling through the cracks, that's your problem to solve.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Some days are mostly administrative: reviewing reports, processing payables, following up on lease files. Other days you're outside more than inside, doing property walks, checking punch list items on a turn, or tracking down something that came up during a resident call. You need a valid driver's license because you'll occasionally run bank deposits or attend off-site training, and you'll use a golf cart on property.

The honest part: this role requires availability beyond a standard 9-to-5. You're expected to be reachable by phone or email outside regular hours except during approved time off. That's standard for community managers, but it's worth knowing upfront if you're weighing this against other opportunities.

What Sets Hillpointe Apart for This Role

Hillpointe controls the full development cycle in-house, from land acquisition through construction to asset management. That matters for a community manager because decisions don't have to travel far up a chain. If something at the property level needs attention, the people making those calls are closer than they would be at a larger third-party management operation. For a manager who wants their input to actually count, that's a real distinction.

Strong candidates here combine genuine comfort with property management software and reporting with the ability to hold a team culture together on the ground. The financial acumen matters, but so does the instinct to build a community that residents talk about positively. Both show up in the work every week.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; property management experience preferred
  • Proficiency in Entrata or comparable property management software
  • Comfortable with budgets, financial records, and percentage-based reporting
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Able to lift up to 20 pounds independently and physically access all areas of the property
  • Flexible availability by phone and email outside standard hours

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Woodland Park Apartments)
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles sit at the intersection of sales, hospitality, and community management. They tend to attract people from retail, hotels, or customer service who want a career with more stability and a clearer growth path. At Woodland Park Apartments in Herndon, Van Metre is looking for someone who can handle both sides of that equation: converting traffic into signed leases and keeping current residents happy enough to renew.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A large part of this role is relationship work. You're greeting walk-ins, following up with prospects by phone and email, running tours, and processing applications. You're also checking in with current residents, tracking service requests, and making sure maintenance communication doesn't fall through the cracks. Van Metre expects leasing consultants to do three exterior property inspections per week and to flag vacant unit punch list items so the make-ready process stays on schedule. That's a detail worth noting: this isn't a role where you hand off property concerns to someone else. You're expected to notice and report them yourself.

Beyond the transactional work, you'll help plan resident events and contribute to grassroots marketing efforts to drive traffic. The company also wants someone comfortable with social media as a leasing tool, which reflects where the industry has moved. Bilingual candidates are preferred, a signal that the Herndon market serves a meaningfully diverse renter population.

Weekend availability is required, as it is at almost every leasing office in the country.

Compensation and Career Context

The base pay range is $20 to $22 per hour, with up to $5,000 in annual bonus paid quarterly, plus leasing and renewal commissions. The full benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, and an annual wellness reimbursement of up to $900. Van Metre also offers company-paid certifications, mentoring programs, and stated growth paths.

That last piece matters for anyone thinking beyond the leasing desk. Consultants who build a track record here, particularly around occupancy performance, renewal rates, and resident satisfaction, are well-positioned to move into an Assistant Property Manager role. That transition is where the skills compound: you've already learned how to read a prospect, work a make-ready timeline, and keep delinquency conversations from becoming confrontations. Assistant managers start applying those same skills to the financial side of operations, including NOI, delinquency tracking, and budgeting. The leasing consultant seat, done well, is one of the better on-ramps into full property management.

  • Prior experience in customer service, sales, or hospitality
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfortable working weekends
  • Able to conduct interior and exterior inspections in all weather
  • Bilingual preferred
  • Familiarity with social media as a leasing tool is a plus

Van Metre has operated in the Washington, D.C. area since 1955. For a leasing consultant, that kind of institutional footprint means mentorship and advancement aren't just talking points. The infrastructure to support both is actually there.

job.title: Leasing Specialist - Part-Time
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on traffic cycles that most conventional communities never experience. Move-in weekends, roommate matching deadlines, and fall lease-up pushes compress a year's worth of leasing activity into a few intense months. Redstone Residential, one of the country's largest third-party student housing operators, manages over 38,000 beds across 20 states and is headquartered in Provo, Utah. This part-time Leasing Specialist role at their Orem community sits right at the front lines of that operation.

What the Role Actually Involves

The day-to-day here combines front desk operations, resident service, and leasing support. You'll handle package intake, manage lobby security, field resident questions, and assist the leasing team during tours and application processing. The role pays $18.00 per hour with the opportunity to earn performance bonuses, and includes a 401(k) with up to 6% matching. It's part-time and non-exempt.

Redstone uses Entrata as their property management platform. Familiarity with Entrata or any other PM software is a plus, though not required. What matters more immediately is a calm, organized presence, strong verbal communication, and the ability to represent the community well when a prospect walks through the door or a resident has a problem that needs solving.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

You'll need to arrive with a service mindset already in place. The qualifications that matter most:

  • One to two years of customer service or sales experience
  • Reliable, professional communication habits
  • Composure under pressure (student housing front desks get busy)
  • Basic computer literacy for correspondence and administrative tasks
  • High school diploma or equivalent

What the role builds is different. Working inside a large third-party management operation gives you exposure to how KPIs are tracked at the community level, how leasing teams coordinate during high-traffic periods, and how a national operator standardizes performance across a large portfolio. Those are transferable skills. Leasing Specialists who develop fluency in traffic reporting, conversion rates, and application workflow often move into full Leasing Manager roles, particularly at operators like Redstone that are actively growing their conventional housing footprint alongside student housing.

One honest note: student housing communities see concentrated stress during lease-up and move-in periods. If you've only worked in low-volume service environments, that intensity takes adjustment. The candidates who do well here tend to stay organized under volume, communicate proactively, and genuinely like working with people, even when those people are stressed about move-in logistics.

job.title: Community Manager - Roving - Northern Nevada Region
job.description:
Roving community manager roles exist because portfolios have gaps. A site manager takes leave, a lease-up needs temporary reinforcement, a struggling property needs experienced eyes on the ground. CloudTen Residential's northern Nevada region has that need across three Carson City assets: The Creek at South Carson, Fifth Street Townhomes, and Fifth Street Pointe. This position covers all three, shifting presence based on where operational weight is greatest at any given time.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On any given week, you might be auditing delinquency at one property, running a staff huddle at another, and doing move-out inspections at a third. The core job is full community management, just spread across multiple locations rather than anchored to one address. That means rent collection, managing delinquent accounts inside landlord-tenant law, budget oversight, leasing activity, make-ready coordination, and resident relations, all running simultaneously across sites. You'll also hire and evaluate on-site staff at properties you're covering, which requires the ability to build credibility quickly with teams you didn't originally train.

CloudTen's portfolio spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning, so the company isn't a single-asset operator with a fixed playbook. Their Carson City sites benefit from that institutional range, and the person in this role should be comfortable applying it across different property types and community profiles.

Pay runs $25.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on experience. A valid driver's license is required since the position moves between sites regularly.

Qualifications and What Separates Strong Candidates

  • Minimum two years of property management experience, or an equivalent combination of education and direct experience
  • Working knowledge of Nevada landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing, and ADA requirements
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and at least one property management software platform
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree is preferred
  • Strong accounting fundamentals: rent rolls, delinquency tracking, budget prep, daily deposits

The candidates who perform best in roving roles tend to have one specific skill that standard community managers can go without: the ability to read a team's operational state within the first few hours on a property. Roving managers don't have weeks to observe before acting. They need to spot what's slipping on a punch list, where delinquency is creeping past acceptable thresholds, and which staff need immediate direction versus space to work. Self-sufficiency matters here more than in a fixed-site role because regional manager check-ins are less frequent when you're the one keeping multiple properties stable at once.

CloudTen offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays. The company describes its culture around direct support for professional growth, which in a portfolio still expanding across the West means genuine movement into regional or senior property leadership for the right person.

job.title: Property Manager at Cason Estates Apartments
job.description:
What This Role Actually Runs On

The core skill set here isn't just operational. It's relational intelligence combined with financial fluency, and knowing when to use each. The Property Manager at Cason Estates in Murfreesboro, Tennessee handles the full picture of a multifamily community: team leadership, leasing performance, resident experience, budget management, and vendor coordination. That's a lot of plates. The managers who do it well aren't just organized. They read people accurately, whether that's a leasing consultant who needs coaching, a vendor who's behind schedule, or a resident who's one bad interaction away from not renewing.

Cottonwood Residential operates a nationally growing portfolio with integrated asset and property management, so this isn't a siloed site role. You'll interact with a Regional Manager on budget planning and financial reporting, and your decisions about delinquency, concessions, and expense approvals connect directly to the asset's NOI. That means your financial acumen gets used daily, not just at month-end.

The Daily Work, Concretely

A typical week pulls you in several directions at once. You might start the morning reviewing T-3 traffic and occupancy numbers, adjust a marketing approach with your leasing team, then spend time in the field doing property inspections or walking make-ready units before they go to self-guided tour rotation. Delinquency follow-up doesn't wait, and neither do vendor coordination calls when a repair is running long. By afternoon you're back at a desk reviewing invoices for proper coding or responding to a resident escalation that your team needs backup on.

Cottonwood uses Entrata, so familiarity with that platform (or similar property management software) will help you get up to speed faster. The self-guided tour operation here adds a layer that some managers haven't dealt with before. Unit readiness and signage need daily attention to keep that channel working properly.

Who Fits This Role and Who Struggles

Three or more years of multifamily property management experience is required, and Cottonwood has set that bar deliberately. This community needs someone who already knows how to run a team, build a budget, and handle a difficult resident conversation without losing composure. A CAM, ARM, or CCRM designation signals that you've invested in the profession, which Cottonwood values.

The managers who thrive here tend to be people who genuinely like developing their teams. Coaching a leasing consultant through a difficult close, or helping a maintenance tech prioritize a punch list, is part of the job. If you're someone who finds management overhead draining and prefers to work alone, this role will wear on you. The team dynamic is real and it matters.

  • 3+ years as a multifamily Property Manager (required)
  • High school diploma or GED (required); college degree preferred
  • CAM, ARM, or CCRM designation preferred
  • Demonstrated experience with budgeting, delinquency management, and financial reporting
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Entrata or comparable system experience a plus
  • Ability to work flexible hours and regularly walk, inspect, and physically engage with the property

Murfreesboro's multifamily market has grown considerably over the past several years as the broader Nashville metro has expanded eastward. Occupancy expectations are high and competition between communities is real, which means your market survey work and pricing awareness directly affect leasing outcomes. Managers who bring sharp competitive instincts to rent positioning tend to make a measurable difference here.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM and the first work orders are already stacking up. A unit turn is half-finished, two HVAC calls came in overnight, and the shop needs a restock before the morning really gets going. The Assistant Maintenance Supervisor is the person who makes sure none of that becomes a crisis.

The Role at Skyline Towers

Berkshire Residential Investments operates as both owner and manager across its portfolio, which means accountability runs deep. At Skyline Towers, the Assistant Maintenance Supervisor works directly alongside the Maintenance Supervisor to keep the physical asset performing at a high standard. That means coordinating make-ready repairs and services, tracking work order volume and quality, and stepping in hands-on with technicians when deadlines are tight.

Daily scheduling is a real part of this job. You'll help the Maintenance Supervisor sequence the day's work so technicians aren't doubling back across the property or waiting on parts. Tour routes and models get a critical eye before prospects ever walk through. Shop organization, equipment condition, supply inventory, and key security all fall within your scope. When a repair crosses into major-expenditure territory, you flag it to both the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager before anything is authorized.

Safety enforcement is non-negotiable here. Berkshire holds its maintenance teams to consistent standards, and the Assistant Supervisor is the person reinforcing those standards at the ground level, both for residents interacting with the team and for technicians working on-site every day.

What Berkshire Expects You to Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on experience across core maintenance disciplines
  • Comfort with property management technology and a track record of adapting to new systems
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • Proficiency with computers and related applications used in day-to-day property operations
  • The physical ability to meet the demands of a full maintenance workload
  • A genuine willingness to mentor and coach the technicians around you

The base hourly range for this position is $32.65 to $37.69, which puts the annual equivalent between approximately $67,900 and $78,300. Berkshire also offers retirement benefits, health coverage, paid time off including parental leave, bonuses, and a 25% rent discount for employees living on-site.

One thing worth knowing: this role tends to build the specific skill set that leads to Maintenance Supervisor positions. If you're already solid technically but haven't had formal supervisory experience, the Assistant Supervisor seat is where most operators develop the scheduling, vendor coordination, and team accountability habits that full supervision requires. At a company that manages its own assets, internal promotion into Maintenance Supervisor and eventually Director of Facilities roles is a realistic path for someone who performs here.

job.title: Temp Turns Help
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a temporary, part-time position supporting unit turns and general property upkeep at a Redstone Residential property in Chicago. The work shifts based on what the property needs that day: cleaning units, running trash, checking make-ready punch lists, assisting the maintenance crew with turnovers, groundskeeping, or driving company vehicles or equipment if you're licensed. You take direction from supervisors, work through the task list, and move on to the next one. Some days you'll work solo; other days you're part of a crew.

The pace during turns is real. Student housing turn seasons are compressed, high-volume pushes where every unit needs to be cleaned, inspected, and ready on a tight schedule. You'll be on your feet, lifting, bending, and moving through units all day. That's the job.

Pay is $17.50 per hour.

What You Bring

  • Reliability. Show up on time, complete the work, communicate if something's wrong.
  • Physical stamina for a full shift of hands-on labor.
  • Ability to follow instructions and shift tasks without friction.
  • Prior experience in cleaning, groundskeeping, or maintenance is a plus, but not required.
  • Valid driver's license if you're assigned to a driving role.
  • Comfortable working independently or alongside a team depending on the day's needs.

Context Worth Knowing

Redstone Residential manages over 38,000 beds across 20 states and operates as one of the larger third-party student housing managers in the country. Temp turns help is a real operational need, not a filler role. Properties depend on this support to get units turned on time. If you're dependable and show up ready to work, you'll stand out quickly. For people looking to break into property maintenance or just want steady part-time work during peak season, this is a straightforward way in.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - The Warwick
job.description:
The Warwick is a Sunrise Management community in San Diego, and this Maintenance Technician role is the kind of position where the work is visible every single day. Curb appeal, unit condition, common area cleanliness, turn times , residents notice all of it, and so does the bottom line.

The core of the job is keeping units rent-ready and service requests closed fast. Sunrise holds a 24-hour resolution standard on resident work orders, and the expectation on turns is 3 to 5 days from vacancy to rent-ready. That turnaround pace matters for occupancy, and someone who treats a punch list as a checklist to finish rather than a suggestion to work through will fit here. You'll handle the full range of general maintenance: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, painting, pool care, and custodial work across common areas including the leasing office, laundry rooms, and recreation spaces.

Beyond reactive repairs, there's a structured preventive maintenance program to stay on top of , monthly PM directives covering lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety checks. You'll track inventory, maintain MSDS records for on-site chemicals, and know where every shutoff and cleanout is located. On-call emergency coverage is part of the schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Pay runs $27 to $30 per hour depending on experience, and this position is bonus-eligible at The Warwick. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, company-paid life insurance, FSA access, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

What the role requires

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • At least 2 years working within property management, with familiarity in software platforms like Entrata, Yardi, or Onesite
  • Comfortable using a mobile device for work order management and documentation
  • Strong time management and the ability to prioritize across multiple open requests independently
  • Customer-facing composure, including handling difficult situations professionally
  • Availability for a flexible schedule with on-call emergency response

One thing worth noting for anyone coming from construction or commercial maintenance: multifamily is a resident-facing environment. How you interact with people while you're working in or around their home matters as much as how well you do the technical work. The best techs in this business treat both with equal care. That combination , solid trade skills and genuine professionalism with residents , is what tends to build a career path toward Maintenance Supervisor and beyond.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Dream Marine Creek sits at 5222 Shadydell Drive in Fort Worth, a property that sits within the broader DLP Capital portfolio. DLP operates at real scale , 14 consecutive years on the Inc. 5000 fastest-growing private companies list , and Dream Live Prosper Communities is where that growth touches the ground. This Community Manager role carries more weight than the title suggests.

The position covers the full operational picture: occupancy management with a 95% target, leasing activity tracking, application approvals, renewals, security deposit dispositions, inspections, and court appearances when notices escalate that far. You're also running a leasing team , onboarding and mentoring agents, hosting monthly meetings, reviewing leads and follow-up quality, and submitting commissions on time. If you've managed a property where the leasing office and the operations side were siloed, that won't fly here. The expectation is that you hold both.

Senior leadership visibility is real in this role. You'll review upcoming properties and renewal strategy with the General Manager, and you'll produce weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance data that actually gets read. That means your numbers need to be clean, your delinquency story needs to make sense, and your occupancy trends need context , not just figures dropped into a report.

What the right candidate brings

  • Multiple years of multifamily property management experience, not just leasing
  • At least 3 years managing direct reports with documented performance outcomes
  • Comfort reading and working from income statements and financial data
  • Experience leading through operational changes or on-site project transitions
  • Familiarity with Appfolio is a plus; G Suite and Microsoft Office are baseline expectations
  • Availability for a flexible schedule that includes weekends

One thing worth calling out for candidates coming from Class A lease-up environments: this role touches single-family coordination in addition to multifamily operations. You'll communicate with single-family teams and assist with cross-portfolio inspections. The scope is wider than a standard garden-style community manager position, and the candidates who thrive here tend to be the ones who can shift context quickly without losing operational discipline on their own site.

DLP leans heavily on its internal execution framework and core values , this is a culture-forward organization, and they're transparent about it. If that kind of environment suits you, the upside is real mentorship structure and a company that promotes from within. If you're the type who prefers to operate independently with minimal alignment requirements, that's worth knowing before you apply.

Benefits include PTO, health, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) matching, educational incentives, volunteer time off, and well-being programs.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 11 PM and a resident's water heater has failed. You're the one who shows up. That's the job, plainly stated, and it matters that you go in knowing it.

Griffis Residential operates a portfolio of luxury apartment communities and is hiring a Maintenance Technician in Denver to work alongside a Service Manager keeping properties running at a high standard. The work covers the full range of building systems: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry. Make-readies are a consistent part of the rhythm here. When a unit turns, you're the one getting it back to move-in condition, which means working through punch lists with accuracy and speed. Beyond turns, you'll carry a portion of the daily service request load, respond to emergency calls within a 30-minute window, and participate in preventative maintenance schedules and community inspections. Pool and spa upkeep is part of the role, including chemical balancing and documentation. You'll also handle the basics that make a property look cared for: litter pickup, snow and ice removal, and common area cleanliness.

What the Role Actually Requires

A year of hands-on maintenance experience in multi-family housing, hospitality, or a comparable setting is the starting point. You should already have a solid working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliances. A CPO license and EPA certification are preferred at hire and required within your first six months. Physical demands are real: lifting up to 75 pounds, working in Colorado's weather year-round, and staying on your feet for most of your shift. Proficiency in English is required; Spanish is a genuine asset in Denver's residential market. Basic computer skills and comfort with work order systems will serve you well. Bilingual candidates stand out here because resident communication is part of the job, not an afterthought.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range runs from $25.00 to $27.50 per hour. Benefits are substantive. Full-time associates receive:

  • 50% rental discount on a Griffis community
  • Quarterly bonuses up to $2,000 annually, plus occupancy and retention bonus programs
  • 11 paid holidays including floating days
  • 120 hours of PTO accrual starting immediately
  • 401(k) with up to 4% company match
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Company-paid short and long-term disability and basic life insurance
  • Up to 6 weeks paid parental leave for primary caregivers
  • Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year
  • Employee assistance program, wellness reimbursements, and a volunteer time off policy

One thing worth noting for anyone coming from hospitality or hotel maintenance: Griffis specifically points out that the schedule here offers more predictability than those industries typically allow. That's a real distinction if you've been grinding through irregular shifts in that world.

Strong candidates bring more than technical competence. The ones who stick and grow in this kind of role stay calm under pressure, communicate clearly with residents who are frustrated, and treat documentation as seriously as the repair itself. The service request log and your maintenance records are part of the property's operating record. How you handle both reflects directly on community performance.

job.title: Grounds Specialist - Jacksonville, FL ~ Tropia
job.description:
Hands, Eyes, and Hustle: What This Role Actually Demands

A Grounds Specialist position lives or dies on two things: sharp eyes and good habits. You're walking this property multiple times a day, and the difference between a community that looks sharp at 9 AM and one that looks sharp at 5 PM is usually someone who notices things and handles them before anyone has to ask. That's the skill set Davis Development is after for Tropia in Jacksonville.

The physical demands are real. You're picking up litter, debris, and pet waste across breezeways, pool areas, common spaces, and anywhere else residents and their dogs roam. Trash and recycling areas get maintained on a set schedule. You'll check and log pool chemical levels daily and vacuum the pool weekly. Grill stations need regular cleaning and safety checks on timers and knobs. General labor tasks fill in the rest of the day, supporting the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager as needs arise. If you've got a CPO certification, that's a genuine differentiator here given the pool monitoring responsibilities.

What You're Bringing to the Property

  • At least one year of general labor experience; multifamily exposure is a plus but not required
  • Comfortable with hand tools, cleaning equipment, and the supplies that come with the territory
  • Able to lift approximately 50 pounds and work beyond 40 hours when the property needs it
  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • CPO certification preferred
  • Time management matters here as much as physical capability. The property doesn't supervise itself between rounds.

One honest note on the role: grounds work in a Florida summer is exactly what it sounds like. Heat, humidity, and outdoor exposure are daily realities. If you're someone who takes pride in a clean, well-kept community regardless of weather, this fits. If you need air conditioning to stay motivated, it probably doesn't.

Working at Davis Development

Davis is a privately held luxury developer and operator with over 25 years in the business. Their model is in-house management, meaning the people running the property are Davis employees, not a third-party shop trying to hit fee margins. On-site teams are expected to operate like owner-operators, which tends to create a noticeably different culture than what you find at large institutional managers. For grounds and maintenance staff, that usually translates to clearer communication and less bureaucratic friction when you need something done.

Benefits include health coverage starting the first of the month after 30 days, a 401(k) with a 4% employer match that vests immediately, company-paid life insurance, PTO with a carryover provision, and training and career development opportunities. For a grounds-level position, the immediate vesting on the 401(k) match is worth paying attention to.

This kind of role is also a reasonable entry point into property maintenance more broadly. Grounds specialists who build familiarity with the property and show mechanical aptitude often transition into make-ready or general maintenance technician roles over time, particularly at companies like Davis that promote from within.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Avanath operates affordable and workforce housing communities, and this Community Manager role at their South Gate property sits at the intersection of compliance, resident services, and day-to-day operations. If you've managed a LIHTC property before, you already know the job is heavier than a conventional community manager position. That's the baseline here.

What the Job Actually Covers

You run the site. That means owning the financial picture, keeping occupancy where it needs to be, pushing delinquency toward zero, and working with the Regional Manager to build and hit the annual operating budget. You'll handle rent rolls, monthly financials, and subsidy voucher submissions when applicable. On the capital side, you'll coordinate across departments when larger projects come through.

Resident relations are a core part of the work, not a secondary function. Avanath structures their communities around resident well-being, so you'll organize retention programs and events, respond to complaints quickly, and connect residents with outside services and agencies when their needs go beyond what the property can provide. You'll maintain confidential resident files and serve as a point of contact across the full resident lifecycle, move-in through move-out.

Staff leadership is the third leg. You'll set performance expectations, run scheduling, give feedback regularly, and manage underperformers with clear documentation. The expectation is that your team reflects your standards, so if curb appeal is slipping or maintenance response is slow, that's on you to correct.

What Avanath Is Looking For

  • 5 to 7 years in property management, with at least 2 years in a community or property manager seat
  • Solid working knowledge of LIHTC and Tax Credit compliance requirements (this is non-negotiable)
  • Demonstrated ability to de-escalate resident concerns before they become formal complaints or violations
  • Comfortable producing financial reports and working within budget constraints
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including interactions with senior leadership
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools

A Note on This Type of Role

Affordable housing management, especially under the Tax Credit program, carries compliance responsibilities that conventional managers don't deal with. Recertifications, income qualification reviews, and regulatory reporting are part of the job calendar. Managers who come from Class A conventional backgrounds sometimes underestimate this layer. If you've worked affordable or mixed-income properties before, that experience will transfer directly and make you more effective from day one.

This role also offers a clear path for growth. Community Managers at mission-driven affordable housing companies often move into Regional Manager or Director of Operations roles as portfolios expand. Avanath has been actively growing its footprint, so internal mobility is a realistic outcome for strong performers.

job.title: Concierge
job.description:
It's 11:30 PM and a resident needs a package pulled from the mailroom, a guest is waiting at the lobby entrance, and your incident log from the evening walkthrough still needs to be filed. That's a normal Tuesday.

Rise Association Management Group manages homeowners' associations across Texas, with a focus on communities that have real amenity and infrastructure complexity. This Concierge position sits at the front desk of a luxury high-rise condominium in the 77004 zip code, covering either the afternoon-to-midnight shift or the overnight shift (midnight to 8 AM), Monday through Friday. Neither shift is glamorous on paper, but both matter more than most people realize. The overnight desk, in particular, requires someone who stays sharp without supervision and handles the unexpected without escalating everything to a supervisor.

What the Role Covers

This is a front-of-house operations role with real responsibility. You'll manage access control, visitor logs, and security monitoring as a matter of daily routine. Package handling, amenity reservations, and resident requests cycle through every shift. You'll walk the property, document what you find, and flag maintenance or housekeeping needs through the right channels. Incident reports need to be accurate and timely. Resident concerns that come through you need to actually get resolved, which means you coordinate with leadership rather than just logging and forgetting.

  • Greet and assist residents and guests with consistent professionalism
  • Manage front desk operations: access control, visitor management, security monitoring
  • Process mail and packages, coordinate reservations, respond to resident requests
  • Conduct property walkthroughs and report maintenance or housekeeping needs
  • Complete shift reports, incident documentation, and administrative tasks
  • Work with leadership to follow through on resident concerns

What You Bring

A high school diploma is required. A background in hospitality or business is a plus, but what matters more is at least a year of experience in a luxury hospitality or upscale residential setting where your standards were held to something higher than average. You communicate clearly in writing and in person. You manage competing priorities without getting flustered. You can lift 30 to 50 pounds when the job calls for it, and you're comfortable on your feet or at a desk for an extended shift. Proficiency in Microsoft Office is expected.

One thing that separates strong candidates from average ones in a role like this: consistency across the whole shift, not just the first hour. High-rise concierge work has a rhythm, and the residents notice when someone cuts corners at 6 AM because they think no one's watching. If you've worked a hotel front desk, you already understand that dynamic. Pay is $16 to $17 per hour depending on experience.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Bigos Management has earned a Star Tribune Top Workplace designation twelve times, which says something about how they treat the people who keep their communities running. This Leasing Consultant role sits at The Cosmopolitan, a 258-unit property in Saint Paul, and covers the full leasing cycle from first phone call to move-in day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your week runs Tuesday through Saturday. Most days start with incoming inquiries, followed by tours, follow-up calls with prospects who haven't committed yet, and paperwork for new move-ins. You'll qualify prospects using company procedures, walk them through lease terms and community rules, and handle move-in inspections. When residents are approaching renewal, you're in that conversation too.

Between guest activity, you'll check vacant units and handle light cleaning to keep them show-ready. It's a mix of sales, service, and operations. No single task dominates the whole day.

You'll also track local competition using public sources like competitor websites, which helps you speak to prospects with confidence about what Bigos offers relative to other options in the area.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • One to two years of customer service or sales experience
  • Prior leasing experience is a plus, but not required
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic comfort with email and web-based tools
  • No active real estate license (company requirement for this role)
  • Ability to walk the property, climb stairs, and lift up to 10 pounds

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly range is $17 to $22, with leasing commissions and renewal bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits start the first of the month after hire and include medical with HSA employer contributions, 401(k) with employer match, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, generous PTO with rollover, life insurance, short and long-term disability, an employee assistance program, educational assistance, rent discount, and a Life Time Fitness membership discount.

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The best leasing consultants treat follow-up as a core skill, not an afterthought. A prospect who tours and doesn't sign right away often converts through a well-timed, genuine follow-up call. If you've worked in a sales or service role where you kept a mental (or actual) list of pending conversations and acted on them consistently, that habit transfers directly here. Leasing experience helps, but persistence and people skills carry more weight than a resume line.

This role also builds a foundation that leads naturally into Assistant Property Manager positions for those who want to move into full-cycle operations over time.

job.title: Front Desk Associate (Full Time)- Perla on Broadway
job.description:
It's 9 p.m. on a Saturday and a package locker is jammed, two homeowners are waiting at the desk, and someone's guest just buzzed the wrong unit three times. That's not a hypothetical. That's Thursday through Monday at a luxury high-rise in Downtown Los Angeles.

Action Property Management is hiring a full-time Front Desk Associate for Perla on Broadway, a luxury HOA in DTLA. The schedule runs Thursday through Monday, 2:30 p.m. to 11:00 p.m., and the pay range is $20.00 to $22.00 per hour. If you've worked a hotel front desk or a fine dining host stand, the rhythm of this role will feel familiar. If you haven't, you'll need at least a year of customer-facing experience and a track record of staying composed when things stack up.

What the Role Actually Involves

The core of this job is the lobby. You're the first and last person residents and guests interact with, and in a luxury HOA, that matters more than most people expect.
