Homeowners paid a premium to live here, and their tolerance for a cold greeting or a lost package is low. Beyond front desk coverage, you'll handle package intake and distribution, monitor lobby access and elevator activity, enforce community policies consistently and professionally, and keep residents informed about community updates via email. You'll field inquiries and complaints directly, which means you need solid judgment and the ability to de-escalate without making it weird.

This is an evening shift, which carries its own texture. Management isn't on-site. You're the responsible party in the building, which means you're making real decisions in real time.

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year of customer service experience in a professional setting
  • Strong telephone etiquette and written communication skills, including email
  • Basic administrative and clerical competency, including Microsoft Office; minimum 30 WPM typing
  • A polished, professional presentation appropriate for a luxury residential environment
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment background check and drug screening; must be 18 or older
  • Experience in hospitality, luxury retail, or fine dining is a genuine advantage here, not just a checkbox

Action Property Management has managed HOA communities since 1984 and operates across nine offices in the West. They offer medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, life and disability coverage, pet insurance, a year-end bonus, ten days of vacation, and a few perks you don't see everywhere, including a birthday holiday and an employee discount program through LifeMart.

One honest note about where this role leads: front desk work at a well-run luxury HOA gives you direct exposure to community operations, vendor coordination, resident relations, and policy enforcement. Associates who pay attention to how the building runs tend to move into assistant community manager roles within a couple of years. The evening shift compresses your learning curve because you're handling things independently from day one.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What the Day Actually Looks Like

This role sits at the operational center of a manufactured home community in Apache Junction. You're supporting the Community Manager on collections, delinquency follow-up, leasing activity, and work order coordination. You're also the person residents reach first when something needs attention. That means your communication skills and your ability to stay organized under pressure get tested daily, in ways that build fast.

Havenpark Communities operates more than 100 manufactured home communities across the country, and they're acquiring more. That scale matters for your career because it creates genuine upward mobility. Assistant Community Managers who perform here tend to move into Community Manager roles as new properties come online. If you've been trying to break into fee management or multi-site oversight, the groundwork starts at this level.

What You Bring

  • Experience in property management, leasing, or a resident-facing operations role
  • Comfort handling collections conversations and following up on delinquency with professionalism
  • Strong organizational habits, especially for tracking work orders and open items
  • A collaborative approach. You'll work closely with the Community Manager, not around them
  • Willingness to travel occasionally on a semi-annual or annual basis as the role requires

Why This Role Compounds

Manufactured housing is one of the more misunderstood segments of residential property management, and that's actually an advantage for someone early in their career. The skills you build here, specifically occupancy management, collections discipline, resident relations in a close-knit community setting, and operational follow-through, transfer directly into conventional multifamily, single-family rental, or even third-party management. You learn the fundamentals without the noise of a large multifamily lease-up, which means you get real reps, real fast.

Havenpark's stated culture centers on respect, collaboration, and what they call stewardship, which in practice means caring about how the community feels to the people living in it. If you're someone who finds satisfaction in keeping operations tight and genuinely connecting with residents, this role gives you a place to do both while building a career path with room to grow.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
Apartment maintenance work rewards people who think across trades rather than within one. At 3300 Tamarac, a Denver community managed by MG Properties, that's exactly the kind of thinking the role demands. You'll move through plumbing calls, electrical troubleshooting, appliance repairs, HVAC work, and painting within a single week, sometimes a single day. The property expects genuine multi-trade fluency, not surface familiarity with any one discipline.

MG Properties has spent over three decades acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. That operational depth shows in how they structure their maintenance teams. Technicians here handle the full range of day-to-day service requests alongside grounds and common area upkeep, unit turns, and on-call rotations for after-hours emergencies. Turn work in particular is worth understanding before you apply: completing make-ready units on schedule is one of the cleaner ways to demonstrate your pace and trade range to a maintenance supervisor, and it matters to occupancy in ways that daily service calls don't always reveal.

The customer service expectation here carries real weight. Residents interact with maintenance staff more directly than almost anyone else on a property team, and how a technician handles a frustrated resident during a service call shapes the community's reputation as much as the repair itself. Reliable transportation and availability for on-call rotation are firm requirements, not preferences.

What the role requires

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general appliance repair
  • Comfort with painting, unit turnovers, and grounds and common area upkeep
  • A customer-first approach and the ability to work within a team structure
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Availability for on-call rotation

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to self-diagnose problems accurately before grabbing parts or calling a vendor. That diagnostic habit, more than speed alone, is what separates technicians who build real credibility with their teams from those who get by. If you've worked a 200-plus unit community before, you've likely developed that instinct out of necessity.

Compensation runs $24 to $25 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing added on top. MG Properties also offers a 401(k) with employer match, full medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, PTO, sick time, and rental discounts. This position is anticipated to close in November 2026.

job.title: Administrative Clerk (Paseo Estero)
job.description:
Front desk roles at affordable housing communities carry more weight than the title suggests. At a property like Paseo Estero, the administrative clerk is often the first and most consistent point of contact for residents, applicants, and outside visitors. That daily presence shapes how the community feels to the people who live there.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Under the direction of the Community Manager, you'll manage the flow of people and information through the building. That means greeting and screening visitors, keeping the daily log and visitor records current, answering phones and routing calls correctly, and making sure incident reports get written clearly and completely when something happens. You'll also monitor the video camera system, maintain the lobby and entrance area, distribute and post resident notices, and complete work orders as they come in.

The pace varies. Some days are steady and routine. Others, particularly around lease renewals, maintenance surges, or resident concerns, require you to handle several things at once while staying calm and professional. Fair Housing compliance applies to every resident and applicant interaction you have, so familiarity with those principles matters from day one.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

You'll need a high school diploma or GED and at least a year of receptionist or administrative experience coming in. Clear written and verbal communication is a real requirement here, since you'll be producing logs, incident reports, and correspondence that become part of the property record. Comfort with Microsoft Word and Excel is helpful. Flexibility is essential because the tasks shift with the day.

What the role builds is different. Clerks who pay attention at a managed affordable housing property pick up operational instincts that transfer directly to leasing coordinator or assistant manager positions. You learn how a property runs: how traffic patterns signal occupancy trends, how documentation protects both residents and management, and how community policies actually get enforced at the ground level. Those are skills that experienced property managers recognize immediately.

The Organization Behind the Property

MidPen Housing has operated in Northern California since 1970 and currently manages more than 142 properties across 12 counties, housing over 22,000 residents. Their model combines affordable housing development with professional property management and onsite resident support programs. That structure means the administrative staff at properties like Paseo Estero work within a larger system that takes documentation, compliance, and resident stability seriously. If you're early in a property management career and want to learn from an organization with real operational depth, this is a credible place to start.

  • Pay range: $17.69 to $19.90 per hour, based on experience
  • Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance
  • 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, and an EAP program
  • Employee education reimbursement available
  • Paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days

job.title: Maintenance Technician III (Shadowbrook, Heatherstone, & Parallel)
job.description:
A work order comes in at 7 a.m.: a unit at Shadowbrook has a water heater issue, there's a turn in progress at Heatherstone, and two minor electrical tickets are waiting across the portfolio. You triage, assign, and get moving. That's the rhythm here.

What the Role Actually Covers

Prometheus is looking for a Maintenance Technician III to support three Bay Area properties: Shadowbrook, Heatherstone, and Parallel, all in Sunnyvale. This is a lead-level position. You're doing hands-on work and guiding a team at the same time.

Day to day, you handle the full range of apartment maintenance: plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repairs, painting. You manage unit turns from start to finish, keeping make-ready timelines on track. You also coordinate with outside vendors, track maintenance-related costs against budget, and process work orders through Yardi. Administrative tasks come with the territory.

The leadership piece is real. You'll mentor junior techs, set the standard for quality and response time, and help the properties hit their financial targets by managing costs and avoiding unnecessary vendor spend. One year of supervisory experience is the floor; two or more is preferred.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • Three to four years of apartment maintenance experience, with solid skills in plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance work
  • Minimum three certificates from recognized maintenance programs (BOMA, IREM, or vocational equivalents)
  • Comfortable with Yardi or similar work order platforms
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Available for on-call rotation and weekend coverage
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. and work in both indoor and outdoor conditions

Compensation runs $35.75 to $37.00 per hour, depending on experience. Prometheus adds standby pay and on-call premium pay on top of that base. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision (dependents included), 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays including your birthday, and tenure-based housing discounts. There's also a referral bonus, renovation bonus, and lease-up bonus structure for eligible work.

One thing worth knowing about this market: Sunnyvale's apartment stock includes a mix of older garden-style communities and more recently renovated product. A tech who can read a property's maintenance history, anticipate recurring issues, and manage vendor relationships without over-relying on outside spend will move faster here than someone who needs close direction on every call. Prometheus is a long-term holder with consistent reinvestment in its properties, so quality of work matters more than quick fixes.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles at mid-size regional operators like Hawthorne tend to carry more community ownership than you'd see at a large institutional shop. The consultant here isn't just turning leads. They're expected to hold the culture of the property, which at Braxton at Woods Lake means handling everything from tours and applications to resident events and social media presence.

What the Role Actually Covers

Day-to-day, you're the first point of contact for prospective residents: answering phones and web inquiries, conducting personalized tours, following up on leads, and walking applicants through the paperwork from application to move-in. That's the core of the job. Alongside the leasing cycle, you're coordinating resident engagement events, keeping common areas presentable, and monitoring competitor properties and local market activity. Hawthorne calls this position a Leasing and Live It Specialist, which signals that the culture piece is taken seriously, not just printed on a poster.

The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4. You'll get one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends come up for community events, so flexibility matters.

Who Does Well Here

  • Confident communicators who can close a conversation in person, by phone, or in writing
  • People who can hear an objection on a tour and respond without getting flustered
  • Anyone with a customer service or sales background comfortable in a commission-eligible role
  • Someone who actually enjoys talking to people, not just tolerates it

A CALP designation is a plus, but Hawthorne doesn't require prior leasing experience. One year in customer service or sales is the baseline. What separates the strong candidates from average ones in a role like this is follow-up discipline. Traffic alone won't hit occupancy goals. The consultants who consistently convert are the ones managing their lead pipeline like it's a job within the job, because it is.

Compensation and Career Path

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions. Hawthorne also runs leasing incentive programs on top of that structure. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday, which is a small thing but a real one), pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave options.

The growth path here is a real one. Leasing consultant to assistant community manager is the standard track in this industry, and Hawthorne has a formal career path program to support that move. If you've been in retail or hospitality and are looking for a landing spot in multifamily, this is a reasonable entry point with a clear next step.

job.title: Leasing Consultant/Recertification Specialist (Part Time)
job.description:
It's Saturday morning, and while most of the office is quiet, you're the one unlocking the leasing center at The Chocolate Factory, walking a prospective resident through the floor plan, and then pivoting to a stack of recertification files that need to go out by end of week. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work Itself

John M. Corcoran and Company, a New England firm operating since 1951, is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant and Recertification Specialist for their Mansfield, MA property. The position runs 20 hours per week, with Saturday (9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) as the fixed day and flexibility built into the remaining hours.

The leasing side of the job covers what you'd expect: showing units, walking prospects through pricing and lease terms, processing applications, preparing lease packages, and coordinating move-ins. But the recertification piece is what makes this role distinct. You'll schedule and conduct tenant recertification interviews, collect and verify documentation, coordinate apartment inspections, and keep resident files accurate and compliant with affordable housing regulations. Waitlist management and applicant processing fall in here too.

Beyond those two tracks, you'll support general property administration: rent collection, maintenance request intake, phone coverage, and occasional marketing tasks like social media updates or website edits.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • At least two years of administrative or customer service experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Solid organizational habits and genuine attention to detail (recertification compliance doesn't forgive sloppy files)
  • Comfort with computers and property management technology
  • Working knowledge of affordable housing regulations is preferred, though not strictly required

The pay range runs $23 to $31 per hour depending on experience, and JMC includes a $1,500 sign-on bonus, paid time off, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match, even for a part-time position.

One honest note about the affordable housing compliance side: recertification work is detail-heavy and deadline-driven. File errors can create regulatory problems, so the candidates who do well here tend to be methodical rather than improvisational. If you've worked with HUD, LIHTC, or similar programs before, that background will carry real weight. If you haven't, your ability to learn documentation standards quickly will matter more than any other quality you bring.

job.title: Assistant Service Manager (Stone Gate)
job.description:
Van Metre has been building and managing properties since 1955, and that kind of institutional continuity tends to produce a maintenance culture that takes standards seriously. At Stone Gate Apartments in Spring Lake, NC, they're looking for an Assistant Service Manager who can share the operational load with the Service Manager and step in with authority when needed.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

This role splits time between field work and coordination. You'll walk the property daily, keeping curb appeal honest and flagging anything that could become a safety or liability issue before it does. Service requests need to get scheduled, tracked, and closed out in Yardi. Turns need to be coordinated on a timeline that keeps occupancy from slipping. Preventative maintenance can't become an afterthought when the schedule gets busy, and it usually does. You'll also audit the key tracking system, manage inventory and purchasing against PO policy, and run safety meetings on a weekly cadence. When the Service Manager is out, the property runs through you.

Beyond the daily rhythm, you'll work closely with the Service Manager on budget guidance, flagging capital improvement needs and communicating maintenance requirements that should feed into the annual budget cycle. The role carries real input responsibility, not just task execution.

After-hours emergency coverage is part of the job. That's worth acknowledging plainly. The team maintains 24/7 coverage, and participation in that rotation is expected.

Qualifications

  • 4 or more years of hands-on maintenance experience, or equivalent formal training
  • EPA Type II or EPA Universal Certification (required at time of hire)
  • CPO Certification (preferred)
  • Prior supervisory or lead experience (preferred)
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Own basic tools and know how to use them safely
  • Availability for some weekend work

Compensation and Growth

The hourly rate runs $23 to $25 depending on experience, with a quarterly-paid annual bonus of up to $5,000 and renewal commissions on top of that. Van Metre also covers certifications and memberships, which matters in a trade where staying current on certifications isn't optional. The PTO package is genuinely generous by industry standards, and the wellness reimbursement of up to $900 annually is a real line item, not a talking point.

What separates strong candidates here from adequate ones is the ability to mentor. The coaching and training piece of this role is listed in the job description, but in practice it shapes how the whole maintenance team performs. If you've only ever executed tasks and haven't had to bring someone else along, that gap tends to show up fast in a supervisory role. Coming in with even one or two years of lead or acting-supervisor experience puts you ahead of the field for a position like this.

job.title: Full-Time Overnight Cleaner (Thu-Mon, 11PM-6AM)
job.description:
Comstock's ParkX division runs a tight overnight operation across its Reston portfolio, and this porter role sits at the center of it. The shift runs Thursday through Monday, 11PM to 6AM, which means you're the person responsible for making sure the property looks right before the morning crowd arrives. That's a real responsibility, and it carries real weight.

The work itself covers the full range of common-area upkeep: lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, public corridors, and any space that sees foot traffic during the day. Pressure washing, window cleaning, trash removal, and routine janitorial tasks make up the bulk of your nightly checklist. When events happen on-site, you'll help with setup and breakdown. When something looks wrong or needs attention, you flag it to management rather than waiting for it to become someone else's problem. Supply inventory, equipment care, end-of-shift documentation, clean storage areas: these are all part of the job, and they matter.

The overnight schedule creates a particular kind of work dynamic. You'll often be moving through the property while it's quiet, without much direct supervision, which means your reliability and self-direction genuinely drive the outcome. The team leans on overnight staff to operate with a high degree of integrity and to hold the standard even when no one is watching. If that kind of autonomous rhythm suits you, this role works well. If you need frequent check-ins to stay on track, it'll be a harder fit.

One thing worth acknowledging: a Thursday-through-Monday overnight schedule asks something real of your personal life. The pay is set at $17.50/hour. Comstock does offer a full benefit package including medical, dental, vision, and 401K matching, plus annual professional development funds and free parking with EV charging access. For candidates who want stability, predictable hours, and room to grow within an expanding portfolio, the structure is there.

What you'll need to bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and sustain physical work throughout the shift (standing, kneeling, climbing, bending)
  • Comfort working in variable conditions including temperature changes, chemical exposure, and outdoor environments
  • Genuine professionalism with residents, guests, and colleagues at all hours
  • Willingness to cover for teammates and step in during events or peak periods when the schedule requires it

Porters who do well in roles like this tend to take visible pride in what a clean, well-kept property communicates to the people who live and work in it. The lobby you clean at 3AM is the first thing a resident sees at 7AM. That connection between the overnight work and the daytime experience of the property is what gives the role its purpose.

job.title: Property Manager (Altitude 970)
job.description:
It's 8:47 a.m. and you're already juggling a maintenance escalation from the third floor, a leasing follow-up on two pending applications, and a quick huddle with your assistant manager about month-end collections. That's the rhythm at Altitude 970, and the right person for this role takes that kind of morning in stride.

BAM Companies is hiring a Property Manager for Altitude 970 in Kansas City, Missouri. The compensation range runs from $65,000 to $75,000, and the role carries full accountability for site operations across leasing, maintenance, resident relations, and financial performance.

What the Role Covers

You'll own the day-to-day operations of the community, which means keeping occupancy where it needs to be, running a tight delinquency process, and ensuring the physical asset reflects well on the brand. That includes overseeing leasing activity and marketing efforts to drive traffic and conversions, managing cost controls within the approved budget, and staying current on fair housing compliance. You'll also lead the on-site team directly, including leasing, maintenance, and administrative staff. BAM places real emphasis on developing the people under you, so mentorship is a core part of the job, not an afterthought.

Financial literacy matters here. You'll be responsible for budgeting, rent collection, and reporting. Candidates who can read a T-12, spot cost variances early, and explain NOI movement to ownership will have a clear advantage over those who treat financials as someone else's problem.

What BAM Is Looking For

  • At least five years of residential property management experience, with Class B or higher preferred
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing a site team
  • Comfort with property management software and CRM tools
  • Strong communication skills across residents, vendors, and ownership
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Operational discipline and genuine attention to detail

Kansas City's multifamily market has stayed active, with steady renter demand across the metro and continued pressure on operators to retain residents rather than chase new leases at the cost of concessions. A manager who understands retention strategy, not just traffic generation, will fit this market well. The ability to build loyalty among existing residents while keeping the leasing pipeline healthy is exactly what sustains NOI at a property like this.

BAM offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, disability, pet insurance, and free life insurance. PTO starts at 88 hours at the 90-day mark and grows to 120 more hours at one year. The company also provides 15.5 paid holidays, housing discounts at BAM properties, and access to internal leadership development programming. For a property manager who wants upward mobility, BAM's internal growth culture is worth taking seriously. Site managers here tend to move into regional or district-level roles as the company expands.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles at owner-operated multifamily companies carry a different weight than those at third-party management firms. When a company owns what it manages, the leasing team's performance connects directly to asset value. At Berkshire Residential Investments, that ownership structure means the Sales and Resident Experience Consultant role sits at the intersection of sales performance and long-term resident retention.

What the Role Demands

The core of this position is converting traffic into signed leases. Berkshire sets a clear benchmark: a minimum 20% closing ratio. That number rewards consultants who qualify prospects well, follow up consistently, and read what a prospect actually needs in a home. Beyond closing, you'll maintain the tour route and model units so every showing reflects the property at its best. Think of it as owning the first impression, every time.

The role also carries real administrative weight. You'll handle written and verbal resident communications with professionalism, stay current on local market conditions and competitive trends, and bring marketing ideas to your property manager. The best candidates here already understand that good leasing is part market knowledge, part relationship skill, and part operational discipline.

  • Drive leasing performance to meet or exceed a 20% closing ratio
  • Keep tour routes, models, and common gathering areas presentation-ready
  • Maintain professional communications with prospects, current residents, and team members
  • Track local market conditions and contribute ideas to improve occupancy and resident satisfaction
  • Handle leasing administration with accuracy and attention to detail

What You Bring and What You'll Build

Berkshire asks for at least two years of transferable customer service experience. That can come from hospitality, retail, or property management itself. What matters is that you already know how to work with a wide range of personalities, stay organized under pressure, and communicate clearly in writing and in person. Comfort with new technology is expected, since leasing platforms, CRMs, and digital communication tools are standard parts of the workflow.

What the role builds is harder to put on a job description. Leasing consultants who develop genuine market fluency, who can speak to concessions, occupancy trends, and competitive positioning with confidence, tend to move into assistant manager roles more quickly. The administrative and sales combination in this position creates a natural on-ramp to full property operations. Closing leases teaches you what drives a prospect's decision. Maintaining the property's presentation teaches you operational standards. Both are foundational for anyone moving toward a management track.

Compensation and Context

The base hourly range runs $23.00 to $25.00, with an annualized equivalent of approximately $47,840 to $52,000. The role is also eligible for performance bonuses, health care benefits, retirement benefits, and paid time off including sick, vacation, and parental leave. Berkshire also offers a 25% rent discount for employees, which is a meaningful benefit if you're considering living at a Berkshire community.

One honest note about what separates strong candidates here: closing ratio expectations are real and tracked. If you've worked leasing roles before, come ready to discuss how you converted traffic, what your follow-up process looked like, and how you handled objections. That's the conversation that will distinguish you.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the largest third-party student housing management companies in the country. Its conventional multifamily portfolio is growing fast. This Maintenance Supervisor role sits at a Taylorsville, Utah community and pays $29.00 per hour for full-time, non-exempt work.

The job is straightforward in scope but demanding in execution. You're responsible for the physical condition of the property: grounds, buildings, unit interiors, and anything that breaks between those points. Turns are a core part of the rhythm here. Getting units make-ready on time, with every punch list item closed before a new resident moves in, directly affects occupancy and the resident experience from day one. That discipline around turns keeps vacancy loss from compounding.

Beyond turns, you'll handle day-to-day repairs, respond to emergencies according to established procedures, and keep curb appeal at a level that reflects well on the community. You'll communicate directly with the Community Manager when issues exceed routine maintenance scope. Strong customer service habits matter as much as technical skill here. A resident's impression of maintenance responsiveness shapes renewal decisions, and renewal rates shape NOI.

The physical demands are real: expect 8 to 10 hour shifts on your feet and occasional lifts up to 75 lbs.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • At least 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience, including plumbing and electrical
  • At least 2 years of HVAC experience
  • Strong attention to detail and genuine customer service instincts
  • Ability to work standing shifts of 8 to 10 hours and lift up to 75 lbs.
  • Prior property management experience is a plus, though not required

Candidates who perform well in roles like this typically combine technical range with the ability to prioritize under pressure. On a busy turn week, you might be coordinating appliance swaps, closing out work orders, and managing a vendor visit simultaneously. The technicians who stand out know how to sequence that work so nothing gets missed before a move-in date.

Redstone offers health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, 3 paid service days, paid parental leave, a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, short-term disability insurance, an employee assistance program, and a continued education benefit. For a maintenance professional looking to grow into a regional maintenance or facilities management track, the scale of Redstone's portfolio creates real upward mobility.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
It's Thursday afternoon. A tenant's recertification deadline is two weeks out, their income documentation is incomplete, and your delinquency report shows three units past the grace period. That's the operational rhythm of affordable housing management, and this role sits right in the middle of it.

The Role at Fairstead

Fairstead owns and manages more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and their Richmond property needs an Assistant Community Manager who understands the compliance and financial rigor that affordable housing demands. This position supports the Property Manager across the full operational scope: HUD 4350.3 compliance, LIHTC reviews, REAC preparation, annual and interim recertifications, and EHS violation clearance. When Management and Occupancy Reviews or investor site visits come around, this role carries real preparation responsibility.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears daily, ensure rents are collected, posted, and deposited, and create purchase orders in Yardi. Delinquency follow-up runs through this role, and you'll work alongside Fairstead's in-house legal team to monitor payment status and coordinate evictions when lease intervention strategies don't resolve the issue. Occupancy is maintained through an active lease renewal program, and resident retention depends on how quickly and professionally you respond to questions, service requests, and complaints.

Day-to-day, you'll also keep maintenance staff informed about move-ins, move-outs, and emergencies, and you'll confirm that service requests are completed on schedule. Phone calls, emails, and messages get answered within a few hours, never more than 24.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management
  • Working knowledge of EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Familiarity with the local Richmond residential market
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to pick up new property management platforms quickly

Candidates who stand out in affordable housing ops tend to be the ones who already know the difference between a routine recertification and an interim triggered by a qualifying event. HUD compliance has a learning curve, but EIV experience and a working understanding of income verification requirements separate people who can hit the ground running from those who need six months to find their footing.

Fairstead's approach to affordable housing includes tech adoption and data-driven operations, so comfort with systems matters here beyond just knowing how to navigate Yardi. The company functions as an integrated owner, operator, and developer, which means the assistant manager at the property level connects directly to a broader platform that includes construction and development. For the right candidate, that's real career runway toward a full Property Manager role and eventually into regional or compliance-focused positions.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Berkeley Heights
job.description:
The Community Manager is out at a training seminar. You're fielding a delinquency call, two maintenance escalations, and a prospective resident who walked in unannounced. You handle all three. That's the job.

The Role

CloudTen Residential operates a diverse multifamily portfolio across the West, including hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects. This Community Assistant Manager position sits at their Berkeley Heights property in Kent, WA, and it's a full-cycle operations role. You'll own the financial side of daily property operations: collecting and posting rent, preparing bank deposits, reconciling accounts, processing invoices, and generating weekly and monthly reports. That work requires not just accuracy but genuine fluency in property management software. Sloppy entries compound into reporting problems fast.

Beyond the ledger, you'll handle leasing activity. That means responding to inquiries, conducting tours, monitoring competitive properties for pricing signals, and supporting lease renewals as part of a broader resident retention effort. You'll also manage move-in and move-out administration, including apartment inspections and security deposit dispositions, all within the timelines and compliance requirements set by Washington State law. Delinquency follow-up, non-payment notices, and eviction coordination under the Community Manager's guidance are also part of the picture. Fair Housing compliance runs through every part of this role.

When the Community Manager is unavailable, you step into the leadership seat. That's not an occasional circumstance. It's a core expectation built into the position from day one.

Pay runs $28.00 to $32.00 per hour depending on experience, and the role carries leasing and renewal bonus eligibility.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires at least two years of property management or leasing experience, solid command of Microsoft Office and property management software, a valid driver's license, and working knowledge of landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing standards, and basic accounting principles. Those aren't things CloudTen will teach you from scratch. You come in with that foundation.

What the role builds is different. You'll sharpen your financial reporting instincts by working alongside a Community Manager who can explain the "why" behind operational decisions. You'll develop leadership judgment by handling real escalations, real team dynamics, and real site issues under conditions where you're expected to solve problems, not wait for direction. The skills you develop here, delinquency management, leasing strategy, compliance fluency, team coordination, transfer directly to a Community Manager position. CloudTen explicitly names growth into leadership as part of this role's trajectory, and their expanding portfolio means those openings tend to materialize.

Strong candidates at this level tend to separate themselves on one specific thing: they close the loop. They follow up on the maintenance request, confirm the deposit was posted correctly, and check that the notice was served within the required window. Average candidates know the tasks. Strong candidates track them.

  • Minimum two years of property management or leasing experience
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and property management software
  • Valid driver's license
  • Working knowledge of Washington State landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable managing competing priorities without close supervision
  • Basic accounting knowledge and comfort with financial reporting

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA options, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off. CloudTen is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug-free workplace.

job.title: Resident Relations Specialist
job.description:
Resident relations roles exist at a lot of properties, but they're often just leasing with a different title. This one at RedPeak is structured differently. The Resident Relations Specialist here is a dedicated post-move-in function, which means you're not chasing traffic numbers or pushing lease conversions. You're managing the experience that actually determines whether a resident renews.

What the Role Covers Day to Day

Your primary job is owning the resident relationship from move-in through renewal or move-out. That means week-one and 30-day check-ins with new residents, handling the full range of concerns that come in by phone, email, text, and in person, and working across leasing, maintenance, and property management to get issues resolved before they escalate. You'll document interactions in the property management system, respond to online reviews, monitor satisfaction trends, and flag recurring complaints to the Multi-Site Manager so patterns don't get buried in day-to-day noise.

You'll also conduct regular property walks, keep an eye on common areas and amenities, and coordinate follow-up when anything falls short of community standards. When the Property Manager is out, you step into a backup role within defined escalation guidelines. Fair Housing issues, legal concerns, or anything with significant financial exposure goes up the chain with a clear summary of what's already been done.

Leasing coverage is part of the job when needed. You should be comfortable conducting tours, assisting with applications, and answering lease-related questions. This isn't your primary function, but the expectation is that you know the leasing process well enough to fill in without disruption.

What RedPeak Is Looking For

  • At least 2 years in property management, hospitality, or a resident or customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of leasing: tours, applications, and lease terms
  • Demonstrated ability to de-escalate difficult conversations and document resolutions accurately
  • Sound judgment about what to resolve independently and what requires escalation
  • Comfort with property management software and high communication volume across multiple channels
  • A collaborative working style, since this role sits at the intersection of leasing, maintenance, and centralized services

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, at the Littleton location. Pay runs $24 to $27 per hour plus bonus eligibility.

Where This Role Leads

Resident relations is one of the cleaner paths into assistant or property manager roles because it builds exactly the skills that matter at the next level: conflict resolution, cross-functional coordination, retention strategy, and operational judgment. You come out of a role like this with a track record on NOI-adjacent metrics, renewal rates, and online reputation management, things that matter on a resume and in an interview for a site leadership position. If you're currently in a pure leasing role and want to move toward operations without jumping straight into manager-level accountability, this is a sensible bridge. The multi-site structure at RedPeak also means you'll have visibility into how decisions get made above the property level, which accelerates that development.

job.title: Central Renewal & Leasing Specialist - Hybrid
job.description:
A resident calls with questions about a rent increase on their renewal offer. You pull up their lease history in Yardi, check current market rents against what they're being quoted, and walk them through the reasoning clearly enough that they sign the renewal the same day. That's the core of this role at Reside Living, and it demands someone who can hold a productive conversation and read a pricing rationale at the same time.

What This Role Actually Involves

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago's neighborhoods, and this specialist position sits at the center of their central operations team. The vast majority of your time, around 95%, goes toward resident renewals. You'll own the full renewal cycle: outbound and inbound communication (calls, emails, texts), explaining rent increases in plain terms, tracking 30-day notice deadlines, coordinating with on-site property managers, and generating the final lease once a resident accepts. When negotiation is warranted, you'll review current market rents against quoted rates and find a close.

Notices to vacate get processed in Yardi for residents who don't renew. The remaining time covers initial lead response work: answering inbound prospect calls, communicating amenity details and availability, and scheduling tours across in-person, self-guided, and virtual formats.

This is a hybrid position, with three or more days per week working from home. You'll report directly to the Vice President of Yield Optimization, which means your renewal data and feedback directly inform pricing and process decisions at a portfolio level.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires at least three years in multifamily property management operations and a minimum of one year managing renewals for a property of 250 or more units. Yardi experience is preferred, and so is familiarity with LRO or comparable yield management tools. Excel and Word are required. The ability to move quickly through software screens while staying present in a conversation with a resident is a practical skill this job tests every day.

  • 3+ years in multifamily operations
  • 1+ year directly managing multifamily renewal processes at scale
  • Yardi experience preferred; LRO yield management experience preferred
  • Microsoft Office proficiency required
  • Strong verbal communication and negotiation instincts
  • Comfort with process improvement discussions and contributing structured feedback

What the role builds is different from what it requires. You'll develop a sharp read on how neighborhood trends and market comps translate into renewal pricing conversations. You'll also gain experience influencing portfolio-level process from a centralized position, a skill set that transfers well into roles like portfolio manager, revenue analyst, or yield optimization specialist. Reside Living notes they're willing to train the right person, so the operational fundamentals matter more than a perfect resume.

Compensation is $30.00 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, life, and disability insurance, 401(k) matching, commuter benefits, 13 days PTO to start, paid holidays, student loan assistance at $100 per month, and a 25% apartment discount after 90 days.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Cottonwood Bayview Apartments
job.description:
A prospect walks in off the street, a little uncertain, maybe mid-move, definitely stressed. The way you greet them in that first thirty seconds sets the tone for everything that follows. At Cottonwood Bayview Apartments in St. Petersburg, that moment happens multiple times a day, and it's what this role is built around.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cottonwood Residential calls this role a Customer Experience Specialist, and the title is accurate. You're the first human contact for prospective residents, the person current residents call when something needs attention, and one of the main connectors between the property and the vendors and contractors who keep it running. That means your day moves between the leasing office, the tour path, and the amenity spaces, with phone calls, texts, and emails woven in between.

Concretely, you'll keep units show-ready, walk vacant homes and common areas daily to catch anything that's slipped below standard, and stay sharp on current pricing and availability so you can answer prospect questions without hesitation. You'll also manage the package room, support community events, and help with social media content. It's a genuinely varied role, and the variety is part of what makes it engaging, though it also means you need to stay organized and shift gears quickly.

Cottonwood has been an early adopter of self-guided tours, which is worth understanding before you join. That technology changes resident and prospect expectations: people arrive having already done a lot of their own research, and they want conversation, not a scripted walkthrough. Your job is less about reciting floor plan details and more about reading people and making real connections.

This is a full-time position with a schedule that includes evenings and weekends. That's standard in leasing, and worth being honest about upfront: the busiest traffic times are evenings and weekends, which is exactly when prospects tour and residents have questions.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Comfortable standing, greeting, and genuinely engaging with people throughout the day, not just at scheduled tour times
  • Quick and clear communicator across phone, email, and text, with a habit of taking detailed notes
  • Detail-oriented enough to notice when a show unit is off or the tour path needs attention before a prospect does
  • Organized when volume is high, especially during busy move-in periods or package-heavy days
  • Open to learning new tools and technology as Cottonwood continues to build out its digital leasing experience

Cottonwood specifically mentions room to grow into management. That's real in property management: strong leasing consultants who understand both the resident relationship side and the operational basics tend to move into assistant manager and property manager roles faster than people might expect. If you want a career path and not just a job, this is a reasonable place to start building one.

Benefits include full medical, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage available within your first thirty days, a 401k and HSA with company match, three weeks of paid time off in your first year, and ten and a half paid holidays annually. There's also a quarterly bonus structure on top of base pay.

job.title: Community Manager Affordable Housing
job.description:
Affordable housing management carries compliance weight that market-rate property management simply doesn't. Between HUD regulations, LIHTC reviews, REAC inspections, and recertification cycles, a Community Manager at an affordable property is running a parallel track of regulatory work alongside the daily operations most managers handle. Fairstead, which owns and operates more than 30,000 units across 28 states, is hiring for that role at one of its Davenport, Iowa properties.

What This Role Actually Involves

The compliance side of this position is substantial. You'll maintain working knowledge of the HUD 4350.3 Handbook, prepare for REAC reviews and Management and Occupancy Reviews, coordinate with the Compliance Department on regulatory responses, and manage annual and interim recertification processes. LIHTC review preparation is also part of the scope, so a TCS certification is required. Candidates with COS or CPO credentials are expected at this level.

On the operations side, you're overseeing day-to-day site performance: rent collection, delinquency pursuit through legal channels, monitoring bad-debt write-offs, documenting lease violations, and coordinating evictions when necessary. You'll supervise maintenance staff and work with your Building Superintendent on bi-annual property walk-throughs. Vendor bids, contractor quotes, unit inspections, and ongoing renovation coordination with the construction team all fall under your oversight. Monthly financial meetings and budget monitoring round out the accountability.

EIV experience is expected. Yardi and RealPage familiarity is preferred and practical given Fairstead's tech-forward operating model.

Who Fits This Role Well

Three years of team supervision experience is the floor, and the affordable housing compliance layer means that generic leasing or market-rate management backgrounds need to be supplemented with actual affordable housing exposure. Candidates who've run a HUD or tax credit property through a MOR or REAC inspection have a real advantage here. Knowing how to intervene early with residents approaching non-compliance, before situations escalate to legal action, is a skill that separates strong affordable housing managers from reactive ones.

Davenport sits in the Quad Cities metro, a stable Midwest market with steady affordable housing demand and limited new supply pressure compared to larger metros. That context matters: occupancy here tends to hold, but keeping it stable requires consistent community management and proactive resident engagement, not just administrative accuracy.

  • COS or CPO certification (required)
  • TCS certification for tax credit properties (required)
  • Minimum three years of supervisory management experience
  • EIV system experience
  • Yardi and/or RealPage experience (preferred)
  • Affordable housing background with direct compliance exposure
  • Bachelor's degree (preferred)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite

Fairstead offers medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 12 paid holidays, 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, FSA, pet insurance, disability insurance, and employee discount programs.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Redfield Ridge
job.description:
Assistant Community Manager roles at growing regional operators tend to offer something the big REITs rarely do: genuine exposure to every layer of how a property runs. At CloudTen Residential, that's the explicit intent. This position at Redfield Ridge in Reno is structured as a deliberate training ground, not a support role that keeps you circling the same tasks year after year.

What You'll Be Doing

The day-to-day splits fairly evenly across financial operations, leasing support, and team coverage. On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection and posting, prepare daily deposits, reconcile accounts, process payables, and maintain weekly and monthly reporting. Delinquency management is real here: you'll serve non-payment notices, track follow-ups, and coordinate eviction proceedings when it comes to that, all with guidance from the Community Manager. Accuracy in the property management software matters a lot at this level, since the reporting integrity flows directly from how transactions are entered.

Leasing responsibilities include responding to inquiries, conducting tours, and helping close prospects on available units. You'll assist with move-in and move-out administration, including apartment inspections on both ends, and help prepare security deposit dispositions in compliance with Nevada law. Fair Housing compliance runs through all of it.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into the lead role. That's written into the job, not a theoretical scenario. It means you need to be comfortable making operational calls and directing the on-site team before you formally hold the top title.

What CloudTen Is Looking For

  • At least two years of property management, leasing, or closely related experience
  • Working knowledge of landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing standards in Nevada
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and at least one property management platform
  • Strong written and verbal communication, plus the organizational discipline to manage competing priorities without dropping details
  • Basic accounting fluency: you don't need a finance background, but you do need to understand what you're looking at in a financial report

Compensation runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with leasing bonuses available on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

Where This Role Leads

CloudTen operates a portfolio that spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects across the West. That variety matters for your career. An ACM who learns the financial and operational side at a stabilized property has a clear path to a Community Manager seat, and in a portfolio with that kind of asset diversity, the CM roles themselves aren't uniform. The skills you build here: delinquency management, NOI-level reporting, team supervision, and leasing conversion, transfer cleanly to larger or more complex properties down the line.

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to be the ones who treat the financial reporting as seriously as the leasing side. A lot of people come up through leasing and are comfortable with traffic and conversions but under-prepared when it comes to reconciling accounts or reading a T-12. If you've already built both sides of that foundation, you'll move through this training track faster.

job.title: Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Luxury multifamily properties carry a specific maintenance burden: the gap between resident expectations and what the building actually delivers on any given day falls squarely on the service team. At a Class A portfolio like Griffis Residential, that gap can be narrow, but closing it consistently is the whole job. This Maintenance Manager role in Denver is built around someone who can keep that gap closed while also running a team, managing a budget, and doing real hands-on work when it's needed.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll lead the property's service team day to day, which means scheduling, supervising, and stepping in yourself. Make-readies need to turn on time. Service requests need to close without residents having to follow up twice. Capital projects and vendor bids need someone who can read a scope of work critically and push back when pricing isn't right. You'll also manage the maintenance budget and coordinate contracted repairs, which means knowing when to do the work in-house and when outside vendors are the right call.

Beyond the reactive work, you'll conduct regular property inspections, track what needs attention before it becomes a complaint or a code issue, and make sure your team operates within safety regulations. CPO and EPA certifications are required (or you need to obtain them within your first six months). The technical range here is real: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, pool systems, drywall, painting, and carpentry all fall under your scope.

You'll also work alongside the Community Manager on hiring, training, and evaluating your team. Setting expectations, giving feedback, and developing people are part of the role, not just managing workloads.

Who Does This Well

  • 2 to 5 years of experience in multifamily or a comparable industry, with 1 to 3 years in a supervisory capacity
  • Strong working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and general building maintenance
  • Comfortable with vendor bidding, budget tracking, and capex coordination
  • CPO license and EPA certification, or the ability to get both within six months
  • Proficient with property management software and intermediate computer skills
  • Spanish fluency is a plus, particularly useful for team communication and resident interactions

The candidates who struggle in roles like this tend to be strong technically but thin on follow-through with people. Scheduling, feedback conversations, and accountability with your crew take as much energy as diagnosing a failed HVAC unit. The candidates who do well carry both without letting one slide when the other gets busy.

One honest note: this is an on-site, hands-on leadership role. After-hours emergencies happen in multifamily. At a luxury property, the expectation for responsiveness is higher, not lower. If that's manageable for you, the upside is a stable schedule with real structure compared to hospitality or hotel maintenance work, which tends to be less predictable year-round.

Compensation runs between $35 and $38.50 per hour. Benefits include a 50% rental discount, quarterly and occupancy bonuses, three weeks of PTO to start, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, full medical, dental, and vision, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually, and paid parental leave.

job.title: Maintenance Technician, J Harbor Park at North Point
job.description:
Maintenance work at the apartment level is a craft, and this role at J Harbor Park at North Point in Reston, VA gives you the foundation to build it properly. Jefferson Apartment Group operates across acquisition, development, construction, and property management, so the people doing hands-on work at their communities are part of a larger operation that takes quality seriously. This is a 190-unit community, and the technician here touches a broad range of tasks daily.

Skills This Role Requires

You'll come in with a working knowledge of basic maintenance tools and common repair tasks. HVAC filter changes, light replacements, unit inspections, and make-ready assistance all require competence with your hands and the confidence to work efficiently without supervision. The ability to lift 50 to 100 pounds and move comfortably throughout the property, climbing stairs, kneeling, bending, and working in tight spaces, is a real physical requirement here, not a formality. On-call availability for evenings, weekends, and holidays is part of the role. That's worth understanding before you apply.

Customer service matters as much as technical skill. Residents expect timely responses and work that's done right the first time. If you've worked in a service environment and know how to communicate calmly with people who are frustrated, that transfers directly to this job.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

A typical day here involves a mix of scheduled preventive maintenance and reactive service. You'll change filters and clean AC vents in both occupied units and vacant ones, assist senior technicians with service requests, support make-ready turns, handle janitorial tasks, and help keep the common areas and breezeways clean and presentable. You'll also help distribute resident communications. It's work that spans the full physical property, so you'll get to know the community well.

Skills This Role Builds

For a technician early in their multifamily career, this role builds something valuable: pattern recognition. When you're working across a 190-unit community on preventive maintenance and service requests, you start to understand how systems behave over time, which units need attention before residents call, and how to prioritize effectively. That operational instinct is what separates an experienced technician from someone just completing tickets. Technicians who develop that skill at this stage tend to move into lead or head maintenance roles faster.

Jefferson Apartment Group is growing, and that matters for career trajectory. Companies with active development and acquisition pipelines tend to have real internal mobility, and technicians who perform well at the property level are well-positioned when new communities come online.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • General maintenance tool knowledge and familiarity with common repair tasks
  • On-call availability including evenings, weekends, and holidays
  • Ability to lift 50 to 100 pounds and meet the physical demands of property work

Compensation runs $23 to $24 per hour. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, and vision coverage for themselves and eligible family members, paid time off, and potential rental discounts.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Property management operators who run manufactured home communities often describe the assistant manager role as the one that teaches you everything. You're close enough to residents to understand what's actually happening on the ground, and close enough to the community manager to see how decisions get made. It's genuinely operational work, and Havenpark Communities builds its assistant roles that way deliberately.

Havenpark owns and operates more than 100 manufactured home communities across the U.S., with 30,000-plus homesites in its portfolio. The company is actively acquiring and growing, which means the people learning the business right now are well-positioned as that growth continues. This Assistant Community Manager role sits at a Clinton Township, MI property and reports directly into the Community Manager.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Your week will mix resident-facing work with the kind of operational follow-through that keeps a community functioning. Resident relations take up a meaningful chunk of time. That includes handling concerns before they escalate, fielding questions, and being someone residents can actually reach when they need help. You'll also support collections, track delinquency, and help keep the leasing process moving for prospective residents.

Work order coordination falls into your scope too. That means communicating with maintenance and vendors, following up on open items, and making sure things don't fall through the cracks. Some travel for training or company meetings may come up once or twice a year, but this is primarily an on-site role.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Prior experience in property management or a related customer-facing role
  • Comfort handling collections conversations with professionalism and empathy
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and reliable about follow-through
  • Able to stay steady when residents are frustrated or situations get complicated
  • A collaborative working style, since you'll be in constant coordination with your Community Manager and maintenance team

Manufactured housing communities attract residents with real roots. Longer tenancies, deeper community ties, and neighbors who know each other by name. That resident profile means relationships genuinely matter here, and an assistant manager who builds trust tends to find the work more rewarding and the job much easier to do well. The candidates who thrive in this role typically combine patience with persistence. They follow up without being told to, and they treat every resident interaction as a reflection of how the community feels to live in.

Havenpark describes its culture around five values: Respect, Grit, Collaboration, Stewardship, and Boldness. Those aren't just words on a wall if the organization truly lives by them. If you're someone who takes ownership, works well with others, and brings a steady, positive presence to a team, this role is worth a close look.

job.title: Property Manager - Multifamily
job.description:
It's late July, and your leasing staff is running ragged closing the last wave of fall move-ins while maintenance is grinding through turn units on a tight punch list. That's the job. You're the one keeping both tracks moving without letting either fall apart.

The Role

PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Property Manager for a student housing community in Newtown, Connecticut. This is a full onsite position with P&L responsibility. You're the site leader: managing staff, owning the budget, directing leasing strategy, and making sure NOI lands where it's supposed to. The turn cycle in student housing is compressed and unforgiving, and PeakMade expects the person in this seat to have already run one before.

On the financial side, you'll build the annual operating budget, report to your Regional Manager with accurate financial data, and monitor rent collections closely. Delinquency management and landlord/resident compliance fall on you. You're also expected to read a T-12, spot trends early, and recommend adjustments before problems compound.

Leasing strategy is a real part of this role. Student housing runs on lease-up cycles, and you'll direct the marketing and sales plans that drive occupancy toward budget. You'll make sure your team knows the product and the competitive set, and you'll stay close to market conditions yourself.

On the people side, you'll recruit, train, coach, and when necessary, document corrective action and handle terminations. Performance reviews, development conversations, and keeping a team functional through the pressure of peak season are all part of the expectation here.

What You'll Need

  • Four or more years of property management experience, full-cycle
  • Two years in student housing or campus-adjacent management, preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to build and manage an operating budget
  • Comfort reading and presenting monthly financial statements
  • Working knowledge of property management software; Entrata experience is a real advantage here
  • High school diploma required; college degree preferred
  • Full-time onsite presence is required, not negotiable

The candidates who tend to do well in this type of role understand that student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The lease-up window is narrow, the turn is concentrated into a few weeks, and your residents (and their parents) have high service expectations. Experience managing those seasonal pressure points specifically is worth more here than raw years in the industry.

Compensation for this role is $80,000 to $85,000 annually. PeakMade also offers 401(k) match, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, a housing discount, mentorship programming, and a few perks that reflect a company that takes retention seriously, including a 10-year anniversary trip and an annual leadership conference.

job.title: Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community PLUS HOUSING
job.description:
Manufactured housing community management sits at an interesting crossroads in multifamily operations. Residents own their homes but lease the land, which creates a distinct relationship dynamic, a different delinquency profile, and a compliance environment that varies meaningfully from conventional apartment management. At a 55+ community, that dynamic gets even more specific. Investment Property Group understands this, and they're hiring a Community Manager for Rio Verde Mobile Estates in Auburn, Washington to run the day-to-day with that full context in mind.

This is an on-site role in the most literal sense: IPG provides a 2-bedroom, 2-bathroom manufactured home on the property, carport and shed included. Living on site is required. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with occasional weekend availability when the property needs it.

What the Role Actually Covers

You're the operational lead for a 100-plus site senior community. That means rent collection, delinquency review, vendor coordination, lease enforcement, and compliance with the regulatory requirements specific to manufactured housing operations in Washington. You'll oversee the application and move-in process for new residents, manage on-site staff through hiring, training, and performance, and serve as the primary point of contact when residents bring concerns to the office. IPG also expects you to maintain active relationships with local community development agencies and law enforcement, which at a 55+ property is often less adversarial and more collaborative than it sounds.

On the financial side, you'll handle bi-monthly deposits, review delinquent accounts, and track resident receivables. You'll be expected to flag opportunities to improve efficiency and profitability, which means reading your numbers and offering real input, not just reporting upward. Marketing vacant lots or homes to maintain occupancy is also part of the job.

What IPG Is Looking For

  • At least one year managing a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Direct experience with rent collection and delinquency management
  • Comfort with property management software and basic accounting systems
  • Strong conflict resolution skills, particularly suited to a senior resident demographic
  • Fair Housing compliance knowledge
  • Vendor coordination experience, from scheduling through quality verification

The compensation range is $34 to $38 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. IPG offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

What separates strong candidates here is a specific combination: the ability to hold firm on community rules and lease enforcement while still being genuinely approachable at the office door. At a 55+ community, residents often have longer tenure, deeper attachments to their homes and neighbors, and higher expectations for responsiveness. A manager who treats every interaction as a transaction will burn through goodwill fast. The best community managers at properties like this run tight delinquency numbers and still know most residents by name. That balance is harder to hire for than it looks, and it's the real qualification IPG is screening for.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians at established third-party management firms like Makowsky Ringel Greenberg tend to work across a portfolio rather than a single address, which means the breadth of your skills gets tested regularly. This role covers apartment communities in Memphis and calls for someone who already knows their way around HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical work, and appliance repair before walking in the door.

What This Role Requires

HVAC certification is a firm requirement here, with Universal certification preferred. Beyond that, the expectation is at least two years of apartment maintenance experience and the hands-on confidence to work independently with minimal oversight. You'll need your own tools and a reliable vehicle with valid insurance, since this position moves between properties. Daily documentation of completed work is part of the job, so comfort with written records matters alongside the technical skills.

The core responsibilities span the full range of residential maintenance:

  • HVAC repair and installation
  • Plumbing and electrical repairs
  • Appliance repair, moving, and installation
  • Lock installation, repair, and rekeying
  • Make-ready work to prepare units for move-in
  • Routine preventive maintenance
  • Supporting other technicians on troubleshooting and repairs
  • Compliance with company safety policies and applicable OSHA standards

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, but rotating on-call coverage is part of the role. If after-hours calls are something you've avoided before, factor that in honestly before applying.

Skills This Role Builds

Working across multiple communities inside a fee-management operation exposes you to a wider variety of building types and repair scenarios than a single-site position typically offers. Over time, that breadth sharpens diagnostic speed and deepens your familiarity with how different properties age and present issues. Technicians who handle portfolio work often develop strong instincts for preventive maintenance prioritization, which is exactly the skillset that opens doors to lead technician and maintenance supervisor roles down the line.

Knowing local building codes and working within OSHA standards also builds a compliance fluency that becomes increasingly valuable as portfolios grow and regulatory scrutiny on habitability tightens in markets across the country.

Compensation and Benefits

The position includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, quarterly and annual performance bonuses, and a fuel allowance that reflects the multi-site nature of the work. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, short- and long-term disability, company-paid life insurance, paid holidays, paid time off, and a 401(k) with profit sharing. Pre-employment screening includes a background check, credit check, and drug screening.

job.title: Exciting Maintenance Super Opportunity - $1,000 Sign-On Bonus: Delhi Community
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Turns are the heartbeat of this role. When a unit goes vacant at Delhi Community, your job is to assess the condition quickly, build a realistic timeline, and get it rent-ready without dragging out the process. That means keeping paint, supplies, and basic materials stocked before you need them, not scrambling after a move-out happens. Occupancy depends on how fast and clean your turns are, and the Community Manager will be counting on you to communicate honestly when multiple units stack up at the same time.

Beyond turns, the work is what you'd expect from a full-scope maintenance superintendent role: work orders, preventive inspections, grounds care, cleaning of common areas, vendor coordination, and building safety oversight. DePaul Housing Management also uses property management software to document work orders and inspections, so comfort with basic technology (or willingness to learn it) matters here.

The on-call piece is real and worth knowing upfront. You'll rotate weekend on-call with the Community Manager and a live-in technician. When it's your weekend, you're considered on-duty from Friday at 4:00 p.m. through Monday at 7:00 a.m. and need to stay within 30 minutes of the property. Emergencies happen, and your phone needs to be charged and reachable. This isn't a dealbreaker for the right person, but it's a genuine commitment and you should go in with eyes open.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance superintendent or in a closely related maintenance role
  • Hands-on skills in some combination of electrical, plumbing, carpentry, painting, and equipment repair
  • Experience with grounds care, snow removal, and exterior upkeep
  • Ability to assess a vacant unit accurately and estimate turnover time without being walked through it
  • Comfort working with the resident population this property serves
  • Basic tech literacy for work order and inspection documentation
  • A habit of planning supply needs ahead rather than reacting to shortages

A Few Things Worth Knowing

DePaul is a housing management organization, which means this property likely serves residents who need stable, well-maintained housing as a foundation. That context shapes the work. Residents here aren't hotel guests, and they're not luxury renters. They're neighbors, and how you interact with them, their families, and visitors day to day matters as much as your wrench work.

The organization's stated priority is employee safety, meaning you won't be expected to take on tasks outside your skill set or without proper equipment. That's genuinely good policy, and worth noting for candidates who've worked places where the pressure to just get it done overrode common sense.

Strong candidates for this role tend to be self-directed planners who don't wait to be told a unit needs attention or a supply is running low. The difference between a superintendent who moves turns in four days and one who takes twelve usually comes down to preparation and communication, not just speed.
