If you've built a track record of tight turns and proactive inspections, that background translates directly here. A $1,000 sign-on bonus is included with this position.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
Leasing is the revenue engine of any apartment community. Everything else, maintenance response times, amenity upgrades, renewal incentives, depends on the front door staying busy and converting. MG Properties has been doing this across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, and they're adding a Leasing Consultant at 3300 Tamarac Apartments in Denver.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You're meeting prospects, qualifying them, getting them through the application process, and coordinating with maintenance so move-ins don't turn into a punch list of complaints on day one. Lease preparation and signing fall to you. So does keeping rental files current and data entered accurately into the system. Resident interaction doesn't stop at move-in either. Handling complaints, fielding maintenance concerns, and nudging timely rent payment are all part of the ongoing work. Monthly administrative tasks round out the cycle.

It's a full-loop leasing role. Traffic comes in, you work it, you close it, and you keep the relationship from falling apart afterward. If you've worked leasing before, you know the rhythm.

Who Fits Here

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience preferred
  • Genuine sales and customer service skills, not just comfort talking to people
  • Professional presentation and written communication
  • Comfortable working within a team and taking direction
  • Organized enough to keep files accurate and administrative work complete

MG Properties promotes from within, and leasing consultant roles are historically where property management careers start. Assistant manager, then manager, then regional, it's a well-worn path for people who combine strong leasing performance with operational discipline. If that trajectory interests you, a company with a 30-year track record and a real portfolio gives you room to actually move.

Compensation runs $22 to $23 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of that. The company also offers profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, vision, and rental discounts. This position is expected to be filled in December 2026.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Roofstock operates in the single-family rental space at scale, and this Maintenance Technician role reflects that model. You're covering a portfolio of scattered-site homes across Columbus rather than working a single community. The skill set this demands is different from apartment maintenance: strong independent judgment, efficient routing across the metro, and the ability to assess each property on its own terms without a maintenance supervisor down the hall.

Skills This Role Runs On

HVAC competency is central here. Type II Certification is required, and Universal Certification is preferred, which signals that refrigerant handling will be a regular part of the work. Beyond HVAC, the role draws on plumbing and electrical troubleshooting at a generalist level. Roofstock is also specifically looking for tech comfort: work orders, communications, and field documentation all flow through mobile apps, so someone who resists digital tools will struggle with the daily rhythm here.

Vendor QA is worth highlighting separately. Auditing work completed by outside contractors requires a different kind of attention than doing the repair yourself. You're reading completed jobs critically, catching shortcuts, and flagging anything that doesn't meet standard before it becomes a resident complaint or a reinspection. That skill carries real value in fee management and third-party models where vendor oversight directly affects NOI.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Routine and emergency repairs across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • Make-readies: preparing vacant units for new move-ins, including punch list completion
  • Move-in, move-out, and onboarding inspections
  • Vendor work audits to verify quality before sign-off
  • Service task management via mobile platform, including posting legal notices as needed

Columbus is a steady market with consistent single-family rental demand, driven partly by its university population and a strong base of young professionals priced into renting. Portfolio-based maintenance here means real daily mileage across neighborhoods like Westerville, Hilliard, and the near east side. Roofstock provides a company vehicle and gas card, which removes the financial friction that makes scattered-site work a dealbreaker at other companies.

What Makes This Role Distinct

The schedule is a genuine differentiator. Full-time hours with no on-call rotation and no weekend requirement is uncommon in maintenance, where after-hours emergencies often come with the territory. That structure appeals to experienced techs who are done trading personal time for unpredictable call-out pay. The $25 to $28 hourly range reflects that, with room to move based on licensure and experience.

Strong candidates here will combine hands-on trade skills with the self-direction to manage a daily route independently. The techs who thrive in scattered-site work tend to think in systems: they sequence their day efficiently, document clearly, and don't need constant oversight to stay productive. If your background is in a single community, this transition is manageable, but the shift in how you structure your own time is real.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Redpoint Gainesville, the Experience Team Member role sits at the center of daily community life. You're the person prospective residents meet on a tour, the one current residents flag down about a maintenance request, and the face of the community at events. Scion operates in student living, which means the energy here is genuinely different from conventional multifamily. Move-in season and Turn periods hit hard and fast, and your ability to stay organized and upbeat when the leasing office is buzzing matters a lot.

On a typical day, you might conduct apartment tours in the morning, help a resident track down a package, post to the community's social channels, follow up on open maintenance requests, and close out the office before rotating onto after-hours on-call duty. The role blends leasing, marketing, and resident relations into one position, and the mix shifts depending on the time of year. During Turn, expect the pace to intensify significantly as units flip and incoming residents arrive.

You'll also relay real-time feedback to the management team on what's working in sales conversations and where prospects are pushing back. That kind of ground-level input shapes how the community adjusts its messaging and concessions strategy, so your observations carry actual weight.

What You Bring

  • Genuine comfort talking with a wide range of people, including students, parents, and community partners
  • Strong reliability and self-discipline, especially for on-call responsibilities
  • Flexibility when priorities shift quickly, which they will
  • Availability during summers, holidays, and Turn periods without exception
  • Clear, professional communication across in-person, phone, and social media channels
  • A customer-first instinct that doesn't switch off when things get hectic

The Honest Picture

Student housing communities operate on an academic calendar, which creates predictable but intense pressure points. The weeks around move-in and move-out are demanding, and after-hours lockout calls are part of the rotation, not a rarity. If you're someone who finds variety energizing and genuinely enjoys working with a college-age population, those dynamics tend to feel manageable rather than draining.

For candidates thinking about where this role leads: Experience Team Members in student living who develop strong leasing skills and community management instincts often move into assistant community manager or leasing manager positions. The combination of sales, marketing, and operations exposure you get here is transferable well beyond student housing if you ever want to pivot to conventional or mixed-use multifamily later on.

Scion requires that candidates be eligible to work in the United States. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

job.title: Community Manager (Mission Gateway)
job.description:
Property management at MidPen asks you to operate across a wider range than most conventional apartment roles. You'll be reading regulatory documents one hour and walking the grounds the next, coaching a leasing clerk on file accuracy in the morning and meeting with a local community partner in the afternoon. The skills this role draws on most heavily are compliance fluency, fiscal discipline, and team development. If you've spent time in affordable housing, you understand why those three can't be separated.

The Skills This Role Requires on Day One

MidPen's portfolio carries real regulatory weight. Mission Gateway operates under affordable housing program requirements, which means you need to arrive with working knowledge of TCAC, HUD, and Fair Housing regulations, not just a general awareness of them. Certification as a Tax Credit Specialist or Certified Occupancy Specialist is expected (or you'll need to earn it within your first six months, at company expense). Correct initial certifications, annual re-certifications, and lease renewals under these programs demand precision. A missed detail in a resident file can create a compliance finding that affects the entire property.

On the fiscal side, you'll manage rent collection, delinquency, security deposits, and bank reconciliation. Residents of affordable communities often face income instability, so delinquency management here requires both firmness and genuine skill in working with people. RealPage experience helps significantly, as does the ability to read and act on your numbers rather than just report them.

What This Role Builds

Leading a property team at this level develops supervisory judgment in a way that's hard to replicate anywhere else. You'll conduct performance reviews, provide ongoing coaching, and make staffing decisions with real consequences for residents and operations. Affordable housing Community Managers who can document compliance, develop staff, and keep NOI on track tend to move into Regional Manager roles, Portfolio Director positions, or operations leadership within mission-driven housing organizations. The compliance depth you build here also transfers directly to fee management environments and third-party affordable portfolios.

MidPen's close integration between Property Management and Resident Services is worth understanding before you apply. You won't be operating a property in isolation. You'll work alongside a Resident Services team whose job is to connect residents with support programs. That coordination requires its own skill: the ability to collaborate across departments with different goals and vocabularies while keeping your own operational responsibilities on track.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Two or more years of hands-on affordable housing experience, specifically with tax credit or HUD-regulated communities
  • At least one year supervising property staff, with examples of how you've helped someone improve or grow
  • Demonstrated comfort interpreting regulatory documents and translating them into daily procedures for your team
  • A genuine orientation toward the residents you serve, not just the operations you manage

Union City sits in the East Bay, where housing costs remain high and the demand for quality affordable units is consistent. Managing well here means residents can stay housed, and that's the ground-level impact this role carries. MidPen has operated in this space since 1970 and maintains a portfolio of over 142 properties across Northern California. The infrastructure, training, and mission alignment are real. The work is also demanding. If you know affordable housing compliance and you want a role where your management skills are fully in play, this is a position that rewards both craft and commitment.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
Lease-up velocity is one of the most consequential metrics in multifamily development, and companies building workforce housing at scale across the Sun Belt need leasing talent that can move where the need is highest. That's the logic behind this role. Hillpointe operates as a fully integrated developer and investment management firm, controlling everything from land acquisition through asset management on market-rate workforce housing communities. When a new community launches or a team needs coverage during peak traffic, a generalist leasing consultant can't always fill the gap fast enough. A floating specialist can.

What This Role Actually Involves

You'll rotate across multiple Hillpointe communities in and around the Savannah area, stepping in during lease-ups, high-traffic periods, and team transitions. The core of the work is leasing: greeting prospects, conducting property tours, tailoring your pitch to what each person actually needs in a home, and following up consistently through phone, text, and email until you close or disqualify. You'll also keep tour paths and model units presentation-ready, because first impressions during a lease-up directly affect absorption pace.

The schedule will include weekends. Traffic peaks on Saturdays, and the communities you support are in active growth mode. Hillpointe offers free rent at an assigned community as part of the position, which reflects both the mobility expectation and the commitment to keeping you embedded in the product you're selling.

  • Travel frequently between portfolio communities based on operational need
  • Cover leasing during team transitions, new community launches, and peak periods
  • Conduct tours and tailor community highlights to each prospect's situation
  • Maintain follow-up cadence across phone, text, and email
  • Keep tour routes, amenity spaces, and units clean and presentation-ready
  • Flexibility to relocate temporarily or permanently if the business requires it

Where This Role Leads

A floating role builds something that a single-property leasing position rarely does: pattern recognition across communities. You'll see how different floor plan mixes affect traffic, how concessions strategies shift during a lease-up versus a stabilized asset, and how management style varies from site to site. That exposure compounds quickly. Leasing specialists who've covered multiple properties tend to move into senior leasing roles, leasing manager positions, or even community manager tracks faster than peers who've only worked one asset, because they've already seen the range of situations a manager has to handle.

Strong candidates for this role are comfortable being the new face in the room repeatedly. You're introduced to a team, expected to perform immediately, and then you move on. That requires genuine interpersonal range and the ability to read a community's culture fast. Previous experience in leasing, hospitality, or sales gives you the toolkit, but adaptability is what separates people who thrive in floating roles from people who burn out in them. If you've ever worked a role where the environment changed constantly and you found that energizing rather than exhausting, that's the signal this is worth pursuing.

job.title: Regional Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Regional maintenance leadership at a multi-site level is a different job than being a strong on-site tech. The hands matter, but so does the ability to coordinate people, manage vendor relationships, and keep multiple properties moving at the same time. Ackermann Group, a Midwest real estate and property management organization with roots going back to 1938, is hiring a Regional Maintenance Supervisor to do exactly that across communities in the greater Indianapolis area.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your days split between being on the tools and stepping back to manage the picture. You'll troubleshoot and repair across trades, including plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting, while also keeping make-ready schedules on track, ensuring vacant units hit market-ready condition, and making sure amenity spaces stay presentable. Snow removal, after-hours emergency response, and preventive maintenance coordination are all part of the job. You'll manage supplies and parts inventory, negotiate with vendors and service providers, and keep the maintenance budget in order across your communities.

On the people side, you'll participate in hiring maintenance staff, run regular team meetings, and work directly with Community and Regional Managers to stay aligned on priorities. Capital improvement projects will also land on your plate at the planning and execution level. This role sits at the intersection of trades skill, supervisory accountability, and operational coordination.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Three or more years of broad maintenance experience, with supervisory experience required
  • EPA Type I and II Certification required; CPO certification preferred
  • Comfortable working in Microsoft Outlook and Office products
  • Valid driver's license, proof of insurance, and reliable transportation (this is a multi-site role)
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The candidates who tend to do well in regional maintenance roles have usually managed the tension between being the most technically capable person on the team and knowing when to let their staff take the lead. Strong vendors relationships help, too. Regional supervisors who've built a reliable bench of contractors they trust, and who can negotiate on rates without burning goodwill, make their own jobs considerably easier over time.

The Organization Behind the Role

Ackermann has been developing and managing properties in the Midwest for over 85 years. That kind of longevity usually signals stability in staffing, consistent processes, and genuine investment in the people who stay. This role comes with competitive hourly pay, quarterly bonus potential, lease renewal commission eligibility, health benefits, a 401k with company match, paid time off including your birthday, an employee rent discount at Ackermann communities, and career coaching and development. The standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies as directed by the Regional Facilities Director. The after-hours component is real and worth factoring in as you evaluate the fit.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Fox Point in Old Farm Apartments
job.description:
A prospect walks into the leasing office at Fox Point, unannounced, mid-morning. You're already on a call, a work order is waiting in the queue, and someone at the front desk needs a package. That overlap is a typical Tuesday in this role.

What the Job Covers

The Customer Experience Specialist at Fox Point in Old Farm Apartments serves as the primary point of contact for prospects, residents, and vendors. Cottonwood Residential properties run self-guided tours, so part of this role is keeping those units clean, staged, and tour-ready every day, not just on weekends or when traffic is expected.

On the leasing side, you'll field prospect questions, walk people through availability and pricing, assist with applications, and follow up with leads to support occupancy goals. You won't hold a standalone leasing title, but conversion and traffic outcomes are very much part of what this position touches.

Day-to-day resident support takes up a real portion of the shift: package retrieval, key distribution, work order entry, and acting as the go-between for residents and the maintenance team. You'll also walk the property routinely to check that amenities, common areas, and tour paths meet company standards. Community events and social media posts are part of the job too, though not the core of it.

What You Need to Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year of face-to-face customer service, sales, hospitality, or administrative experience
  • Comfort learning property management software (Cottonwood uses Entrata)
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office
  • Ability to stand, walk the property, and occasionally lift items over 50 pounds
  • Flexibility to work extended hours when needed, including early arrivals before office open
  • Multifamily experience is a plus, not a requirement

Strong candidates in this type of role know how to context-switch without dropping the ball. You might handle a frustrated resident call, then immediately greet a prospect walking through the door, and neither interaction should feel rushed or secondhand. That ability to reset quickly between interactions is what actually separates good performance from average in this seat.

Millcreek is an active rental market with a mix of long-term residents and younger renters who lean on self-guided and digital-first experiences before ever talking to someone in person. Being comfortable with that tech-forward leasing model matters here. Cottonwood was an early adopter of self-guided tours, and this role is part of making that experience work at the property level.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
This role runs on two core skill sets: technical breadth and team management. You need both. A Maintenance Supervisor at a residential community who can diagnose an HVAC issue but can't get a team moving efficiently is only half the job. Same goes the other direction. Waypoint Management Services is hiring someone who can hold both sides together at their Miami property.

The Technical Side

The hands-on work covers the full range: plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, pool and amenity upkeep, pressure washing, painting, and preventive maintenance on HVAC systems and building infrastructure. You'll also manage the make-ready process for vacant units, which means inspecting, coordinating repairs, and getting apartments to move-in standard. EPA Section 608 Type I and II Certification is required before you start. CPO is preferred, which matters in Miami where pool compliance is taken seriously year-round given the climate and usage frequency.

You'll manage vendor and contractor relationships too, making sure outside work gets done safely, on schedule, and to the property's standards. That requires clear communication and follow-through, not just scheduling calls.

The Leadership Side

You'll assign daily work orders, train and support the maintenance team, and keep operations running across the community at whatever pace the day demands. Maintenance records, documentation, and inventory management fall under your watch. That's not glamorous work, but it's what keeps the operation from unraveling. Strong supervisory candidates have usually learned that the paper trail matters as much as the wrench work.

Emergency on-call coverage is part of this role. Evenings, weekends, and holidays happen. Miami summers bring weather events that can create multiple simultaneous issues. If that's a dealbreaker, better to know now.

What Makes the Difference Here

Candidates who stand out in this role typically have a reputation for proactive property inspections rather than reactive fixes. Catching a failing component during a routine walk saves significantly more time and money than addressing the same issue after a resident complaint or a failed unit turn. If your default is to wait for a work order, this position will be a friction point.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; technical training or certifications are a plus
  • Prior multifamily or residential maintenance experience required
  • Previous supervisory or team leadership experience strongly preferred
  • EPA Section 608 Type I and II Certification required
  • CPO Certification preferred
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds independently; up to 50 with assistance
  • Comfortable working outdoors in South Florida weather conditions year-round

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off, floating holidays, an employee housing discount, and performance-based bonus opportunities. The benefits package is solid for a residential property management role at this level.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
Attention to detail, calendar management, and the ability to hold many open threads at once without dropping any. Those are the core skills this role runs on. Property Management Associates is hiring an Administrative Assistant to support both their Residential Department and their COO out of Culver City, and the scope is genuinely wide.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On any given day you might be updating listings on RentCafe, auditing utility accounts, tracking down a city ordinance update that affects a property in the portfolio, and then pivoting to manage the COO's calendar before end of day. The residential portfolio runs into the thousands of units across Los Angeles and Orange County, so the data you maintain (spreadsheets, databases, advertising records) has real downstream consequences. Inaccurate listings mean bad traffic. Missed utility setup steps mean billing headaches that property managers have to untangle later.

You'll also occasionally provide front-office support at individual properties throughout LA and Orange County. That's not a surprise drop-in request, but it is part of the job, so you'll need to be comfortable working across locations and interacting with residents, vendors, owners, and site staff with the same professionalism you'd bring to a corporate setting.

Training coordination also falls to this role. Keeping residential department training schedules organized and on track requires the same follow-through muscle as the rest of the job: knowing where things stand, what's outstanding, and what needs a nudge.

Skills That Make Someone Good at This

  • Intermediate to advanced Excel and Outlook. Spreadsheets are central here, not occasional.
  • Strong written communication. You'll be drafting correspondence to a wide range of people, residents to ownership.
  • Comfort learning new online systems quickly. RentCafe and similar platforms aren't complicated, but you have to be willing to figure them out without hand-holding.
  • Genuine organizational discipline. Not the "I'm a pretty organized person" version. The kind that holds up when you have six competing deadlines.
  • Yardi experience is a plus, as is any background in residential property management.

The honest difference between a strong candidate and an average one here is initiative. The COO and the residential department need someone who tracks things down before being asked twice and flags problems early. If you need step-by-step direction to complete most tasks, this role will feel like friction for both you and the team.

The Company and the Role's Place in It

PMA has operated in Southern California for over 30 years and manages both residential and commercial properties at scale. For someone earlier in their property management career, the exposure in this role is real: you're working directly with a COO, touching regulatory research, advertising operations, utility billing, and training logistics across a large portfolio. Those are threads that connect to property accounting, compliance, and operations work. If you eventually want to move into a property manager role, a regional coordinator position, or an operations-focused role at a larger company, the visibility you'd build here is useful.

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contribution, a 401(k) with company match, and paid time off. There's also an early Friday release. The role is full-time and based in Culver City.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Las Vegas, NV
job.description:
It's 7:45 a.m. and a resident just flagged a leak under their kitchen sink. Before morning is out, you've also swapped a breaker, walked a make-ready with the manager, and logged a punch list item on a vacant unit that's supposed to turn by Friday. That's a solid Tuesday at a Berkshire property in Las Vegas.

What the Work Looks Like

Berkshire Residential Investments manages its own portfolio, so maintenance techs here work inside a vertically integrated operation. You're not bouncing between third-party accounts. You own the physical condition of one community, and that ownership shows up in how the property performs. Curb appeal affects traffic. Unresolved work orders drag resident satisfaction scores. A sloppy make-ready can push a turn past market timing.

Day to day, you'll handle the full range of residential maintenance: plumbing, appliances, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You'll support management in keeping the community up to corporate standards, enforce safety protocols, and keep the shop organized, inventory accounted for, and keys secured. Inspections are part of the rhythm too. Berkshire puts a real premium on how their communities look from the street, and you'll share that responsibility.

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with computers and related software for logging work orders and communication
  • Strong written and spoken English skills
  • A service mindset that extends to residents, prospective residents, and teammates equally

The candidate who stands out here brings genuine versatility. Las Vegas properties run hard year-round. HVAC demand peaks in summer, and the desert climate creates its own maintenance patterns: dust infiltration, UV wear on exterior materials, and cooling systems that don't get much of a break. A tech who's worked Nevada properties before will recognize those cycles without needing a ramp-up period.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, solid insurance, and a 25% rent discount. They describe themselves as a people-first organization, and their in-house ownership model backs that up. When the company owns and manages its own assets, there's alignment between keeping residents satisfied and protecting long-term NOI. That's a different environment than a fee management shop where the priorities can drift.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing communities run on leasing cycles that leave little room for drift. When occupancy targets slip or renewal momentum stalls, everything else on the budget feels it. The Leasing Manager role at Redstone Residential exists right at that pressure point: close enough to the Community Manager to understand the full operational picture, and close enough to prospective and current residents to actually move the needle.

Redstone manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the largest third-party student housing operators in the country. Their conventional multi-family portfolio is growing alongside their student housing business, so the people joining now will have real visibility into how a scaled, expanding organization operates. This position is based at the community level, compensated at $15 per hour, and classified as full-time, non-exempt.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A lot of this job is people work: touring prospects, fielding calls, responding to emails, and keeping the energy on the leasing floor focused and positive. You'll work inside Redstone's Entrata-based leasing workflow, support SEO and social marketing efforts through company-standard tools, and help the team hit weekly and monthly leasing goals through both new lease conversions and renewal campaigns. You'll also maintain resident ledgers to keep balances accurate, which means you're not purely front-of-house. There's real administrative responsibility woven into this role alongside the sales and relationship work.

The Community Manager sets the direction, but a good Leasing Manager keeps things moving when the manager is pulled into budget reviews or vendor conversations. That means you'll interact with residents, prospects, fellow leasing staff, and occasionally ownership-facing reports. The team dynamics here matter as much as individual performance.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Strong customer service instincts, especially with residents who have complaints or questions about their ledger
  • Comfortable in a high-traffic environment where priorities shift mid-morning and the phone doesn't stop
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office, Gmail, Google Drive, and Dropbox
  • High school diploma or GED required; some college experience is a plus
  • A natural communicator who can keep a prospect engaged on a tour and write a clear follow-up email an hour later

One honest note about student housing specifically: lease-up seasons are intense. There are stretches where traffic spikes and the team runs hard for weeks. If you've worked in retail or hospitality during peak seasons, you already know the rhythm. It's manageable, but it's real. The teams that do well here tend to be genuinely collaborative rather than purely competitive with each other.

Redstone offers health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, three paid service days, paid parental leave, and a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match. They also include a continued education program, which is worth noting for anyone who sees this as a step toward a Community Manager or regional role down the road. Leasing Manager experience at a company this size translates well when you're ready to make that move.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work in student housing runs at a different tempo than conventional multifamily. At The Verge at Grand Forks, a Scion Group community serving the University of North Dakota market, turns cluster at the end of academic leases, service requests come from residents with limited patience and even less knowledge of how apartments work, and the on-call rotation is real. The Facilities Technician role here draws on a specific combination of trade knowledge, communication skill, and organizational discipline that most general maintenance positions don't require in equal measure.

The Skills This Role Uses Every Day

The technical foundation is broad but not exotic. You'll work across appliance repair, basic carpentry, plumbing and fixture repair, painting, and electrical and lighting. HVAC-adjacent tasks show up regularly: cleaning coils and condensers, maintaining air filters, lubricating equipment as part of a structured preventive maintenance schedule. The job also requires you to document your work clearly, including parts used, follow-up needed, and time spent. That documentation habit is something many technicians underinvest in, and it matters here. Scion runs standardized operating procedures, and your daily notes feed into that system.

The communication side carries equal weight. Residents in student communities often submit vague service requests, don't know how to describe a problem accurately, and may be difficult to reach for scheduling. Translating unclear requests into efficient repair visits, setting expectations, and closing the loop with residents takes interpersonal skill that goes beyond being polite. It shapes how the property's service reputation gets built.

What the Role Builds

Technicians who move through student housing tend to develop faster diagnostic instincts than those in stable, lower-turnover communities. The volume and variety of turn work at lease end, preparing apartments for the next round of residents, builds make-ready efficiency that transfers directly to any multifamily environment. You'll also develop familiarity with preventive maintenance scheduling, which is a skill set that opens doors to lead technician and maintenance supervisor roles over time.

The CPO certification, required or intended within six months of hire, adds a credential that's broadly portable across properties with pool amenities.

What Scion Expects You to Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver's license
  • Certified Pool Operator credential, or commitment to obtain it within six months
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule that includes after-hours and weekend emergency response
  • Physical capacity to stand for a full shift and lift up to 100 pounds
  • Basic computer proficiency for work order and documentation systems
  • Clear written and verbal communication habits

Scion offers health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, PTO, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

job.title: Front Desk Associate - West Ocean (32-hours)
job.description:
It's 7 pm on a Saturday and a resident's guest is at the front desk, a package hasn't been picked up, and the lobby needs a quick walk before the evening crowd comes through. That's the rhythm of this role, and the people who thrive in it know how to stay composed, courteous, and organized all at once.

The Role at West Ocean

Action Property Management is hiring a part-time Front Desk Associate for West Ocean, a community in Long Beach. This is a Thursday through Sunday position, 2:00 pm to 10:30 pm, at $21.00 per hour. The shift runs through the busiest window of resident activity, so your presence at the front desk directly shapes how residents and guests experience the building every evening.

Day to day, you'll manage lobby access control, greet residents and guests, handle incoming calls, and distribute parcels. You'll complete the Daily Activity Report at the end of each shift and maintain the front desk area, lobby, and elevator bank. When resident or guest concerns come up, you're the first point of contact, which means your judgment and follow-through matter. Familiarity with the association's governing documents is part of the job, not optional background knowledge.

What Action Is Looking For

Candidates must be 18 or older and able to clear a pre-employment background check and drug screening. At least one year of customer service experience is required. Action specifically values candidates who come from hospitality, luxury retail, or fine dining, environments where presentation, pace, and service standards are non-negotiable. Hospitality Management students and recent graduates are a strong fit here.

  • Polished, professional appearance and demeanor
  • Proactive approach to resident and guest needs
  • Strong judgment and a solutions-first mindset
  • Positive, collaborative attitude with the broader team

Action Property Management is the largest privately owned HOA management company in the West, serving more than 300 communities across nine offices with a team of nearly 900 people. That scale means real infrastructure behind you: training, technology, and a defined career path if you want to grow in community management.

One thing worth noting for candidates new to HOA management: concierge-style front desk work at a residential community runs differently than hotel or retail. Residents aren't guests passing through. They live there, and long-term relationships with the front desk team matter to them. The skill set transfers well from hospitality, but the context is its own. Strong performers in this role often move into Community Assistant or Community Manager tracks over time.

Qualifying team members receive medical, dental, vision, pet insurance, 401(k) with company match, life and disability coverage, and paid time off including vacation, sick time, and company holidays.

job.title: Director of Service & Construction - Houston
job.description:
Picture yourself standing in the middle of a Houston property mid-renovation, punch list in hand, while simultaneously fielding a call from a regional VP about capex variance and coordinating an insurance claim from last month's weather event. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

The Scope of the Position

AIR Communities, one of the largest multifamily ownership groups in the country, is hiring a Director of Service and Construction to anchor their Houston market operations. This sits within AIR's Asset Quality and Service team, which means you're embedded in operations rather than siloed in a construction department. You'll work directly alongside community managers, service managers, general managers, regional property managers, and VPs to keep the portfolio performing.

The construction side is genuinely broad. You'll own project management and oversight for renovation programs including AIR's internal "AIR Edge" upgrade initiative, coordinate design-build workflows, manage vendor and contractor relationships, and keep projects on schedule and within budget. On the compliance side, you'll track and ensure execution of jurisdictional requirements such as REAC, MOR, 40-year inspections, facade and balcony reviews, and SCEP obligations. Those aren't checkbox items here. They're a core part of what you're accountable for.

Beyond construction, the role carries real financial weight. You'll support annual capex PCA compilation for budget reviews, contribute to R&M and COE budget development and execution, and work with property-level P&Ls to support NOI and EGI performance. Power BI and Excel proficiency are required, and the ability to run basic IRR analysis will come up. Familiarity with Entrata, Coupa, Brivo, and SmartRent is also part of the day-to-day toolkit.

Acquisitions and dispositions are part of the job as well. You'll participate in PCA reviews, on-site inspections, and budget development during due diligence, and take point on post-acquisition renovation leadership once a property joins the portfolio.

Regular travel across Houston-area communities is required, along with periodic travel to national-level meetings.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • A degree in construction management, engineering, architecture, property management, or a closely related field (strongly preferred)
  • At least four to six years of multifamily or facilities maintenance and operations experience
  • Demonstrated experience managing service operations across a portfolio of multifamily assets
  • Hands-on experience running multiple construction projects simultaneously and independently

The candidates who tend to excel in roles like this are the ones who can hold both sides of the job without letting one drag down the other. Construction directors who can't read a P&L become cost centers. Ops leaders who can't manage contractors become bottlenecks during capex season. AIR is specifically looking for someone who bridges those two worlds, which is part of what makes this role worth paying attention to from a career standpoint.

In terms of trajectory, this type of regional director role in a national platform is one of the cleaner paths toward VP of Asset Quality, Director of Operations, or even regional COO work. The combination of financial fluency, construction oversight, compliance accountability, and team development you'll build here translates directly into senior leadership positions across both owner-operator and third-party management environments.

Base compensation is $145,000 to $165,000 with an annual target bonus. AIR also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, a rent discount at AIR communities, paid parental leave of up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and reimbursement for job-related certifications and licenses.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Residential property maintenance in Northern Virginia runs at a specific pace. Alexandria's rental stock skews toward older mid-rise and garden-style buildings that carry real mechanical complexity, and residents in this market hold their communities to high standards. Bozzuto operates at the upper end of that expectation, and this Maintenance Technician role is central to meeting it.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, the work spans service ticket resolution, preventative maintenance, and make-ready preparation on vacant units. Turns are where you'll see the full range of the trade: HVAC checks, plumbing fixes, appliance repairs, punch list items that need to be caught and closed before a new resident moves in. Beyond turns, you're responsible for the physical condition of the community overall, including grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general cleanliness. Bozzuto communities carry a premium presentation standard, so attention to how a space looks matters as much as whether it works.

The role includes weekend and evening availability, plus participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's a real part of the job. On-call maintenance is one of the more demanding aspects of property-level work, and candidates who have done it before will have a better sense of what they're signing up for.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • Some background in building maintenance or a trades education, at a beginner-to-intermediate skill level in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Reliable personal transportation for commuting and on-call response
  • Physical capability to lift and move 25 to 50 pounds frequently during the course of normal duties
  • Comfort using property management software, apps, and work order systems
  • Strong communication skills and a professional presentation when interacting with residents

One thing worth noting: Bozzuto will cover the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification after your 12-month anniversary. For technicians who haven't yet earned it, that's a meaningful credential to add without paying out of pocket. EPA 608 Universal opens doors across commercial and residential HVAC work, so the investment Bozzuto makes here has real career value beyond this specific position.

The salary range for this role is $50,000 to $51,500, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Senior Maintenance Technician - Cortland North Brookhaven
job.description:
It's 10 PM on a Tuesday and a resident calls in: no heat. You're on call, you know HVAC, and you go handle it. That's a normal part of this job, and it's worth knowing upfront.

Cortland's North Brookhaven community is looking for a Senior Maintenance Technician to function as the technical backbone of the maintenance team. This position sits just below the Service Manager in the org structure, which means you're mentoring junior techs, stepping into the lead role when the manager is out, and owning the more complex work orders that need real diagnostic skill rather than a basic fix.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

The bulk of the work covers advanced troubleshooting and repair across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and general building systems. Preventative maintenance on HVAC equipment is a consistent part of the schedule, not an afterthought. You'll also monitor building and security systems including automatic doors and cameras, manage the team's tools and parts inventory, document completed work, and flag recurring issues so they get addressed before they become bigger problems.

Unsafe conditions get corrected fast. That's a non-negotiable part of this role, and you're expected to make sure your team moves with the same urgency you do. Resident interactions come with the territory too. When you're fixing something in someone's home, how you communicate matters as much as how well you repair it.

On-call rotation is real here. Emergencies don't schedule themselves, and this position participates in after-hours response. If that's a dealbreaker, that's worth knowing now rather than after you start.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • Universal EPA 608 certification required; CPO preferred
  • 3 to 5+ years in maintenance, facilities, or multifamily housing
  • Advanced skills in HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliance repair, and building systems
  • Comfortable mentoring junior technicians and supporting team leadership
  • Strong troubleshooting instincts and solid communication with residents and staff
  • Physically able to lift heavy items, use tools safely, climb ladders, and work in varying weather
  • Willing to participate in on-call and emergency response schedules
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

The candidates who tend to stand out at this level aren't just technically sharp. They anticipate what the team needs, keep the preventative maintenance program on track without being told, and treat resident communication as part of the craft. A tech who can fix a condenser unit and explain the situation to a resident without making them feel like an inconvenience is genuinely hard to find.

Cortland is a vertically integrated multifamily owner and operator, ranked among the top 10 in the country. They handle design, construction, and property operations in-house, which tends to mean there's more internal structure and resources available to the maintenance team than you'd find at a smaller fee management shop.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company manages more than 720 million square feet of commercial space across the United States, which means an assistant property manager here isn't working in a vacuum. The institutional clients, the reporting standards, the operational discipline , all of it runs at a scale that teaches you things a smaller shop simply can't.

This role sits on the commercial side, covering office, retail, and industrial properties. Houston is an appropriate market for that mix. The energy sector still drives significant office demand in submarkets like the Energy Corridor and Westchase, while the broader metro continues to absorb industrial space at a pace that keeps third-party management firms like LPC consistently busy. You'll be working within that context, supporting a Property Manager across the day-to-day and longer-cycle responsibilities that keep institutional assets running cleanly.

On the financial side, expect to get hands-on with operating expense reconciliations , CAM and OpEx , which means coordinating closely with accounting and understanding how lease language translates into billable charges. You'll assist in preparing monthly reporting packages for clients, reviewing vendor invoices against authorization limits and management agreement terms, and helping with budget preparation. This is the kind of financial exposure that builds real competency, not surface-level familiarity.

Operationally, the role covers tenant relations, lease administration (setup, changes, system updates), vendor procurement and bidding, and coordinating move-ins and move-outs including walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams. You'll also support emergency response planning and participate in required drills. Property inspections happen monthly at minimum, and travel to assigned sites is part of the job. This is fully in-office.

What Lincoln is looking for

  • A bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience; 1 to 2 years of related work in commercial property management
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office, with comfort in AP and CMMS platforms a plus
  • Ability to work through financial terms and calculations , percentages, reconciliations, basic analysis , without needing to be walked through every step
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to handle tenant interactions professionally
  • Strong organizational habits and a genuine interest in building toward a management role
  • Current U.S. work authorization, without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future

Where this role typically leads: assistant property managers who develop fluency in CAM reconciliations, client reporting, and lease administration at a firm like LPC tend to move into property manager roles carrying their own portfolios. The combination of institutional-grade financial discipline and direct tenant management exposure is exactly what that next step requires. Candidates who stand out are those who treat the reporting and reconciliation work as a skill to master rather than an administrative chore , that's where the real learning compounds.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Bella Vista at Elk Grove Apartments
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Bella Vista at Elk Grove is a 200-plus unit apartment community, and MG Properties needs a technician who can move across all the trades without losing momentum. The day-to-day covers the full spectrum: service requests from residents, appliance diagnostics and repairs, plumbing and electrical work, painting, and HVAC. You'll also handle turns, which means executing make-readies and working through punch lists to get vacant units rent-ready on schedule. Groundskeeping and common area upkeep are part of the rhythm too. On-call rotation is real here, so you should go in knowing that after-hours calls will come, and your response time matters both for resident satisfaction and for protecting the property.

Monthly bonuses are part of the compensation structure, which signals that MG Properties ties performance to reward directly. The base range runs $22 to $26 per hour depending on experience, with profit sharing, a 401k match, and rental discounts rounding out the package.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience, ideally at a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • A service-oriented approach with residents. Technical skill matters, but so does how you communicate when someone's heat is out
  • Reliable transportation (required, not optional)
  • Comfort with on-call rotation and the flexibility that comes with it

Where This Role Leads

Technician roles at mid-size regional operators like MG Properties are worth taking seriously from a career-building standpoint. If you're consistent across turns, responsive on call, and start picking up HVAC certification or EPA 608 if you don't already have it, you're building the profile of a Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor within a few years. Regional operators that manage communities across multiple markets often promote internally because institutional knowledge about their systems and standards is genuinely valuable. The trades experience you accumulate here, especially on a larger garden-style property, transfers cleanly to Class A communities, lease-up assignments, or lead roles with broader scope.

MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, so there's organizational depth to grow within. That's a different situation than joining a smaller operator where advancement depends on someone leaving.

job.title: Manager, Resident Experience (Delinquency & Eviction Specialist)
job.description:
Delinquency management at a single-family rental platform operates differently than it does at a conventional multifamily property. The portfolio is geographically spread, the resident base is varied, and the compliance requirements shift constantly across jurisdictions. This role sits at the center of all of that.

What This Role Actually Involves

Roofstock is hiring a Manager to lead its Delinquency and Eviction team in Dallas. The team handles the full cycle of delinquency resolution across a large SFR portfolio: monitoring DQ rates, managing Legal Rent Demand Notice programs, overseeing bankruptcy cases, and coordinating HAP and Section 8 delinquency. You'll own the team's delinquency percentage as a KPI and report it directly to owner clients in monthly business reviews, which means you're accountable to the data and to the people whose assets depend on it.

Day to day, you'll supervise a tiered team of Jr. Specialists, Specialists, and HAP Specialists. You'll run 1:1s, set performance targets, handle recruiting when seats open, and build training materials that keep pace with changes in local and state eviction law. You'll also manage relationships with eviction attorneys in multiple markets, which includes onboarding new counsel as the portfolio expands into new geographies.

The cross-functional piece is real. You'll coordinate with property managers, legal, and senior leadership, and you'll work directly with product and engineering teams on workflow automation. Roofstock is a tech-forward company, and this team relies on automated workflows to manage volume. If you've used AI tools or process automation in a collections or eviction context, that carries weight here.

Qualifications Worth Highlighting

  • At least two years in property management and two years managing a team
  • Hands-on experience with collections, delinquency resolution, or eviction processes
  • Comfort with property management software (Yardi, AppFolio, or similar) and reporting tools
  • Strong grasp of eviction procedures: filings, writs, and attorney coordination
  • Familiarity with Section 8 or HAP programs is a genuine differentiator here
  • Experience with workflow automation or AI-assisted team tools is a plus

Where This Role Leads

Managers who build real fluency in delinquency operations at scale tend to move toward Director-level roles in resident relations, asset management operations, or portfolio compliance. The skill set compounds well: you're developing data interpretation habits, regulatory literacy across multiple states, vendor management experience, and the ability to translate operational metrics into client-facing narratives. Those skills transfer directly into senior ops roles, especially as the SFR sector continues to professionalize and institutional investors demand tighter reporting from their management partners.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this specific role is the ability to hold two things at once: empathy for residents navigating genuine hardship, and accountability to portfolio performance. The best delinquency managers know how to structure a payment plan conversation and still hit their DQ targets. That balance is harder to teach than eviction law.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Leases turn together, renewals happen in waves, and the resident base cycles almost entirely each year. If you want to build leasing skills quickly, a student property compresses years of conventional experience into a single lease-up cycle. The Experience Team Member role at The Reserve at Mt. Plainant, Scion's property serving Central Michigan University, puts you at the center of that cycle.

Where the Skills Come From

This role draws on three skill sets simultaneously: sales, marketing, and property operations. On the sales side, you're conducting tours, fielding objections, and following up with prospective residents who are often making their first-ever housing decision. That's a specific kind of consultative selling that sharpens quickly because the feedback loop is short. On the marketing side, you're contributing to social media, identifying local outreach opportunities, and helping plan resident engagement events. These aren't isolated tasks. In student housing, community programming directly supports renewal rates and referral traffic, so you see the connection between effort and outcome in real time.

The administrative layer matters too. Package management, maintenance request coordination, office organization, and after-hours lockout coverage are the operational basics that every property depends on. Doing them well at this stage builds habits that carry forward into assistant manager and manager roles, where operational discipline is the difference between a clean T-12 and a messy one.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

During the academic year, the rhythm is prospect-heavy on weekends and operations-heavy during the week. Summer and Turn periods shift everything toward move-out coordination, make-ready oversight, and getting units back to market condition before the incoming class arrives. Turn at a student property is concentrated and demanding. You'll be expected to be available during those periods, along with holidays when leasing decisions often happen. The on-call rotation for after-hours coverage is part of the role and worth understanding before you apply.

What This Role Builds Toward

Scion operates a significant student housing portfolio, which means internal advancement is a realistic path. Experience Team Members who develop strong leasing metrics and operational habits typically move into assistant manager roles, where they take on delinquency tracking, leasing reporting, and direct involvement in budgeting conversations. The skills you build here, particularly reading prospect objections and turning them into actionable feedback for management, translate directly into the property management track at any operator, student or conventional.

Strong candidates bring genuine comfort with a diverse student population, flexibility when priorities shift mid-day, and enough self-direction to manage tasks without close supervision. Scion is specific about work authorization: all candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S., and visa sponsorship isn't available.

job.title: Maintenance Technician I (Markham)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance role covering the full scope of day-to-day upkeep at a Prometheus residential community in Cupertino. The bulk of your time splits between two areas: completing service requests from residents and turning units between leases. Turns require moving through a punch list efficiently. You're diagnosing and repairing plumbing, appliances, carpentry, electrical, and paint issues across both occupied and vacant units. Minor repairs are yours to complete independently. Major mechanical systems require your troubleshooting skills even when the fix escalates to a specialist.

On-call availability is part of the job. Emergencies don't follow business hours, and Prometheus builds standby pay and on-call premium pay into the compensation structure to reflect that reality. The hourly range runs $27.75 to $28.75, with semi-annual discretionary bonuses and additional incentives tied to renovations, lease-up activity, and referrals.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, hands-on rather than supervisory
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and painting at a residential level
  • Comfort with basic computer use for work order systems
  • Physical capability to handle outdoor work, lifting up to 50 lbs., climbing, and sustained physical activity throughout the shift
  • A high school diploma or GED
  • Strong communication skills, written and verbal, in English

Where This Role Can Take You

Maintenance Technician I is genuinely one of the better entry points into a long-term property management career. The skills you build here compound quickly. Technicians who develop strong turn efficiency and can handle a wide range of repairs without escalation tend to move into Technician II roles, then Lead Tech, and eventually Maintenance Supervisor or Facilities Manager positions. At companies with a large portfolio like Prometheus, that path is internal rather than requiring a job change. The renovation bonus structure signals that there's also a track toward capex project work for techs who prove reliable on larger-scope repairs.

Prometheus extends benefits that are notable in the multifamily space: fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision for eligible employees and dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts. The housing discount in particular is worth noting for someone working in the Bay Area. These aren't perks to gloss over.

If you're two years into apartment maintenance and want a stable platform to develop your trade skills and build toward a supervisory role, this posting is worth a close look.

job.title: Leasing Consultant- Lease Up
job.description:
It's a Saturday morning at Evolve at Lake Norman. A couple walks in, still deciding. You've got maybe 45 minutes to show them something that feels like home. That's the core of this job.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is staffing up a lease-up community in Mooresville, NC, which means traffic is high and the pressure to convert is real. This isn't a stabilized asset where you coast on renewals. Evolve at Lake Norman needs to fill units, and your leasing activity directly drives that.

What the Job Covers

Day to day, you're handling incoming leads across phone, email, and web, then converting those conversations into tours and applications. You'll walk prospects through units, manage the paperwork side of the leasing process (applications, verifications, move-in docs), and follow up consistently with anyone who didn't sign on the spot. You'll also support renewal goals and help maintain the common areas and office so the property always looks ready to show.

Beyond leasing, you'll help plan and attend resident events. Hawthorne treats community engagement as part of the job, not an afterthought. You'll also track what competitors are doing and help with social media and local outreach to keep the property visible.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off per week to keep the total at 40 hours. Occasional evening availability may come up for events.

What Hawthorne Wants to See

  • One year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Strong communication skills across in-person, phone, and written channels
  • Comfort with objection handling and the ability to guide a prospect toward a decision
  • A valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or GED
  • CALP accreditation is a plus if you already have it

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental leave, and company-paid life insurance.

One thing worth knowing about lease-up roles specifically: they build skills faster than stabilized properties. You'll handle higher volume, sharper objections, and more objection types in your first six months here than you might see in two years at a fully occupied community. Consultants who perform well in lease-ups tend to move into assistant community manager positions quickly. Hawthorne has a formal career path program designed to support exactly that kind of progression.

job.title: Maintenance Technician 2 - Austin Park Apartments
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Austin Park Apartments, a 226-unit community in Miamisburg, Ohio, you'll work through the full cycle of residential maintenance alongside a team that handles everything from service requests to make-readies. A typical week pulls in a range of work: turning a vacant unit through the make-ready process, knocking out intermediate repairs across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and appliances, and keeping up with the exterior grounds and janitorial tasks that hold a property's curb appeal together. You'll also participate in move-in and move-out inspections, help manage maintenance inventory, and rotate through after-hours emergency call coverage when the schedule requires it.

Pool water management and seasonal snow removal are part of the job too. These aren't afterthoughts. They're the kinds of tasks that define how a community looks and how residents experience it day to day. Preventive maintenance rounds out the rhythm, keeping equipment running before problems get expensive.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience covering multiple trade areas
  • Comfort working both independently and as part of a maintenance team
  • Attention to detail on punch list items during make-readies and inspections
  • A valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • EPA Type I and II, CAMT, or CPO certifications are a real advantage here, not required but genuinely valued
  • Willingness to participate in an on-call emergency rotation

What This Role Builds

Ackermann Group positions this as a training role by design. If you've got solid foundational skills but haven't yet worked across all trade areas with consistent depth, this is the structure that closes those gaps. Working at a 226-unit community gives you volume. You'll see a high enough mix of unit conditions, repair types, and resident interactions that your diagnostic instincts sharpen faster than they would at a smaller property.

Technicians who come in reliable and detail-oriented tend to move toward a Maintenance Technician 1 role or eventually a Maintenance Supervisor position as they build proficiency. The path is real, especially inside a company like Ackermann, which has operated in the Midwest since 1938 and promotes career coaching as part of its employee investment. The quarterly bonus structure and lease renewal commission potential are also worth noting because those aren't typical for a maintenance role, and they signal that Ackermann treats this position as a contributor to the property's overall performance, not just a labor function.

One honest note on the on-call rotation: after-hours emergency requests are part of the job. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., but rotating emergency coverage is a real commitment. If you've handled that before and you're comfortable with it, you'll fit the expectation. If it's new, know going in that it comes with the role.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
You're sitting across from a resident whose rent posted late, and before the conversation ends, you need to understand the ledger, reset the relationship, and make sure the paperwork reflects what actually happened. That's a representative two minutes in this role.

Waypoint Management Services is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for their multifamily community in Daytona Beach, FL. The position sits directly below the Community Manager and touches nearly every functional area of the property: leasing performance, financial oversight, resident relations, and administrative compliance. Weekend availability is required as part of the rotation.

What the Role Demands on Day One

You need to arrive with at least two years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience. The financial side of this role isn't introductory work. You'll be tracking delinquency, supporting eviction processes, contributing to rent recommendations based on occupancy data and market surveys, and keeping the rent roll and lease records accurate. Yardi experience is preferred and will shorten your ramp time considerably. Microsoft Office fluency, comfort with social media platforms, and strong written communication are baseline requirements.

On the leasing side, you'll support the team's performance and training, help execute marketing strategy, and monitor competitor activity to keep the property positioned correctly in the local market. The Daytona Beach multifamily market sees seasonal occupancy shifts tied to tourism and the university population, so reading traffic patterns and adjusting strategy accordingly is a real part of the job, not a theoretical one.

What the Role Builds Over Time

Assistant Community Managers who treat the financial reporting as a learning tool, not just an administrative task, are the ones who move into Community Manager roles. This position gives you direct exposure to NOI-level thinking: understanding how delinquency, make-ready timelines, renewals, and occupancy interact to produce financial results. That systems-level view is what separates candidates who grow into full property leadership from those who stay in supporting roles.

You'll also build skills in team development, which is undervalued at this stage but critical later. Supporting leasing staff means diagnosing why numbers are soft and correcting the behavior, not just flagging the outcome.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Minimum 2 years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience preferred
  • Yardi experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Weekend rotation availability required

Waypoint offers a compensation package that includes monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, 401(k) with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one with progressive increases, two floating days annually, commuter benefits, an employee referral program, and professional development training.

job.title: Community Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Antler Creek is a new build-to-rent community in Oklahoma City, and this role runs daily operations there solo. You're the only on-site team member, which means you handle leasing, resident experience, property appearance, vendor coordination, and community standards without a colleague in the next office. Centralized support teams back you up on applications and move-ins, but the face of the community is you.

On the leasing side, you'll manage the full prospect journey: responding to inquiries, conducting tours, tracking traffic and conversion metrics, and pushing toward occupancy targets on a lease-up timeline. You'll also support outreach through local events, digital campaigns, and partnerships with nearby businesses. When a prospect becomes a resident, you coordinate with the Applications and Move-In teams to make sure paperwork is clean and units are ready on schedule.

Day-to-day resident experience falls here too. Community walks, handling concerns as they come up, coordinating with vendors, keeping the property looking sharp. BTR residents often expect a level of service closer to apartment living than traditional single-family rentals, so responsiveness and follow-through matter more than in some property types.

This position starts as temporary with the possibility of converting to permanent.

What You Bring

  • 1 to 3 years of leasing experience, ideally including lease-up or new construction
  • Active real estate license (required)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Solid grasp of Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort working independently and managing competing priorities without direct oversight
  • Strong communication skills across phone, email, and in-person interactions
  • Background in leasing, hospitality, or customer service

Context Worth Knowing

BTR communities are growing fast, and operators are still refining what the role of an on-site specialist looks like at scale. Evergreen uses centralized support for back-office functions, so this position focuses on the human-facing side of operations. That's a real advantage if you prefer working with people over paperwork, but it also means you need to be comfortable coordinating across teams you don't directly manage. Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be organized self-starters who don't wait to be told when something needs attention. If a unit isn't ready or a resident hasn't heard back, you notice and fix it.

Evergreen is headquartered in Dallas with operations across SFR and BTR portfolios. For someone early in a property management career, on-site experience at a lease-up BTR community builds skills that translate directly to community manager roles at larger multifamily properties.

job.title: Service Manager (Sablemill Lease-Up)
job.description:
The punch list isn't done yet, the first resident moves in on Friday, and your phone's already showing three open work orders from yesterday's building walk. That's week one at Sablemill, and the cadence doesn't slow down from there.

The Role at Sablemill

Van Metre is launching Sablemill Apartments, a brand-new 281-unit Class A community in Charlotte, and they need a Service Manager to own maintenance operations from construction handoff through full stabilization. This isn't a position where you inherit a running property with an established team and documented procedures. You're building the service function from scratch: hiring and training technicians, establishing preventive maintenance schedules, setting up inventory controls, and creating service standards before the first resident ever signs a lease.

The role moves through three distinct phases. Pre-opening puts you in close partnership with construction, development, and the Property Manager to walk units, clear punch-list items, confirm building systems are commissioned, and coordinate warranty work with contractors. During lease-up, you're managing apartment readiness and move-in inspections alongside a steady ramp in occupancy, keeping work orders from stacking while simultaneously supporting tour readiness and curb appeal. Once the community stabilizes, the focus shifts to the long game: preventive maintenance, structured turns, budget oversight, team development, and vendor accountability.

Participation in the on-call rotation is a real part of this job, especially during opening and peak lease-up periods when move-in volume is highest and the building systems are newest and least predictable.

What Van Metre Needs From You

  • Prior experience as a Service Manager or Maintenance Supervisor in multifamily, with direct exposure to a lease-up, new construction, acquisition, or major property transition
  • Solid command of apartment maintenance fundamentals: unit turns, building systems, PM scheduling, work-order management, and safety compliance
  • Proven track record building and holding a service team accountable, not just supervising one that already exists
  • Experience managing contractors and service vendors, tracking inventory, and monitoring maintenance expenses
  • Familiarity with Yardi, HappyCo, or comparable platforms for work orders and inspections
  • EPA and CPO certifications, or the ability to obtain them
  • Valid driver's license and availability for rotating on-call coverage

Compensation runs $68,000 to $76,900 annually depending on experience, plus a lease-up bonus of up to $15,000 tied to occupancy targets. After stabilization, annual bonus eligibility continues. Benefits include 401(k) with company match, tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, an $900 annual wellness reimbursement, and a generous PTO structure that includes holidays, personal days, a birthday, and a day for your annual physical.

One thing worth knowing if you're evaluating this role: Service Managers who run a successful Class A lease-up tend to carry real weight on their resume. The combination of pre-opening coordination, team-building from zero, and occupancy-ramp execution is a skill set that translates directly to Regional Maintenance Director tracks and multi-site leadership. Charlotte's multifamily pipeline remains active, and operators pay attention to who delivered clean lease-ups.
