On any given weekend (and weekends are part of the regular schedule here), you might be walking a prospective resident through a unit, following up on a delinquency, reviewing concession strategy with the manager, coaching a newer leasing agent through a close, and planning a resident event. The work doesn't silo neatly. That's actually the point. Professionals who've held this kind of role for a year or two consistently find that the combination of leasing fluency, team supervision, and operational exposure makes them credible candidates for Property Manager roles faster than people who spent that same time doing pure leasing or pure admin work.

Cupertino is a high-demand Silicon Valley submarket. Residents are sophisticated, expectations run high, and the competition from other Class A communities is real. Knowing your market intimately, down to effective rents, concession trends, and traffic patterns across comparable properties, is part of what this role demands day-to-day.

Pay runs $33.25 to $36.25 per hour, plus a $200 per-lease incentive, weekend shift premium, and a semi-annual discretionary bonus. Medical, vision, and dental are fully company-paid. There's a 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and educational assistance including tuition reimbursement.

What Prometheus is Looking For

  • At least two years of leasing experience, with a track record of closing and some exposure to coaching others
  • Comfort with the operational side: occupancy reporting, collections, pricing input, and resident file management
  • Customer service instincts that hold up under pressure, including with difficult resident situations
  • A schedule that can accommodate regular weekend availability
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred; a high school diploma or GED is required

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of leasing skill and genuine interest in leading a team. Plenty of people can lease well. Fewer can also set goals clearly, give useful feedback to newer agents, and keep the team's energy up through the routine stretches. If you've already started doing informal coaching in a previous role and found you were good at it, that's a real signal you're ready for this step.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Assistant Community Manager role sits at the intersection of leasing performance and financial accountability. At a company like Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the larger Southeast-focused multifamily operators, that means you're genuinely expected to work both sides: converting traffic into signed leases and keeping the ledger clean afterward.

What This Role Demands

You'll need at least two years of property management experience to step in here with confidence. The financial side of this position is real work. Rent collection, payment posting, delinquency follow-up, ledger audits, and coordinating eviction procedures when residents don't respond to outreach. These aren't tasks you learn on the fly. You'll also step into the Community Manager's responsibilities when they're out, so your ability to keep the team focused and operations steady matters from day one.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, work incoming leads, guide prospects through applications, and push for renewals that protect occupancy. Social media content for the community falls in your lap too, which requires a different kind of thinking than most traditional leasing duties.

The schedule reflects what the role actually is: the office runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours, and occasional evenings or weekends come with the territory for resident events. One weekday off keeps the week at 40 hours.

What This Role Builds

If you're aiming toward a Community Manager seat, this is the right chair to be sitting in. The combination of leasing, financial reporting, delinquency management, and team coverage gives you a complete picture of how a property runs. You'll develop the financial fluency that trips up many ACMs who spent their early careers focused only on leasing metrics without ever touching a T-12 or working through a delinquency report.

Hawthorne offers a formal Career Path Program specifically designed to move people from this role into Community Manager positions, which makes their stated intent concrete rather than aspirational.

Qualifications Worth Knowing

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior ACM experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus

Compensation includes an hourly base rate plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

The property is Wilmont at Hendersonville, located in Hendersonville, NC. Candidates who already understand the relationship between occupancy, delinquency, and NOI will find this role gives them room to apply that knowledge directly, not just observe it from a supporting position.

job.title: Concierge-Part Time
job.description:
It's 2 a.m. on a Sunday and a resident locked themselves out. You're the only point of contact in the building. How you handle the next ten minutes sets the tone for that resident's entire week.

Rise Association Management Group operates as a third-party fee management firm focused exclusively on Texas community associations. This particular opening sits inside a luxury high-rise condominium in the 77019 zip code, one of Houston's more established urban corridors, and the role carries a schedule that reflects real overnight and swing coverage: Sunday and Monday midnight to 8 a.m., Tuesday 4 p.m. to midnight. Part-time hours, but the responsibility level at the front desk during those windows is full-time in every practical sense.

What the Role Covers

The concierge is the building's face, gatekeeper, and first responder all in one shift. Day-to-day tasks include greeting residents and guests, controlling property access, monitoring cameras, and flagging anything unusual to management per established front desk protocols. You'll complete Daily Activity Reports, write incident reports when needed, and stay current on amenity availability and community activities so you can answer questions without fumbling.

The service component goes deeper than desk work. This role handles package processing, coordinates transportation and reservation requests, fields questions about local dining and cultural events, and assists with housekeeping arrangements. A genuine working knowledge of the surrounding Houston area, what's open, what's worth recommending, what's changed, matters here. Residents at this tier expect answers, not "let me look that up."

There's also light administrative and tech support involved: PowerPoint assistance for reports and presentations, engagement with building systems, and helping homeowners troubleshoot queries. The ability to lift 30 to 50 pounds is a real requirement, not a formality, given package handling at scale in a high-rise setting.

Who Fits This Role

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; a background in hospitality management or business administration is preferred
  • At least one year of experience in luxury hospitality or upscale residential property management
  • Strong verbal and written communication, the kind that holds up at 3 a.m. with a frustrated resident
  • Solid organizational skills and comfort managing several competing priorities at once
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and willingness to engage with building technology platforms
  • Professional presentation and demeanor throughout every shift, including overnight

The honest challenge of this schedule is that two of the three shifts are overnight. That filters out a lot of applicants, which is fine. The candidates who do well here tend to be self-directed, calm under pressure, and genuinely comfortable being the sole point of contact in a quiet building. If you've worked front desk at a boutique hotel or a Class A residential property and liked the rhythm of overnight work, this translates directly.

Pay runs $16 to $16.75 per hour.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
PeakMade Real Estate manages student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country. This Maintenance Technician role sits at a property in Charleston, South Carolina, and it's a hands-on, full-scope position covering everything from daily service requests to scheduled preventative maintenance to unit turns.

Day to day, you're moving between service requests, pool chemical logs, exterior cleanup, and whatever the make-ready schedule demands. In a student housing environment especially, turns are intense and time-compressed. When a semester ends, dozens of units need to be punched and ready before the next wave of residents arrives. Speed matters, but so does doing the work right the first time.

You'll work alongside the Maintenance Supervisor to manage parts inventory, follow the preventative maintenance calendar, and keep curb appeal sharp. On-call rotation is part of the job. Emergencies don't wait, and this role requires someone who can respond without needing a lot of hand-holding.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in apartment or student housing
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • Reliable transportation and the ability to live within 30 miles of the property
  • Comfortable working weekends, holidays, and rotating on-call shifts
  • Able to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights on ladders, and handle outdoor work in extreme temperatures
  • Your own hand tools

Pool maintenance is part of the scope here, so CPO certification (or willingness to obtain it) is worth noting. PeakMade offers technical certifications including HVAC and CPO, plus a leadership development track for those looking to move into a Maintenance Supervisor role over time.

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be self-directed on the small stuff. Supervisors notice who handles the routine without being reminded and who communicates clearly when something is outside their scope instead of guessing. That combination of initiative and honesty is what separates good techs from great ones.

PeakMade offers a 401(k) match, paid parental leave, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, monthly renewal bonuses, and a 10-year anniversary trip, among other perks.

job.title: Resident Manager
job.description:
Tuesday morning, 8:45 a.m. You've got a prospective resident arriving at The Teller House for a tour in fifteen minutes, a make-ready punch list to review with the Chief Engineer, and a leasing consultant who needs coaching on a renewal conversation scheduled for noon. That's the job, compressed into a single hour.

The Role Across Two Communities

FLATS, by Collective Residential, operates with a design-forward identity that leans hard into creative urban living. The Resident Manager position covers two Chicago properties: The Teller House, a high-rise with 176 apartments, and The Winnie, a low-rise with 84 units. Both communities offer studios and one-bedrooms. You're responsible for the full resident life cycle at both addresses, from first tour through move-out, and you report to the Property Manager while directly supervising the leasing team.

Day-to-day, that means conducting personalized tours that actually close, leading renewal conversations that are specific enough to address each resident's situation, managing the make-ready process alongside the Chief Engineer, and handling resident complaints through to real resolution. You'll also run property inspections to keep curb appeal where it needs to be, coordinate resident events, and oversee reputation management across review platforms and ILS channels. The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, and this is a fully onsite role with no hybrid option.

On the team side, you'll hire, train, and develop leasing consultants, run performance reviews, approve timesheets, and build the kind of service culture that shows up in customer experience scores. Reporting runs daily, weekly, and monthly, covering leasing activity and operational metrics tied to owner performance goals.

What This Role Builds

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2 or more years of management experience in lieu of a degree
  • 2 to 3 years in multifamily leasing or property management
  • Demonstrated background in customer service and team leadership
  • Familiarity with landlord-tenant law
  • Strong Yardi and Microsoft Office 365 skills (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Teams)
  • A leasing or broker's license, or the ability to obtain one within 120 days of hire, per Illinois state law

Compensation sits between $55,000 and $65,000 annually, with a 10% KPI bonus paid quarterly. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, and paid time off.

From a career trajectory standpoint, the Resident Manager title is one of the more useful seats in multifamily. You're close enough to leasing to keep those instincts sharp, and close enough to operations to start building the judgment that Property Manager and Regional roles actually require. Managing two assets simultaneously, a high-rise and a low-rise with different physical profiles and resident mixes, gives you exposure that a single-property role doesn't. Candidates who tend to move quickly from here are the ones who treat the reporting not as paperwork but as diagnostic data, and who can develop leasing staff without micromanaging them. Those two skills compound fast.

job.title: Concierge (Part-Time | Weekends) | Luxury High-Rise Central Fort-Worth
job.description:
Weekend concierge roles at luxury high-rises tend to get overlooked, but they carry real weight. Saturday and Sunday mornings are when move-ins happen, when guests arrive, when something inevitably goes sideways, and when there's no full management team on site to absorb it. The person at the front desk is the building.

The Property and the Schedule

This position is based at T&P Lofts in Sundance Square, one of the more recognizable addresses in central Fort Worth. Worth Ross Management Company handles luxury multifamily and HOA assets and has a reputation for holding its front-line staff to hospitality-grade standards. The schedule is straightforward: Saturday and Sunday, 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., part-time. If you're looking to supplement income from a primary hospitality or service job, this kind of consistent weekend block tends to work well logistically.

What the Role Actually Involves

You'll own the front desk during peak weekend hours. That means greeting residents, guests, and vendors, managing building access, logging packages and deliveries in BuildingLink, and handling whatever residents bring to you with composure. Vendor coordination and authorized access management are part of the daily rhythm, as is maintaining resident privacy without being cold about it. High-rise concierge work at this level expects you to read a situation quickly and decide what to handle yourself versus when to escalate.

  • Professional, service-forward communication with residents and guests
  • Building access control and guest or vendor check-in management
  • Package and delivery logging using BuildingLink
  • Resident concern triage and escalation when appropriate
  • Confidentiality and discretion as a baseline expectation, not an afterthought

Who Does Well Here

Prior experience in hospitality, hotel front desk, or luxury residential settings translates directly. The technology component is light but important, so comfort with property management or concierge platforms matters. What separates a strong candidate from an average one in this specific role is tone under pressure. Weekend mornings at a high-rise can go from quiet to complicated fast, and residents at this tier expect their concerns to be met with calm professionalism regardless of what's happening behind the scenes. A high school diploma is the minimum education requirement, though relevant service experience carries more weight than credentials here.

Worth Ross is an award-winning operator in this space, which generally means internal standards are documented and enforced. For someone who takes service seriously and wants a structured, professional environment to work in on weekends, that's a feature rather than a friction point.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Regional management at a multi-state operator means something specific: you're splitting your time between Michigan and Kansas, covering a portfolio of apartment communities where the property managers report to you and the buck stops with you. Peak Management is hiring for that seat, and they're looking for someone who can drive NOI, read a T-12 without hand-holding, and still walk a property with enough attention to detail to catch what a site team has gone blind to.

What the Role Covers

You'll carry oversight of multiple communities across two states, which means your weeks look different depending on where the fires are. Travel runs between 50 and 75 percent, so this is a road role in the truest sense. On the ground, you're coaching property managers, reviewing operational performance, and making sure leasing, marketing, and reporting are all functioning at a level that protects occupancy and asset value. Off-site, you're in the numbers: identifying delinquency trends, flagging underperformance, and keeping an eye on anything that's dragging NOI.

Peak expects its regional managers to carry real fluency in Fair Housing compliance, and that's non-negotiable at this level. You also need a track record of improving properties over time, not just holding steady, but actually moving the needle on long-term value.

What Strong Candidates Actually Bring

The candidates who tend to thrive in multi-state regional roles are the ones who've already managed through a lease-up or a significant value-add turn, because those experiences build the diagnostic instincts this job demands. You learn to tell the difference between a property that's struggling because of market softness and one that's struggling because of management problems. That distinction shapes every conversation you have with your site teams.

  • Demonstrated experience supervising property managers, not just leasing staff
  • Comfort with analytical reporting and operational benchmarking across a portfolio
  • Working knowledge of leasing and marketing strategy, including traffic conversion and concession management
  • Strong Fair Housing compliance background
  • Ability and willingness to travel 50 to 75 percent of the time, consistently

Compensation and Culture

Peak includes a sign-on bonus with this offer, along with a competitive base, medical, dental, and life insurance, PTO (they throw in your birthday, which is a small thing that most companies don't bother with), and a 401(k) with an employer match. They've framed their culture around a short set of values: optimism, accountability, care for people, and a low-drama environment. That last one is worth taking seriously. Regional roles carry enough inherent pressure that the internal culture either compounds the stress or absorbs it, and Peak seems to have made a deliberate choice about which direction they want to go.

If you've got the portfolio experience and you're comfortable operating across state lines, this is a legitimate opportunity to run something with real scope.

job.title: Leasing Agent- Dover Farms Apartments
job.description:
A prospect calls on a Saturday morning, thirty minutes before your scheduled tour, asking if the two-bedroom is still available. You already know the answer, you know the floor plan, and you know exactly what to say to get them in the door. That's the rhythm of leasing at Dover Farms Apartments in North Royalton.

The Role at Dover Farms

Banyan Living is hiring an experienced leasing agent to drive occupancy and resident satisfaction at this North Royalton community. This is a full-cycle leasing position. You'll conduct tours, process applications, run credit and background checks, and prepare lease agreements, all while keeping Fair Housing compliance front and center. You'll also work alongside management to sharpen marketing efforts and support traffic generation when occupancy needs attention. When junior leasing staff need guidance, you're the person they come to.

North Royalton sits in the southern Cuyahoga County submarket, where garden-style communities compete on value and community feel rather than amenity arms races. Prospects here tend to be thorough: they compare options, ask detailed questions, and respond well to an agent who actually knows the property inside and out. That local dynamic puts a premium on relationship-building over high-volume transactional leasing.

What Banyan Living Is Looking For

  • At least one year of residential leasing experience, with a solid working knowledge of leasing procedures and property management software
  • Strong familiarity with Fair Housing regulations and lease documentation requirements
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and comfort learning new property management platforms
  • Communication and negotiation skills that hold up across prospect calls, tours, and lease signings
  • Availability to work evenings and weekends when leasing traffic calls for it
  • Prior experience mentoring or supporting junior leasing team members is a plus

Strong candidates in a role like this tend to separate themselves on follow-through. Processing an application accurately and on time, keeping prospects warm between inquiry and approval, and catching a documentation issue before it becomes a problem at move-in: those details matter more than a high-energy tour pitch. If you've worked in a community where delinquency and retention were actively tracked, you'll understand why the relationship with a current resident carries as much weight as closing a new lease.

Banyan Living offers health, dental, life, and disability insurance, PTO, sick leave, and paid holidays. Employees also receive a 35% rent discount and access to ongoing training opportunities.

job.title: Leasing Sales Consultant - Solay & Alleia at Presidio
job.description:
Leasing is a sales job. That's easy to forget when you're scheduling tours and processing applications, but the consultants who actually hit their numbers remember it every day. This role at Solay and Alleia at Presidio leans on sales skills first: prospecting discipline, follow-up cadence, closing, and the ability to read a prospect and move them forward. If that framing excites you, read on.

The Skills This Role Runs On

AIR Communities uses a structured sales process, which means your ability to follow a repeatable system matters as much as raw personality. You'll work through the full leasing cycle: initial inquiry, appointment setting, community tours, and conversion. Traffic comes in; your job is to close it. The consultants who consistently exceed monthly goals here tend to have one thing in common: they treat follow-up as non-negotiable. A prospect who doesn't lease on the first tour is a relationship, not a dead lead.

You'll also need relationship management skills that extend past move-in. Building rapport during the inquiry phase and carrying it through the resident journey affects renewals, referrals, and the overall reputation of the community. Customer service chops from hospitality, retail, or restaurant backgrounds translate well here, sometimes better than people expect.

Fair Housing compliance is a baseline requirement, not an afterthought. You'll need to know it and apply it consistently.

Day-to-Day Reality

You'll split time between two neighboring communities, Solay and Alleia at Presidio, so context-switching between properties is part of the rhythm. Weekends are part of the schedule; that's when a lot of traffic comes through. The commission structure is tiered across several variables: unit type (higher rent, updated finishes, larger floor plan), lease term (18-month terms earn more), and hitting monthly goals at different threshold levels. That kind of structure rewards consultants who know how to position a unit's strengths and who can articulate value when a prospect is comparing options.

Base pay runs $20 to $22 per hour, and AIR offers a 25% rent discount at any of their communities, including the option to live onsite. There's also a seasonal unpaid winter break after peak season that some people find genuinely useful, and you keep your benefits during it.

What Good Candidates Bring

At least one year of sales or customer service experience is the floor, not a formality. The candidates who stand out typically have a measurable track record: a quota they hit, a goal they exceeded, a sales process they followed with consistency. If you can describe your previous performance in specific terms, you're already ahead of most applicants.

  • Documented history of meeting or exceeding sales or service goals
  • Comfort working a structured process rather than winging it
  • Flexible availability including weekends
  • Reliable transportation (you're supporting two communities)
  • Strong written and verbal communication

Leasing consultant roles are a common entry point into property management, and consultants who develop their closing skills and learn the operational side of a community often move into assistant manager or manager roles from here. AIR offers training and tuition assistance, so the path exists if you want it.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - 207 East
job.description:
Leasing is a numbers game dressed up as a people job. Traffic, closing ratios, occupancy targets , the metrics are always there. But the consultants who actually hold communities together are the ones who treat every prospect like a real person rather than a unit to fill. Olympus Property, a three-year consecutive winner of the National Apartment Association's Top Employer award, is hiring a Leasing Consultant for 207 East in Edgewood, WA, and they're looking for someone who can do both: hit the numbers and actually care about the outcome.

What the Role Looks Like Day to Day

You're the first face a prospect sees when they walk through the door. That means your morning might start with a stack of follow-up calls from yesterday's tours, transition into back-to-back showings in the afternoon, and wrap with lease paperwork for someone moving in next week. You'll explain unit layouts and options, walk prospects through pricing, and close on new leases. You'll also handle move-in prep: getting keys ready, completing the lease file, and making sure the handoff to a new resident is clean.

Beyond the leasing cycle, you're involved in resident retention. That includes planning and running resident events, visiting local businesses and locators to keep traffic coming in, and responding to resident concerns before they become bigger problems. The admin side of the role is real too: data entry into the property's resident database, maintaining accurate traffic logs, and keeping your product knowledge current across all available floorplans and unit variations.

The schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday with rotating hours between 9 AM and 6 PM, and weekends are required. Monthly after-hours availability for resident events is part of the job. That's worth knowing upfront.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • At least one year of apartment leasing experience, or a solid track record in a high-volume, customer-facing role such as hospitality, retail, or restaurant service
  • Genuine comfort with sales conversations, including closing without being pushy
  • Strong administrative follow-through: the lease file has to be right before that resident picks up keys
  • Availability for weekends and periodic evening events

Pay starts between $19.00 and $21.00 per hour depending on experience, and the role includes monthly leasing commissions and resident renewal bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, and an apartment rental allowance, among others.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from outside the industry: the consultants who advance fastest in leasing roles tend to be the ones who take renewal retention seriously from day one. Closing a new lease is visible; keeping a resident from going month-to-month and eventually churning is quieter work, but it's where NOI gets protected. If you're thinking about where this role leads, strong consultants typically move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions, where that retention instinct becomes even more valuable.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Leasing is a sales job with a customer service wrapper. At Franklin River Apartments in Southfield, that means two core skills carry most of the weight: reading people quickly and communicating clearly across every channel. You'll field phone calls, respond to written inquiries, and conduct in-person tours, sometimes all in the same hour. The ability to shift tone and approach without losing consistency is what keeps traffic converting to signed leases.

Attention to detail matters here beyond the obvious. Application processing, move-in paperwork, and renewal documents all pass through you before going to the manager for approval. Errors at that stage cost time and trust. Candidates who treat administrative accuracy as part of the sales job tend to outperform those who treat it as a separate chore.

What You'll Spend Your Time On

  • Touring prospective residents and following up with a mix of phone and written outreach
  • Processing applications, move-in packages, and renewal paperwork for manager review
  • Inspecting vacant units, models, and common areas to confirm they're show-ready
  • Following up on move-ins and maintenance requests to confirm resident satisfaction
  • Supporting site marketing efforts, including outreach to local businesses and employers
  • Helping plan and attend resident events

Yardi experience gives you a head start. Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations is a plus, and Paragon will train the right person either way. The schedule is guaranteed full-time at 40 hours per week, which gives this role more stability than hourly positions common in leasing.

Working at Paragon

Paragon Properties manages communities across Michigan and has built a reputation as a fee management operator that takes internal advancement seriously. This role comes with a formal training program and a clear path upward, from consultant to assistant manager to property manager, for people who perform. The leasing move-in bonus adds a direct financial incentive tied to the work you're actually doing.

One honest note: resident-facing roles require consistency even on slower days. Strong candidates treat every prospect like a high-priority lead regardless of the traffic volume that week. That mindset, more than raw charisma, is what separates a good leasing consultant from one who hits company benchmarks month after month.

Starting pay is $18.50 per hour, negotiable based on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision with a short waiting period, employer-contributed 401(k), paid holidays, and a rent discount.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Cottonwood Clermont Apartments
job.description:
A prospect walks in mid-tour with questions you didn't expect, your phone is ringing with a maintenance inquiry, and a package delivery just arrived at the front desk. This is a Tuesday. The Customer Experience Specialist role at Cottonwood Clermont Apartments rewards people who read a room quickly, shift priorities without losing focus, and still end each interaction with genuine warmth.

What the Role Covers Day to Day

This is a full-cycle leasing and hospitality position. You'll field inquiries across phone, email, and text, ensuring every prospective resident gets accurate, timely information about pricing and availability. You'll keep apartments show-ready by walking vacant units, inspecting the tour path, and confirming the make-ready condition meets Cottonwood's standards before a scheduled showing. Move-in readiness isn't just a punch list item here; it's part of the brand promise.

Beyond the leasing side, you'll greet everyone who comes through the office door, including residents and vendors, manage the package room daily, support community event planning, and contribute to social media marketing efforts. Cottonwood was an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, so you'll also support that leasing channel, which means understanding how prospects move through the process independently and being ready to follow up meaningfully.

The schedule is full-time and includes evenings and weekends. That flexibility is a real part of the job, not fine print.

What You'll Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires:

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills across multiple channels
  • A genuinely upbeat, service-first attitude with residents, prospects, and vendors
  • Attention to detail when inspecting units and common areas for tour readiness
  • Comfort with technology and digital leasing tools
  • The ability to handle a fast-moving front office without losing composure

The role builds:

  • Deep fluency in the leasing lifecycle, from initial traffic through move-in
  • Experience with community marketing and resident engagement programming
  • Vendor communication and relationship management skills that transfer directly into assistant manager or property manager roles

Cottonwood frames this position as a career entry point with an explicit path toward management. Leasing consultants who develop occupancy instincts, understand concessions and pricing strategy, and build rapport with residents consistently are the ones who move into those next roles. The habits you build here, following up quickly, keeping accurate notes, owning the resident experience, are the same habits that define effective managers in this industry.

job.title: Asset Management and Acquisitions Intern
job.description:
You're sitting across from the VP of Asset Management, walking through a monthly property narrative together, when he stops and asks you what you think is driving the NOI shortfall. That moment, early in a ten-week program, is exactly the kind of exposure this internship is built around.

What This Internship Actually Covers

BAM Companies, a vertically integrated multifamily owner-operator based in Carmel, Indiana, is bringing on an Asset Management and Acquisitions Intern to work directly alongside the VP of Asset Management and Director of Acquisitions. The work spans two of the most analytically demanding departments in the business, with deliberate exposure to the rest of the organization woven throughout the program.

On the acquisitions side, you'll support underwriting of potential deals, compile and interpret market data, assist with due diligence review, and contribute to rent and sale comp analyses. On the asset management side, you'll review monthly property financials and narratives, track performance across a multi-state portfolio, and help maintain the operational checklists that keep asset oversight consistent. You'll also contribute to building out the 2026 budget templates, which puts you inside a real planning process, not a simulation of one.

Other work includes cost/benefit analyses on specific contracts or systems, competitive property research, and ad hoc projects that arise as priorities shift. The program closes with a capstone presentation, giving you practice turning analytical work into something you can defend in a room.

  • Underwriting support for potential acquisitions
  • Market research: rent comps, sale comps, competitive property analysis
  • Monthly financial review and asset performance tracking
  • Due diligence facilitation
  • Budget template development for 2026
  • Cross-departmental project work (finance, accounting, operations)
  • On-site visits to BAM apartment communities
  • Capstone presentation at program conclusion

Who Builds Real Skills Here

This role requires proficiency in Excel and comfort with financial modeling. You should already understand basic real estate valuation concepts and be able to move between quantitative analysis and written communication without losing precision in either. You're a rising junior or senior pursuing a degree in Real Estate, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a closely related field.

What separates strong candidates from adequate ones is intellectual initiative. The job description specifically calls out the ability to identify opportunities for analysis before being asked. That means coming into a project, seeing what the data doesn't yet show, and building something to surface it. Candidates who wait to be handed a task list will underperform here. Candidates who read a financial summary and ask a sharper follow-up question will thrive.

BAM's portfolio spans Indiana, Ohio, Illinois, Arkansas, Pennsylvania, Missouri, and Iowa, so you'll be reading assets across varied markets during one program. That breadth is genuinely unusual at the internship level. For students who want to enter multifamily investment, acquisitions, or asset management after graduation, the exposure to underwriting, portfolio-level performance tracking, and budget planning in a single ten-week window builds a resume that reads with real specificity.

job.title: Leasing and Resident Experience Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position lives at the intersection of sales, operations, and hospitality. You'll use leasing conversion skills daily, but the job also demands strong data literacy. Occupancy trends, renewal percentages, lease expirations, lead source performance, and resident satisfaction scores all feed into decisions you'll make and recommendations you'll present to senior leadership. If you can read a report and translate it into a concrete action, that's the core competency here.

Communication runs a close second. You're coordinating between onsite teams, Regional Managers, a Roving Leasing Agent, and a Resident Services Professional. Clear written and verbal communication keeps all of that aligned, especially when you're stepping into communities during a Community Manager vacancy and need to maintain leasing momentum without skipping a beat.

What You're Actually Managing

Sunrise Management is hiring for a Leasing and Resident Experience Manager based in San Diego, with a salary range of $62,400 to $72,800 depending on experience. The scope is portfolio-wide, not site-specific.

Day to day, you'll own the renewal pipeline across the portfolio. That means tracking lease expirations, launching renewal campaigns, monitoring conversion rates, and flagging retention risks before they become turnover. You'll also develop and enforce leasing strategy across multiple communities, watching traffic volume, pricing trends, concessions, and competitor activity to keep occupancy targets on track.

When a community loses its Community Manager, this role fills the operational gap. You coordinate tours, process applications, handle resident communications, support move-ins, and keep service requests moving. It's hands-on coverage with real operational weight, not just oversight from a distance. A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required because regular travel between properties is part of the job.

You'll directly supervise two roles: a Roving Leasing Agent and a Resident Services Professional. That means setting measurable goals, coaching performance, managing workload priorities, and conducting reviews. Multi-site leadership experience helps a lot here because balancing staffing needs across a portfolio requires judgment that single-site experience doesn't always develop.

What Makes This Role Work at Sunrise

Sunrise positions itself around resident hospitality, and that framing matters for how this role is evaluated. Occupancy and renewal numbers are the primary metrics, but resident satisfaction scores and online reputation metrics are also tracked and reported to the Regional Vice President. Candidates who treat leasing as purely transactional will find the expectations here broader than expected.

The strongest candidates for this type of role tend to share one trait: they treat renewal outreach with the same urgency as new leasing. Many leasing professionals are wired to chase new traffic and let renewals coast on autopilot. Here, renewals are a managed process with campaigns, timelines, and conversion tracking. If you've built renewal programs from scratch at a previous employer, lead with that.

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Hospitality, Property Management, or related field preferred; equivalent experience considered
  • At least five years of progressive property management, leasing, or resident experience required
  • At least two years of supervisory or leadership experience preferred
  • Multi-site experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required
  • Proficiency with marketing platforms and performance reporting expected

job.title: Maintenance Apprentice
job.description:
Avanath operates affordable workforce housing communities across the country. This Maintenance Apprentice position sits at their Escondido property on Morning View Drive and reports directly to the Community Manager. It's a ground-level role built for someone who wants to grow their maintenance career in a structured, team-oriented environment.

Day to day, the work covers a wide range of tasks: completing resident work orders, helping turn vacant units through the make-ready process, walking the grounds, pressure-washing common areas, and assisting with routine property inspections. You'll build punch lists for vacant units, coordinate with vendors when needed, and track inventory so supplies stay stocked. The role also involves contributing to preventative maintenance and supporting cost-control efforts by repairing rather than replacing parts wherever possible.

Avanath emphasizes promotion from within, so this apprentice position has a clear path forward. Technicians who show initiative here typically move into full Maintenance Technician roles, then toward Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor over time. Hands-on experience across grounds, make-readies, and work order management builds exactly the skill set hiring managers look for at the next level.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of grounds or porter experience
  • Comfort operating property maintenance equipment including pressure washers and leaf blowers
  • Ability to perform minor repairs across plumbing, electrical, or general carpentry
  • Basic knowledge of Fair Housing laws and OSHA safety requirements
  • Strong attention to detail and solid time management habits
  • A professional, courteous manner with residents, staff, and vendors
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Physical demands are real here. Expect frequent standing, walking, bending, and occasional work on uneven ground or elevated surfaces. You may also travel to sister communities to provide maintenance support when needed, and as essential staff, you're expected to show up during inclement weather.

If you've been doing grounds and porter work and want a role where you can start picking up broader maintenance skills while earning a path toward a Technician title, this is a reasonable next step.

job.title: Entry Level Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance is one of the most skill-dense entry points in property management, and this role at Bigos Management's Willow Pond community in Burnsville builds a broad technical foundation fast. You're working across grounds, common areas, and apartment units, which means your hands are on almost every system a residential property runs on. That kind of cross-training compounds quickly.

What This Role Actually Builds

The core of this position is supporting daily operations at a 312-unit garden-style community, with a partial split to a second site. You'll work directly alongside experienced maintenance staff on make-readies, which means learning how to turn units efficiently from move-out to rent-ready condition. That process, furniture removal, paint touch-up, cleaning, and punch list repairs, is one of the most teachable and transferable skills in residential maintenance. Technicians who get fast and thorough at turns become indispensable quickly.

Beyond make-readies, the daily scope includes:

  • Grounds upkeep: trash removal, sweeping walks, watering, and winter ice control
  • Work order completion in apartments and common areas covering minor plumbing, electrical, HVAC, light carpentry, and painting
  • Regular property walks to catch maintenance and cleanliness issues before residents report them
  • Tool and supply inventory alongside the onsite team

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, with Monday and Thursday at Willow Pond and the other three days split between Hidden Valley in the morning and Willow Pond in the afternoon. Reliable transportation is required for that split.

Skills That Transfer

Entry-level maintenance roles at multi-family properties tend to sort candidates into two groups pretty quickly: those who treat every work order as a task to close, and those who treat it as a chance to understand a system. The second group ends up as lead technicians, service managers, and eventually maintenance supervisors. At a company the size of Bigos, with a portfolio that has earned Star Tribune Top Workplace recognition eleven times, there's room to grow into those positions. Getting your Certified Pool Operators license within six months of hire, which this role recommends, is one concrete early step in that direction.

The minor plumbing and HVAC exposure you get at this level is the same exposure that, over time, leads to EPA 608 certification and the ability to take on more complex systems. The time management and self-direction skills you build handling multiple open work orders daily translate directly into managing a maintenance team later. None of that is theoretical here. It's just what happens when someone pays attention.

What Bigos Offers for This Position

Pay for this role runs $18.00 to $22.00 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal bonuses available. Benefits start the first of the month after hire and include medical with HSA employer contribution, 401(k) with employer match, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, PTO with rollover, company-paid life insurance and disability coverage, educational assistance, and a rent discount. A Lifetime Fitness membership discount is also included.

Zero to two years of residential maintenance or assistant-level experience meets the baseline here. If you bring solid mechanical instincts, a professional attitude with residents and vendors, and the physical readiness for a hands-on outdoor and indoor schedule through Minnesota winters, this is a strong place to start building a career in property maintenance.

job.title: Roving Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a roving leasing role, which means you won't be anchored to a single property. Bozzuto is looking for a Leasing Consultant who can move fluidly across a portfolio spanning St. Petersburg, Tampa, and the broader Greater Tampa area. On any given day, you might be touring a prospect through one community in the morning and following up with leads for a different property in the afternoon. Flexibility and organization are prerequisites, not bonuses.

The core of the work is converting interest into signed leases. That means following up with every prospect, giving tours that feel personalized rather than scripted, and staying knowledgeable enough about each community in your rotation to speak to its specific neighborhood appeal. St. Pete and Tampa have distinct identities, and residents shopping in those markets know the difference. Strong candidates will quickly learn what makes each property's location compelling, whether that's proximity to the waterfront, walkability, or access to major employment corridors.

Beyond tours and follow-up, you'll also carry social media responsibilities. That includes creating and posting content for platforms like Facebook and Instagram to generate awareness and keep prospects engaged. The weekend schedule here is real and worth understanding upfront: three weekends per month on-site, with two weekdays off in exchange. That's industry-standard for leasing, but it's a lifestyle commitment you should plan around.

What You Bring

  • Proven comfort in a customer-facing sales environment, ideally leasing or retail
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to tailor your pitch to different types of prospects
  • Hands-on experience with social media content creation, specifically Instagram and Facebook
  • Competency with property management software, CRMs, or similar platforms
  • A polished, professional presentation and genuine comfort initiating conversations
  • Reliable transportation to travel between properties across the Tampa Bay area

Context Worth Knowing

Roving roles tend to accelerate leasing careers faster than single-site positions. You'll see how multiple properties perform, understand how management adjusts concessions and traffic strategies across a portfolio, and develop a broader view of operations than most entry-level leasing consultants ever get. That exposure can lead naturally into a senior leasing role, an assistant manager position, or a portfolio-level support role with a larger operator.

Bozzuto manages properties at the upper end of the quality spectrum, so the expectations for resident experience and brand consistency are high. Candidates who thrive here typically combine genuine warmth with a structured follow-up discipline. Charm without follow-through won't move the needle on occupancy. The posted salary range runs $47,000 to $49,000, with additional bonus eligibility, plus a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 20 days of PTO, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Leasing Consultant- Russellville Commons
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Leasing at Russellville Commons means you're the first real impression a prospective resident gets of the property. You'll greet prospects, qualify applicants, walk units, and guide new residents from application through lease signing. Behind the scenes, that translates to keeping rental files current, entering data accurately, and making sure every move-in is coordinated with the maintenance team so the apartment is genuinely ready when a new resident arrives. You'll also stay in regular contact with current residents, handling complaints and following up on rent payments when needed. The administrative side of the role matters here: monthly paperwork, organized files, and clean data entry aren't afterthoughts.

MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over three decades, with a focus on acquisition, development, rehab, and management. That scale means there's real infrastructure behind you, and the company has a stated track record of promoting from within.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred)
  • Genuine sales instincts paired with strong customer service follow-through
  • Comfort with leasing software and data entry, since occupancy reporting depends on accurate input
  • Professional communication skills in both in-person and written contexts
  • The organizational discipline to keep files, lease documents, and administrative tasks in order across a busy leasing cycle

Where This Role Can Take You

A leasing consultant position done well builds a specific and transferable skill set: you learn to read traffic patterns, understand what drives concessions decisions, and develop a feel for occupancy trends before they show up in a report. Those instincts are exactly what assistant managers and property managers rely on daily. Strong leasing consultants who also demonstrate comfort with the administrative side of the role, resident relations, and lease compliance tend to move into assistant manager roles faster than those who treat leasing as purely a sales function.

Portland's multifamily market has seen meaningful rent pressure over the past few years, which means leasing teams are expected to do more than just show units. Understanding traffic sources, following up consistently, and converting leads efficiently all matter more in a tighter market. If you're early in your property management career, this environment sharpens those skills in ways that translate directly to any future leasing or management role.

Benefits include monthly and quarterly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, PTO, and rental discounts.

job.title: Maintenance Technician at Sugarmont Apartments & Townhomes
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at apartment communities carry a lot of the resident experience on their shoulders. A leaking faucet or a broken AC in a Utah summer isn't just a work order. It's a person's home, and how quickly and cleanly you resolve it shapes how that resident feels about living there. At Sugarmont Apartments and Townhomes, Cottonwood Residential is looking for someone who understands that dynamic.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you'll move through a mix of scheduled make-readies and incoming resident requests. Plumbing, electrical, general carpentry, HVAC troubleshooting. The scope is broad, which keeps the work from getting monotonous, but it also means you need a genuine foundation across trades rather than deep expertise in just one. EPA Type II or Universal certification is required before you start, and you'll need a valid driver's license. CPO certification is a plus if you have it.

The physical side of this role is real. You're on your feet for most of the day, climbing stairs and ladders, working in tight spaces, and occasionally lifting up to 50 lbs. Evenings, weekends, and on-call rotations for after-hours emergencies are part of the schedule. The Service Manager provides support during those calls, so you're not handling urgent situations entirely alone, but you need to be comfortable responding when residents need help outside normal hours.

Who Tends to Fit Well Here

Strong candidates in this kind of role share a few qualities that go beyond technical skill. They communicate clearly with residents while the work is happening. They leave the unit clean. They close the loop. A technician who fixes the problem but leaves a resident feeling brushed off hasn't fully done the job. Cottonwood emphasizes service quality and resident connection as core values, so the interpersonal side of maintenance work genuinely matters here.

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Meaningful HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Plumbing, electrical, and carpentry skills across residential repairs
  • Valid driver's license
  • Ability to work on-call and cover after-hours emergency calls
  • CPO certification (a plus, not a requirement)

Benefits and Growth

Cottonwood offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage available within your first 30 days, along with a 401k with company match, HSA match, 10.5 paid holidays, and three weeks of paid time off in your first year. For a maintenance role, that's a solid package that reflects how the company values this work.

For technicians who build strong skills here, the natural path often leads toward a Lead Tech or Service Manager role. Communities like Sugarmont give you exposure to a varied unit mix including townhomes, which adds scope to your experience compared to a flat garden-style property. If you're early in your maintenance career and want to grow, that variety is genuinely useful.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance
job.description:
You're mid-turn on a two-bedroom at Craigdell Gardens, patching drywall and lining up the paint match, when a call comes in about a leaking shut-off valve in another unit. That's a normal Tuesday in this role.

Birgo is hiring a Maintenance Technician for its apartment community on Craigdell Road in New Kensington, PA. The position covers the full scope of residential maintenance work: make-readies and turns, drywall, painting, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, and HVAC repairs, along with scheduled preventative maintenance. You'll also rotate through on-call coverage for after-hours emergencies, with mileage reimbursed for travel throughout the workday. Beyond Craigdell Gardens, there's occasional opportunity to support other Birgo properties across the Western PA region.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

New Kensington sits in a market where Birgo operates workforce housing, and the residents here depend on things getting fixed right and fast. The pace of turns matters because vacant units directly affect occupancy, and occupancy affects everything else. Strong technicians in this kind of environment know how to move through a punch list without cutting corners. You're not just fixing things; you're directly affecting whether someone has a safe, functioning home.

On-call rotation is a real part of this job and worth acknowledging honestly. Emergency calls come after hours. If that kind of availability doesn't fit your current situation, this role will be difficult. If it does, the compensation and weekly pay structure reflect that trade-off.

What Birgo Needs From You

  • Eligibility to work in the United States
  • Valid driver's license and personal, insured transportation
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift and carry 50 pounds without assistance
  • Comfort working in confined spaces, on ladders, and on staircases
  • Safe, competent use of power tools
  • Hands-on experience across at least several of the core trades: plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, HVAC, or carpentry

Pay runs $24 to $27 per hour depending on experience, paid weekly. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contribution, a 401(k) match, paid time off and sick time, a boots and uniform program, professional development reimbursement, discounted rent at Birgo properties, and a profit-sharing program. Mileage is reimbursed for work-related travel.

Technicians who grow in this kind of role often develop the breadth to move into lead maintenance or property-level facilities management. Working across multiple sites in a regional portfolio also builds exposure to different property types and condition levels, which sharpens diagnostic instincts faster than single-site work typically does.

job.title: Resident Services
job.description:
Some property roles ask you to specialize. This one asks you to cover ground. The Resident Services Coordinator position at Berkshire 15 and Central Place draws on a specific combination of skills: front-facing resident communication, leasing support, service coordination, and the kind of situational awareness that keeps a property humming when multiple departments need help at once.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Relationship-building sits at the center of everything here. Residents call because they need something, and you're the person who either has the answer or knows exactly who does. That requires genuine comfort with high-volume phone communication, the ability to shift tone quickly between a prospective renter tour and a maintenance follow-up call, and enough familiarity with leasing to step in when the leasing team needs an extra hand showing units or working renewal conversations.

Attention to detail matters more than it might appear on paper. Processing service requests sounds administrative, but the follow-through piece, confirming completion and checking in with residents, is where satisfaction scores are actually won or lost. Coordinators who track those loops closely tend to build the kind of resident trust that shows up in renewal rates.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

This is a multi-site position covering Berkshire 15 and Central Place, so reliable transportation between locations is a practical requirement, not a footnote. On any given shift, you might greet a prospective resident in the morning, field maintenance requests through the afternoon, and wrap up by supporting the team on a lease renewal outreach effort. The variety is real.

  • Supporting leasing traffic and stepping in to show units as needed
  • Handling inbound calls as the primary voice of the property
  • Coordinating service requests from submission through resident follow-up
  • Assisting with lease renewal outreach and resident retention efforts
  • Contributing ideas for resident events and satisfaction initiatives

Berkshire manages its own properties in-house, which means the teams you're working alongside, leasing, maintenance, management, are all under the same umbrella. That structure tends to make cross-departmental coordination faster and less fragmented than in third-party management environments, and it gives coordinators real visibility into how a property operates end to end.

What Makes a Strong Fit

Candidates who do well in this role usually have a natural comfort with ambiguity. The day shifts depending on what the property needs, and the ability to reprioritize quickly without losing track of open items is what separates coordinators who thrive from those who feel scattered. Prior experience in leasing or resident relations at a Class A or B community helps, but the interpersonal instincts matter as much as the resume line.

The posted hourly range runs from $24.57 to $25.96, with full benefits including health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a 25% rent discount. Berkshire positions this role as part of a people-first culture with personal development plans built in, which is worth taking seriously if career growth in property management is on your radar. Coordinators who learn both the leasing and operations sides of a site often move into assistant manager or leasing manager roles with a stronger foundation than those who've only done one or the other.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
CloudTen Residential runs a genuinely varied book of multifamily assets. Hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, value-add repositioning projects. For a maintenance tech, that kind of portfolio means you're not doing the same thing every shift, and that's either appealing or it isn't.

This position is based in Berkeley Heights, Kent, WA and pays $30 to $33 per hour depending on experience. There are also leasing and renewal bonuses available at the property level, which is a detail worth noting because it's not standard for every maintenance role.

The day-to-day work covers the full range: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, pool upkeep, and keeping common areas clean and presentable. Turn work is part of the rhythm too. The expectation is that vacant units are rent-ready within three to five days, which requires you to prioritize quickly and work without a lot of hand-holding. Service requests get a 24-hour resolution window, and when parts are on order or something creates a delay, you're expected to communicate that clearly to both the community manager and the resident.

On-call emergency response is real here. This is worth stating plainly: you'll carry availability for after-hours calls, evenings, and weekends. If your personal schedule doesn't flex easily, that's worth thinking through before applying. The properties need coverage, and the expectation is responsiveness when something goes wrong at 10pm.

Preventive maintenance is a consistent part of the role too, not an afterthought. Monthly PM directives cover lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety checks. You'll also track inventory, maintain MSDS records for chemicals on site, and document vacant unit status. The documentation side of this job is real, and candidates who treat paperwork as secondary tend to create problems down the line.

What this role generally requires

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • Valid driver's license in good standing
  • Comfort with a mobile device and basic computer tasks (work orders, communication, documentation)
  • Ability to work independently and manage your own time without constant supervision
  • Strong communication skills, including with residents who are frustrated or in a difficult situation
  • Flexible availability including weekends, evenings, and holidays

The candidates who tend to do well in roles like this are the ones who already know what they don't know and ask good questions rather than guessing on unfamiliar systems. CloudTen's portfolio spans property types that range in complexity, so intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn specific systems actually matters here. The tech who shows up with confidence, documents their work cleanly, and communicates proactively when something's off is the one who earns trust quickly.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance, FSA access, paid vacation and sick leave, and paid holidays. CloudTen is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug-free workplace policy.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager - Inkwell at Baseline ~ Broomfield, CO
job.description:
Assistant property manager roles at luxury communities ask a lot. You're handling leasing one hour and chasing delinquency the next. At Inkwell at Baseline, a Davis Development community in Broomfield, CO, the expectation is that you can shift between those two modes without losing composure in either one.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The leasing side is active: greeting and touring prospective residents, walking them through qualifications, preparing files, and helping close renewals. You'll also support marketing efforts and resident events aimed at pushing occupancy to target. The operations side is where the real depth lives. You'll manage applications, track rents, and handle delinquency including the legal non-payment process when it comes to that. Yardi accuracy is your responsibility, so if you're sloppy with records, this role will make that apparent quickly. You'll do property walk-throughs, follow up on work orders, and keep the community looking and functioning at a level consistent with a luxury standard.

Resident issues will land on your desk too. Some of those conversations are straightforward. Some aren't. Davis specifically calls out maintaining a calm demeanor, and that's not filler language. It reflects the reality that you'll handle conflict regularly, and how you handle it reflects directly on the community's reputation.

What Davis Development Looks For

  • At least one year of assistant property manager experience
  • Lease-up experience at luxury communities is a plus
  • Proven sales, marketing, and customer service background
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable working across teams and with people at different levels of the organization
  • A bachelor's degree in a related field is preferred but not required
  • Proficiency with or willingness to learn Yardi

Candidates who stand out in roles like this are the ones who don't need reminding to follow through. Leasing skills get you in the door, but it's the operational discipline, keeping files clean, staying on top of delinquency before it compounds, catching problems on walk-throughs before residents do, that separates a strong assistant manager from one who's just passing through.

The Company Behind the Property

Davis Development is a privately owned luxury developer and management company with more than 25 years building and operating multifamily communities across the country. Their model is in-house management, meaning the people running these communities work directly for Davis, not a third-party firm. They describe their on-site teams as owner-operators, and that framing is meaningful. You're expected to make decisions that matter, not wait for someone else to call the shot.

Benefits include health coverage (medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health) starting the first of the month after 30 days, a 401(k) with a 4% employer match that vests immediately, company-paid life insurance, paid time off with a carryover provision, and access to a company apparel store allowance. Training and development are part of the package as well, which matters if you're thinking about a path toward property manager or beyond.

Davis Development is an equal opportunity employer. No third-party recruiter inquiries, please.

job.title: Community Manager - Portland
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Community management at an affordable housing portfolio pulls on a specific combination of skills: financial oversight, compliance knowledge, and genuine people work. At Avanath, all three carry equal weight. You'll read budget comparisons and rent rolls with the same attention you give a resident concern at the front desk. LIHTC and Tax Credit compliance isn't background knowledge here. It shapes daily decisions around eligibility, file management, and subsidy voucher submissions.

Strong interpersonal skills matter in every property management role, but affordable housing puts that skill set under real pressure. Residents often face housing instability, and you function as a resource hub connecting them to services and agencies beyond what the property itself can provide. That requires listening without judgment, communicating clearly under stress, and knowing when to escalate and when to handle something directly.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Operationally, you own the full scope of on-site management. That includes:

  • Monitoring delinquency and driving toward 0% through consistent rent collection systems
  • Managing accounts payable, vendor relationships, and contractor performance
  • Preparing monthly financials and reports accurately and on time
  • Partnering with your Regional Manager on the annual operating budget
  • Overseeing capex projects and coordinating across departments when needed
  • Maintaining occupancy goals through leasing of new and turned units
  • Ensuring curb appeal and physical presentation stay at a high standard

On the people side, you lead and develop a full on-site team. You set schedules, give direct feedback, run performance reviews, and handle the day-to-day challenges that come with managing staff in a high-contact environment. Resident events and retention programs also fall to you, and you'll be expected to build relationships with regulatory agencies and social service partners in the community.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Avanath specifically needs someone with 5 to 7 years in property management, including at least 2 years in a manager seat, and verified LIHTC experience. That last point is non-negotiable. Tax credit compliance has meaningful legal and financial consequences, and the learning curve matters.

What actually separates strong candidates in this type of role is the ability to hold both sides of the job at once. The managers who struggle tend to be strong on either the financial side or the resident relations side, but not both. Affordable housing community managers need to run tight books and still show up for residents as a genuine advocate. Avanath's model is built around that balance, and their reputation in workforce housing reflects it.

If you've worked in LIHTC communities, built real relationships with housing agencies or social services, and led teams through high-occupancy, compliance-heavy environments, this role fits the skills you've already developed.

job.title: Concierge (16 Hour Part-Time)- 181 Fremont
job.description:
High-rise HOA concierge work is a specific kind of service job that most people outside of property management don't fully understand. It's not a hotel front desk. It's not a leasing office. It's a fixed-schedule, relationship-driven role inside a residential community where the same residents walk past you every day and hold you to a high standard because they live there.

Action Property Management, the largest privately owned HOA management company in the West, operates over 300 communities out of nine offices. Their portfolio runs toward luxury and they've built a reputation over four decades on professionalism and follow-through. 181 Fremont is one of their flagship San Francisco properties, and they're bringing on a part-time concierge for 16 hours per week.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

At a luxury high-rise like 181 Fremont, the concierge is often the first person a resident or guest encounters. You're managing package intake, handling access control, fielding questions from residents, and keeping a close eye on who comes and goes. The building has standards, and your job is to uphold them consistently, not just when it's easy.

Part-time in HOA concierge often means fixed shifts, so your schedule is predictable. But the nature of the work means you need to stay sharp for the full duration of your shift. A quiet lobby can shift quickly, and residents at a property like this expect a professional, calm response regardless of what's happening behind the scenes.

Who Fits This Role

  • Someone who's comfortable working independently without constant supervision
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially under pressure
  • Experience in hospitality, residential property management, or a related service role
  • A professional demeanor that holds up when residents are frustrated or demanding
  • Attention to detail for access logs, package tracking, and incident reporting

The honest part: residents at luxury HOA communities can be exacting. You'll occasionally deal with complaints that feel disproportionate, requests that fall outside your actual scope, and moments where you have to hold a firm but polite line. That's part of the job. If that dynamic sounds manageable rather than exhausting, you're probably the right fit.

For candidates thinking about where this kind of role leads, HOA concierge experience at a high-profile property is a genuine resume asset. It demonstrates you can operate inside a structured, professional environment with high resident expectations. People who do this work well often move into assistant community manager or community manager positions within HOA management companies.

job.title: PT Concierge (Weekends) - Downtown Dallas
job.description:
Concierge roles at luxury high-rise and mid-rise communities tend to look simple from the outside. In practice, they're the front line of resident experience, and at a downtown Dallas high-rise, that means holding a lot of the building's reputation in your hands on a Saturday morning when management isn't around.

The Role at Victory Park

Worth Ross Management Company runs HOA and residential operations across Texas, and this part-time weekend position covers Saturday and Sunday mornings, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., at their Victory Park property in downtown Dallas. The pay is $17 to $17.50 per hour.

You're the first person residents and guests see when they walk in. That means controlling access, logging vendors, handling packages through BuildingLink, and knowing residents by name. The expectation isn't just to check IDs at the door. It's to anticipate needs, field complaints before they become escalations, and keep everything documented and organized so the Lead Concierge and AGM have clean handoff notes when the week starts.

Package management is a bigger part of this than people expect. Coordinating deliveries, logging them accurately, and getting them to residents in a timely way takes real attention to detail, especially on weekends when volume can spike. Emergency response is also part of the job. You need to recognize alarms, react without hesitation, and follow building protocols correctly.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Prior concierge or front desk experience in a hotel or residential setting
  • Comfortable working independently on weekends without a manager on-site
  • Proficient in MS Office and adaptable to building management software (BuildingLink experience is a plus)
  • Ability to lift 30 to 50 pounds and move through the building quickly when needed
  • Multilingual ability is a genuine advantage in a downtown Dallas high-rise environment
  • Steady under pressure, especially when residents are frustrated or an emergency is developing

Worth Knowing Before You Apply

Weekend morning shifts at high-density residential buildings have a particular rhythm. Resident traffic picks up early, vendor scheduling requests come in fast, and you're expected to handle it all without someone looking over your shoulder. The candidates who do well here tend to have a hospitality background where they learned to stay calm, stay organized, and actually remember people's names. That last part sounds small. It isn't.

Worth Ross has a track record in the HOA management space and tends to promote from within when concierge staff demonstrate reliability and service quality. For someone building a career in residential property management, a concierge role at a well-run downtown property is one of the cleaner paths toward a front office or assistant manager position.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Founders Hall is a student housing community in Tempe, Arizona, which puts it squarely in the orbit of Arizona State University, one of the largest universities in the country by enrollment. Managing student housing at that scale means your leasing calendar is dictated by academic timelines, your turns are compressed and intense, and your resident base turns over in ways that traditional multifamily doesn't. The Property Manager role here carries the full operational weight of that reality.

Yugo operates nearly 40,000 beds across 88 U.S. properties, so this position connects to a genuinely global organization. The reporting line is to a Regional Property Manager, and you'll be expected to communicate property performance clearly: occupancy trends, delinquency, budget variance, operating expenses. That means knowing your numbers well enough to explain them, not just read them off a report.

Day-to-day, the role covers the full spectrum of property operations. You'll lead the on-site team, oversee rent collection and delinquency management, coordinate leasing and marketing activity, manage vendor relationships, and handle the turn process when the academic year wraps. Student housing turns tend to be high-volume and time-compressed. Getting hundreds of units ready in a narrow window before move-in requires tight coordination between leasing, maintenance, and outside contractors.
