That's a meaningful part of this job, and candidates who've run turns at student or university properties will feel the difference immediately.

Financial oversight includes reviewing T-12 performance, contributing to annual operating and capex budgets, and identifying opportunities to improve NOI. You'll also monitor local market conditions, track competitor pricing, and help keep Founders Hall positioned competitively in the ASU-area market.

What you'll bring

  • At least three years of supervisory experience in residential property management or a related operational role
  • Hands-on experience running a property, with student or university housing experience a strong differentiator
  • Proficiency in Entrata, Yardi, RealPage, or a comparable property management platform
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and applicable federal, state, and local compliance requirements
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to manage both team performance and resident relations effectively
  • A bachelor's degree in business or a related field, or equivalent residential management experience

Compensation is $70,000 to $75,000 annually, plus a fully compensated two-bedroom apartment on-site. The total package also includes health, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) with 4% employer match, three weeks of PTO, paid parental leave, and eleven paid holidays.

The candidate who does well in this role typically has enough operational range to move fluidly between a budget conversation in the morning and a resident complaint in the afternoon without losing focus on either. Student housing rewards managers who can build real culture within a community, keep their team motivated through a demanding leasing cycle, and hold occupancy without letting delinquency creep up. Those three things together are harder than they look, and the operators who get all three right tend to advance quickly in this segment of the industry.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Pre-lease cycles start months before a bed turns, traffic spikes hit hard in late fall and early spring, and closing a college student often means closing their parents too. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Leasing Manager for their Reno community to own that cycle from the top of the funnel down to a signed lease.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is an onsite leadership position, which means you're building the team as much as you're working the traffic. You'll hire, onboard, and develop both full-time and part-time leasing staff, then set the standard for how the desk runs day to day. Customer service, tour quality, closing ratios, lease renewal execution: all of it runs through you.

On the digital side, PeakMade expects real fluency with social platforms. Instagram and Facebook content, graphics built in Canva, photo editing in Lightroom or VSCO, and active reputation management through platforms like Reputation.com and JTurner are part of the weekly rhythm here. A property's online presence directly influences traffic, and traffic drives occupancy. That connection is real and measurable.

You'll also collaborate with the property manager on the annual marketing plan, coordinate lease-up events and renewal programming, and maintain accurate prospect data so the team can track where leads are dropping off and adjust. Occupancy targets, closing ratios, and retention goals are the scorecard.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least 2 years of leasing experience in off-campus student housing specifically. Conventional multifamily experience doesn't transfer cleanly to this model.
  • Prior leadership or supervisory experience, even informal mentoring or shift lead responsibility counts here.
  • Comfort working some evenings and weekends, particularly during peak traffic periods.
  • Hands-on proficiency with social media content creation and property management software.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills that connect with 19-to-22-year-olds and their parents in the same conversation.

One honest note on what separates good from great in student housing leasing: the ability to manufacture urgency without pressure tactics. College renters are price-sensitive, heavily influenced by peers, and often deciding in groups. Managers who understand that dynamic and build genuine rapport consistently outperform those who rely on scripted closes. If you've tracked your own traffic-to-lease conversion and improved it, that story will matter in an interview for this role.

Compensation is set at $52,000 annually, with monthly, quarterly, and annual commission and bonus opportunities available on top of base. PeakMade also offers a housing discount, 401(k) match, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, and access to a mentorship program for those looking to grow within the organization.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Where You'll Be Working

Midtown Place Apartments in Memphis sits in one of the city's most active residential corridors, a neighborhood with genuine walkability and consistent rental demand. For an assistant property manager, that kind of location means steady traffic, a mix of resident profiles, and the opportunity to develop your leasing and operations skills on a property that stays busy year-round. Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is a well-established regional operator, and this role reflects their preference for hiring people who already understand how residential communities function.

What the Role Covers

This is a full-cycle leasing and operations position. On the leasing side, you'll handle all stages of the apartment rental process, from initial contact through closing. You'll track daily traffic, which matters more than it sounds. Consistent traffic logging feeds into occupancy projections and tells the property manager how the property is performing against its leasing goals.

On the operations side, you'll collect and record rental payments, process service requests from residents, and conduct daily inspections of the model unit, common areas, and amenities. You'll also assist with vacant apartment inspections, which ties directly into the make-ready cycle. Knowing what a unit needs before a turn gets started saves time, cuts costs, and keeps move-in dates realistic.

When the property manager is unavailable, you step into that role. That's standard for this position level, but it means you need to be comfortable making decisions, not just executing tasks.

Saturday availability is required. That's part of the job and worth knowing before you apply.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

You'll need one to two years of residential leasing or management experience coming in. Familiarity with property management software is also expected. OneSite and Yardi are the preferred platforms here, so experience with either one will reduce your ramp-up time. You'll also need reliable transportation, a valid driver's license, and proof of insurance, along with the physical ability to walk the property and climb stairs during inspections.

What this role develops is your operational range. Leasing professionals who take on assistant manager responsibilities build fluency in the administrative and financial side of property management: payment processing, delinquency tracking, maintenance coordination, and daily reporting. These are the skills that distinguish a strong leasing consultant from someone ready to manage a property independently. If you're looking to move toward a property manager role in the next few years, this kind of position is where that transition happens.

  • 1 to 2 years of residential leasing or property management experience
  • Proficiency with OneSite or Yardi preferred
  • Weekend availability, including Saturdays
  • Ability to walk the property and navigate stairs
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance
  • Must clear credit, background, and drug screening

MRG offers a competitive salary with a performance bonus program, full medical, dental, and vision coverage, short and long-term disability, company-paid life insurance, an apartment discount, paid holidays and PTO, and a 401(k) with profit-sharing. That's a meaningful benefits package for a role at this level in the market.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This position covers two Louisville communities, Devonshire and Lyndon Crossings, with a combined unit count of more than 470. Your day runs across work orders, preventive maintenance, and apartment turns. That means HVAC troubleshooting, plumbing repairs, electrical fixtures, appliance issues, drywall, and light paint work. You'll also manage equipment and supply inventory, keep up with grounds care, and handle seasonal tasks including snow removal. Pool maintenance may be part of the mix depending on the community.

After-hours on-call is part of the job. Peak pays an on-call premium for it, but set your expectations accordingly: some nights and weekends, you'll get a call.

With 470-plus units split across two properties, the work volume is real. Strong candidates know how to triage. A clogged drain and a non-functioning furnace in January are both urgent, but they're not equal. The technicians who perform well here move efficiently, communicate clearly with residents, and don't let a full work order queue turn into a backlog.

What You Bring

  • Prior maintenance experience at an apartment community or comparable residential setting
  • Hands-on familiarity with HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and basic appliance repair
  • Ability to troubleshoot problems independently without waiting on a supervisor to direct each step
  • HVAC certification is preferred but not a hard requirement
  • Physical readiness: ladder work, confined spaces, lifting up to 50 pounds, outdoor work in all weather
  • Professionalism with residents. You're often the only person from the company they see face-to-face

Compensation and Context

Pay ranges from $17 to $27 per hour depending on experience. The package includes medical, dental, and life insurance, paid time off (plus your birthday), a 401(k) with employer match, an on-call premium, and a sign-on bonus.

Peak Management operates across multiple communities, so strong technicians here have a clear path toward senior tech or lead maintenance roles as they build tenure and skills. If you want to grow within a multi-property company rather than stay in a single-site dead end, the structure is there.

job.title: Community Manager | Rambler Atlanta - Atlanta, GA
job.description:
Rambler Atlanta is a student housing community, which means this role comes with rhythms that standard multifamily doesn't. Lease-up pressure concentrates around academic calendars. Turnover hits hard and fast in summer. Residents are often living on their own for the first time, which shapes how you handle everything from delinquency conversations to maintenance requests. If you've managed in that environment before, you already know what that means. If you haven't, it's worth being clear-eyed about it before you apply.

LV Collective is looking for a Community Manager to run day-to-day operations at Rambler Atlanta. The scope is full-cycle: budget ownership, team leadership, leasing oversight, resident relations, vendor management, and financial reporting. You'll carry the P&L, manage on-site staff across leasing and maintenance, and serve as the connection point between what's happening on the ground and what corporate leadership needs to know. Monthly variance analysis, delinquency tracking, occupancy reporting, and rent collections all fall on this role.

Resident engagement at a student property carries real weight. It's not a nice-to-have. Retention at this asset type depends on whether residents feel connected to the community, and that work falls to the manager as much as anyone. You'd be planning and executing programming, fielding concerns directly, and keeping the brand experience consistent across every touchpoint.

The evenings and weekends piece is real. This isn't a five-days-and-done position. Student housing communities have activity that doesn't stop at 5pm, and a manager here needs to be reachable and willing to show up when something needs them.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: comfort with financial statements that tell a complicated story. Student housing occupancy can look healthy on paper while delinquency or concessions erode NOI quietly. Managers who catch those variances early and adjust strategy before month-end are the ones who actually hit their targets.

LV Collective uses Entrata, and familiarity with it matters. If you've built reporting in Entrata or used it to track traffic and leasing velocity during a lease-up cycle, that's a real advantage here.

What the role requires

  • 4 or more years in property management, with student housing or multifamily experience
  • Demonstrated experience managing budgets, analyzing financials, and driving NOI
  • Experience leading on-site teams and holding people accountable to performance
  • Proficiency in Entrata (preferred), Microsoft Office, and Google Workspace
  • Strong communication skills across resident, staff, vendor, and corporate relationships
  • Experience with lease-up or new development openings is a plus

If you've built a team culture at a property that was underperforming and left it in better shape, or managed a summer turn without losing your mind, that experience is exactly what this role is built for.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
It's August, and move-in weekend is two days away. You're walking the property with a punch list in hand, confirming turns are complete, coordinating with your maintenance supervisor on a handful of last-minute work orders, and fielding a call from your leasing team about a question on a new resident's account. That's the rhythm at The Soto, Yugo's student housing community in Eugene.

The Role

Yugo operates nearly 40,000 beds across the U.S., and The Soto is one of 88 properties in that portfolio. As Property Manager, you report to the Regional Property Manager and carry full operational accountability for the community. That means staffing, financials, leasing performance, maintenance oversight, and resident experience all sit in your lane.

On the financial side, you'll manage accounts receivable and payable, own delinquency and eviction processes, and work through budget prep and variance analysis. You'll review occupancy trends and operating performance regularly, and you'll look for ways to strengthen NOI, whether by growing revenue or trimming unnecessary expense. Capital projects and vendor contracts are part of the job too, from bid coordination through completion.

Leasing and marketing aren't just a support function here. You'll oversee retention initiatives, track competitor pricing, and keep the community positioned competitively in the market. You'll ensure the leasing office and model units stay sharp and ready, because student housing traffic moves fast and first impressions close leases.

On the people side, you'll recruit, train, and develop your team, hold regular staff meetings, and manage performance when needed. You'll also handle resident complaints, disturbances, and policy violations, which in student housing means maintaining clear boundaries while keeping the community atmosphere positive.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of supervisory experience in residential property management or a closely related field
  • Direct experience managing a student or university residential community is a strong plus
  • Comfort with property management platforms such as Entrata, Yardi, or RealPage
  • Solid grounding in Fair Housing regulations and compliance requirements
  • A bachelor's degree in business or a related area, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Carbon Literacy Certification, or willingness to complete the training

The salary range for this position is $70,000 to $75,000, with bonus eligibility and a benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with 4% employer match, three weeks of PTO, paid parental leave, and eligibility for comped on-site housing.

One thing worth knowing if you're considering this role: student housing runs on an academic calendar, and the weeks around lease-up and move-in are genuinely demanding. Strong candidates for this type of position have usually built their instincts for managing surge periods, keeping a team focused under pressure, and recovering quickly when things don't go according to plan. That adaptability carries directly into broader multifamily leadership roles over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Meadow Creek
job.description:
Meadow Creek sits in Boulder, a market where quality renters have real options and maintenance responsiveness is one of the sharpest differentiators between a community that retains residents and one that bleeds them. AIR Communities knows that. Their tech stack and shop organization reflect it. This role is a real maintenance technician position at a well-run Class A community, and the day-to-day reflects that expectation.

The work divides roughly into two streams: turns and service requests. Turns mean following a structured make-ready process so that every unit hitting the market is genuinely move-in ready, not just passable. Service requests mean troubleshooting whatever the day brings, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, building systems. AIR uses technology to route and prioritize work orders, which keeps techs moving efficiently rather than burning time triaging at the shop. The shop itself is fully stocked, which sounds like a minor detail until you've spent 45 minutes hunting down a part that should've been on the shelf.

On-call is part of the job. At least one week per month, you'll need reliable transportation and the ability to respond to emergency calls outside business hours. That's the honest part of this role that doesn't get softened: Boulder residents in Class A units expect fast response, and on-call nights are real. Budget for that when you're thinking about fit.

Pay runs $25 to $28 per hour depending on your actual skill set and trade depth. There's also a quarterly customer service bonus of up to $1,500 for techs who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores. That number isn't trivial. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a genuine benefit if you're open to living onsite or nearby.

AIR's internal development program, Ascend, is designed around individual growth paths rather than a one-size training module. For a tech who wants to move into lead or maintenance supervisor territory over the next few years, that kind of structured development is worth paying attention to. Multifamily maintenance careers tend to advance through demonstrated trade depth and resident service scores, and this environment rewards both.

What you'll bring

  • At least 2 years of maintenance experience in multifamily, facilities, or building maintenance
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Availability for flexible scheduling including evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation
  • Reliable transportation for emergency response during on-call shifts
  • Physical ability to handle equipment and machinery as the work requires

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be thorough on turns, not just fast. A punch list that's actually complete before a move-in beats a quick turn with callbacks every time, and the best techs know the difference.

job.title: Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Village Green has operated residential communities since 1919, which means this Maintenance Service Manager role carries real institutional weight. The team has systems, history, and standards. Your job is to keep a San Antonio apartment community running at a level that protects asset value and keeps residents renewing.

The Skills This Role Runs On

HVAC and mechanical systems knowledge sits at the center of this position. You'll field work orders spanning EPA Universal-level refrigerant work, boiler and chiller maintenance, plumbing systems, water heaters, electrical, and appliances. That breadth matters because you're not just turning wrenches. You're triaging, prioritizing, and deciding what gets done today versus what goes on the capex list. Identifying capital improvements and pulling bids is part of the job, as is preparing the maintenance portion of the annual budget. Monthly energy management reports land on your desk too, which means you're reading consumption trends and putting recommendations in writing.

Team leadership is the other core skill set. You'll supervise maintenance staff directly: distributing work orders, managing schedules, and keeping the make-ready pipeline moving so turns don't stall occupancy. You'll also be involved in interviewing candidates when the team needs to grow. Mentoring existing staff is just as important as recruiting them. A preventative maintenance program only works when the whole crew understands it and executes it consistently.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Two years of supervisory experience in apartment, hotel, or similar facilities maintenance is the baseline. What separates a strong hire from an average one is the combination of mechanical depth and genuine coaching instincts. Technicians who got promoted because they were the best at repairs sometimes struggle to delegate and develop others. This role needs someone who can diagnose a complex HVAC issue at 8 AM and run a productive team huddle at 8:15. Customer service matters too. Residents interact with maintenance staff more directly than any other department, and every completed work order is a retention moment.

Proficiency with maintenance software is required. Work order documentation, completion rates, and aging reports are all tracked, and you'll need to stay on top of that data to run an efficient operation.

Working at Village Green

Village Green holds multi-year recognition from Great Place to Work and Best Workplaces in Multifamily, both of which reflect how the company manages its people internally. The company's approach is to invest in associates with training and tools rather than just filling seats. For a Maintenance Manager, that tends to mean real support on capital projects and access to resources rather than being stretched thin and expected to improvise. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, a bonus program, and a 401(k) with a company match.

San Antonio's multifamily market has stayed active, with steady demand keeping occupancy pressure real across the metro. Keeping turns tight and preventative maintenance current directly affects NOI here. This is a role where your operational decisions show up in the numbers.

job.title: Cortland Duluth Maintenance Hiring Event - 11/10/2026
job.description:
What's Happening and What You'll Do

Cortland is holding an in-person hiring event at their Duluth, GA community on Tuesday, November 10th from 10:00am to 2:00pm, with on-the-spot interviews for two roles: Maintenance Technician and Service Technician. The address is 1335 Herrington Rd, Duluth, GA 30096. Bring your resume, driver's license, and copies of any certifications you hold (EPA, CPO).

The Maintenance Technician role covers the full range of building systems: HVAC diagnosis and repair, electrical, plumbing, appliances, flooring, railings, and structural components. You'll run preventative maintenance schedules on HVAC units, keep parts inventory stocked, document completed work orders, and stay in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. You'll also flag hazards and monitor building systems like automatic doors and security cameras to support asset preservation. Active EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) is required. Experience range is 2 to 5 years.

The Service Technician role is the entry point. You'll handle basic repairs, make-ready tasks on vacant units, daily grounds upkeep, and resident service requests. EPA certification isn't required here. One year of relevant experience is enough to qualify. This role is a strong fit for someone with a solid work ethic and general handyman skills who wants to grow into a full technician position.

What You Bring

  • Maintenance Technician: 2 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience, active EPA certification, technical skills across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and the ability to manage multiple open work orders without dropping the ball
  • Service Technician: 1+ year in maintenance or facilities work, basic repair skills, comfort with hand tools, reliable and punctual, strong customer service instincts
  • Both roles require physical capability: lifting, ladder work, and outdoor conditions in Georgia heat
  • Both roles require a high school diploma or equivalent

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Cortland is one of the larger vertically integrated multifamily operators in the country, which matters here. Their in-house maintenance structure means technicians tend to have clearer escalation paths than you'd find at a smaller third-party management shop. Service Technicians who build their skills and earn their EPA certification have a direct route to Maintenance Technician roles within the same company, without starting over somewhere new.

The Duluth submarket sits in the northern Atlanta metro, an area with a dense concentration of garden-style and mid-rise communities. Cortland operates multiple properties in the region, so technicians who perform well often have the option to move across communities or into lead roles as the portfolio grows. On-call coverage is part of the Maintenance Technician job, so come in knowing that's a real expectation, not a footnote.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
A tenant emails at 8:47 a.m. about an HVAC issue in their suite. By 9:15, you've logged the work order in the CMMS, coordinated with the building engineer, and drafted a response that keeps the relationship intact. That's a routine Tuesday in this role.

What This Role Covers

Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Assistant Property Manager in Los Angeles to support day-to-day operations across commercial, industrial, or retail assets. The scope is genuinely broad. You'll help the Property Manager keep tenants responsive and satisfied, process vendor invoices against management agreement terms and authorization limits, and contribute to monthly reporting packages and budget deliverables on the client's schedule. CAM and operating expense reconciliations are part of your workload, handled in coordination with the accounting team rather than in isolation.

Lease administration is a real part of this position: setting up new leases in the system, processing amendments, and keeping reporting current. You'll also coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, join property walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams, and assist with vendor bidding and procurement. Emergency preparedness planning and drills are included. This is a fully in-office role with regular property visits, so you're physically present and accountable to the assets you manage.

The salary range is $75,000 to $80,000 annually, with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), life insurance, long-term disability, and paid time off.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build

This role requires a few things on day one:

  • 1 to 2 years of related experience, with a bachelor's degree preferred (experience combinations considered)
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite
  • Familiarity with accounts payable and CMMS platforms
  • Working knowledge of financial terms, including the ability to calculate percentages, discounts, and conduct basic financial analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly the ability to handle tenant and vendor relationships with a constructive tone
  • Commercial real estate experience (office, retail, or industrial) is preferred but not required

What the role builds is equally worth naming. Operating expense reconciliations are one of the more technically demanding skills in commercial property management, and working through them regularly here develops fluency that transfers directly to senior property management positions. You'll also develop the ability to manage direct reports, because this role includes supervising and directing team members, which is meaningful experience at the assistant level. Lincoln's size means exposure to institutional client reporting standards and asset types that many smaller firms can't offer.

Strong candidates tend to combine organizational discipline with genuine communication skill. CAM reconciliations and lease administration require precision. Tenant relations require a different kind of intelligence. The people who grow quickly here are the ones who treat both as equally important parts of the craft.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Bexley at Whitestone in Cedar Park is a busy community, and this role touches nearly every part of daily operations. You'll work the leasing side: answering internet leads, taking calls, booking tours, processing applications, pulling together lease paperwork, collecting deposits, and getting signatures. You'll also handle the resident side once they're in the door: renewals, notices to vacate, early terminations, pet addendums, transfers, and account questions. When units turn, you'll walk them with maintenance to confirm the make-ready is actually ready before a new resident moves in. You'll post rent, chase balances, and process move-out dispositions. On top of that, you'll help plan and host resident events.

The schedule is weekdays 9 to 6, with Saturdays 9 to 5 on a team rotation. Sundays are off. Occasional after-hours support comes with the territory, particularly around resident events or weather situations. That's worth knowing upfront.

There's also a leadership component here. Weinstein expects their Assistant Managers to help train the team and contribute to hitting community goals. This isn't a pure leasing role or a pure admin role. You'll need to be comfortable moving between both and covering gaps when the team needs it.

What You Bring

  • Prior property management experience is a plus, but not required. Strong candidates from hospitality, retail management, or sales leadership transition well into this work.
  • Some form of management or supervisory experience is required. Weinstein will train the property management specifics, but they need someone who already knows how to lead people.
  • Comfort with difficult conversations. Residents don't always come to the office happy. You'll handle complaints, late payment follow-ups, and tough renewal negotiations on a regular basis.
  • Attention to detail matters here, especially around lease paperwork and security deposit dispositions. Errors in those areas create downstream problems.
  • Organization and follow-through. You'll juggle open work orders, pending applications, and resident requests simultaneously on any given day.

Context Worth Having

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company with more than 70 years in the business and a portfolio of over 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. Family-owned at that scale tends to mean flatter communication and more direct access to decision-makers than you'd find at a large REIT or institutional operator. The trade-off is that expectations are high and they want people who take ownership.

Pay starts at $23 per hour and increases with experience. Quarterly bonuses are included. Benefits cover health, dental, vision, 401k with company match, a rent discount, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, and birthday time off. The training program is structured, which matters if you're coming from outside the industry. Many people in leadership at Weinstein started in leasing or assistant roles, so the path upward is real for candidates who perform.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of genuine customer patience and comfort with accountability. The leasing and admin tasks can be learned. Handling a frustrated resident or following up on a delinquency balance without letting it affect your next interaction is harder to train, and it's what Weinstein needs at the assistant level.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant General Manager for one of its communities in Miami's 33137 market, a zip code that covers Edgewater and parts of the Upper East Side. This is an active, floor-level management role. You're not a back-office operator. You're on the ground, leasing, managing delinquency, coaching staff, and keeping the property looking sharp.

What You'll Actually Do

Your days split between two modes: operational support and direct leasing. When the General Manager is out, you run the community. That means handling resident concerns, keeping the team on task, and making decisions. When the GM is present, you focus on your own performance: conducting tours that convert, collecting rent, posting receipts, and chasing down delinquency before it becomes a problem on the month-end report.

You'll also own the resident experience side of things. That means following up after move-ins, resolving complaints with actual care rather than scripted responses, and staying visible in the community. Bozzuto ties retention goals directly to how well the team handles everyday interactions, so the small stuff matters here.

Weekend availability is part of the job. Expect one to two weekends per month in exchange for two weekdays off. Prospective residents look at apartments on Saturdays and Sundays. You need to be there for that traffic.

What You Bring

  • At least two years in property management, hospitality, or retail, with real exposure to rent collection, accounts receivable, and budget basics
  • A four-year degree or comparable work experience
  • Comfort with Yardi or similar property management software
  • Confidence running social media (Facebook, Instagram) to support leasing and community engagement
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You'll be talking to prospects, residents, vendors, and ownership-level stakeholders
  • A sales instinct. You need to close leases, not just show units

Context Worth Knowing

The AGM role at a company like Bozzuto is one of the cleaner paths to a General Manager or Community Manager position. You're learning financial oversight, team leadership, and leasing strategy simultaneously. Candidates who advance quickly tend to be the ones who treat delinquency management and NOI awareness as seriously as the leasing side. The people who stall are usually strong on traffic and tours but hands-off when it comes to collections and accountability conversations.

Miami's rental market moves fast and residents have options. That makes genuine service quality, not just amenity packages, a real differentiator. If you've worked in a competitive urban market before, that experience will translate directly here.

Compensation sits in the $64,000 to $65,000 range with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Senior Property Manager
job.description:
You're reviewing a delinquency report before your first tenant meeting of the day, already flagging two lease expirations coming up in the next six months that need renewal strategy before the client call this afternoon. That's the rhythm of this role: financial precision and relationship management running in parallel, constantly.

What This Role Actually Covers

Lincoln Property Company is hiring a Senior Property Manager in Sacramento to oversee a commercial portfolio that may span office, industrial, and retail assets. You'll serve as the owner representative for institutional clients, which means the monthly reports, annual budgets, and variance analyses you produce aren't internal formalities. They're client deliverables that directly shape how ownership evaluates the asset and your team's performance.

Day-to-day responsibilities include full lease administration oversight: tracking expirations, covenants, restrictions, and financial covenants that affect NOI. You'll manage AR proactively, including preparing legal notices with client approval, and you'll direct vendor sourcing and contract compliance, potentially consolidating procurement across the portfolio to drive savings. Emergency response planning, property inspections, and capex recommendations are also in scope.

This is a supervisory position. You'll recruit, hire, train, and formally evaluate direct reports, and you'll be expected to provide genuine strategic guidance rather than just administrative oversight. Lincoln's model rewards managers who develop their teams as much as they develop their assets.

What the Right Candidate Brings

  • 5 to 8 years of commercial property management experience, including direct exposure to office, retail, or industrial assets
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent experience considered
  • Active California real estate license required
  • CPM or RPA designation, or active candidacy, preferred
  • Proficiency in Yardi or MRI; Kardin familiarity is a plus
  • Strong Excel skills for budget modeling, variance reporting, and long-range capital planning
  • AP and CMMS system experience required
  • Working knowledge of commercial leases, property taxes, financial instruments, and construction processes

The candidates who stand out at this level aren't just competent operators. They can read a T-12, identify where NOI is drifting from proforma, and explain it to a client in plain language before the client asks. They also understand that tenant retention is a financial strategy, not just a service goal. Keeping a tenant from going MTM or dark on a big-box space protects the asset's value in ways that show up clearly in any disposition scenario.

From a career standpoint, this role builds the full skill set that feeds into regional or portfolio director positions. Senior PMs who own client relationships at Lincoln, manage mixed-use or multi-asset portfolios, and develop subordinate managers are the profile that gets considered for regional leadership. Sacramento's commercial market, with its government, healthcare, and industrial mix, gives you exposure to asset classes that transfer well across institutional portfolios nationally.

Compensation is $130,000 to $150,000 annually. This is a fully in-office position at Lincoln's Sacramento location.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician (Future Growth) - Broomfield, CO
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer in the National Apartment Association for three consecutive years, and this lead maintenance role in Broomfield reflects why. It's a pipeline position, posted ahead of confirmed growth in the market, which means the right candidate steps in ready to build something rather than simply inherit it.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day scope here is genuinely broad. You'll run maintenance operations for an apartment community: scheduling your team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads, coordinating with outside contractors, and keeping the turn process moving so vacant units come back online clean and on time. That means hands-on work alongside your crew on HVAC, mechanical, electrical, and structural repairs, plus staying current on preventative maintenance schedules for pools, irrigation, appliances, and building exteriors.

Inspections are a significant part of the role. Monthly, quarterly, and annual property walkthroughs are your baseline, and you'll also inspect show units and make-ready apartments in close coordination with the leasing and business management teams. Service request tracking, inventory management, and vendor communication all run through property management software, so comfort with digital workflows matters.

You'll also carry hiring and development responsibilities for the service team, which puts leadership skills on equal footing with technical ability.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of hands-on experience in residential, commercial, or apartment maintenance, including time in a supervisory capacity
  • EPA 608 certification and demonstrated HVAC competency
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with on-call rotation as needed
  • Organized approach to parts and supply inventory so shortages don't stall turns or repairs
  • Comfort working across teams, including leasing staff and property management, not just within a maintenance silo

Context Worth Knowing

Broomfield sits in one of the more active multifamily corridors along the US-36 corridor between Denver and Boulder. Class A and B communities in the area compete on maintenance responsiveness and curb appeal as much as on amenities, so a lead tech who keeps service request times tight and turns moving efficiently makes a direct impact on resident retention and NOI. The pay range for this role sits at $35 to $36 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of that. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among other offerings.

Candidates who tend to excel in roles like this one know how to shift between working hands-on and stepping back to manage their team without micromanaging. If your instinct when a service request comes in is to think about both the fix and how it fits into the broader workload for the week, that's the mindset Olympus is looking for here.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Bella Vista at Elk Grove Apartments
job.description:
Leasing consultants at garden-style apartment communities in the Sacramento suburbs wear a few hats at once: salesperson, file keeper, move-in coordinator, and the first face a frustrated resident sees when something goes wrong. At Bella Vista Apartments in Elk Grove, that's exactly the job.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Most of your time splits between the leasing office and the property itself. You'll greet prospects, walk units, qualify applicants, and get leases signed. When a new resident moves in, you're coordinating with maintenance to make sure the unit is ready and the process goes smoothly. That coordination matters more than it sounds. A rocky move-in is the kind of first impression that's hard to undo.

The administrative side is real and consistent. Rental files need to stay current and accurate. Data entry into the property management system has to be done right, because bad data causes problems downstream for everyone. Month-end brings its own stack of paperwork. You'll also handle resident concerns directly, including maintenance follow-ups, payment issues, and complaints. Not every resident conversation is easy, and this role doesn't pretend otherwise.

  • Greet and qualify prospective residents, tour units, and close leases
  • Prepare lease documents and oversee signing with new residents
  • Coordinate with the maintenance team on make-ready timelines and move-in readiness
  • Maintain accurate rental files and enter data into the property system
  • Support monthly administrative tasks and keep property paperwork organized
  • Interact professionally with current residents on maintenance concerns, complaints, and rent collection

Who Fits This Role

MG Properties prefers candidates with at least one year of property management experience, though what they're really screening for is someone who can sell and still stay organized. Strong candidates in leasing tend to be the ones who treat follow-up as a habit, not a reminder. If you can close a lease on a Saturday afternoon and then sit down and get your files updated before you leave for the day, that's the rhythm this job runs on.

Professional etiquette matters here. Elk Grove is a growing suburban market with a mix of families, young professionals, and long-term residents. The person in this seat represents MG Properties every time they pick up the phone or walk a prospect to a unit.

Compensation and Growth

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of base. The company also offers profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and a rental discount. PTO includes 10 days per year, 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, and 40 hours of paid sick time.

MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years and has a track record of promoting from within. For a leasing consultant who wants to move into an assistant manager or property manager role, this is the kind of company where that path is real, not just a line in a job posting.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Hawthorne Residential Partners, the Leasing Consultant role sits at the center of the community's daily rhythm. Your mornings might start with a stack of unread inquiry emails and a handful of scheduled tours. By afternoon, you're walking a prospect through a unit, reading what they care about, and adjusting your presentation on the fly. You'll close the day following up on applications, tracking down a missing verification document, and making sure the leasing office looks sharp for tomorrow. Saturdays bring a different energy: shorter hours, motivated traffic, and often the highest-conversion day of the week.

Beyond tours and paperwork, this role has a community-building dimension that leasing roles at smaller operators often lack. You'll help coordinate resident events, contribute to social media outreach, and keep a working knowledge of competing communities in the Cary market. Occupancy and renewal goals are shared targets, so your results connect directly to the property's NOI picture even at the consultant level.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Confidence communicating in person, by phone, and through written channels like email and web chat
  • Comfort following a defined process for applications, move-in paperwork, and lead follow-up
  • A valid driver's license
  • A CALP designation is a plus, though Hawthorne provides development resources if you're working toward it

Strong candidates tend to be people who genuinely enjoy the persuasion side of leasing: identifying what a prospect needs, addressing hesitation directly, and guiding them toward a decision without pressure. If you find that kind of conversation energizing rather than draining, you'll fit the rhythm of this role well.

Where This Role Takes You

Hawthorne operates a formal career path program, and the Leasing Consultant position is a recognized entry point into property management leadership. The natural next step is Assistant Community Manager, where you'd take on more operational responsibility including delinquency tracking, reporting, and vendor coordination. The skills you build here, reading traffic patterns, working renewal conversations, and managing leasing paperwork accurately, transfer directly to that next level and beyond.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep hours at 40. Resident events may occasionally extend into evenings. Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, along with a full benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, and pet insurance, among others.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Fee management operators like Bozzuto run on tight NOI discipline and resident retention numbers that compound over time. The Assistant General Manager role exists because property performance at that level requires two people who can own the outcome, and the AGM carries full operational weight when the GM is out of the building.

This position sits at a community in Saint Petersburg, FL. The day-to-day splits between leasing activity and financial operations. You're conducting tours that convert traffic into signed leases, posting rental receipts, and managing delinquency closely enough that it doesn't quietly drag the T-12. You're also the person on the floor two weekends a month when prospective residents are actively shopping, which is exactly when converting traffic matters most. In return, you get two weekdays off during those weeks.

Where the Role Actually Lives

Resident retention is a big part of this job's contribution to NOI. Losing a resident triggers a turn, a make-ready, potential concessions to fill the unit, and a gap in rental income. The AGM role is one of the primary buffers against that cycle. Every resident interaction, from a maintenance concern to a lease renewal conversation, is an opportunity to keep occupancy where it needs to be. You're also the person coaching and holding the leasing team accountable when the GM steps away, which means your influence on traffic-to-lease ratios is direct.

Bozzuto uses Yardi, so familiarity with that platform will shorten your ramp time. Social media content creation is part of the role as well, specifically platforms like Instagram and Facebook where community brand presence affects both traffic and resident engagement.

What You Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years working in one of those industries
  • Working knowledge of rent collection, accounts receivable, and basic budget exposure
  • Comfort with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Sales instincts that show up in leasing conversations, not just on paper

The AGM role is a natural stepping stone toward General Manager. Operators who spend time here building delinquency discipline, leasing conversion habits, and team management experience tend to move into GM positions with a clear picture of what the full P&L responsibility looks like. That context is harder to get any other way. The salary range for this position runs from $65,000 to $69,000, with bonus eligibility on top of base, along with Bozzuto's benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, paid time off, 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What This Role Actually Involves

At Lincoln Property Company's Burlingame office, this Assistant Property Manager position sits at the center of day-to-day commercial operations. Lincoln manages an enormous portfolio spanning office, industrial, retail, and life science assets across the country, and this role supports that work at the property level. You'll work alongside a Property Manager to keep tenants, vendors, and ownership clients aligned, and you'll touch nearly every functional area of the property's operations, from financial reporting to lease administration to physical inspections.

That breadth is worth taking seriously before you apply. This isn't a single-track administrative role. On any given week, you might be reviewing vendor invoices against authorization limits, coordinating a tenant move-out walkthrough, pulling data for a CAM reconciliation, and helping draft sections of the monthly ownership report. The variety keeps things interesting, but it also demands that you stay organized and communicative when priorities compete.

Core Responsibilities

  • Support tenant relations by ensuring building staff and vendors respond to issues promptly and within the terms of lease and management agreements
  • Review and recommend approval of vendor invoices in compliance with LPC policies and applicable authorization thresholds
  • Assist with monthly reporting and budget package preparation for ownership clients
  • Collect and draft operating expense reconciliations (CAM/OpEx) in coordination with the accounting team
  • Manage lease administration tasks including setup, amendments, and system updates
  • Coordinate and document tenant move-ins and move-outs, including participation in walkthroughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams
  • Support procurement and vendor bidding processes
  • Assist with emergency response planning and participate in required drills
  • Conduct regular property inspections and travel to assigned properties as needed
  • Provide direction and performance guidance to any direct reports in the role

Who Tends to Succeed Here

Candidates who do well in this kind of role typically combine solid financial literacy with genuine people skills. CAM reconciliations and invoice approvals require comfort with numbers and attention to contractual detail. Tenant communication, vendor coordination, and ownership reporting require clarity, patience, and the ability to keep a professional tone when things go sideways. Those two skill sets don't always come in the same package, and the people who bring both tend to move quickly in commercial property management.

Lincoln looks for a bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, with one to two years in a related property management or real estate role. Proficiency in Microsoft Office is expected, and familiarity with accounts payable and CMMS platforms will help you get up to speed faster. Experience with commercial office, retail, or industrial properties is a meaningful advantage at this level.

One practical note: this position is fully in-office in Burlingame, with regular travel to assigned properties. The Burlingame submarket sits within the broader San Francisco Peninsula commercial corridor, which carries higher tenant expectations around service levels and communication responsiveness. You'll feel that in the pace and the standards tenants bring to their interactions with the management team.

The compensation for this role is set at $85,000 annually. Lincoln's benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k), flexible time off, company-paid life insurance and long-term disability, and an employee assistance program. The company also emphasizes internal development through mentorship and training, which matters if you're thinking about where this role leads. Assistant Property Manager is a common stepping stone toward a Property Manager or Senior PM title, particularly for those who build strong ownership reporting skills and develop relationships across the vendor and tenant base early.

job.title: Business Manager - Aiya
job.description:
Property management companies lean on their Business Managers to do work that doesn't fit neatly into a single job description. You're part financial analyst, part HR lead, part facilities director, part leasing coach. At a Class A community like Aiya in Gilbert, AZ, that breadth is the whole point. Olympus Property is looking for someone who can hold all of those threads at once and still deliver results to regional leadership each month.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Business Manager title here is the property manager role. You run the asset. That means owning the financials from budget forecasts and annual business plans to monthly NOI performance reviews with your Regional Manager and VP. It means watching occupancy and delinquency closely, understanding what's driving your numbers, and adjusting strategy before a problem compounds. On the leasing side, you oversee renewal programs, retention efforts, and the sales training your office staff needs to convert traffic into signed leases.

You'll also direct maintenance operations. That's not just keeping units in make-ready condition for turns. It includes bidding and negotiating vendor contracts, overseeing one-time capital projects, and keeping amenity and common areas at the standard a luxury resident expects. Regular property inspections are part of the routine, not an occasional task.

The schedule is full-time Monday through Friday, with hours ranging between 8 AM and 6 PM. After-hours availability for resident events and emergencies is a real expectation, not fine print. If your current role has a hard stop at 5 PM every day, that's worth thinking about before applying.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years of multifamily property manager experience, with Class A or luxury experience preferred
  • Comfortable inside RealPage/Onesite and Knock, or able to get there quickly
  • Confident reading and presenting financial performance data, not just pulling reports
  • Experience managing a mixed team of leasing and maintenance staff
  • Steady under competing deadlines and comfortable shifting priorities mid-week

The candidates who tend to succeed in roles like this aren't just good operators. They're credible coaches. Your leasing team needs someone who can actually teach sales technique, not just set occupancy targets. Your maintenance team needs clear direction and accountability. You need to hold both, consistently, while keeping your regional leadership informed and your residents satisfied. That combination is harder to find than the job description makes it sound.

Base pay runs $80,000 to $85,000 depending on experience, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program among other offerings. Olympus Property has earned recognition as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years, which suggests the culture language in their postings reflects something real.

job.title: Appliance Repair Technician - Temporary (Full-Time or Part-Time)
job.description:
A resident calls in that her refrigerator stopped cooling overnight. By 9 a.m., you're in her apartment, running diagnostics, and by noon the compressor issue is identified and parts are ordered. That's a typical morning at Bexley Crossing at Providence.

Weinstein Properties is bringing on a temporary Appliance Repair Technician at this Ballantyne-area community for an assignment expected to run up to 60 days, with the possibility of extension based on property needs. Both full-time (up to 40 hours per week) and part-time schedules are available, and the company wants someone who can commit to at least 30 days. Weinstein owns and manages its communities directly, so the onsite team tends to be cohesive and invested in the property rather than juggling multiple client accounts.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

The core of this role is residential appliance repair across the community, both in occupied apartments and vacant units going through turns. You'll diagnose and fix refrigerators, washers, dryers, dishwashers, ranges, ovens, and similar appliances, troubleshooting electrical, mechanical, and operational issues and replacing faulty components as needed. You'll also handle appliance installations and replacements as they come up.

Work orders are managed electronically, so comfort with a mobile device or digital system matters. When your appliance queue allows, you may assist the onsite maintenance team with general work orders or make-ready tasks, but appliance repair is the primary focus here.

Because you'll be working inside residents' homes, professionalism and basic communication skills matter as much as your technical ability. Residents notice when a technician is courteous and organized. The team notices when you clean up after yourself and close out work orders accurately.

What This Role Calls For

  • Hands-on experience diagnosing and repairing residential appliances across all common types
  • Ability to work independently and manage a work order queue without close supervision
  • Comfort with hand tools, power tools, and appliance diagnostic equipment
  • Physical capability to lift up to 75 lbs and handle stairs, kneeling, and bending throughout the day
  • Reliable transportation to the property
  • Willingness to assist with general maintenance tasks as a secondary responsibility
  • Ability to pass a background check
  • Prior apartment maintenance experience is a plus, though not required

One thing that tends to separate strong candidates in a role like this: speed without shortcuts. In a community setting, there are always more work orders than hours. Technicians who can accurately triage on the first visit, order the right part the first time, and return promptly to close out the repair build goodwill fast with both residents and the maintenance supervisor. Those who reschedule often or leave repairs open create friction for the whole team.

If you've spent time doing route-based appliance service and you're ready to work from one location for a defined period, this is a straightforward fit.

job.title: Community Manager (414 Petaluma)
job.description:
Affordable housing property management sits at the intersection of compliance-heavy operations and deeply human work. The Community Manager role exists because someone has to hold both of those realities at once: keeping a property financially sound and regulatorily airtight while also being the person residents actually trust. At MidPen Housing, a nonprofit with over five decades of affordable housing development across Northern California, that dual expectation is baked into the culture.

This opening is for 414 Petaluma, a community in MidPen's portfolio of more than 142 properties serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. You'd report to the Property Manager and lead a small on-site team, with day-to-day accountability for everything from fiscal operations to resident certifications to unit turns.

What This Role Actually Involves

On the operations side, you'll manage rent collection, security deposits, delinquency, and bank deposits. You'll run re-certifications and income verifications under HUD, TCAC, and other regulatory frameworks. Compliance documentation, Fair Housing protocols, lease renewals, waitlist management, and incident reporting are all yours. You'll also coordinate preventative maintenance schedules, conduct daily property inspections, and make sure unit turnovers happen within established timeframes.

On the people side, you'll supervise and coach your on-site staff, build relationships with community partners and local agencies, and serve as the steady presence residents turn to when something goes wrong. MidPen's Resident Services team works alongside property management, so you won't be the only support system, but you will be the most visible one.

One honest note: affordable housing compliance, especially in a tax credit property, generates a real documentation load. Strong candidates tend to be people who find structure useful rather than burdensome, and who can context-switch between a sensitive resident conversation and a certification audit without losing focus on either.

What MidPen Is Looking For

  • An associate degree plus at least three years of multifamily residential management experience, with a minimum of two years specifically in affordable housing (or an equivalent combination)
  • At least one year of supervisory experience with demonstrated ability to develop staff
  • Tax Credit Specialist (TCS) or Certified Occupancy Specialist (COS) certification, or the ability to earn one within six months (MidPen covers the cost)
  • Current working knowledge of Fair Housing laws, with the ability to pass the FHA assessment within the first 60 days
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and RealPage property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to read and interpret regulatory documents

The pay range for this role is $25.62 to $28.82 per hour, based on experience and qualifications. Company-provided on-site housing is available, which is notable given Petaluma's rental market. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, an employee education reimbursement program, FSA options, an EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

For candidates thinking about trajectory: Community Manager roles at well-run affordable housing nonprofits often develop into Property Manager or Regional Manager positions, particularly for people who strengthen their compliance credentials and demonstrate consistent NOI performance over time. MidPen's scale across 12 counties means internal mobility is a realistic path, not just a talking point.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Harken)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Prometheus calls this role a Neighbor Ambassador, and the title reflects something real about how the job works. At their Harken community in Los Altos, you're the first person a prospective resident meets, and often the one they remember most when it's time to renew. The day-to-day splits across three lanes: customer experience, sales, and operations.

On the customer side, you're making sure current residents feel genuinely looked after, not just processed. On the sales side, you're guiding prospects through the leasing experience from first inquiry to signed agreement. And on the admin side, you're handling the operational basics that keep a community running: market surveys, rental agreements, advertising posts, and neighborhood-level reporting. Los Altos sits in one of the tightest and most expensive rental submarkets in the Bay Area, which means prospects arrive informed and selective. Your job is to earn their trust, not just capture their interest.

Weekends are when traffic peaks, so your schedule will include Saturday and Sunday. Your regular days off fall during the week, and Prometheus offers a weekend shift premium to reflect that commitment.

What You Bring

  • A background in customer service, sales, or a client-facing role, even outside property management
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to adapt your approach to different people quickly
  • Comfort working independently while staying accountable to a team
  • Enough organizational discipline to juggle leasing activity and administrative tasks in the same shift
  • A genuine interest in building a career in property management, not just filling a role temporarily

Prometheus is open about hiring from outside the industry. If you've come from hospitality, retail, or another service environment and you have the instincts for connecting with people and closing, the company is structured to bring you up to speed on the property management side.

Compensation and Career Context

The hourly rate runs from $25.00 to $26.25, with a $200 incentive per signed lease and a discretionary semi-annual bonus. Additional bonuses apply for referrals, training coaching, lease-up performance, and renovation projects. Medical, dental, and vision coverage is 100% company-paid, including for eligible dependents. The benefits package also includes a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts.

For someone early in a property management career, this type of leasing role builds a foundation that transfers directly to assistant manager and then property manager positions. The administrative exposure here, specifically the reporting, market survey work, and leasing operations, gives you a clearer picture of how a property performs than most pure leasing roles do. Candidates who advance quickly tend to be the ones who treat the admin side as seriously as the sales side rather than viewing paperwork as secondary to touring.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Cottonwood Apartments
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisors at Cottonwood Residential are doing real operational work, not just delegating. At Cottonwood Apartments in Millcreek, Utah, you'll own the full maintenance function for the community: directing your team through daily work orders, managing the make-ready schedule, running a preventative maintenance program, and keeping vendors accountable to scope and timelines. When an HVAC system needs attention or a plumbing repair escalates, you're the one with the technical knowledge to assess it and the leadership to route it correctly.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day covers a lot of ground. You'll assign and prioritize work orders each morning, inspect units and common areas for maintenance needs and safety risks, coordinate vendor scheduling, and track inventory and supply orders against the property budget. Make-ready units will flow through your team, and you're responsible for the quality and pace of that process. You'll also own the administrative side: purchase order tracking, SDS logs, required documentation, and accurate records for equipment and vendor services. Resident communication matters here too. When a maintenance concern comes in, your team's response time and professionalism directly affect satisfaction and retention.

You'll hire, onboard, and develop your maintenance technicians. That means coaching people through technical gaps, setting performance expectations, and building a team culture built around safety and accountability. Entrata experience helps you manage the work order system and keep everything closed out correctly.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of multifamily maintenance experience, with 2 or more years supervising a team
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Strong hands-on knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) preferred; CAMT preferred
  • Comfort with budget management, vendor coordination, and inventory tracking
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Entrata experience is a plus
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly, with occasional heavier lifts supported by team members
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation

Where This Role Takes You

Maintenance Supervisor is one of the clearest stepping stones in multifamily operations. The skills you build here, budgeting, vendor management, team development, preventative maintenance planning, translate directly into Regional Maintenance Director or Facilities Manager roles as your portfolio grows. Companies like Cottonwood Residential, which operates across a national multifamily portfolio, tend to promote from within as they scale, and supervisors who demonstrate financial discipline alongside technical competence move up faster than those who lead on technical skill alone. If you've been a strong technician looking to grow into leadership, or an experienced supervisor looking for a company with operational depth, this is the kind of role where those skills compound.

Cottonwood Residential operates as a fully integrated real estate company, meaning maintenance leadership here connects directly to asset-level decisions, not just day-to-day repairs. That's a different context than working for a third-party fee management shop, and it gives you broader visibility into how property performance is actually measured.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Future Opportunity
job.description:
Leasing roles at owner-operators like Berkshire Residential tend to develop skills that third-party management jobs simply can't replicate at the same pace. When the company owns what it manages, leasing consultants sit closer to real performance conversations around occupancy, traffic conversion, and resident retention. That context compounds quickly for people who pay attention to it.

What the Role Covers Day to Day

Berkshire is building a pipeline for leasing talent in the Nashville metro, posting this as a future opportunity across their portfolio. The core of the work is conversion: turning qualified traffic into signed leases and maintaining a closing ratio of at least 20%. That number is concrete, and it gives you something to track your own growth against. Beyond closing, you'll keep tour routes and model units in showcase condition, stay current on local market conditions and competitor trends, and bring marketing ideas to the property manager. Resident communications, both written and verbal, are part of the daily rhythm alongside administrative work that requires real attention to detail. The expectation is professional, responsive service for prospective residents, current residents, and your fellow team members equally.

Berkshire describes the culture as entrepreneurial, and the leasing consultant role reflects that. You're not just processing applications. You're contributing to how the property markets itself and how residents experience the community from first contact through renewal conversations.

What Berkshire Is Looking For

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience in any service environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort adapting to new technologies (leasing CRMs, digital communication tools)
  • Energy and genuine interest in working with a wide range of people
  • Organizational discipline and administrative accuracy

The base salary range runs from $40,700 to $46,900, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include health coverage, retirement, paid time off including parental leave, and a 25% rent discount. Personal development plans are part of the package, which matters more than it sounds for people thinking about what comes next.

Where This Role Leads

Leasing consultant is the most direct on-ramp to assistant manager and then property manager roles in residential property management. The skills that get built here, closing discipline, market awareness, resident relationship management, and administrative accuracy, transfer cleanly into those next-level positions. Nashville's multifamily market has seen sustained lease-up activity and continued Class A and B development, which means experienced leasing professionals with strong conversion track records are consistently in demand across the region. Consultants who learn to read their own metrics, traffic sources, closing ratios, delinquency trends, and understand how leasing activity connects to NOI tend to accelerate into management faster than those who stay focused only on the front-of-house experience. This posting is worth getting on Berkshire's radar even before a specific opening is confirmed.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 a.m. for a leaking faucet. By the time you've closed it out, you've also flagged a worn supply line, noted a caulking issue around the tub surround, and updated inventory because you used the last of a part. That's a typical hour for a Maintenance Technician at Berkshire Residential's Central Place community.

The Work Itself

Berkshire owns and manages its own portfolio, which means the maintenance team answers to an operator with a genuine long-term interest in how the property holds up. This role covers the full range of day-to-day upkeep: appliance repairs, plumbing, electrical work, carpentry, and general building maintenance. You'll support the make-ready process, keep curb appeal sharp, and enforce safety standards consistently. Inventory control, equipment care, and key security all fall within your scope. Customer service matters here too. Residents interact with maintenance more than almost any other department, so how you communicate and follow through shapes the living experience directly.

This is an in-house maintenance position, not third-party work, which changes the nature of accountability. When something stays broken or looks neglected, the team that manages the asset also feels the consequence in resident satisfaction and renewal rates. That ownership mentality runs through how Berkshire structures its teams.

What the Role Requires vs. What It Builds

Coming in, you'll need at least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting. Competency across the core trades is required: plumbing, electrical, appliances, and basic carpentry. Computer literacy matters too since work orders and communication happen through property management platforms. Clear written and verbal communication in English is a baseline requirement.

What the role develops over time is systems thinking. Technicians who grow in this environment learn to move from reactive repairs toward proactive preservation, spotting the punch list items during a routine visit before they become capital expenses. That shift in mindset is what separates a solid technician from one who becomes a lead or service manager. Berkshire's structure of personal development plans suggests the company actively invests in that progression.

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of appliances, plumbing, electrical, and carpentry
  • Ability to manage inventory and equipment with attention to detail
  • Strong communication skills, written and verbal
  • Comfort with computers and related property management tools

The base salary range runs from $52,000 to $58,240 annually, with placement determined by experience and qualifications. The position includes health care coverage, retirement benefits, paid time off including sick and parental leave, bonuses, and a 25% rent discount for those who live on-site.

job.title: Porter
job.description:
Porter roles at affordable housing communities carry more weight than people expect. The property's daily appearance shapes how residents feel about where they live, and at a portfolio the size of Fairstead's, maintaining that standard consistently across common areas, grounds, and building exteriors is a real discipline, not a background task.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Each day starts with a property walk. You're checking curb appeal, scanning for safety issues, and identifying anything that needs immediate attention before residents are moving through common spaces. From there, cleaning responsibilities cover the full exterior and interior common areas: floors, carpets, vents, restrooms, lobbies, and building entrances. You'll handle scheduled tasks like carpet cleaning, stripping, waxing, and buffing alongside the daily sweep-and-mop routine. When spills or other cleaning emergencies come up, you respond promptly. In colder months, snow and ice removal from sidewalks and entrances becomes part of the rotation, along with placing appropriate hazard signage whenever conditions warrant it.

You'll also track supply inventory and flag replenishment needs to management before they become a problem. That kind of proactive communication is part of the role's value. A supervisor shouldn't be discovering a supply shortage on the same day someone needs it.

Skills This Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

Coming in, you need attention to detail, genuine interest in custodial work, and the ability to manage a flexible schedule that can include weekends and on-call availability. Physical stamina matters here. The job moves, and it moves outdoors as much as indoors.
