What this role builds is worth naming clearly. Porters who pay attention to what they're seeing on their daily walks develop a trained eye for property conditions that maintenance teams rely on. You learn how a well-managed property presents itself, what deferred attention looks like before it becomes a repair order, and how to communicate problems in a way that actually helps. Those habits transfer directly into maintenance technician roles, groundskeeping leads, and eventually facilities coordination positions for candidates who want to grow within property management.

The Company Behind the Role

Fairstead operates a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, focused specifically on affordable housing. They're an integrated owner, operator, and developer, which means decisions about how properties are maintained connect back to people who care about long-term community outcomes, not just short-term cost reduction. That context matters for someone doing ground-level work every day.

  • Employer-contributed medical insurance through Meritain
  • Employer-paid vision coverage
  • Company-matched 401(k): 100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%
  • Paid time off including sick leave
  • Employer-paid life insurance
  • Flexible spending account
  • Pet insurance and disability coverage
  • Employee discounts on appliances and apparel

If you take pride in how a property looks and want to work for an organization where that pride has a real audience, this is a place to build something longer-term.

job.title: Lease-Up Community Manager
job.description:
Lease-up management occupies its own category within multifamily operations. Getting a new community to stabilized occupancy requires a different skill set than running a seasoned asset: you're building systems, training people, and chasing traffic all at once, often before the dust has fully settled. Dream Live Prosper Communities, a subsidiary of DLP Capital, is hiring a Community Manager specifically for this phase at their Dream Winter Haven property in Winter Haven, FL.

This isn't a seat-warmer role. DLP describes this position as larger in scope than a typical community manager job, and that framing is accurate for lease-up work. You're accountable for occupancy targets (the benchmark here is 95%), financial performance against a community budget, and the human systems that make both happen. You'll report directly to a General Manager and own your numbers.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A meaningful portion of your week will sit at the intersection of leasing operations and team oversight. That means reviewing and approving applications in Appfolio, monitoring lease documents and move-in files, and keeping marketing materials current for available units. You'll also track leasing activity and deliver weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance reporting. Monthly leasing meetings are yours to run: availability, agent incentives, challenges, and commission submissions all come through you.

On the team side, you'll onboard, train, and mentor new Leasing Agents. That's a real responsibility, not a footnote. During lease-up, your agents are often newer to the property and sometimes newer to the industry. How quickly they ramp affects your occupancy curve directly. You'll also handle the less glamorous operational pieces: security deposit dispositions, court-related notices, property inspections, and coordination with single-family teams.

Weekends and flexible scheduling are part of the job. Lease-up doesn't follow a Monday-Friday timeline, and candidates who thrive here understand that going in.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least 3 years of lease-up experience in multifamily, with demonstrated results on occupancy timelines
  • 3 or more years managing direct reports in a property management setting
  • Comfort reading and working with financial statements; you understand how your decisions connect to NOI
  • Strong communication skills across multiple audiences: residents, leasing staff, ownership, and vendors
  • Experience with Appfolio is a plus, as is familiarity with G-Suite and Microsoft Office
  • A track record of change leadership, which in lease-up often means building processes that didn't exist before you arrived

The managers who do well in lease-up roles tend to be organized enough to build systems under pressure and flexible enough to abandon a system that isn't working. They also know how to keep a leasing team motivated during the stretches when traffic is inconsistent and results feel slow. That combination of structure and steadiness is harder to find than the job posting makes it sound.

The position includes monthly and quarterly bonus potential tied to performance, along with a full benefits package: health, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) with matching, PTO, and additional well-being and educational programs.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This community manager role at Avanath sits at the intersection of affordable housing compliance and genuine community building. You're running day-to-day operations for a workforce housing community in New Hampshire: managing the full resident lifecycle from move-in through move-out, keeping delinquency as close to zero as possible, overseeing turn and make-ready timelines, and keeping occupancy on target. You'll also prepare monthly financials, work with your Regional Manager on the annual operating budget, and submit subsidy vouchers where applicable.

The compliance side carries real weight here. Avanath operates LIHTC properties, which means Tax Credit qualification knowledge isn't a nice-to-have, it's a baseline expectation. You'll need to keep resident files audit-ready, meet all eligibility requirements set by local, state, and federal agencies, and respond to any potential housing violations quickly and correctly. On the capital side, you may coordinate large capex projects across multiple departments, which requires clear written communication and the ability to keep several moving parts organized simultaneously.

Beyond the numbers, this role puts a premium on resident relationships. You'll run retention programs and resident events, serve as an internal advocate for residents when escalating concerns to senior leadership, and connect residents to outside services and agencies when their needs go beyond what on-site staff can provide. The expectation is that residents feel heard and supported at every point in their tenancy.

You'll also carry full responsibility for your team: setting goals, delivering feedback, managing schedules, holding people accountable, and building a culture where staff feel trusted and challenged. That's a real leadership function, not a secondary one.

What You Bring

  • 5 to 7 years in property management, with at least 2 years in a community or property manager seat
  • Working knowledge of LIHTC and Tax Credit compliance requirements
  • Demonstrated ability to de-escalate resident concerns before they become formal complaints or legal issues
  • Experience preparing budgets, reviewing financial performance against budget, and producing accurate monthly reports
  • Comfort communicating with senior executives, regulatory agencies, and social service partners
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel for rent rolls and financial tracking
  • A track record of leading and developing on-site teams

Where This Role Fits in Your Career

Affordable housing management builds a skill set that carries significant weight. The compliance discipline required under LIHTC programs, combined with the relationship management demands of workforce housing, produces managers who handle complexity well. Community managers at mission-driven affordable housing operators tend to develop stronger regulatory literacy and resident advocacy skills than peers at conventional market-rate sites, and those skills transfer directly into Regional Manager and Compliance Manager tracks. If you want to grow toward multi-site oversight, demonstrating strong NOI performance alongside low delinquency and clean compliance files is the combination that gets attention.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Student housing maintenance operates at a different tempo than conventional multifamily. Turnover is compressed into weeks, not months, and the resident base cycles almost entirely each year. A Maintenance Supervisor at a student community near Clemson University has to run a tight make-ready operation, manage preventative maintenance across a busy lease cycle, and build a team that performs consistently even when the calendar pressure is highest. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring for exactly that role at their Clemson property.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Expect to spend the majority of your time, roughly 60 to 70 percent, doing hands-on repairs rather than managing from a distance. You'll handle service requests, walk the property daily to catch curb appeal and liability issues early, and keep a preventative maintenance schedule running that protects the asset long-term. The rest of your time goes toward directing your team, coordinating vendors and contractors, and working alongside the Property Manager to keep operations within budget. During turn season, that balance shifts hard toward organizing and supervising the make-ready process, scheduling workers, overseeing contractors, and ensuring vacant units come back to market clean and rent-ready.

The technical range here is real. You'll need working knowledge across HVAC, intermediate plumbing and electrical, appliances, carpentry, sheetrock, pool care, landscaping, irrigation, and more. EPA Type II certification is required coming in. CPO is preferred and available through PeakMade if you're not already certified. You'll also manage the maintenance shop, supply inventory, hazard communications, and OSHA compliance, so the administrative side of the role matters even if the wrench time is primary.

Who Builds Well From This Role

Candidates with multifamily maintenance supervisory experience will adapt quickly, but student housing adds its own layer. Move-ins and move-outs are dense and time-boxed, deferred items compound fast, and resident communication requires patience and consistency. The people who thrive here combine trade competency with the ability to run a team through high-volume periods without letting standards slip.

From a career trajectory standpoint, a Maintenance Supervisor role in student housing builds skills that transfer directly into Facilities Manager positions, Regional Maintenance roles, or Director-level facilities leadership at larger operators. PeakMade offers a facilities leadership program and additional technical certifications, which matters if you're thinking about where this job leads, not just what it pays now.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • 2 or more years of maintenance supervisory experience, multifamily strongly preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and reliable personal vehicle required
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Must supply basic hand tools
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights, and perform physical tasks in outdoor conditions

PeakMade is an Atlanta-based operator focused on off-campus student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country.

job.title: Maintenance Technician at Luxury Apartments
job.description:
Bluecore Residential has built a portfolio of over 10,000 units and $2 billion in assets since 2004, and their maintenance teams carry real weight in how those assets perform. This Maintenance Technician role at their Raleigh luxury community puts you at the center of daily operations: turning units, resolving service requests across plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and handling HVAC work end to end.

What You'll Actually Do

Day to day, you're working through a service request queue, coordinating closely with the Maintenance Supervisor, and tracking work order status and make-ready progress in Yardi. Bluecore holds a 7-day standard for completing turns, so your pace and planning matter. You'll also use Sparkle as an inspection tool, manage parts inventory to keep costs in check without cutting corners, and rotate through on-call coverage for emergency requests. Preventative maintenance and community appearance fall under your watch too. This isn't a role where you wait for work to come to you.

Bluecore operates with a notably flat structure compared to most third-party management companies. Their maintenance techs are encouraged to surface problems directly and push back on what isn't working, which means your observations about recurring repair patterns or supply chain gaps can actually change how the property runs. For technicians who've spent time under heavy regional oversight, that operational autonomy is a genuine shift.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on apartment maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general repairs
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • CPO certification (preferred but not required, and Bluecore offers full reimbursement if you need to get there)
  • Comfort with property management software, or genuine willingness to get there quickly
  • Reliable transportation for on-site duties and on-call response
  • A sense of urgency that carries through from the first work order of the day to the last make-ready punch list item

Where This Role Can Take You

Maintenance Technician roles at well-run luxury communities are a strong foundation for a longer career in property operations. Techs who develop HVAC depth alongside solid soft skills around resident communication and team coordination often move into Maintenance Supervisor positions within two to three years. From there, the path toward Maintenance Director or Facilities Manager opens up, especially inside a company managing assets at this scale. The Yardi fluency and inspection discipline you build here transfers cleanly across any portfolio you work with later. Bluecore's certification reimbursement policy also means you can add credentials like CAM or CPO on the company's dime, which accelerates that trajectory considerably.

Raleigh's multifamily market has remained active, with ongoing lease-up activity and strong occupancy across Class A product. That means demand for skilled technicians who can hold a 7-day turn standard and keep resident satisfaction scores healthy. If you want to grow inside a company that measures your contribution and gives you room to make calls, this is a reasonable place to build that next chapter.

job.title: Leasing & Marketing Associate | Rambler College Park South - College Park, MD
job.description:
Student housing lease-ups run on a compressed cycle. A property like Rambler College Park South lives and dies by its ability to convert campus traffic into signed leases before the fall rush closes out, which means the Leasing and Marketing Associate role here carries more weight than the title might suggest. This isn't a front desk job with a few tours sprinkled in. It's a full leasing and community-building function wrapped in one position.

What This Role Actually Covers

On the leasing side, you'll guide prospective residents through tours, assist with applications, and track every lead and interaction through a CRM. The expectation is that you own the prospect relationship from first inquiry to signed lease, not just the handshake at the front door. You'll also support front desk operations, handle inbound calls and emails, and step in wherever the leasing operation needs coverage, including evenings and weekends during peak traffic periods.

The marketing work is genuinely hands-on. You'll plan and execute resident events, collaborate with the social media intern on content that supports both community engagement and leasing goals, and keep a sharp eye on the tour path presentation. You'll also shop competing properties and bring back intel that feeds the team's strategy. If you have instincts for what makes a space feel welcoming or what kind of event actually draws residents out of their apartments, those instincts get used here.

Skills Required vs. Skills You'll Build

The role requires strong interpersonal communication, basic organizational discipline, and the kind of social fluency that comes from being genuinely connected within a campus community. If you're already involved in student organizations or have experience as a brand ambassador, you're bringing a real asset, because peer influence and authentic community presence are hard to teach quickly.

What the role builds is equally valuable for a property management career. You'll develop CRM habits that carry into any leasing or assistant manager position. You'll learn how to read traffic patterns and adjust leasing tactics mid-cycle. Working alongside the Leasing Manager on coaching newer team members will sharpen your ability to communicate sales concepts clearly, a skill that becomes essential if you grow toward a Leasing Manager or Community Manager role down the line.

Strong candidates at this level tend to share one quality that's easy to overlook: they treat the tour path with the same attention they give to the conversation. A prospect who walks a well-maintained, thoughtfully staged tour route before they've exchanged ten words with a leasing associate has already started forming an impression. The associates who get that connection close more leases.

  • Prior experience in sales, leasing, hospitality, or customer service is a plus
  • Comfort with social media content and event planning strengthens your candidacy
  • Availability on evenings and weekends is required, particularly during high-traffic leasing periods
  • Familiarity with student life at or near the University of Maryland is a genuine advantage

LV Collective is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Beam Patrol Officer, Public Safety
job.description:
Beam Living sits at the intersection of institutional capital and street-level operations. As a Blackstone-backed multifamily portfolio company, they manage some of the more recognizable residential communities in New York City, and their Public Safety team is a direct extension of the resident experience. This Patrol Officer role is about presence as much as protection.

The day-to-day is what you'd expect from a residential patrol position: covering designated checkpoints, responding to noise complaints during quiet hours, handling lockouts, and acting as the first point of contact when something goes sideways on property. You'll liaise with local law enforcement when incidents escalate, log everything through the Command Center, and represent the community to residents who may be annoyed, anxious, or just locked out at 2 a.m. The Good Neighbor policy is yours to uphold, which means difficult conversations handled calmly and professionally, not escalated unnecessarily.

In a dense urban multifamily setting like New York City, the patrol function carries a lot of weight. Residents in high-occupancy buildings are living close together, and small tensions (loud music, hallway disputes, package theft) can compound fast if nobody's paying attention. A good patrol officer reads a building's baseline and notices when something's off before it becomes a call log entry. That situational awareness, built over time, is what separates the effective ones from the ones who are simply present.

What you'll need to bring:

  • 0 to 3 years in security or law enforcement (residential experience is a plus)
  • A valid New York State security license
  • A valid driver's license
  • Genuine comfort with emergency response at any hour
  • A professional appearance and the discipline to maintain it consistently
  • Discretion around resident and employee information

The hours are real. "Willingness to respond to emergency situations no matter the time of day" is not filler language in this role. If that part gives you pause, this probably isn't the right fit. If it doesn't, and if you're drawn to environments where your presence actually changes how safe people feel in their homes, this is a reasonable place to build toward something more.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Homestead Park, Moulton Plaza)
job.description:
MidPen Housing has managed affordable housing across Northern California since 1970, with a portfolio of more than 142 properties serving over 22,800 residents. This Maintenance Technician role covers two Sunnyvale communities: Homestead Park and Moulton Plaza. The residents here include working families, seniors, and people with special needs. What you keep running matters in a way that's easy to measure: a unit that turns in four days instead of ten, a plumbing issue resolved before it becomes a mold problem, a well-lit common area that feels safe at 10 p.m.

What You'll Actually Do

Day-to-day, you're splitting time between reactive work orders and scheduled preventive maintenance. Electrical repairs on appliances, fixtures, switches, and circuits. Plumbing repairs across water and sewage systems. Rough and finish carpentry, painting, flooring, appliance installs during turns. You'll also maintain landscaping and irrigation systems to MidPen standards and keep common areas clean and secure.

Turns are a meaningful part of this role. You'll take vacant units through the full make-ready process: punch list, painting, flooring, fixtures, and final inspection, all within the timeframes the Community Manager tracks. Tight turn cycles protect occupancy, and at an affordable housing property, every day a unit sits vacant is a day a resident on the waitlist keeps waiting.

You'll also carry a rotating on-call schedule, covering 24/7 emergency maintenance for seven consecutive days at a time, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. That's the honest reality of this position. In return, you're part of a team with actual structure: a Community Manager you report to directly, junior groundskeeper staff you coach and oversee, and contractor relationships you help coordinate through bidding, scheduling, and completion monitoring.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED plus at least three years of hands-on maintenance experience, preferably in property management
  • Strong plumbing knowledge and demonstrated electrical repair experience across appliances, circuits, and fixtures
  • Rough and finish carpentry skills, structural and cosmetic
  • Familiarity with OSHA safety standards and landscape maintenance practices
  • Ability to coach and train junior staff, with solid written and verbal communication
  • Basic computer skills for work order entry and documentation
  • Valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
  • Physical capability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly, work outdoors in all weather, and handle tasks requiring climbing, bending, and confined-space work

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing maintenance carries a few operational realities that differ from market-rate work. Capex cycles tend to be more deliberate, so your ability to extend the life of systems through solid preventive maintenance schedules and accurate documentation carries real weight. Inventory control matters too: supplies and equipment need to be managed carefully when procurement moves through an approval process. Technicians who document well, communicate clearly with the Community Manager during move-ins, move-outs, and annual inspections, and treat residents with consistency tend to build strong tenure at properties like these. The pay range for this role runs $25.00 to $28.13 per hour, based on experience and qualifications.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Residences at Breckenridge
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at garden-style communities like this one sit squarely at the intersection of hands-on trade work and team management. At 208 units, you're big enough to have a maintenance team under you but close enough to the work that you're still turning wrenches regularly. That balance defines the job.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The Residences at Breckenridge is a 208-unit community in Hilliard, Ohio, managed by Ackermann Group, a Midwest operator with roots going back to 1938. The Maintenance Supervisor here reports to the Community Manager and carries dual responsibility: keeping the physical asset running and keeping the team organized enough to do it consistently.

Day-to-day, you're coordinating the make-ready schedule, tracking service requests through to completion, managing parts inventory, and making sure amenities stay market-ready. You're also the person your team looks to when something goes sideways on a plumbing call or an HVAC unit acts up mid-August. Specialist-level troubleshooting across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, HVAC, and painting all fall within scope. Preventive maintenance planning, vendor negotiations, capital improvement coordination, and budget management round out the administrative side. And yes, after-hours emergency on-call is part of the rotation. That's the job.

Ohio winters also mean snow removal is a real operational responsibility, not an afterthought.

What Ackermann Is Looking For

  • Three or more years of maintenance experience with demonstrated supervisory responsibility
  • EPA Type I and II Certification (required)
  • CPO and CAMT certifications (preferred)
  • Aquatherm system experience (preferred, worth noting if you have it)
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office products for documentation and reporting
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The certifications matter here. EPA Type I and II is a hard requirement. CPO and CAMT aren't required but they signal the kind of organized, credentialed technician Ackermann tends to promote.

Where This Role Fits

Maintenance Supervisors who build a track record managing budgets, leading teams, and delivering clean turns tend to move into Service Manager or Regional Maintenance Director roles at operators like Ackermann. The financial acumen piece specifically, knowing how to manage a maintenance budget and negotiate vendor rates, is what separates candidates who stay in Supervisor seats from those who move up. If you've been a strong technician but haven't owned a budget, this role will stretch you in that direction.

Ackermann offers health benefits, a 401k with company match, PTO including your birthday, quarterly bonus potential, lease renewal commission, and an employee rent discount across their communities. They also mention career coaching, which at a company this size typically means real access to leadership rather than a line in an HR document.

Schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with on-call rotation as assigned.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Community management at a multifamily property touches almost every professional skill at once. You're reading financials in the morning, coaching a leasing agent through a tough objection by afternoon, and fielding a vendor dispute before the day ends. The person who does this well holds all of those threads without dropping any of them.

Waypoint Management Services is filling a Community Manager seat at one of their multifamily communities in Vero Beach, Florida. The role calls on financial fluency, team development instincts, resident relations experience, and operational discipline in roughly equal measure. If you've spent years on just one of those, this probably isn't the right fit. If you've genuinely worked across all of them, read on.

On the financial side, you'll own budget prep, expense control, collections follow-through, and capital project tracking. That means being comfortable pulling performance data, spotting where NOI is slipping, and bringing solutions rather than just questions to ownership conversations. Strong accounts receivable habits matter here. Delinquency doesn't manage itself, and the expectation is proactive intervention before it compounds.

Leading a Team That Has to Deliver Every Day

You'll recruit, coach, and hold accountable a team of leasing and maintenance professionals. That's a wide range of personalities, priorities, and daily pressures under one roof. Waypoint's stated culture is built on accountability alongside collaboration, which means your job is to set clear expectations and then actually follow through when people don't meet them. That takes both relationship skills and a willingness to have hard conversations without letting things fester.

Building a talent pipeline is also part of the job description. Good community managers don't just fill open roles when they appear. They stay connected to the industry, know who's good, and have names ready when turnover happens. If you've networked actively within property management circles, that's a skill Waypoint values explicitly here.

Leasing, Marketing, and Market Awareness in Vero Beach

Vero Beach is a smaller coastal market with a resident base that skews older and value-conscious, and competition for quality renters is real. A Community Manager here needs to understand local demand patterns, track competitive communities through regular market surveys, and build leasing strategies that reflect what actually drives traffic and closes. Generic digital campaigns won't carry the load on their own.

You'll need at least three years in a property manager role specifically, and five-plus years in multifamily overall, including exposure to Class A communities. Yardi proficiency is expected from day one, not something you'll pick up on the job.

Compensation includes a quarterly manager bonus, monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, 120 hours of PTO in year one with progressive increases, two floating days, medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one, and a 401k with company match.

  • 3+ years as a property manager
  • 5+ years in multifamily property management, including Class A experience
  • Budgeting, AR/AP, and capital project management background
  • Yardi and CRM platform proficiency
  • Demonstrated team leadership and employee development track record
  • Fair Housing knowledge and leasing procedure fluency
  • Bachelor's degree preferred

What tends to separate strong candidates in a role like this is the ability to stay solution-oriented when multiple things are going sideways at once. Residents escalating, maintenance behind on turns, a leasing consultant who's struggling, and a budget variance that needs explaining. The people who thrive aren't the ones who avoid that pressure. They're the ones who've learned to triage it without losing their composure or their team's trust.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Geographic property management, where one manager owns accountability across multiple buildings in a defined area, demands a different skill set than managing a single community. You're coordinating maintenance, leasing, resident relations, and team development across dispersed locations, which means your judgment about where to spend your time is itself a core competency. CYM Living's model in Elkhart puts that accountability squarely on the Property Manager they're hiring now.

What This Role Actually Requires

CYM Living is a vertically integrated national firm that combines data and technology with what they describe as hyperlocal customer service. That combination matters for understanding this position. You'll work inside AppFolio as a functional tool, not just a reference system, so comfort moving through property management software quickly is a real requirement. You'll also need reliable transportation, because routine drive-bys and building visits across your geographic territory are built into how this role operates, not optional extras.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct showings, negotiate lease terms, and make the case for property features to prospective residents. On the operational side, you'll follow maintenance and repair requests through to resolution, collect monthly rent, and run collection procedures when accounts fall behind. Resident complaint handling comes with the territory too, and your phone etiquette and follow-through will shape retention as much as any concession would. Strong knowledge of landlord-tenant law and real estate administrative processes is expected coming in.

The team development piece carries real weight here. CYM Living's stated culture centers on empowering growth from within, so developing the people around you is part of your performance, not a side task.

Skills You'll Build in This Structure

Multi-site management sharpens a specific kind of operational thinking that single-property roles rarely develop. When your portfolio spans several buildings, you get fast at triage, at reading which issue needs your physical presence versus a phone call, and at managing relationships with residents who never see a front office. That skill transfers directly into regional or district management. Property managers who've run dispersed portfolios are consistently more competitive for those next-level roles because they've already been doing the judgment work that regional positions require.

Working within AppFolio at this level also builds reporting and data fluency. Over time, you'll move from navigating the software to reading patterns in it: delinquency trends, turn timelines, maintenance cycles. Those are the signals that inform NOI decisions at the ownership level, and understanding them makes you a stronger operator at every stage of your career.

  • Proven property management or related field experience (preferred)
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, and mobile communication tools
  • AppFolio experience or willingness to learn quickly
  • Strong negotiation and customer service skills
  • Reliable personal vehicle (required)
  • Flexible availability to accommodate showing schedules
  • Leadership and team development capability

CYM Living offers a competitive salary based on experience, along with health, dental, and vision coverage, a retirement plan with employer match, paid time off, and ongoing professional development.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Student housing runs on a tighter operational calendar than most multifamily segments. Move-ins cluster around academic start dates, delinquency spikes follow financial aid disbursement cycles, and lease-up season compresses into a window that punishes slow follow-up. The Assistant General Manager role at Yugo Charlotte College Downs sits at the center of all of it.

Where Your Skills Get Used

This position draws on a specific combination: financial accountability, leasing execution, and resident relations, all running simultaneously rather than in sequence. On the financial side, you'll manage rent collections, track delinquency, process deposits, and support month-end close. That means your eye for accounts receivable has to be sharp. Budget tracking and expense management are part of the day-to-day, not quarterly check-ins.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, respond to inquiries, process applications, and monitor competitor pricing and amenity offerings. Student housing occupancy is a leading indicator of a community's financial health, and keeping traffic converting at a strong rate requires consistent follow-up and genuine product knowledge. You'll also support lease renewal efforts and retention initiatives, which at a student property means understanding what keeps residents re-signing versus pulling them toward off-campus alternatives.

Vendor coordination and property inspections round out the operations side. You'll work with maintenance teams and contractors to keep service requests moving and ensure common areas, model units, and leasing spaces stay tour-ready year-round.

What This Role Actually Demands

You need at least one year of residential property experience, and prior work at a university or college community carries real weight here. Yugo uses Entrata, so familiarity with that platform or comparable property management software will shorten your ramp time considerably.

Strong candidates in student housing understand that the resident population skews younger and often less experienced with lease terms, billing cycles, and conflict resolution. Patience, clarity, and the ability to de-escalate difficult situations matter more here than in most multifamily settings. Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable, and you'll be expected to apply it consistently across every interaction.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; residential operations experience accepted in lieu of a degree
  • Minimum one year of experience in residential property management or a related field
  • Entrata experience or comparable property management software proficiency preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to handle delinquency follow-up, financial documentation, and reporting
  • Carbon Literacy Certification, or willingness to complete the training after hire

The Yugo Context

Yugo operates at genuine scale in the student housing sector, nearly 40,000 beds across 88 U.S. properties. That size means internal processes are developed, training resources exist, and there's a defined career path for strong operators who want to move toward a General Manager role. The compensation for this position ranges from $24 to $26 per hour, with bonus eligibility, health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with 4% employer match, three weeks of PTO, paid parental leave, and company-paid short-term and long-term disability and life insurance.

College Downs is one property within a system that takes performance data seriously. If you want a role where your leasing metrics, delinquency numbers, and NOI contribution are visible and valued, this is the kind of operation built around exactly that.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Stone Gate)
job.description:
Stone Gate Apartments in Spring Lake, NC is a residential community that needs a technician who can handle the full range of day-to-day maintenance work without a lot of hand-holding. Van Metre has been doing this since 1955, and their properties reflect that institutional attention to upkeep and curb appeal.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll report to both the Service Manager and Property Manager, which is standard for this kind of role. Most of your week will be a mix of resident service requests, make-ready work on vacant units, preventative maintenance rounds, and property walks to stay ahead of anything that could become a liability. Turns are part of the job. So is the punch list work that comes with them. You'll be expected to track what you do, manage your own inventory, and flag concerns up the chain before they become bigger problems.

After-hours coverage rotates. This position is on call once every six weeks for a full week to handle emergency calls. That's a lighter on-call burden than many communities run, but it's real, and you should go in with eyes open about it. Weekend work is part of the regular schedule.

What You Bring

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience, or documented trade training
  • Working knowledge of appliance repair, electrical, and plumbing
  • Basic HVAC understanding; Universal CFC Certification is preferred
  • Familiarity with current OSHA and building safety standards
  • Your own basic tools and a valid driver's license

The technicians who stand out in this type of role aren't necessarily the ones with the longest list of certifications. They're the ones who communicate clearly with residents, close out requests without creating callbacks, and notice the slow leak or the worn breaker before a 2 a.m. call becomes a flooded unit.

Compensation and Career Path

Pay runs $20 to $22 per hour depending on experience, and there's an annual bonus potential of $5,000, paid out quarterly. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), paid certifications, tuition reimbursement, and a $900 annual wellness reimbursement. Van Metre also offers a rental discount for employees, which matters if you're considering the Spring Lake area.

For a technician who builds a track record at Van Metre, the natural next step is Service Manager. Companies like Van Metre that manage and develop their own assets tend to promote from within on the maintenance side, particularly when someone has shown they can own a property's systems and train newer staff. Getting your EPA Universal Certification and expanding your HVAC skills while in this role positions you well for that move.

job.title: Client Service Extraordinaire- Austin TX
job.description:
HOA management firms live or die by their frontline communication. Association managers carry the strategy, but the person fielding homeowner calls, routing service tickets, and keeping board members informed is the one who actually shapes how residents experience the company every single day. Rise Association Management Group is hiring for that role, titled Client Service Extraordinaire, based in Houston's 77098 zip code.

What This Role Actually Looks Like

This is a high-volume customer service position embedded inside a growing third-party HOA management company. You'll field inbound calls and emails from homeowners, residents, and board members covering the full range of association life: billing questions, deed restriction concerns, architectural review requests, access issues, and maintenance reports. The expectation is a two-hour response window on service tickets, which means your day moves fast and your organizational habits need to be airtight.

You'll work closely with Association Managers, Facilities Managers, and the Accounting team to push issues to resolution rather than just logging them. That coordination piece is real work. Getting an answer back to a homeowner on a billing dispute means you're following up internally, not just forwarding the email and hoping. Rise uses the EOS (Entrepreneurial Operating System) framework to structure their operations, which brings more process discipline than you'd find at most regional AMCs.

The position is Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with occasional overtime. Pay runs $18 to $20 per hour.

What Rise Is Looking For

  • Three to five years of professional work experience, with at least one year in property management or hospitality preferred
  • High school diploma required; two years of college coursework preferred
  • Strong conflict resolution skills and composure when conversations get difficult
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel and Outlook, plus accurate data entry
  • Organized enough to manage digital and physical filing systems simultaneously
  • Clean written communication and familiarity with professional business correspondence

Benefits include 20 days of PTO annually, 10 paid holidays, group health insurance with 75% employer-paid premiums, life and AD&D insurance, optional dental, vision, and short-term disability, and a 401(k).

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this are the ones who understand that HOA residents are also homeowners with real financial stakes in their community. Tone matters. Someone who can de-escalate a frustrated board member's call about a landscaping vendor and still document the issue cleanly for the manager's follow-up is worth a lot more than someone who's simply friendly. The two-hour response SLA is a real accountability measure, so if you've worked in environments with defined service expectations, that experience translates directly here.

job.title: Front Desk Package Attendant - Azzurra
job.description:
A resident texts the front desk at 2 PM: a birthday gift arrived and they need it delivered before their guest does. You already know where it is. You logged it this morning, stored it correctly, and you can have it upstairs in five minutes. That's the rhythm of this role at Azzurra, a community managed by Action Property Management in Los Angeles.

What This Role Covers

This is a full-time, Monday through Friday position running from 11:00 AM to 7:30 PM, which means you're working the heart of the delivery window and the peak hours of resident traffic. Your core responsibility is package lifecycle management: scanning and logging incoming parcels into the management app, storing them in the correct locations, retrieving them from the loading dock, conducting two daily audits, and delivering to units when requested. You'll also sort and distribute USPS mail as it arrives.

Alongside package operations, you serve as a lobby presence. That means monitoring access, using the master phone directory to announce guests and deliveries to residents, and coordinating with on-site staff when a situation needs attention. You'll provide front desk and loading dock coverage as needed, which gives you visibility into how a high-end HOA community actually runs day to day. Pay for this position ranges from $21.00 to $23.00 per hour.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires at least one year of customer service experience, a clean background check and drug screening, and a professional appearance and demeanor that fits a luxury residential environment. Action specifically values candidates from hospitality, fine dining, or upscale retail, and actively seeks hospitality management students or recent graduates. If your background is in a hotel front desk or a high-end restaurant, you already understand the standard being set here.

What the role builds is equally worth noting. Working at the intersection of operations and resident relations in an HOA setting sharpens skills that translate directly into assistant community manager and concierge services coordinator positions. You'll develop comfort with property management software, learn how access control and lobby protocols function in a managed community, and get daily practice handling resident concerns with composure under time pressure.

Skills this position requires:

  • Customer service experience (minimum one year)
  • Professional presentation appropriate for a luxury residential property
  • Strong organizational judgment for package tracking and storage
  • Proactive, solutions-oriented communication with residents and guests

Action Property Management has operated as a privately held HOA management company since 1984 and now serves more than 300 communities across nine offices. Benefits for qualifying team members include medical, dental, vision, pet insurance, a 401(k) with company match, paid vacation, sick time, and company-observed holidays.

job.title: Leasing and Engagement Specialist
job.description:
Wendover Management runs a portfolio of affordable and workforce housing communities across the Southeast, and this Apopka-based role sits right at the intersection of leasing, resident relations, and community programming. It's a broader scope than a typical leasing consultant position, so if you've ever wanted your work to feel like more than just filling units, this one's worth a closer look.

What You'll Actually Do

The leasing side of this role covers the full cycle: tours, applications, documentation, follow-up, and renewal conversations. You'll track unit availability, assist with rent collection, and keep leasing records accurate. That's the foundation. But a meaningful portion of your week will go toward things that don't show up in a standard leasing job description.

You'll help plan and run resident events, manage the community activity calendar, and coordinate with local organizations to build genuine connections between residents and the broader neighborhood. You'll support social media content on platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, which means translating what's happening at the property into content that actually attracts prospective residents. One of the more distinctive responsibilities here is coordinating The Wonder Kids Youth Club, an after-school program that requires activity planning, participant supervision, and a real commitment to creating a safe environment for young residents. If you've worked with youth programs before, that experience will serve you well. If you haven't, be honest with yourself about whether that's a fit before applying.

You'll also coordinate concierge services, handle vendor communication, and support the Community Manager and Assistant Manager across day-to-day administrative needs. This role is on-site, physically active, and includes weekend hours when leasing traffic or events call for it.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish (required, not preferred)
  • Background in property management, leasing, or residential customer service
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office, property management software, and social media platforms
  • Strong organizational habits and the ability to shift between tasks without losing track of details
  • Professional presence and communication skills across in-person, phone, and written channels
  • Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. and walk the property regularly
  • Reliable local transportation for occasional errands or marketing runs

Who Tends to Thrive Here

Candidates who do well in roles like this one usually have a genuine comfort with variety. On a given day you might be walking a prospective resident through a model unit in the morning, coordinating a vendor request before lunch, posting a community update to social media, and wrapping up by supporting an afternoon youth club session. People who need a tightly defined lane tend to find that exhausting. People who get energy from switching context and seeing immediate impact on the people around them tend to find it rewarding.

The bilingual requirement reflects the real demographics of the community you'd be serving. Residents who speak Spanish as a primary language aren't a niche population here. Your ability to communicate with them directly, without a workaround, shapes their experience in ways that matter. That's worth stating plainly because it's not a checkbox. It's a daily functional need.

Compensation includes a competitive base plus performance-based bonuses. This is an on-site, full-time position in Apopka, Florida.

job.title: Property Administrator
job.description:
Commercial property management runs on paperwork, relationships, and financial accuracy in equal measure. When a portfolio falls behind on AP coding, COI tracking, or AR follow-up, the Property Manager loses hours they don't have. The Property Administrator role exists to close that gap, keeping the back office sharp so the front-facing work can happen on time.

Stream Realty Partners, a full-service commercial real estate firm founded in 1996 and operating coast to coast across office, industrial, retail, and other asset types, is hiring a Property Administrator for its Phoenix operations. This is an onsite, hands-on position supporting the day-to-day management of a commercial portfolio.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant portion of this role lives inside the financials. On the payables side, you'll code and verify invoices against the approved budget before routing them to the Property Manager for sign-off. On the receivables side, you'll run monthly AR reviews and help prepare late notices and default notices when tenants fall behind. You'll also support the preparation of monthly and quarterly financial reports, which means you need to be comfortable reading numbers and understanding what they represent, not just entering them.

Beyond the ledger, you'll manage vendor and tenant Certificates of Insurance, a detail that sounds routine but creates real liability exposure when it slips. You'll draft and coordinate service contracts, log work order requests, schedule move-ins and move-outs, and help plan tenant events. The front desk function is part of this role too: phones, visitors, deliveries, and message routing all run through this position.

Yardi experience is a plus. Microsoft Excel and Word proficiency is expected from day one.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • A bachelor's degree (preferred) with coursework or work experience touching accounting, finance, business administration, or real estate
  • Basic accounting fluency. You should understand debits, credits, and how an invoice moves through an approval workflow
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when working across multiple tenants, vendors, and budget line items simultaneously
  • Clear written and verbal communication. You'll interact with tenants, vendors, and internal teams regularly
  • Genuine interest in growing inside commercial property management, not just filling a coordinator seat

One honest note on career trajectory: Property Administrator roles in commercial real estate are well-established pipelines into Property Manager positions. Candidates who treat the financial reporting and vendor management components as learning opportunities rather than administrative chores tend to move up faster. The AP/AR experience here maps directly to what a PM handles at the portfolio level, and firms like Stream promote from within when the fundamentals are strong.

job.title: Apartment Service Technician (HVAC/EPA Certified)
job.description:
Morguard operates as a fully integrated real estate investment and management company, and their onsite maintenance teams carry real weight in how communities perform. At the technician level, this kind of role is where hands-on skills get sharpened into genuine expertise. The person who excels here builds a reputation across every trade, and that reputation travels.

The Work Itself

This is a full-time position running Sunday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, at a multifamily community in Aurora, CO. You'll work under the Lead Maintenance Technician and Community Manager, handling the daily flow of resident work orders, participating in preventative maintenance programs, and contributing to unit turns when apartments go vacant. Make-ready work is a core part of the job. Turning a unit well, closing the punch list clean, and getting it leased-ready on schedule directly affects occupancy and the community's overall performance.

Daily property walks are part of the rhythm here. You'll know your grounds, your buildings, and the mechanical systems running beneath them. When work orders come in, the expectation is thorough diagnosis, not surface fixes. Communicating proactively with your supervisor when something runs longer than expected is treated as professionalism, not a weakness.

You'll also participate in the on-call rotation, splitting after-hours emergency coverage with your teammates. Each on-call week earns a $100 stipend paid directly to you, regardless of whether you're called out.

What You Bring

  • HVAC Type I and Type II certification, or EPA Universal. This is a firm requirement, not a preference.
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, drywall, painting, carpentry, appliance repair, and basic electrical troubleshooting
  • Prior experience in a multifamily setting, specifically closing work orders and completing unit turns
  • Comfort responding to after-hours emergencies as part of a shared rotation
  • High school diploma required; technical school background is a plus

Pay, Benefits, and Where This Role Leads

The hourly rate runs $25 to $26, with quarterly bonuses of up to 5% of annual salary based on performance. Morguard offers employer-provided medical insurance, a 401(k) with dollar-for-dollar matching and immediate vesting, paid time off including summer hours, and an education reimbursement program. There's also an employee housing discount within their portfolio, subject to availability.

From a career standpoint, a technician who consistently closes work orders cleanly, communicates well, and handles turns efficiently is the natural pipeline for Lead Maintenance Technician roles. From there, the path to Maintenance Supervisor or Regional Facilities positions is straightforward in companies of Morguard's scale. The HVAC certification you already hold is the credential that distinguishes you at every step. Technicians who also build fluency in capex projects and vendor coordination tend to move fastest into supervisory tracks.

What separates strong candidates here is less about the breadth of certifications and more about the quality of follow-through. A technician who documents accurately, communicates without being prompted, and treats each work order as a direct reflection on the resident's experience is the one who earns expanded responsibility. Morguard invests in that kind of person.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant- Cortland Chisholm Trail
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set that doesn't always get the credit it deserves. At its core, it's persuasion, empathy, and organization working together at the same time. The Leasing and Sales Consultant role at Cortland Chisholm Trail in Fort Worth calls on all three, often within the same conversation.

What This Role Actually Demands

Your days will center on people: prospects calling to ask about availability, walk-ins who showed up on a whim, and current residents who stop by the office with questions. What separates strong leasing consultants from average ones here isn't just charisma. It's the discipline behind the charm. Following up with a lead the same afternoon, keeping CRM notes accurate after every interaction, tracking conversion rates without being asked, and adjusting your pitch when something isn't working. The consultative side matters, too. You're listening for what someone actually needs and matching it to what the community offers, not running through a script.

Beyond the one-on-one sales work, you'll manage the community's social media presence and help plan resident events that build real connection among people who live there. That's a broader scope than many leasing roles carry, and it means your work touches both occupancy and retention.

The Relationships You'll Manage

You'll spend most of your time with prospects and residents, but the internal dynamics matter just as much. Cortland operates as a vertically integrated company, meaning design, construction, and management run through the same organization. That structure gives you more internal resources to draw on than you'd find at a third-party management shop, but it also means brand standards are taken seriously. How you present the community, how you handle a complaint, how you show up on a tour: these things reflect a company with real brand investment. You'll get coaching on all of it, and the expectation is that you act on it.

Cortland is one of the ten largest multifamily owners and operators in the country. Working inside that scale means you're not figuring things out from scratch. There are systems, processes, and performance benchmarks already in place. Your job is to execute within that structure and push your own numbers.

A Good Fit for This Role

  • At least six months of experience in sales, customer service, or a role where you were held to measurable goals
  • Comfort with CRM tools, or a genuine willingness to learn them quickly
  • Organized follow-up habits. Leads go cold fast, and timeliness is part of the job
  • A coachable disposition. Feedback here is specific and frequent, and it's meant to help you hit your targets
  • A polished, professional presence that fits a premium brand environment

Fort Worth's rental market has stayed competitive, with steady population growth and continued apartment development along the southwest corridor near Chisholm Trail Parkway. That means traffic exists, but so does competition. The consultants who perform well in this market are the ones who close on the first visit when possible and nurture prospects who need more time rather than letting them go quiet.

For someone building a career in multifamily, a leasing consultant role at a company like Cortland is a real starting point. The skills you develop here, pipeline management, objection handling, resident relations, CRM fluency, all carry directly into roles like assistant manager, leasing manager, or community manager down the line.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Administrative work at a large real estate firm demands a specific combination of organizational precision and communication fluency. This role at Lincoln Property Company's Humble, TX office puts both to work every day. You'll manage calendars and coordinate meeting logistics for a team, which sounds straightforward until competing deadlines and shifting priorities require you to make judgment calls without being asked. You'll draft and proofread correspondence and memos, process invoices and expense reports, maintain filing systems, and handle department purchase orders. The throughline across all of it is accuracy. Errors in data entry, invoice processing, or correspondence reflect directly on the team you support.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook, is a real requirement here. Calendar management and internal coordination run through Outlook. Reports and correspondence go through Word. Expense tracking and departmental data often live in Excel. If you can move fluidly across all three without friction, you'll spend less time on mechanics and more time on the actual work.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

On a typical morning, you might reconcile a purchase order, confirm room bookings for two afternoon meetings, and route a memo for signatures before noon. Onboarding support for new team members adds another layer when it's active. Order and supply tracking for the office is an ongoing task with no clear finish line. The role is fully in-office during standard business hours, so the rhythm is consistent and structured.

Lincoln operates across a broad portfolio including multifamily, commercial, industrial, and mixed-use assets. That scope means the team you're supporting may work across multiple asset types or client relationships simultaneously. Background in commercial real estate is a genuine advantage here because the vocabulary and workflow expectations differ from general corporate admin. You'll encounter terminology related to property operations, client reporting, and leasing activity. Familiarity with that context reduces the learning curve.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Two years of administrative or clerical experience is the baseline. What separates candidates who do well in this environment is the ability to manage a varied workload without waiting for someone to sequence it for them. Lincoln describes its culture as encouraging an entrepreneurial mindset, and even in an administrative function, that means taking ownership of your workload and flagging problems early rather than waiting for direction on every task.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • 2+ years of administrative or clerical experience
  • Commercial real estate experience preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)
  • Ability to prioritize independently across multiple concurrent tasks
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Lincoln offers a full benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with traditional and Roth options, flexible time off, paid sick leave, and company-paid life insurance and long-term disability coverage.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Montair at Somerset Hill
job.description:
Tumwater sits in a quieter pocket of the South Sound, but it draws steady renter demand from state government employment, the nearby JBLM workforce, and residents priced out of Olympia proper. Montair at Somerset Hill operates in that kind of market, where occupancy holds well but retaining residents through renewal cycles matters just as much as putting new traffic through the door. The Assistant Manager role here is built around both.

The Day-to-Day

This position covers the operational and financial core of the property. You'll handle rent collection and daily deposits, maintain resident files with accuracy and confidentiality, track delinquency, and step into the property manager role when the Business Manager is out. Alongside that, you're inspecting make-ready apartments before move-ins, reviewing final account statements at move-out, and staying close enough to the sub-market to flag anything that might affect occupancy or income.

You'll also carry a share of leasing responsibility. When traffic is heavy or the team needs coverage, you're showing units. You're participating in resident retention events and community programming. And when residents have complaints, you're the one addressing them directly, not routing them through a queue.

Olympus uses RealPage and Knock (Onesite), so familiarity with that stack is a real advantage coming in. Candidates who've managed collections, coordinated move-out dispositions, or handled liability referral protocols in a prior onsite role will get up to speed faster.

What the Schedule Looks Like

  • Full-time, Monday through Friday, generally 9 AM to 6 PM
  • Flexibility for resident events after hours
  • First weekend of each month required
  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant is required

Growth and Culture

Olympus has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025). That kind of consistency usually reflects something real about how the company runs internally, and in this case the emphasis is on internal mobility and recognition. The Assistant Manager title is a well-worn path to a Business Manager seat, and Olympus has formal career pathing to support that progression. Compensation is experience-based with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay, plus a benefits package that includes an apartment rental allowance and tuition reimbursement.

If you've built solid financial habits onsite, know how to run a leasing office with attention to detail, and want to work toward running a property on your own, Montair at Somerset Hill is a reasonable next step.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Part Time
job.description:
Part-time leasing roles tend to attract people who want steady hourly work without the full 40-hour grind. What makes this one worth a closer look is the company behind it. Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, operates more than 60 communities across five states, and runs a hands-on model that puts real weight on customer experience rather than just occupancy numbers.

The position is at Bexley at Heritage in Wake Forest, NC. Starting pay is $18/hour, with increases based on experience, quarterly bonuses, and a 10% rent discount. The schedule runs about 20 hours per week, with most or all Saturdays required and flexible weekday hours negotiated around your availability.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're the first person a prospect talks to, and often the last touchpoint before they decide to sign or walk. That means touring units, answering questions by phone and email, following up on leads, and helping current residents feel heard when they have concerns. But this isn't a pure sales role. Administrative tasks, property walks, inspecting make-ready units, and pitching in on community appearance are all part of the job. Weinstein is upfront: everyone does a little bit of everything.

Some days will be interrupted constantly. A prospect walks in while you're mid-task, a resident has a complaint, and your to-do list shifts on the fly. That's not unusual for leasing work at any property. Knowing it going in makes it easier to handle.

Who Does Well Here

Weinstein explicitly welcomes people without leasing experience, and they mean it. Their training program is built for that. What they're actually filtering for is reliability, warmth with strangers, and a genuine interest in helping people find a home. Strong candidates for this specific role tend to come from retail, hospitality, or customer service backgrounds where they've handled high-interaction environments without losing their composure.

  • Comfortable talking to people in person and in writing
  • Organized enough to manage follow-ups and administrative tasks alongside tours
  • Available most Saturdays without it being a recurring conflict
  • Able to take direction during training and apply it independently afterward

For the right person, this is a legitimate entry point into property management. Weinstein promotes from within, and leasing is the traditional starting point for site managers, assistant managers, and eventually community director roles. A part-time leasing position that gives you real training and Saturday traffic exposure builds the foundation faster than many full-time roles that keep consultants siloed in one task.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Leasing Consultant role at 3300 Tamarac Apartments puts you at the center of the community's daily traffic. You'll greet and qualify prospective residents, walk units, and convert interest into signed leases. That means understanding fair housing compliance well enough to screen applicants correctly and consistently, preparing lease packages, and coordinating with the maintenance team to make sure move-ins go smoothly from a punch list standpoint, not just a paperwork one.

Day-to-day, you're also maintaining rental files, entering data accurately into property management software, and helping with the monthly administrative close. When residents come to you with complaints or maintenance concerns, you handle those conversations professionally and follow them through to resolution. Rent collection and delinquency follow-up are part of the rhythm too. This is front-line leasing work: visible, fast, and detail-dependent.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or related leasing experience (preferred)
  • Sales instincts and customer service habits that hold up under pressure
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry
  • Professional communication skills, written and verbal
  • The organizational discipline to keep files current and paperwork clean
  • A team orientation. MG Properties promotes from within, which means your coworkers today are often your future peers at higher levels

Where This Role Fits in the Craft

Leasing Consultant roles build a specific skill set that transfers directly into senior leasing, assistant manager, and eventually property manager positions. You develop fluency in the full prospect-to-resident lifecycle: traffic generation, conversion, application processing, lease execution, and move-in coordination. If you're early in a property management career, this is one of the cleaner paths toward understanding how occupancy decisions affect NOI at the property level.

MG Properties has been acquiring and operating apartment communities across the Western U.S. for more than 30 years. Denver is a competitive multifamily market, and 3300 Tamarac sits in that context. Strong candidates here will know how to handle objections during a tour, recognize when a concession conversation is appropriate, and understand that consistent occupancy is built through dozens of small interactions done well, not just the occasional great tour. If you've worked a leasing office and learned to treat every walk-in as a real opportunity, this role will use that skill immediately.

job.title: Community Manager (Celestina Garden Apartments)
job.description:
Celestina Garden Apartments sits in Sonoma County, one of the more expensive housing markets in Northern California. The residents MidPen serves here have limited options and real stakes in stable housing. That context shapes this role in ways a conventional property management job doesn't.

What You'll Actually Do

Day to day, you're running the full operation at Celestina Garden. That means rent collection, delinquency follow-up, security deposit accounting, and bank deposits handled correctly and on time. You'll process applications, certifications, and re-certs under HUD, TCAC, and Fair Housing requirements. Affordable housing compliance isn't paperwork for its own sake. A missed re-cert or a documentation error can affect a resident's housing eligibility, so accuracy here carries real consequences.

You'll lead a small site team, which means performance reviews, coaching, and being the person who sets the tone when things get difficult. You'll manage unit turns within established timeframes, keep a preventative maintenance schedule, and walk the property regularly to stay ahead of curb appeal and repair issues. When emergencies happen, and they will, you're the one coordinating the response.

MidPen's model pairs property management with onsite resident services. You won't run those programs, but you'll work closely with that team. Building that relationship matters. A community where property staff and services staff operate in silos is harder to manage and harder to live in.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of multi-family residential management experience, with two of those years in affordable housing specifically
  • One year of supervisory experience, with a track record of developing staff rather than just directing them
  • Tax Credit Specialist (TCS) or Certified Occupancy Specialist (COS) certification, or the ability to obtain one within six months (MidPen covers the cost)
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and the ability to pass the FHA test within your first 60 days
  • Comfort with RealPage and the Microsoft Office Suite
  • An associate degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Affordable housing management is a different discipline than conventional Class A or B work. The compliance layer is heavier. Resident populations often include seniors, families, and individuals with special needs who bring more complexity to the community dynamic. Difficult conversations with residents happen, and they require patience and clear judgment. The paperwork load is real. So is the impact when the operation runs well.

Company-provided on-site housing is available, which is a meaningful benefit in a market where Sonoma housing costs are significant. Pay ranges from $25.62 to $28.82 hourly based on experience, with a full benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, 403(b), paid parental leave, and tuition reimbursement. Candidates who move from this role into senior property management within nonprofit affordable housing often find the compliance depth they built here travels well across LIHTC portfolios anywhere in the state.

job.title: Helper A - Residential Maintenance Technician Local 399
job.description:
This is a union maintenance position at The Belmont, a residential property at 3170 N Sheridan Rd in Chicago's Lakeview neighborhood. You'd be working Tuesday through Saturday, 2pm to 10pm, under Local 399 at a starting rate of $29.39 per hour.

The shift matters here. An evening schedule means you're the person residents reach when something goes wrong after work hours. Service requests, water infiltration reports, after-hours calls when you're on rotation. You'll work under and alongside the Building Engineer, handling work orders, assisting with apartment turns, running preventative maintenance tasks like HVAC filter swaps and sewer rodding, and coordinating vendor access when repairs go beyond the scope of in-house work. Janitorial and grounds duties are also part of the job, including snow removal when Chicago winters demand it.

Reside Living expects EPA certification and at least one year of full-time maintenance experience. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and hot water systems are the core mechanical skills they want. You'll document your work through a mobile app, so comfort with a smartphone and basic computer literacy matters.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • EPA certification (current)
  • Minimum one year of full-time maintenance or related field experience
  • Familiarity with mechanical systems: plumbing, electric, HVAC, hot water heaters
  • Proficiency with Outlook and Microsoft Suite
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs regularly; occasional heavier loads with assistance
  • Comfortable on ladders, stairs, and on your feet for the majority of your shift

Benefits come through Local 399 and include full health coverage. Reside also offers free employee parking, a $50 monthly phone stipend, and a 25% rent discount after 90 days, which carries real weight given Lakeview rental prices.

One thing worth knowing about this shift: the 2pm to 10pm window is quieter for coordinating vendors and project work, but busier for resident interaction. Most residents are home by then. That means your customer service manner shows up constantly, not just when you choose to engage. Strong candidates in this type of role understand that how you talk to a resident in the hallway is as much a part of the job as fixing what brought you there.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager at Cottonwood Ridgeview Apartments
job.description:
Cottonwood Residential operates a growing national multifamily portfolio, and the Assistant Property Manager at Cottonwood Ridgeview in Plano sits right at the center of how that portfolio actually performs. This is an operational role with real financial responsibility, real people dynamics, and regular moments where you'll need to step up and own decisions without the Property Manager in the room.

Day to day, you're covering a wide range: posting rent, processing applications, staying current on unit availability and pricing, walking the property, coordinating with vendors, and responding to residents who need answers quickly. You'll also support leasing efforts directly, which means you need to be comfortable talking with prospects, understanding what moves people to sign, and following through on the administrative side of the application process. The community uses Self-Guided Tours, so part of keeping that running smoothly falls to you too, including unit readiness and daily inspections.

The team support piece carries genuine weight here. You'll assist with onboarding new hires, help set expectations for consistent performance, and occasionally need to deliver hard feedback. When the Property Manager is out, you're not just holding down the fort. You're making the calls, fielding escalations, and keeping the community running. That's a real leadership expectation, and candidates who've only observed that kind of responsibility from the sidelines will feel the difference quickly.

One dynamic worth knowing: Plano sits in a competitive DFW submarket where Class A communities have trained renters to expect a polished, responsive experience. Residents here aren't comparing you to the budget complex down the street. They're comparing you to every other well-amenitized option they toured last weekend. That raises the bar on follow-up speed, communication quality, and how move-ins are handled.
