What separates strong candidates for an acquisition lease-up or stabilization role like this is the ability to read a T-12 critically and identify where the previous ownership left money on the table, whether through deferred maintenance, weak renewal pricing, or bloated vendor contracts. Candidates who bring that analytical lens alongside people skills tend to hit the ground faster and earn the confidence of ownership earlier.

What Peak is Looking For

  • Five or more years managing a multifamily property at scale
  • Demonstrated experience supervising leasing or maintenance staff
  • Hands-on budget preparation and financial reporting experience
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Strong leasing and operations fundamentals
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Peak Management offers medical, dental, and life insurance, PTO including your birthday, on-call premium pay, a 401(k) with employer matching, and a sign-on bonus. The company's core values lean hard into accountability and optimism, so if you tend toward drama or blame-shifting, this culture probably isn't the right fit. If you're the kind of manager who walks in on day one ready to assess, prioritize, and build, this role has real runway.

job.title: Regional Property Manager - Multi-Family Properties
job.description:
Regional Oversight With Real Operational Weight

Regional roles in multi-family management tend to fall into two categories: glorified troubleshooters who spend their days putting out fires, and genuine portfolio stewards who drive NOI with intention. CYM Living is building toward the latter. This is a vertically integrated firm headquartered in Chicago with deep roots in real estate investment, and they want a Regional Property Manager in Indianapolis who can own the full picture across a portfolio of multi-family communities.

The scope here is what you'd expect from a serious regional position. You'll be accountable for occupancy, revenue, and NOI performance across multiple properties, with regular site inspections, financial reviews, and variance analysis built into your rhythm. Budget ownership is real: you'll develop annual operating budgets, track month-over-month performance against those budgets, and bring a point of view on where expenses can be tightened without sacrificing asset condition. Delinquency and bad debt are yours to monitor and manage. Capital projects, renovations, and property transitions fall under your coordination as well.

On the people side, you'll recruit and develop Community Managers and support staff, run performance evaluations, and contribute to succession planning. CYM's stated emphasis on internal growth means the expectation is that you're building a bench, not just filling slots. Escalated resident issues and compliance matters, from fair housing to local landlord-tenant law, land on your desk when site teams need backup.

What the Role Actually Requires

  • 5 to 7+ years of progressive multi-family property management experience, with at least 3 years in a multi-site or regional capacity
  • Demonstrated track record managing budgets and hitting NOI targets
  • Working knowledge of fair housing regulations and applicable landlord-tenant law
  • Proficiency with property management software (Yardi, AppFolio, RealPage, Entrata, OneSite, or comparable platforms)
  • Valid driver's license and comfort with regular regional travel between properties
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent professional experience

What Separates Strong Candidates

The candidates who perform well in regional roles like this one have usually spent real time on-site before moving up. They know what a well-run make-ready program looks like, they can read a T-12 without needing someone to walk them through it, and they've personally coached a struggling Community Manager back to competency instead of just replacing them. Financial fluency matters here, but so does the credibility that comes from having actually managed a lease-up or worked through a difficult occupancy recovery. Indianapolis has a competitive mid-market multi-family environment with a mix of garden-style and mid-rise product, so familiarity with that asset class and price point will serve you well.

CYM Living's model combines data-driven decision making with what they describe as hyperlocal customer service, which in practice means the Regional Manager needs to be comfortable pulling performance reports and interpreting traffic trends, while also staying connected enough to individual communities that resident satisfaction doesn't slip through the cracks. It's a balance that takes experience to hold well.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance- Royal Oaks Apartments
job.description:
Banyan Living runs Royal Oaks as a luxury apartment community in North Royalton, Ohio. This Maintenance Technician position covers the full scope of day-to-day property upkeep: service requests, preventative maintenance, make-readies on vacant units, and building system repairs.

What the Work Looks Like

Your days split between scheduled work and reactive work. On the scheduled side, you're running preventative maintenance on building systems, inspecting equipment, and prepping turns so units are ready for incoming residents. On the reactive side, you're handling resident service requests across plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and you need to move on them promptly. Documentation matters here too. You'll track completed work and manage supply inventory so nothing falls through the cracks.

You'll work directly with the property management team. When an issue escalates or needs coordination, they need someone who communicates clearly and doesn't leave problems open longer than necessary.

What You Need

  • At least one year of maintenance or related hands-on experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical systems, and general repairs
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and a customer-service mindset when dealing with residents
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and handle physical work throughout the shift
  • Availability for on-call and emergency coverage
  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical certifications are a plus

Compensation and Benefits

Pay is bi-weekly. Benefits include medical, vision, dental, short and long-term disability, life insurance, and an employee assistance program. You also get paid holidays, PTO, and a 401(k). If you live on-site, there's a 35% rent discount.

One thing worth knowing: make-ready quality directly shapes the first impression a new resident gets. Technicians who treat turns with the same attention they give emergency calls tend to build stronger reputations within the property team, and that visibility often leads to lead tech or facilities coordinator roles as a company grows its portfolio.

job.title: Maintenance Service Manager
job.description:
Condominium maintenance management sits in its own category. You're not running a leasing operation, you're running a building, and the residents who own their units have high expectations and a direct financial stake in how well systems are maintained. When the boiler goes down in January or the fire suppression system throws a fault, the property manager's first call goes to the Maintenance Service Manager.

Taylor Management Company is hiring for that role at a condominium property in Summit, New Jersey. A valid New Jersey Black Seal Boiler Operator License is required before you apply. That's non-negotiable here, and it narrows the candidate pool considerably.

What the Job Actually Covers

This is a full-scope building systems role with a supervisory layer on top. Day-to-day, you're overseeing HVAC, boilers, plumbing, electrical, fire protection, and life safety systems, coordinating both reactive repairs and a structured preventive maintenance program. You'll also manage and schedule the maintenance staff, which means you're accountable for their work quality, their training, and how they interact with residents.

Resident-facing communication matters here. Condo owners are not renters, and they'll let you know it. Responding to service requests and emergencies with professionalism and follow-through is part of the job as much as any mechanical skill. You'll maintain records, track compliance, and handle the administrative side with basic proficiency in Microsoft Office and whatever maintenance management technology the property uses.

On-call coverage is real. Nights, weekends, holidays when systems don't care about your schedule.

What You Need Coming In

  • Valid New Jersey Black Seal Boiler Operator License
  • At least five years of commercial or residential building maintenance experience
  • Minimum three years in a supervisory capacity
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and life safety systems
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and safe work practices
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills (useful for unit turns and punch list items)
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds, work on ladders, and handle outdoor work in all weather
  • High school diploma or equivalent; trade or technical school background preferred

The candidates who stand out in roles like this are the ones who can troubleshoot a mechanical problem and then clearly explain what happened and what was done to fix it, to both their staff and to a condo owner who's standing in the hallway asking questions. Technical skill gets you in the door; communication keeps the property running smoothly. Additional bonus opportunities are available beyond base compensation.

job.title: Make Ready Technician/Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Lynco Properties is hiring full-time maintenance and make-ready technicians for their apartment communities in Lawton, Oklahoma. Pay runs $18 to $21 per hour depending on what you bring to the table, and the role comes with health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k), and paid time off.

The work is split between two lanes: make-readys and general maintenance. On the make-ready side, you're turning vacant units for move-in. That means painting, swapping out fixtures, replacing appliances, addressing plumbing, and working through the punch list until the apartment is genuinely ready to lease. You'll pull from the make-ready board and coordinate with the property manager on priorities and timing.

Day-to-day maintenance covers work orders in occupied units, grounds upkeep, common areas, and amenities. You'll also handle scheduled preventive tasks on a weekly, monthly, and quarterly basis. Material and supply orders go through the property manager for approval, so you'll need to communicate proactively when inventory is running low.

On-call rotation is part of the job. Weekend availability is required. If that's a dealbreaker, this role isn't the right fit.

One thing that separates solid candidates here: the ability to self-manage across both types of work without needing constant direction. Make-readys have a rhythm, but occupied-unit repairs are unpredictable. The techs who perform well can switch gears, work cleanly inside residents' homes, and keep a unit's timeline on track without letting work orders stack up.

What you'll need

  • At least one year of property maintenance experience
  • Your own tools
  • Reliable transportation
  • Working knowledge of painting, basic plumbing, appliance repair, and fixture replacement
  • Ability to work on-call and weekends
  • Dependable, team-oriented, and motivated to work without close supervision

Experience with HVAC, electrical, or other skilled trades will likely put you at the higher end of the pay range. Apply with a clear picture of your hands-on background.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community managers at stabilized conventional properties carry a deceptively broad mandate. Occupancy, NOI, team culture, resident retention, vendor oversight, and ownership reporting all land on the same desk. At a company the size of Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the larger Southeast-based multifamily operators in the country, the expectation is that the person running a community functions as a general manager, not just a leasing lead with an elevated title.

Meridian at North Hills sits in one of Raleigh's most competitive submarkets. North Hills has absorbed significant Class A and B supply over the past several years, which means renewal strategy and resident retention carry real weight here. Strong occupancy at this location requires more than traffic. It requires a manager who understands pricing, concessions, and what keeps a resident from going MTM or not renewing at all.

What the Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne describes this as a coach, culture ambassador, and business strategist position, and that framing is accurate. You'll own budget management, delinquency tracking, deposit accounting, and financial reporting. You'll run leasing alongside your team, including tours and lead follow-up, while also driving renewal conversion and monitoring occupancy targets. Vendor relationships, work order oversight with maintenance, and regular property inspections are part of the weekly rhythm. Resident escalations, online review responses, and resident event planning round out the community-facing side of the role. Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms in use.

Team leadership here means hiring, training, and holding accountability for both office and maintenance staff. Weekly team meetings, performance coaching, and connecting individual development to Hawthorne's internal career path program are all expectations of the role.

  • Two years of property management experience required, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of community manager experience in multifamily, highly preferred
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office familiarity preferred
  • CAM, CAPS, real estate license, or property management license preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • High school diploma or GED required

What Separates Strong Candidates

The managers who perform well in roles like this read a T-12 the same way they read a punch list. They spot delinquency trends before they compound, and they understand how a single bad renewal month affects NOI at the end of the quarter. Financial fluency isn't a bonus here. It's woven into the day-to-day. The other differentiator is genuine investment in team development. In a market like Raleigh, where leasing talent turns frequently, a manager who builds a team people want to stay on creates a compounding retention advantage. Hawthorne's internal career path program, which maps a trajectory from Community Manager toward Regional Manager, signals that the company rewards managers who develop their people rather than simply covering for turnover.

Office hours run Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturday 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends may come up for resident events. Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Maintenance managers at affordable housing portfolios wear a lot of hats. On any given day, you might be walking units to build a punch list, coordinating a vendor for a boiler repair, or coaching a technician through a task they haven't handled before. At Fairstead, this role sits at the center of all of that, and the expectation is that you can lead from the front, not just direct from an office.

What This Role Actually Involves

Fairstead's Champaign property needs someone who can supervise a maintenance team while still getting hands-on when the situation calls for it. You'll oversee the repair and upkeep of building systems, electrical equipment, and mechanical components, making sure inspections happen on schedule and that the property stays clean, safe, and code-compliant. Special projects will pull you into a leadership position, and some of them will require overtime. That's worth naming honestly up front.

Day-to-day, you'll balance reactive work (emergencies happen in any residential setting) with planned maintenance, and you'll need the organizational discipline to keep both tracks moving without letting one swallow the other. Yardi experience is a plus here, and Fairstead does lean into tech and data tools more than a typical affordable housing operator, so comfort with systems matters.

Core qualifications include:

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience, with depth in at least one trade
  • Solid working knowledge of building and mechanical systems, tools, and safety protocols
  • Experience supervising or mentoring other maintenance staff
  • The ability to implement and refine maintenance policies and procedures
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; Yardi knowledge is a plus

The People Side of This Job

A maintenance manager in affordable housing interacts with a wider range of people than many comparable roles. Residents often have fewer options and higher stakes when something goes wrong in their unit. That context shapes how good managers in this space communicate, follow through, and prioritize. The best candidates here aren't just technically sharp. They're consistent, calm under pressure, and clear with both their team and the residents they serve.

You'll also work alongside a property management team and, periodically, with Fairstead's broader platform, which spans development and construction as well as operations. That integrated structure means decisions get made with more context than they would at a purely third-party management shop, and it tends to give on-site leaders a clearer line of sight into why things are being done the way they are.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this position runs from $27 to $29 per hour, depending on skills, experience, and location. Fairstead offers a benefits package that includes medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company matching (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and a flexible spending account. Pet insurance, disability coverage, and employee discount programs round out the package.

For someone with a strong trade background who's ready to step into or grow within a supervisory role, this is a solid place to build. Fairstead's scale across 28 states means internal mobility is a real possibility for people who perform well and want to take on more.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Delaware Pines - Part-time
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Part-time maintenance work at a residential community in Huntington Beach demands more technical range than most people expect. At Delaware Pines, managed by Sunrise Management, a part-time technician touches plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, pool maintenance, and custodial upkeep, sometimes all in a single shift. The breadth isn't a list of edge cases. It's the actual daily scope, and it rewards people who've built genuine hands-on experience across trades rather than deep expertise in just one.

The pay range for this role sits at $25 to $26 per hour depending on experience. The position is part-time and not eligible for company benefit plans.

What the Work Actually Involves

A strong portion of the role centers on keeping units rent-ready and common areas in good shape. The standard for vacant unit turns is 3 to 5 days, so your ability to assess a punch list quickly and work through it efficiently matters. Service requests carry a 24-hour resolution expectation, and when parts or outside factors create delays, clear communication with both the Community Manager and the resident is part of the job, not an afterthought.

Beyond unit work, you'll manage preventive maintenance on a scheduled basis: checking lighting, fire safety equipment, pool and spa systems, and life-safety signage. Knowing the location of gas, water, irrigation, and electrical shutoffs is a baseline expectation. You'll assist with move-in and move-out inspections, track vacant unit status, and maintain accurate inventory of tools and supplies. On-call emergency availability is required, including evenings and weekends.

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • Comfort using a mobile device for work orders and communication
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and holidays
  • Self-directed work style, you'll often operate without direct supervision
  • Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to problem-solving
  • Resident-facing composure, including the ability to handle difficult situations professionally

What This Role Builds

Technicians who start in part-time roles like this one often develop something that's harder to teach than any specific trade skill: the discipline to prioritize across competing demands on a compressed schedule. When your hours are limited, your sequencing decisions matter. You learn to distinguish between what's urgent and what's scheduled, and that instinct carries into every maintenance role that follows, including lead tech and supervisor positions.

Sunrise Management operates with a resident-hospitality orientation, which means the soft skills this role sharpens, clear communication, professional presentation, handling difficult interactions with composure, are treated as part of the craft, not separate from it. For a technician building a career in residential property management, that framing tends to stick.

job.title: Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
Affordable housing management runs on a different set of rules than conventional multifamily. The compliance layer is thick, the regulatory calendar never really lets up, and residents depend on the property in ways that go well beyond month-to-month convenience. That's the environment this Community Manager role operates in, at a Fairstead property in Boaz, Alabama.

What This Role Actually Involves

The core of the job is keeping a HUD-regulated property running on every dimension at once: occupancy, compliance, finances, and physical condition. On the compliance side, you'll own the full cycle of certifications, annual and interim recertifications included, and you'll need to know the HUD 4350.3 Handbook well enough to write responses to regulatory agencies and work alongside the Compliance Department when residents fall out of lease or program requirements. REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits all land on your desk to prepare for and coordinate.

Financially, you're watching delinquency closely, pursuing collections through the appropriate legal channels, monitoring bad-debt write-offs, and attending monthly budget reviews with your regional team. On the maintenance side, you'll coordinate preventive and emergency work with your Building Superintendent, manage vendor bids and contractor quotes, document unit inspections, and stay in close contact with the construction team if any renovation work is active on site.

Resident-facing responsibilities are woven into every week. Move-in and move-out coordination, lease violation documentation, eviction processing when necessary, and handling the steady stream of questions and requests that residents bring to the office all require consistency and a calm, organized approach.

What Qualifications You'll Need

  • At least three years of management experience that included supervising a team (property management background preferred, though hospitality, retail, or restaurant management is considered)
  • COS or CPO certification is required
  • TCS certification if the property carries a tax credit component
  • Hands-on experience with EIV, and familiarity with Yardi or RealPage
  • Affordable housing program knowledge, particularly HUD-regulated occupancy
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred but not required

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The compliance requirements here are specific and consequential. A candidate who has personally prepared for or sat through a MOR or REAC inspection carries a real advantage over someone who has only worked conventional multifamily. So does someone who understands how EIV discrepancies get resolved, or who has written a response to a regulatory finding. The technical side of affordable housing occupancy is learnable, but coming in with that foundation means you're contributing from the first month rather than spending it getting up to speed on program rules.

Fairstead operates as an integrated owner and manager with a portfolio across 28 states, which means community managers here have access to centralized compliance and construction resources that smaller operators can't offer. For someone looking to grow in affordable housing management, that organizational infrastructure tends to create clearer paths toward regional or portfolio-level roles over time.

job.title: Grounds Specialist - Botanic Miramar Beach ~ Destin, FL
job.description:
Beachside luxury communities like Botanic Miramar Beach carry a visual standard that residents pay a premium to live inside. A single neglected breezeway or a cloudy pool can undercut everything the leasing team works to sell. The Grounds Specialist role exists to make sure that never happens.

This is a daily-presence, eyes-on-the-property position at Davis Development's Destin community. You're walking the grounds throughout each shift, pulling litter, debris, and pet waste from breezeways, pool decks, and common areas before residents notice them. Trash and recyclables get handled on schedule. Pool chemistry gets checked and logged every day, with a full vacuum cycle weekly. Grills get cleaned and their timers and knobs inspected regularly to keep things safe. You'll also pitch in on general labor tasks supporting the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager as needs come up.

Davis Development operates as an owner-operator from the inside out. Their on-site teams aren't executing orders from a distant regional office; they're making real decisions daily. For a grounds role, that means your judgment about what the property needs matters. You notice the things others walk past.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of general labor experience; multifamily background is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) certification preferred
  • Comfortable with hand tools, cleaning equipment, and related supplies
  • Able to lift approximately 50 lbs regularly
  • Strong time management and communication skills across all channels
  • Availability to work over 40 hours per week when the property needs it

What Davis Development Offers

Benefits begin on the first of the month after 30 days of employment and include medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health coverage. The 401(k) plan includes a 4% employer match that vests immediately. Company-paid life insurance at one times base salary, a PTO package with carryover, a company apparel store allowance, and ongoing training and career development round out the package.

One practical note for candidates: Destin's Gulf Coast climate means this role runs outdoors year-round, through humid summers and variable winters. Pace and physical stamina matter here more than they might at an inland Class B community. CPO certification, even if you don't have it yet, is worth pursuing early. Pool compliance is taken seriously at luxury communities, and holding that credential opens up maintenance career paths that pure groundskeeping doesn't.

job.title: Customer Service Coordinator
job.description:
Single-family rental at scale runs on coordination. At Evergreen Residential, a Dallas-based SFR and build-to-rent platform founded in 2021, the Customer Service Coordinator role sits at the intersection of resident relations, maintenance operations, and the kind of real-time problem-solving that keeps portfolios performing. If you've built communication and organization skills in property management or a high-volume service environment, this role puts both to work every day.

Skills This Role Develops and Demands

Resident-facing work in institutional SFR is different from traditional multifamily. You're supporting residents in scattered single-family homes rather than a single property, which means your coordination instincts matter more than walking a leaseup or monitoring foot traffic at a leasing desk. The skills that compound here: triaging inbound calls and escalations, tracking work order pipelines across a service request dashboard, and translating maintenance updates into clear resident communication. You'll also get exposure to smart home technology, including lock access, account setup, and troubleshooting. As SFR operators increasingly differentiate on tech-enabled resident experience, that's a transferable skill set.

The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 9am to 6pm, with Saturday offering a work-from-home option. Occasional evening and overtime hours are part of the role. That's worth knowing before you apply.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day to day, you're handling inbound calls and routing them correctly, supporting residents on portal questions and ledger inquiries, and coordinating with field operations teams to make sure service requests get resolved on time and meet company standards. You'll conduct resident welcome calls, troubleshoot smart home issues, and serve as the internal subject matter expert for maintenance workflow. The ledger work, both prospect and resident-side, gives you exposure to how income and charges flow in a managed SFR portfolio.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • At least one year of administrative or customer service experience; property management background preferred
  • Prior use of property management software is a plus
  • Calm under pressure, especially on escalated calls
  • Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Adobe
  • Strong organization and time management, with consistent follow-through on deadlines
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills

Where This Role Leads

Coordinators who learn the operational rhythm of an institutional SFR platform, work order management, resident lifecycle touchpoints, ledger basics, and tech-enabled service, tend to grow into operations specialist, portfolio coordinator, or assistant property manager roles. At a company like Evergreen, which is still building its operational infrastructure and has leadership with deep SFR institutional roots, there's real exposure to how a modern third-party management platform is structured. That's a different kind of education than you'd get at a legacy multifamily operator. The candidates who stand out here aren't just organized. They read a situation quickly, stay composed when a resident is frustrated, and close the loop without being asked twice.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Property management at this level runs on a specific blend of financial literacy, team leadership, and operational awareness. At The Whit and Ridgewood Arches, a combined 164-unit portfolio in Minneapolis, the Property Manager keeps occupancy healthy, delinquency low, and the physical asset in good shape while developing a site team that actually performs. Bigos Management has earned Star Tribune Top Workplace recognition eleven times, which tells you something about how the company treats its people internally. That culture runs both directions: toward employees and toward residents.

The financial side of this role is real. You're managing rent collection, tracking delinquent accounts, working evictions when necessary, and submitting accurate reports to your Regional Manager. You'll do market research using public-facing sources to inform pricing recommendations. If you've ever prepared a T-12 or watched NOI move based on concession decisions, that mindset applies here. You're not just executing tasks. You're thinking about what the numbers mean for the property's overall health.

What You're Actually Managing Day to Day

On the leasing side, you're overseeing activity to keep occupancy maximized. That means watching traffic, understanding what's driving or limiting conversions, and making sure the site is positioned correctly in the market. On the maintenance side, you're building the turn schedule, coordinating make-ready inspections, managing the punch list process, and working with the roving maintenance team on anything beyond routine upkeep. You'll also monitor preventative maintenance programs and regularly walk the property to assess its condition and appearance.

The leadership piece is direct. You supervise site employees, handle coaching and development, and maintain a team environment consistent with Bigos' core values around relationships, quality, and accountability. Fair housing compliance and workplace safety are non-negotiable components of how you operate.

  • 3 to 5 years of management experience, with property management preferred
  • 1 to 2 years in a Property Manager or supervisory role preferred
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a strong plus
  • CRM designation preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required; degree in property management preferred
  • Active real estate licenses are not permitted in this role
  • Solid grasp of federal fair housing law and applicable local provisions

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Minneapolis has a competitive multifamily market with a wide range of product types. Managing two named communities under one umbrella means you're balancing distinct resident profiles and operational rhythms simultaneously. Managers who excel here tend to be detail-oriented on the financial side without losing sight of the resident experience. They know how to coach a team through a high-turn period without letting quality slip. They read delinquency reports early in the month, not at the end. And they document unit conditions thoroughly because it protects the property and keeps the make-ready process efficient.

The pay range runs $65,000 to $75,000. Bigos offers a competitive benefits package that includes 401(k) with employer match, HSA with employer contribution active from the first of the month after hire, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, PTO with rollover, volunteer time off, life insurance, short and long-term disability, educational assistance, an employee assistance program, a rent discount, and a Life Time Fitness membership discount.

job.title: Full-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a sales role. That sounds obvious, but plenty of candidates come in expecting a hospitality gig and get surprised by the close rate expectations. At PeakMade, this position is structured around conversion, and the skills you'll use most are the ones that live at the intersection of sales discipline and resident experience.

The Skills This Role Runs On

The core of this job is multi-touch follow-up. Calls, texts, emails, CRM notes, all of it done consistently and quickly. PeakMade is looking for someone who already knows what a pipeline looks like and who doesn't need to be reminded that a lead that goes cold costs the community real money. Strong product knowledge matters here too: pricing, availability, concessions, and a working understanding of the competitive set in the submarket. You're not just selling an apartment, you're selling this apartment over the three other communities a prospect toured this week.

Tour delivery is the other major skill set. High-traffic leasing seasons reward consultants who can read a prospect, build rapport quickly, and create genuine urgency without being pushy. The best performers in this type of role know how to tailor the walk to what the prospect actually said they needed, not just what's on the brochure.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Day to day, you're converting inbound leads across phone, email, and in-person channels, delivering tours, following up with prospects throughout the sales cycle, and maintaining accurate records in whatever CRM platform the community runs (Yardi, Entrata, and RealPage are all mentioned). You'll also handle lease paperwork, deposit collection, and move-in and move-out coordination, so administrative accuracy is part of the job, not an afterthought. During turn season, you'll support the make-ready process alongside the broader team.

  • 1+ year of sales or leasing experience with measurable conversion results
  • Hands-on experience with a property management CRM
  • Demonstrated multi-touch outreach discipline
  • Availability to work weekends and peak leasing hours

What's Worth Knowing About This Role

Student housing leasing, which is PeakMade's primary space, has a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Lease-up activity tends to compress into defined windows, traffic spikes seasonally, and the prospect pool often includes parents as decision-makers alongside the residents themselves. If you've worked conventional garden-style or mid-rise leasing before, the skills transfer cleanly, but the pace and dynamic shift. Strong performers in this environment tend to combine genuine hustle during peak season with the kind of consistent follow-up discipline that keeps prospects engaged over a longer consideration cycle.

The role is commission-eligible, which means your earnings track directly to your closing performance. PeakMade also offers housing discounts (terms vary by community), PTO, wellbeing days, 401(k) match, and growth opportunities into leadership. The Houston location puts you in one of the more active student housing and multifamily markets in the country, which matters for long-term career development in this industry.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
A prospect calls about a two-bedroom at The Westbury, but after a few questions, Champion Hills at Windyke is the better fit. You know both properties well enough to make that call confidently, schedule the tour, and follow up the same day.

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is hiring a full-time Leasing Manager to own the leasing function across two neighboring southeast Memphis apartment communities: The Westbury and Champion Hills at Windyke. Each property has its own Property Manager and Assistant Property Manager, so you're not running operations. You're running leasing. That means traffic, follow-up, applications, move-ins, and occupancy, across both sites, coordinated with two property teams.

The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, with one Saturday off per month. Pay ranges from $25 to $27 per hour, plus $130 commission per move-in and quarterly and annual bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, disability, and other insurance options, a 401(k) with profit-sharing, paid time off, and paid holidays.

What the Job Covers

Day to day, you're responding to leads across every channel, conducting tours, comparing units across two communities with prospects, and moving applications through to approved move-ins. You'll also provide direction and support to the Leasing Consultant assigned to the two-property campus and help coordinate Saturday leasing coverage.

Beyond the front-end sales cycle, you'll assist with renewals, resident relations, leasing paperwork, and file accuracy. You'll keep both property managers informed on leasing activity, priorities, and pipeline.

What MRG Is Looking For

  • At least two years of apartment leasing experience, required
  • Prior experience in a senior leasing, leasing manager, assistant manager, or multi-site leasing role, preferred
  • Strong follow-up habits and organized approach to managing leads and applications
  • Comfortable providing day-to-day guidance to another leasing employee
  • Proficient with CRM software and general computer use
  • Valid driver's license, proof of auto insurance, and reliable transportation
  • Able to pass background, credit, and drug screenings

The candidate who stands out will have handled multi-site or high-volume leasing before, because splitting attention across two communities while keeping both pipelines moving takes a different kind of organization than single-property leasing. If you've managed your own traffic board, coached a junior leasing consultant, and still kept your close rate up, this role fits that profile well.

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is an established Memphis property management company with room to grow for the right person.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
The Overlook at Sugar Hill needs a leasing consultant who understands that occupancy is built one conversation at a time. This is a front-line sales and service role where your daily traffic numbers, conversion rate, and follow-up habits directly shape the community's performance. Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country, runs a purpose-driven culture they call "Live It." That culture starts at the leasing desk.

What You'll Actually Do

Your mornings typically start with incoming leads from the previous evening: web inquiries, voicemails, emails. You respond quickly, because speed-to-contact is one of the most predictable factors in lead conversion. From there, the day moves between tours, application processing, and follow-up calls to prospects still deciding. You're not just showing apartments; you're reading what matters to each prospect and connecting the community's lifestyle to their specific needs.

  • Conduct personalized tours and respond to phone, email, and web inquiries with urgency
  • Convert leads to signed leases through consistent follow-up and relationship-building
  • Complete leasing applications, verification paperwork, and move-in documentation accurately
  • Support occupancy and renewal goals alongside the community management team
  • Coordinate and participate in resident events that drive retention
  • Monitor competitor properties and local market activity to stay sharp on positioning
  • Assist with social media and outreach marketing for the community

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Saturdays from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. One weekday off per week keeps the total at 40 hours. Occasional evening availability may be needed for resident events.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Confidence communicating in person, by phone, and in writing
  • A natural ability to handle objections and guide prospects toward a decision
  • Comfort with leasing software and digital communication channels
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP certification is a plus, not a prerequisite

Trajectory and Compensation

Hawthorne operates a structured Career Path Program, and the leasing consultant role is a known entry point into assistant community manager positions. That promotion typically comes with exposure to budgets, delinquency management, and NOI reporting. Getting there means building a track record in leasing conversion and resident satisfaction first.

Compensation combines an hourly base with monthly leasing and renewal commissions, plus performance incentive programs. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

What separates strong candidates here is follow-through. Plenty of people can give a good tour. The consultants who actually move the occupancy needle are the ones who call back the undecided prospect on day three, who remember what the prospect said about their commute or their dog, and who treat every renewal conversation with the same energy as a new lease. That's the difference between filling apartments and building a community.

job.title: Leasing Professional - Roving - Temporary - Berkeley Heights, Creekwood Apartments
job.description:
Roving leasing roles sit at an interesting intersection of sales ability and operational flexibility. CloudTen Residential is bringing on a temporary full-time Leasing Professional to rotate across properties in the Berkeley Heights area, stepping in where leasing traffic and staffing needs demand coverage. The pay runs $25 to $28 per hour depending on experience, with leasing bonuses available at assigned sites, and the position qualifies for CloudTen's standard benefit plans despite being temporary.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

On any given day, you might be prepping an apartment for a showing (light cleaning, basic make-ready checks), walking a prospective resident through the community, or working through a stack of rental applications in the management system. CloudTen uses OneSite and Entrata, so fluency with at least one of those platforms keeps you productive from day one rather than spending your first week figuring out the software.

Because this is a roving position, you'll carry the full leasing cycle with you from site to site: phone inquiries, in-person tours, objection handling, securing commitments and deposits, and completing move-in paperwork. You'll also keep an eye on community conditions during site visits and flag any deficiencies to the on-site manager. A valid driver's license is required since you'll be transporting marketing materials and moving between locations.

  • Tour and lease apartments across multiple properties, handling the full process from prospect contact through executed lease
  • Process rental applications accurately and in compliance with Fair Housing requirements
  • Assist with move-in and move-out inspections, with attention to consistent documentation
  • Set up and transport signage and marketing collateral as needed at assigned sites
  • Accept and route maintenance requests professionally when on-site
  • Review property database entries for accuracy and flag advertising discrepancies
  • Support market survey preparation when assigned

What CloudTen Is Looking For

One to two years of leasing experience is preferred, and lease-up experience carries real weight here. Lease-up environments demand a faster pace and sharper sales instincts than stabilized communities, and a roving professional who can walk into a high-traffic situation and close deals without a long ramp-up period is genuinely valuable. Prior sales experience (two years or more) rounds out the profile they're building.

Strong candidates tend to be self-directed, organized, and comfortable adapting quickly. When you're rotating across sites, you don't have the luxury of leaning on institutional familiarity with a single property. You need to absorb new floor plans, community features, and pricing quickly, then present them confidently. That adaptability is what separates candidates who thrive in roving roles from those who prefer the consistency of a single-site position.

The Bigger Picture

CloudTen's portfolio spans a wide range of product types, including hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning. For a leasing professional, that kind of exposure across property types builds a resume that travels well. Even in a temporary capacity, working across multiple communities gives you practical insight into how different assets are positioned, priced, and operated. That cross-site experience often accelerates the path toward a community manager role for candidates who are organized and growth-oriented.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor, The Beam
job.description:
Leading Maintenance at a Luxury Mid-Rise in New London

A Maintenance Supervisor role at a luxury mid-rise carries a different weight than one at a garden-style community. At a 203-unit property like The Beam, you're coordinating multiple service categories simultaneously, keeping the physical plant of a multi-story building operating at a standard that matches what residents are paying for. Jefferson Apartment Group, a vertically integrated firm with acquisition, development, construction, and management under one roof, brings that same full-cycle perspective to how they run their communities. That context matters when you're the person responsible for how the building actually performs day to day.

What the Role Actually Involves

This position splits your time between hands-on maintenance work and team leadership. You'll build the priority work schedule for service and janitorial staff, ensure all service requests get completed, and continuously inspect the property to catch deficiencies before residents do. That kind of proactive eye separates good supervisors from reactive ones.

On the operational side, you'll also:

  • Order parts and supplies within budgetary guidelines and actively manage overtime costs
  • Ensure all unit entry notifications are left after each service visit
  • Keep mechanical inspections current and maintain proper key control
  • Work alongside the Community Manager to bid major contracts annually and contribute to the maintenance portions of the annual budget
  • Conduct performance reviews for maintenance and janitorial staff
  • Be available for after-hours emergency calls, including evenings, weekends, and holidays

Budget involvement at this level is worth flagging. Many Maintenance Supervisors spend years without touching a budget. Contributing to the annual budget process here builds a skill that opens doors to Regional Maintenance Director and Director of Facilities roles later in your career.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year of multifamily maintenance experience, a solid foundation in tools and general maintenance trades, and the physical capacity to handle the full demands of the position, including lifting 50 to 100 pounds and moving through a multi-story building throughout the day. HVAC certification is preferred and will put you ahead of other candidates. Lease-up or new construction experience is also preferred, which fits given Jefferson's development background.

What the role builds is equally important. Leading a team through daily triage, communicating professionally with residents, and contributing to capex planning all sharpen the judgment and organizational discipline that define strong maintenance leadership. Supervisors who can hold a high curb appeal standard while keeping service costs controlled are the ones who advance within third-party and in-house management operations alike.

Pay ranges from $35 to $40 per hour. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, performance-based bonus potential, and possible rental discounts.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's 8 a.m. on a Monday and you're already walking lot lines, noting a resident's skirting that needs attention, checking in with maintenance before the morning fills up, and pulling up last week's delinquency numbers before you sit down with anything else. By noon you've handled a lease inquiry, approved a vendor invoice, and called a resident whose rent is five days late.

The Operation

This is the Community Manager role for Havenpark's property in Canby, OR, a manufactured home community of 270 homesites. You're running the full P&L: collections, occupancy, leasing activity, vendor coordination, and the physical condition of the grounds. Havenpark operates 100+ communities nationally, and this property is one piece of a portfolio with serious operational depth behind it, but on-site, the decisions are yours.

Delinquency management is a real part of the job. Manufactured home communities tend to have a resident base that's relationship-driven, which means collections require judgment and consistency in equal measure. You'll track aging weekly, follow established protocols, and know when to escalate. Occupancy and leasing are ongoing: you'll field traffic, move prospective residents through the process, and keep your eye on how the community's lot occupancy trends month to month. Your budget is your scorecard. You'll manage expenses, report on variances, and understand how capex decisions and vendor spend flow through to NOI.

You'll lead a small on-site team. That means hiring well, setting expectations clearly, and holding people accountable without burning them out. Havenpark's stated values, including Grit and Stewardship, aren't decorative here. They describe the pace and the ownership mentality the company expects from people running their communities.

What Havenpark Is Looking For

  • Prior experience managing a residential community, ideally with direct P&L or budget responsibility
  • Comfort with collections and delinquency follow-up, including resident-facing conversations that require both firmness and professionalism
  • Experience leading on-site staff, even a small team
  • Competency with property management software and basic financial reporting
  • Strong communication skills across resident interactions, vendor relationships, and internal reporting

Manufactured home community management has its own learning curve if you're coming from apartments or conventional residential. The resident relationships tend to run longer and deeper, turnover carries different economics, and the physical management of the land itself adds a layer that doesn't exist in a mid-rise or garden-style apartment context. Candidates who've managed MHC properties before will ramp faster, but strong operators from adjacent residential backgrounds can translate their skills effectively if they're willing to learn the asset class.

What separates a strong candidate here is the ability to treat every metric as a signal rather than just a number. Low occupancy tells you something about your leasing process or your community's curb appeal. High delinquency tells you something about resident screening or follow-through on collections. The managers who thrive in this type of role read the data and then go walk the property to understand what's actually happening.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Student housing maintenance runs at a different pace than conventional multifamily. Turns are compressed into a few weeks before the academic year starts, pool logs need to stay clean all summer, and when something breaks at 11pm the night before move-in, someone has to answer the phone. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their College Station community, and they're clear about what the job actually involves.

What You'll Actually Do

Day-to-day, you're working service requests, keeping up with a preventative maintenance schedule, and helping maintain curb appeal across grounds, breezeways, and common areas. You'll assist with turn events when the lease cycle flips, which in student housing means coordinating make-readies on a tight calendar with little margin for punch list items that drag. Pool maintenance is part of the scope here, including chemical logs that need to stay accurate and current. You'll carry on-call rotation responsibilities, so after-hours calls are a real part of this job. HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances: you're expected to troubleshoot and repair across all of it, not hand everything off to vendors.

You'll also work alongside the Maintenance Supervisor to track inventory, stay within budget guidelines, and support hazard communications compliance. Resident-facing communication matters here too. Student renters have high expectations and a low tolerance for delays, and how you handle a complaint often matters as much as how fast you fix the problem.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of maintenance experience, apartment industry experience preferred
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • Ability to troubleshoot HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances independently
  • Reliable transportation and ability to live within 30 miles of the property
  • Comfortable with weekend, holiday, and rotating on-call schedules
  • Physically able to lift up to 50 pounds, work on ladders above eight feet, and handle outdoor work in Texas heat
  • Your own hand tools. This is standard in the trade.

The Bigger Picture

PeakMade specializes in off-campus student housing, and College Station is a high-volume college market with a large renter population tied directly to Texas A&M. The community you'd be serving sees predictable seasonal pressure, particularly around August move-in and the summer turn. Technicians who can stay organized during that window and keep their work quality consistent under volume tend to build real credibility fast in student housing operations.

PeakMade offers technical training, HVAC and CPO certification support, and a facilities leadership track for those who want to grow toward a supervisory role. Monthly renewal bonuses and a 401(k) match are also part of the package, along with parental leave benefits that are genuinely above average for this industry.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Marc San Marcos
job.description:
MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for more than 30 years. Their portfolio spans multiple states, and they promote heavily from within, which means a leasing role here has a real path forward for the right person.

The open position is at Marc, a residential community in San Marcos, CA. The job centers on converting traffic into signed leases. You'll greet prospects, qualify applicants, walk units, and shepherd people through the leasing process from first contact to move-in day. That last part matters: you'll coordinate with maintenance to make sure new residents aren't moving into a unit with an open punch list.

Administrative work is part of the job too. Rental files need to stay current, lease documents need to be accurate, and data entry has to be done right. When residents have complaints or maintenance concerns, you're often the first point of contact. Rent collection support falls under this role as well.

Weekend availability is required.

What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred)
  • Strong sales instincts and genuine customer service skills
  • Professional communication, written and verbal
  • Comfort with leasing software and data entry
  • Ability to work weekends

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, plus monthly and quarterly bonuses and company profit sharing. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, PTO, and rental discounts.

San Marcos sits in North San Diego County, a market with steady renter demand driven by Cal State San Marcos, a growing life sciences employment base, and limited new supply relative to other parts of the county. Occupancy pressure is real, which means leasing skills here get tested consistently, and a consultant who can close efficiently becomes valuable quickly.

Leasing is where most property management careers start, and at a company that promotes from within, strong performers here move toward assistant manager and property manager roles. If that trajectory interests you, this kind of role builds the foundation: sales, compliance, resident relations, and administrative accuracy all at once.

job.title: Community Manager- Student Housing
job.description:
Student housing management draws on a specific blend of skills that most conventional multifamily experience doesn't fully develop: the ability to run a full annual turn at scale, manage a high-energy leasing cycle tied to an academic calendar, and maintain financial performance against revenue targets that reset every year. The Community Manager role at Lark Baton Rouge calls on all of those at once.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Scion places this position at the center of property operations, and the skill set reflects that. Financial management is a constant: you'll own the budget process from preparation through month-end close, manage NOI through both revenue growth and expense discipline, and produce variance explanations that hold up under scrutiny. Alongside that, you'll carry full responsibility for leasing velocity, gain-to-lease performance, concessions strategy, and market rate positioning. Those two tracks, financial and leasing, run in parallel and require fluency in both.

People management is the third skill set this role demands heavily. You'll hire, develop, and hold accountable a team of leasing and maintenance staff, and you'll need to be the kind of leader who can plan for succession so the property runs smoothly when you're not on site. On-call responsibility is real here. Student housing communities don't pause for off-hours, and the GM is the primary responder when escalations arise.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

  • Lead the annual turnover process: coordinating vendors, setting team expectations, managing overtime budgets, and hitting make-ready deadlines before move-in
  • Monitor KPIs in property management platforms (Entrata preferred) and act on the data rather than just reporting it
  • Oversee facilities compliance including permits, preventative maintenance schedules, and curb appeal across common areas and amenities
  • Manage reputation across review platforms as part of the broader customer experience strategy
  • Partner with legal and accounting teams on vendor contracts, risk management, and monthly financial reporting
  • Ensure Fair Housing compliance and safety training across all onsite staff

The Baton Rouge Context and What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Baton Rouge is a student housing market anchored by LSU's enrollment, which runs well above 35,000 students. The demand cycle here is reliable but compressed: pre-leasing for the following fall starts early, competition among purpose-built student communities is real, and the annual turn window between July and August is intense. A GM who has managed high-volume turn seasons at a similarly sized property will have a clear operational advantage over someone learning that process for the first time here.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is comfort operating at the intersection of numbers and people. Plenty of managers can read a T-12 or run a leasing team. Fewer can do both well while also being the face of the community to residents, the accountability partner for staff, and the primary contact during a 2 a.m. emergency. Scion's model asks for all of that in one person, and the candidates who thrive are the ones who find that range energizing rather than exhausting.

Scion brings a dedicated student housing platform to this role, which means the training, systems, and organizational infrastructure are built specifically for this asset class rather than adapted from conventional multifamily. For a manager who wants to grow within student housing specifically, that focus has real career value.

job.title: Future Opportunity Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at an apartment community pulls on a wider skill set than most people expect. Plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, curb appeal, key control, inventory management , all of it lands on one person's plate in a given week. Berkshire Ninth Street is collecting applications from maintenance technicians who are ready for that kind of range.

What This Role Actually Demands

Berkshire Residential owns and manages its own portfolio, which means maintenance techs here support a team with a direct stake in asset performance. Every deferred repair affects NOI. Every slow turn affects occupancy. Every safety issue carries liability. The people who do this job well treat the physical plant like it belongs to them, because in an important operational sense, it does.

Day-to-day, you'll handle work orders across systems: appliances, plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry. You'll also help manage the shop, control inventory, and keep equipment organized. Curb appeal is part of the job description, not an afterthought. On a given morning, you might close out three work orders, inspect a vacant unit on the punch list, and help a resident troubleshoot a faulty HVAC before noon. That kind of context-switching is normal here, and it rewards techs who are organized and don't need a lot of hand-holding between tasks.

The Skills That Matter Here

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core systems: appliances, plumbing, electrical, and carpentry
  • Comfort with basic computer use for work order platforms or maintenance tracking software
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English, since work order documentation and resident interaction are both part of the role
  • A track record of treating safety protocols as non-negotiable, not suggestions

What It Looks Like Working for Berkshire

Berkshire Residential operates as a vertically integrated company , ownership and management under one roof. That structure tends to reduce the friction maintenance techs often feel at fee-managed properties, where ownership and operations speak different languages. Here, the priorities align. The company also puts real weight on career development; technicians who build a strong track record have a credible path toward lead tech and maintenance supervisor roles over time.

The candidate who stands out brings genuine technical range, takes pride in make-readies being done right the first time, and communicates proactively when something needs to escalate. Closing work orders fast matters. Closing them correctly matters more.

job.title: Maintenance Lead (Sunset Creek, Sunset Pines, Fair Haven Commons)
job.description:
A maintenance lead role at a nonprofit affordable housing organization carries responsibilities that go beyond typical apartment maintenance work. You're managing operations across multiple communities simultaneously, which means your coordination and leadership skills get tested every single day, not just when something breaks.

What This Role Actually Covers

This position oversees maintenance operations for three Fairfield communities: Sunset Creek, Sunset Pines, and Fair Haven Commons. The scope runs from hands-on trades work in electrical, plumbing, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair to team scheduling, vendor selection, bid review, and contractor oversight. You'll manage unit turns for move-ins and move-outs, coordinate annual inspections, run preventive maintenance programs, and keep common areas clean and safe. On-call emergency rotation is part of the job. So is accurate recordkeeping and managing inventory and supply procurement across all three sites.

MidPen's portfolio includes affordable communities serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. That means inspections here follow REAC, TCAC, and MOR standards, not just standard market-rate property protocols. If you've worked in affordable housing before, you already know the difference. If you haven't, this role will build that knowledge quickly.

Skills Required vs. Skills You'll Build

Coming in, you need at least five years of hands-on maintenance experience across the core trades plus three years supervising a crew. Multi-trade proficiency, working knowledge of affordable housing inspection standards, and the ability to manage vendors from bid to completion are baseline requirements. Strong communication matters too. You'll be working with residents, contractors, community partners, and internal teams, and the ability to write clearly and speak directly shapes how well that all goes.

What this role builds is different. Managing three properties at once sharpens your ability to triage competing priorities under real pressure. Leading a team through inspections with regulatory consequences develops the kind of compliance discipline that transfers across the affordable housing sector. Coordinating with MidPen's onsite Resident Services team also gives you a clearer picture of how maintenance quality connects directly to resident stability, which is a perspective that makes better maintenance professionals.

Who Does Well in This Role

The candidates who thrive here bring a few things that aren't always spelled out in job postings. First, genuine interest in coaching their team rather than just completing work orders themselves. Second, comfort with documentation, because TCAC and REAC inspections reward organized recordkeeping and penalize gaps. Third, a calm, consistent approach to resident interactions. Affordable housing communities often serve residents navigating real hardship, and the maintenance team is frequently the most visible face of management in a resident's daily experience.

  • High school diploma plus five years of broad maintenance experience (or equivalent combination)
  • Three years of supervisory experience with apartment turns and crew oversight
  • Working knowledge of REAC, TCAC, or MOR inspection standards
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and basic computer applications
  • Ability to perform physically demanding work across varying outdoor conditions
  • Valid driver's license (implied by multi-site responsibilities)

The pay range is $30.00 to $33.75 per hour, based on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, and an EAP program.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and operates workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and their maintenance team sits at the center of that mission. A Maintenance Technician here isn't just fixing things, they're the reason residents feel at home and properties hold their value. This opening covers two Central Florida locations: Daytona Beach and DeLand.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your days involve working through resident work orders, conducting inspections, and keeping common areas, amenities, and building systems running properly. Make-readies are a real part of the rhythm here. When a unit turns, you're preparing that apartment for the next resident, which means completing punch lists, addressing any deferred issues, and getting the space genuinely move-in ready, not just surface clean.

Beyond reactive repairs, you'll run preventive maintenance checks, manage your parts inventory, coordinate with vendors and contractors when work goes beyond in-house scope, and keep documentation tight. That last part matters more than people expect. Accurate records protect the property, support budgeting, and make your own life easier when a recurring issue shows up six months later.

This role includes a rotating on-call schedule, so evenings and weekends are part of the deal. That's a real commitment, and it's worth knowing going in.

What Hillpointe Needs From You

  • Hands-on mechanical aptitude with the ability to diagnose and repair issues across building systems
  • Experience with preventive maintenance routines and pre-move-out inspections
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant recycling (or willingness to obtain it)
  • Valid driver's license for on-property golf cart operation
  • Comfortable reading technical manuals, schematics, and blueprints
  • Solid communication habits with residents, management, and contractors
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly and work in varying outdoor conditions
  • High school diploma or GED, plus relevant experience or training
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and PPE requirements

Team Fit and Growth

Because Hillpointe controls development, construction, and operations in-house, their maintenance staff tends to work alongside people who genuinely understand how buildings go together. That context helps. You're not just executing work orders in isolation. You're part of a team that has line of sight into the full property lifecycle.

Technicians who build strong diagnostic habits and take ownership of their units often grow into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles. If that trajectory interests you, this environment gives you the exposure to get there. Hillpointe's focus on workforce housing also means you're working with residents who depend on well-functioning homes, which adds real weight to the work without making it abstract.

job.title: Full-Time Overnight Lead Cleaner (Thu-Mon, 11PM-6AM)
job.description:
Overnight facility cleanliness is one of those operational foundations that residents notice immediately when it slips and almost never consciously appreciate when it's working. For a company like Comstock, whose ParkX brand positions itself around premium parking and mobility experiences, the overnight cleaning crew is doing real brand work between 11 PM and 6 AM while most of the organization sleeps.

This Lead Cleaner position covers Thursday through Monday on the overnight shift at a Reston, VA property. The lead component matters here. You're not just running a checklist; you're taking ownership of the shift, completing required end-of-turn documentation, and ensuring a clean handoff to the next crew. That accountability structure is closer to a shift supervisor function than a standard porter role.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this role is maintaining common areas, lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public-facing spaces to a standard that holds up to daylight inspection. Pressure washing, window cleaning, and trash collection are regular duties. When events run late or the next day brings a scheduled gathering, you'll support setup and breakdown of those spaces as well. You'll also monitor cleaning supply inventory, keep the supply room organized, and flag any equipment damage or maintenance concerns to management. The shift runs independently, so self-direction is genuinely required, not just a line on a job description.

Physical demands are real. Expect extended time on your feet, lifting up to 50 pounds, working in variable temperatures (outdoors in Northern Virginia winters), and regular exposure to cleaning chemicals. A valid driver's license without major violations is required.

Qualifications Worth Having

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to work Thursday through Monday, 11 PM to 6 AM, including occasional extended hours around events
  • Strong reliability and time management; overnight shifts amplify both when supervision is minimal
  • Comfort working with a diverse range of residents, guests, and property staff in a professional, courteous manner
  • Problem-solving instincts for situations that come up mid-shift without a manager on-site

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) matching, life insurance, free parking with EV charging, parental leave, and annual professional development funds. Comstock also notes genuine advancement opportunities within its growing portfolio, which matters for anyone thinking about where overnight facilities work can lead.

On that point: lead cleaner roles at mid-rise and mixed-use properties often serve as a practical entry point into facilities coordination or property operations. The documentation habits, inventory tracking, and shift-handoff discipline you build here transfer directly to maintenance tech roles and, eventually, facilities management positions. The overnight schedule is demanding, but the independence and lead-level responsibility compress your learning curve faster than a supervised daytime role where someone else is making the calls.

job.title: Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
Fairstead operates more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states as an integrated owner, operator, and developer. That integrated structure matters here: when compliance, construction, and property management sit under one roof, the Community Manager at a Fairstead property isn't waiting on a third party to make decisions. You're close to the platform. That said, this specific role in Annapolis, Maryland carries real weight on its own. Affordable housing compliance means the margin for administrative error is thin, and the regulatory calendar never really stops.

The day-to-day here runs on two parallel tracks: financial performance and compliance. On the financial side, you're watching delinquency closely, directing monthly rent collection, pursuing arrears through legal channels when necessary, monitoring bad-debt write-offs, and attending monthly budget review meetings. On the compliance side, you're staying current with the HUD 4350.3 Handbook, managing REAC prep, clearing EHS violations, coordinating Management and Occupancy Reviews, handling LIHTC reviews, and conducting annual and interim recertifications. Those tracks intersect constantly. A tenant with lease compliance issues is often also a delinquency problem, and resolving it requires coordination across compliance, legal, and regional leadership.

You'll also supervise maintenance operations, conduct unit inspections, manage vendor bids and contractor quotes, and run bi-annual walk-throughs with the Building Superintendent. Fairstead properties often carry ongoing renovation and construction activity, so expect to coordinate site access, track project updates, and work directly with the construction team to keep violations off the books.

What strong candidates bring

  • At least three years of management experience that included direct team supervision
  • COS or CPO certification (required)
  • TCS certification for tax credit compliance
  • EIV system experience
  • Familiarity with Yardi and RealPage (preferred)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Affordable housing experience; HUD compliance knowledge is central to this role
  • Bachelor's degree preferred

The candidates who genuinely thrive in affordable housing community management tend to be detail-oriented on certification paperwork without losing sight of the human side of the work. Recertification seasons get compressed, MOR timelines don't move for anyone's convenience, and residents often have complex circumstances. Keeping occupancy healthy, delinquency in check, and compliance audit-ready at the same time is a skill that takes experience to do well. If you've built that discipline somewhere, this role puts it to use. The salary range for this position is $72,000 to $75,000.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager, EDE Apartments
job.description:
Most multifamily communities operate in a rhythm: lease, retain, operate, repeat. The Assistant Community Manager role exists to keep that rhythm steady when the Community Manager is pulled toward bigger-picture decisions. At EDE Apartments in Frederick, MD, that means owning the operational middle ground between leasing activity and financial accountability across 350 luxury units.
